The first one will help you find out the name of the land you are lying on.
And the other will help you calibrate that bizarre watch on your wrist.
Alright, now it's finally the right time to make things clear. Open your mouth and throw up whatever you have, sea water, questions ... Just get them all out, right here.
Who on earth are you? #Where's the guy who used to talk to me?
Oh, darling, it's an honor to be your first question and the one haunting your mind.

But I'm going to let you down, I'm afraid. I don't have any breathtaking stories to tell, just one simple fact after another. You know, the most popular topic among women my age is the healthy oatmeal our teeth can barely handle.

Luckily, my ears are more reliable than my teeth. I can still nag like I always do, answer questions to my knowledge, and have a little chit chat with you sometimes. So, to summarize it, just consider me a kindhearted chatterbox.
Oh darling, why not let it be? You're all on your own now. Don't ask for more when you already have someone to talk to, even if I'm only nagging most of the time.
We gotta let the past be the past, like how we deal with old newspapers, because all I speak is one simple fact after another.
Anyways, we will keep each other company for quite a while.
Where am I?
Finally, a question about yourself. In front of you is a boundless sea. All you can see, besides the beach you are lying on, is water, water, and water ...
A cry for help will be drowned out by the waves, and even the strongest legs are tied to the ground here and cannot break free.

See? There's no way to leave, but it's a good opportunity to have an island tour. The locals have good manners, so I think you can ask them to show you around. That's at least better than just goofing off.
What time is it now exactly?
Not even you can avoid asking this question. But a kindhearted soul already told you that time is moving forward as it used to be, step by step. So, the time is ... the year 2007.
Yes, time is back on the right track, going where it's supposed to be. Raindrops literally drop again, and no one goes back to the past anymore ... Well, some miss the good old days, though.

Oh ... You still doubt it, don't you? I can see it in your eyes. Don't get me wrong, I'm on your side. After all the hard times I have experienced, if anyone told me that my life was just a boring dream, one neither good nor bad, I would throw a shoe at them!
Enough with the riddles.
I can tell you are being burned by anxiety. But to find the "time" you want, we need to comb through the situation, like how you do with your hair.
Time is like a Sachertorte, and now it has been divided into many pieces. On the largest piece stands the white chocolate card—yes, the last good days of the 20th century.

The gentlemen are still growing handlebar mustaches, and the ladies have not yet flattened the curves on their bodies. New money buys one art piece after another to show off their good taste. They don't even mind turning their homes into museums.
A cafe named San Marco officially opens, gathering the most outstanding intellectuals and writers of the time. They talk and laugh there, as if nothing could stand in their way.
Then the cafe receives a neurologist whose briefcase carries the interpretation of dreams, and celluloid film and projectors become a new means of expression for artists.
At this point, helmets remain intact in the warehouse, gauze only works in hospitals, bullets only fly in the firing range, and the flame that swallows lives is not even lit ...
But soon, soon enough ... the young people who swore to retrieve their homeland will take up daggers and guns to fulfill their oath.

Buildings will shake like a leaf, and rocks will fall off and hit the walls. Screams will try to break free from people's throats. At that moment, a clip will be loaded secretly, in the name of supreme honor.
A golden age is about to end. A vortex of blood is already swirling in the river of time, waiting to devour everything that passes by.

When that actually happens, all the beautiful curves derived from nature, the <nobr>bee-shaped</nobr> brooches, the punch, the eiderdown duvets, everything will be destroyed, leaving only an insurance contract behind, and it doesn't even work.
Even this cafe will be smashed into concrete pieces.
See? We have combed the hair now. Everything I just talked about is the "time" you want.

Heh heh, you wouldn't buy the nonsense about the fairness of time when you reach my age.
It actually feels different between those who keep their eyes shut and those who keep theirs open; likewise, those who kill never share the same feeling with those who are killed; this is also true between those who have enough food to eat and those who are starving ...
Alright, that's it. I've talked enough. Now get up, darling, and brush the sand off yourself. Trust me, you will find your own answer to this era.

As you can see, this school on the island lives in a box made by the truth. Even if they have a donut in their hands when they are hungry, they still see a topological space—like the cute ring attached to an initiation toy—it's not food anyways.
But if you give them a puzzle, they will enjoy it like the best Kaiserschmarrn ... Oh, my apologies. I was not talking about the one you are holding.
It doesn't taste good.
No. With all due respect, that thing in your hand is pretty old: the mold on it seems to come from the 18th century, judging from the smell. I'm sure you know it will make you sick if eaten.
But we have to admit, it is not just ordinary mold. It reminds us of the story in which, once, a merchant's son looked up at the night sky and found the answer to the stars for us.
The young man firmly believed that the movement of the stars and the sun follow certain laws, just like how the delicate gears in a watch work together.
And his point was even proven correct by Zeus's grandfather! When another gentleman observed the sky through the reflecting telescope he took great pains to make, a celestial body was exactly there.
What was it called ... Emm, 19.6, the eighth number in the sequence, the seventh planet in the solar system, and the legendary God of the Sky.
If the world was not created by God, are there any theories we can use to explain such a beautiful law?

Yes, the one that says it never actually exists. Anyone can see the breach in this number sequence. That is the planet, which is supposed to be the fifth number in the sequence. I mean, how come we have never seen it before, if it does exist?
Either God is wrong or we've been blind all this time. What do you think?
God is wrong. #We've been blind all the time.
Oh, darling, I forgot that you are one of the boring people from the modern times.

You need to understand that we are talking about a forgotten masterpiece from the 18th century. Back then, everyone still believed that the imaginary creatures living on the stars got to witness the birth of God's creations and the everlasting temperature changes up there were set to punish the exiles. How romantic.
Yes, such a planet definitely exists, and as expected, it was discovered in the end. Yes, that's the Ceres. It only took that great mathematician an hour to find its orbit through calculation.
Oh, what great astronomy, what great mathematics, what great creation.
It was a beautiful dream, but it was still ended, eventually, by another discovery: the eighth planet.
Not the Ceres, nor the Uranus, but a new planet. People found it through more precise astronomical data and calculation, proving that the number sequence found by the merchant's son was only a myth.
Now we are clear of what we've been talking about: it's an unsolvable puzzle. It makes no sense from the very beginning.
We found the Ceres because it happened to be there. It is real, and no one can deny its existence.
In other words, we can perfectly prove the rationality of mathematics because we INVENTED it.
It's been a good dream, I suppose.

Now imagine that you're walking alone in the darkest valley ever, trying to drag your fragile body upward as much as possible before it is worn out. Hoarse cries squeeze their way out of your mouth to ask for response from the gods. Suddenly, an afflatus dawns on you. The next moment, a miracle happens: you are already at the top of the mountain, witnessing the rise of a huge celestial body from the skyline.
Even if it's only in your imagination, you have just witnessed the dawn of the Creation and the shock is real.
Come closer. That's right. Take a few more steps and immerse yourself in the shadow, including that hat. You don't want those good ears to hear this private conversation.
That pad of paper from the miss, yes, the one wielding the ruler, is quite valuable. I can tell it is of a certain age and records quite a lot of anecdotes.

One visitor to the island took out a baguette from his luggage. To share it with others, he made an attempt to parcel it off. Another visitor fell to the ground and happened to sit on a quart measure and break it ...
You can learn the punishments for them from the paper: the former was thrown into the sea, while the latter, into the further sea.
Only God knows how this <nobr>wine-dark</nobr> sea holds so many visitors.
Perhaps they can also resort to the debate.

Oh, the debate! That's really a pain in the neck for that logical, pragmatic assistant of yours, isn't it? People always tend to mark what they can't figure out as "arcanists' doings," as if things would make sense once they do so.
But it won't change the fact that the debate is only a game involving sophistry, improvisation, and straw man fallacy. So what makes it superior to beans, if the Form is what they are really after?
Anyways, whoever fools the others first will win the game, no arcanum at all.
And that argument of hers is the best attraction for the audience ... A special number, a "0."
The boundary between positive and negative numbers, huh? #Perhaps "∞" is a better choice.

You are neither positive nor negative, which means ... you don't belong to either side. Now imagine one side as an orderly line and the other as those wandering around. The wanderers can smell the abnormality in you, and of course, no one in that line sees you as one of them.
In a restaurant, fruits are served without the seeds, but in a farm, the seeds are retained for the next harvest.
Is there any value in the seeds? It depends on what you see when you look at them.
The moment you realize that, you have come to the crossroad of fate.
That's ambitious, darling, and I love it! But you need to know that infinity is the most unfamiliar thing for the people, and that's why it triggers the most curiosity.
Whoever tries to eat up this elephant with one bite will get all bloated and pinned by their own weight, waiting to die like a turtle upside down.
By then, I guess you would be eager to throw up the elephant and turn back into the adorable, easygoing "0" we all like.

See, just like you, people are always on the way to finding something that can satisfy them undoubtedly, as if what they already have was disappointing. They stare at the flame of the matches, read the tea leaves in the cup, and bustle around the instruments with star patterns ...
Now, back to the number we just talked about ... Oh my, it's the prediction of your whole life. Can you believe that?
You owe that spirited little genius a <nobr>thank-you</nobr> ... By the way, what do you see in her number?
A clever trick. #A number, "37."
Oh yes, of course, 37 is larger than 0.
But it's not so stable as 0. These prime numbers, they are just hard to divide ... because they have very few things in common with others.

That's why she's always so energetic, highly and solely focused on what she takes an interest in. She has nothing like the characteristics of the ones you know in the gray and white house. Those people are proud of themselves for having kindhearted factors around them.
As their teaching goes, it's always dangerous to be unique.
But some look up at her again and again exactly because they can sense the danger in her.
You are also a good example. You've been looking up, haven't you?
I always know you're a quick learner. You're very good at noticing new things.
That's right. 37 is only 37, a nice, unique prime number which equals the word "genius." At least everyone prefers to think this way.
Why not deify the one that is able to reach the truth when you have the chance? It's much easier to pin your hopes on others than to blame yourself.
I guess you also did that, right, darling?
It's okay. She never says no. She just lets the hopes pile up on her shoulder ... because she simply doesn't care at all.
What a good, good child.
Oh, look at you, climbing out of the cave in the allegory, all dusty and dirty like a little savage.
They must have tried to fill your little brain with long preachment, but you should feel lucky because at least they didn't give you a quiz right after that.
I was not listening. #What they said is true.
Oh, that's our expert on <nobr>absent-mindedness</nobr>. Yes, we should bear in mind those glory days of yours back in school.
Oh, how modest you are. Looks like you didn't spend all your student days catching tree frogs.
Try to reach the corners of your mind, if you would, and there you will find another bunch of people standing in front of a stone table.
Yes, those people in gowns, white gowns with gray diamond patterns. One of them was standing on the stairs, gathering all the little vacant eyes to his side. What was he called? Give me a second ...
Teacher, instructor, tutor, educator ... Just titles like that, no names at all. No one gets to write down their names on that banner, after all.
But they have nothing to complain about. You know what they say, "What is reasonable is real; that which is real is reasonable."

They showed you a broad avenue in their teachings, where you could enjoy a sense of security with all the solid ground, convenient automobiles, and warm sunshine. And at the end of the avenue even lies an inspiring mission, to which you are expected to devote your whole life.
There is a distinction between good and bad here, and it's as clear as our innate sense of right and wrong, like a floor of black and white tiles. Any stains on it will be noticed immediately.

But in fact, there exists another path in the woods. It's much less traveled, leading to the unknown darkness which cannot be seen with eyes or proved false. You may even experience indescribable chaos and madness there. This path, however, has an excellent view, and it's one of a kind: the plants are thriving with bursting energy, and the flowers are blooming in a delightful atmosphere.
... So, which will you take?
Perhaps the avenue. #I'm interested in the path.

Oh, of course, as you've been on it all the time. But that's exactly why you know how ... inflexible it is. You know that even better than any of those old fellas who have spent decades on it, don't you?
Just because you've been on it doesn't mean you can expect a comfortable journey, darling.
But luckily, there's still one more way you can take. It would be a good choice if you want to enjoy the scenery without getting lost in the darkness.

Oh, that's not an easy choice to make. This grandma must give you a round of applause. I would have even pinned a boutonniere to your suit if I had one. But I have to remind you, those things in there are not easy to deal with. They can drive you insane, and you have to be very careful ...
You've seen the living proof: many were freaked out after they came back, and people had to tie and lock them up; others even dug their own graves.
Oh my, that was a bit over the top. I hope I didn't scare you, darling.
Another way?
I'm sure you know that myth.
"You shall take the soul of your love out of the underworld, yet you shall not look back." That's right. You shall pass by the sleeping sirens, yet you shall not make a sound.
The ones with a belief set off. They entered the dark woods barefooted, yet moved so smoothly as if they were walking on the avenue.
They kept their mouths shut and eyes forward. They never turned back, never picked up what was not theirs, never set foot on the forbidden lands, and never looked straight at the sacred greatness.
They showed frugality, patience, and wisdom in the face of hunger and danger.

So the beasts continued to lurk in the shadow, and the ones with a belief passed through the woods safely until the path disappeared along with the direction sign. Then the first one to look back gave an exclamation before being exiled.
Is it really reasonable to take it?
Think about what I just said, "That which is real is reasonable."
Never look back in the woods, darling! If you don't want to be turned into a pillar of salt which can do nothing but wail, then ... NEVER, EVER look back.
Yes, we'd better stay awake, stay calm, stay cautious all the time.

But then there comes the problem: how can anyone ... how can you ignore your love for those thriving plants and blooming flowers? How are you supposed to deal with the unstoppable feeling that overflows like a melody when it is stirred up by the beauty of the scenery?
Of course, you will cry the loudest cry, dance the wildest dance, drink the strongest drink, and vomit all the filth inside you.
After all, there is no need to enter the woods if the <nobr>soul-stirring</nobr> scenery is not what you are after, right?
It doesn't sound like a good way.
No, so you'd better let it slip your mind, darling.
Just let it go, and hurry forward. Remember to keep your eyes shut and hold your breath.
When you do so, the scenery will no longer mean anything to you, nor will the fragrance of the flowers. You will get out of the woods and reach where the truth lies.
Is that what you want? Don't worry. We have plenty of time. You may come back at any time and pick another way.
Come here. Place your hand on it. Feel the texture. The craft is one of a kind, not some cheapie you can get from the flea market.
I mean it. This is a kilim, and even the most traditional, delicate, and expensive kind. It has applied fiery red as the dominant color, and the stitches are perfectly neat.
Where does it come from?
From the sea, just like you, darling.
It arrived with a meerschaum pipe, a glass jar, a pack of sugar cubes, and a child in panic.
Both she and the kilim were born on the land where the craft originated. Their appearances apply the same dominant color, and the patterns in them share similar complexity.
Who is the child?

Oh, your curiosity is aroused? But we are not done with the carpets yet. You've always gotta get a souvenir or two every time you reach a new place, so you will have something to show when you tell the stories one day, right?

Look at these handmade fabrics. How splendid ... Those incredible patterns were the only thing on the craftswomen's minds when they made the carpets. It's safe to say they have spent their whole life improving their skills at using the vertical loom, and that's how we get these carpet knots arranged in beautiful lines.
But they are just people like us. What if they get distracted? What if the carpet knots go off the right track and get tied to the wrong threads?
Then you will be in trouble, big trouble! All the problems in the universe will come at you, and the situation will be even worse than the bureaucratic system of a millennial empire.
Damn it! Damn it! DAMN IT! #Can't we do something to fix it?
Calm down. Many swear like you do when there is nothing they can do.
They always step into the same river named Mistake again and again. That's why we need THEM, those crossing the river with their rulers, spanners, tool boxes, and dusty faces.
I like the pragmatic quality in you. I'm sure it will make your life even more wonderful. The people will be impressed and line up to tackle the problems for you.
Oh, don't be mad. Some make troubles, and others deal with the troubles. That happens.
You know, every question has a questioner when they are raised. Likewise, every error has a corrector when they are corrected. That's how we get to know THEM.
Them?
The Correctors, an ancient profession.

Their duty is to remove the loose threads and iron out the wrinkles on the carpets. In the language of this island, that is to check the calculations on the papyri and even the holes on the punched tapes.

No one is capable of doing this job except the altruists, because it is similar to unraveling a ball of wool. Besides finding the end of the threads, you must always pay attention to the cats. Yes, the cats. They may jump on the ball and make things even worse.
And she, the <nobr>red-haired</nobr> little girl with the carpet in her arms, was overwhelmed at the beginning.

Not yet familiar with the ruler, she tried her best to find the end of the threads. So the cats took the opportunity to jump on her together and left countless scratches on that little forehead. Poor girl.
See, that's the problem every Corrector has to deal with: their job is to correct errors, but what if their own existence is also part of the errors?
Oh, it's no big deal. There is more than one loom in this world.
She left the complicated patterns behind and came to this simple kingdom featuring numbers only.

There she made the first contact with the spinning loom named geometry. She had never seen anything like that before, and it was almost impossible for her to comprehend how it worked. She could hardly convert the numbers on the books into an actual diagram in her brain.

Without a whole picture of what she was working on, she resorted to her hard work, and more hard work. Then a long time passed, leaving one wound after another on her fingers. Later, the wounds even became calluses.
In the end, her hands were no longer tender, but tough enough to resist the damage from the loom. Yes, she has won a place on this island for herself.
I am happy for her.

Yes, she's a quick learner. She learned even faster than some of the locals, but that was not enough, because she has been outmatched by her playmate, the leading one in the field of mathematics on the island.
That girl is like a perfect piece of satin born by nature. It is decorated by the beauty of mathematics and geometry, no manual work involved.
In order to reach the showcase where that perfect piece lies, and ... to stay on the right track and fit into the school ...
She has done everything she could.
But, BUT! She is still the most distinctive carpet there.
Anyone can tell that as long as they spend some time on the island.
It's not wrong to be distinctive.
Of course not. She's only a bit "different" from others.
So she will continue to weave on the loom until one day the spindle pierces her callus and the fire burns everything to the ground.
Shh, I should stop here. You know that mathematician who was thrown into the sea? He died because he said something he shouldn't have.
Cut not wood on a public road; open not an unwanted bottle.
I don't know what to say next. I guess the best line for this circumstance is, "See you later."
If you look at the ground after the "rain," you can often see a wet, long trail like this one.
At the end of the trail, there may be a snail slowly crawling forward. Yes, "forward." The snail marks the direction for us.
But, what if we don't see any snails at either end? How are we going to distinguish the direction to the future from that to the past?
We need a criterion. #Sorry, but I have no idea.
"Criterion," well said, darling. To figure something out, you always need to make deductions based on facts and logical reasoning.

What you see is not necessarily true, but what is logical is, because we haven't witnessed or experienced anything illogical so far. If something like that actually happens, it must be because we are too ignorant to understand it for the moment.
This point was firmly believed by those researchers who worked in the house like canned sardines.

It remained true to them until the first drop of rain rose. The sardines suddenly found that the knowledge they possessed couldn't support the point anymore. The can was opened, revealing a completely different thinking pattern to them.
Whatever they used to mend the can, there was still a crevice left between the inside and the outside, and it could be ripped open again at any time.
Oh, you just figured out how those researchers handled matters: face the ignorance and do everything they could to find the answers.

When the rain rose, they struggled to collect every component left, hoping to preserve the castle built by science. Unfortunately, the effort was in vain. Another wave washed away the castle and restored it to quicksand.

Even so, they still worked hard in that house like canned sardines to record what was happening, because they believed at least the can holding them was a safe place. Yet in the end, they found that the can was only another sandcastle on the beach.
Everything they were familiar with disappeared when the first drop of rain rose.
What happened then?
The chaos didn't last. If it really was the rain that swept away the snail and messed up time ... then, we should look at the silver lining.
Does it mean we will find out the truth of time once the secret of the rain is revealed? There has never been a shortcut like this one, since time is only an intangible concept.

So then, observation stations were built all over the globe. The staff learned how to collect and keep the valuable samples efficiently in no time. The little boxes they used to store the raindrops are still being upgraded even now.
Order and silence were brought back to the labs. Every piece of gear was placed back on the right track.
It was a grand feat, and no one could have accomplished it inside this huge, cumbersome machine except another machine. She took no sides and sought only predictable results.

That's why she made a decision as soon as she read that report and its attachment on her desk. The former was about a delicate component which flapped like a butterfly in that huge machine, and the latter was a piece of paper full of circles and dots.
Then she stored the information on her hard disk and destroyed the report.
And the paper which claimed to have recorded the locations where the "Storm" might happen—yes, the one with the <nobr>butterfly-like</nobr> drawings—was retained for data comparison.
She seems satisfied with the result.

Not long ago, the previous UTTU Flash Gathering came to a peaceful end amidst the applause and cheers of the Uluru Games. Remembering the sweat and the shouts, it's as if the flames in the torch are still burning. During the event, arcanists and humans alike took to the field with enthusiasm, reveling in the pure joy of competition. We noticed that after the games, many spectators remained absorbed in their books, giving a silent curtain call to this historic sporting event.

Now, those returning from the mists have brought with them stories and curiosities from ancient Eastern lands—about a travel interview, a collection of observations, a local chronicle, and the birth and death of a question. Writing with a soft brush is indeed a unique experience, but words are always faithful and eternal messengers. To this end, the UTTU Flash Gathering awaits your visit amidst the fragrance of wine in the quiet alleys.

Welcome to UTTU. This is a magazine.

Don't skip this page.
Unlike those useless prefaces filled with boring platitudes, this one is important.
Reader's guide

1. Don't doubt the truth of UTTU. We only tell true stories that happened to real arcanists.
2. You only need one copy of UTTU. After you make the seasonal subscription, the copy will update itself on 15th every month.
<line-height=120%>
3. Whenever the copy updates itself, please place it below a cupboard or the firewood in a fireplace, but do not leave<line-height=80%>
any fire or light. Then step back to 8.8 feet away and wait for <nobr>10-15</nobr> minutes. It is normal to hear
the sounds of sewing and crawling during the update.<line-height=110%>
4. Don't be confused about the interviews of artworks. Please note that anything can be an artwork: they can be alive, <line-height=80%>or dead. Whoever has a story to tell can be deemed an artwork.

5. You might smell a fine aroma from the pages while reading an interview. This is normal. 6. Do not be shocked by live photographs, and do not let any of them come in contact with dark coffee or matches. 8. Keep UTTU away from fire. This is an arcanum magazine and is definitely not fireproof.

<margin=0.2em>9. Although it's not fireproof, UTTU is waterproof, but please do not soak it in water for long. If you do so by mistake, please prepare enough insect repellent.<line-height=125%>
<margin=0em>10. Don't ask where article 7 is.
11.  If you see any ads about nightmare recycle on the attached pages, do not call<line-height=100%>
the number on it or make any attempt to catch those monsters. If your children report strange <nobr>goings-on</nobr> to you, comfort them with one extra milk candy before bedtime.<line-height=130%>
12. Try to enjoy reading UTTU.

like a weaver in silence, or a moth light trap in the dark night.

The Wilderness consists of multiple <color=#cc492f>hexagonal Islands</color>. You can <color=#cc492f>decide each one's orientation</color> when you place it.
Environments and Blocks
An island consists of 7 parts: 6 blocks and the center
Plain
Every block may have one of the four environments, each of which provides <color=#cc492f>1 Prosperity</color> of the corresponding type.
On an island, blocks of the same environments which are not directly connected must be connected through the center
Connect the Blocks

On an island, <color=#cc492f>blocks of the same environments</color> which are not directly connected can be connected through the center

Expansion Task

Oasis
There are oases floating in the Wilderness. They contain different environments.

Connect <color=#cc492f>oases</color> to the <color=#cc492f>Wilderness</color> to form islands.
Blocks connected to an oasis enjoy <color=#cc492f>double</color> Prosperity.
Islands already connected to one oasis cannot benefit again from a second oasis.

Being small also means not having the strength to move rocks.

Carbuncles cannot fight other critters. Consider your moves carefully.

About your unfamiliar friends

Your friends, who don't share your "eccentric brain wiring," are all here.
They don't quite fit in with the established rules that you know so well, but for the sake of comprehension, let's set aside the gap between science and arcanum and try to understand the rules as best we can.
Reunion of Fires Gameplay Intro

Move the character to within four blocks of the bonfire to light it.
Lighting all the bonfires on the field will result in challenge success.

The area in front of the guardian statue is very dangerous.
Stepping into it will result in an attack, leading to challenge failure.

Move towards the guardian statue from a <nobr>non-frontal</nobr> direction
to defeat it.
Once a bonfire is lit, it will not go out. If you fail the challenge midway, you will automatically revert to the state when the bonfire was just lit.
After lighting the bonfire, the character will gain energy. Tapping on a statue on the character's <nobr>cross-shaped</nobr> path will consume energy to launch a fireball at it, destroying it.
Patrolling statues will move straight ahead in their current direction.
When unable to move forward, the patrolling statues will turn around. If a statue encounters a character, the challenge will fail.
The statue starts in an idle state.
When a character passes directly in front of it, the statue will activate and begin chasing the character at the beginning of the next round. If the character is caught, the challenge fails.
<nobr>Wind-eroded</nobr> ground becomes fragile when stepped on by characters or statues.
Stepping on more fragile ground will cause it to collapse, causing characters or statues above it to fall. Collapsed ground cannot be crossed.
When a slate trap is triggered, crossbows across the map will fire straight ahead, destroying the first character or statue they hit.
Ulu does not trigger <nobr>wind-eroded</nobr> ground or slate traps, but also cannot cross collapsed ground.
As the Driven Snow Falls Gameplay Intro
1. Each advance distance is random. Reaching the target altitude allows for a Safe Retreat.
2. You can check your current state and that of the area.
3. You can check the materials gained from this exploration.
4. Each advance will consume AC. Retreating before reaching the target altitude will cause a loss of materials gained.
5. Displays the current and maximum altitude of the area.
1. Record events are considered special events. Once encountered, they will not appear again.

1. Upon reaching the target altitude, you can still attempt to challenge the maximum altitude. However, if your AC turns negative during the challenge, you will be forced to withdraw immediately and lose some materials.
Revival Journey Gameplay Intro
1. Complete the character's Revival Journey tasks for corresponding rewards.
2. Unlock subsequent Revival tasks upon meeting conditions.
3. Claim the final reward upon completing all Revival Journey tasks for a character.
4. Revival Journey tasks are marked on the map with a special color.
5. <nobr>Quick-positioning</nobr> is possible by tapping on a character's portrait on the map or the "Go" button in tasks.
Hotspots Exploration Gameplay Intro
1. Players assist Ulu in traversing every inch of the Hotspots to help Ulu recall the past.
2. Tapping an unlocked location on the map allows for <nobr>quick-positioning</nobr>.
3. Tasks will appear on the map as elements.
4. Dispatch character for the torch relay. Sending in characters that meet the criteria under certain conditions can shorten the relay time.
5. Completing the torch relay unlocks other areas along the route.
Companion's Journey Gameplay Intro
1. Once the Companion's Journey begins, players will receive special combat bonuses in battle.
2. Building connections with Eucalyptus Pods obtained during the Revival Journey provides special bonuses to the Fire Totem.
3. Only one of the blessings can be chosen per location.
Strange Doctor periodically enters [Mastermind] status with reduced DMG Taken.
When "Futurism" runs out of [Energy], Strange Doctor enters [True Form Exposed] status with increased DMG Taken.
Darkness of the Abyss periodically attacks and inflicts [Frostbite]. When [Frostbite] reaches 5 stacks, the target enters [Freeze] status. When [Freeze] ends, the target loses massive HP.
Targets in [Frostbite] must act twice in one round or receive a [Purify] incantation to avoid the [Freeze] status.
Gold in the Cave will periodically attack the target with the highest ATK, leaving them in [Disarm] status. Choose an appropriate party member to receive the attack.
Try to inflict [Stats Down] and [Neg Status] effects on Gold in the Cave to weaken the enemy and strengthen allies.

Seven arcanist organizations, including Manus Vindictae, have been identified as terrorist organizations.
Powered by the Mesmers, the Foundation became partners with several mental health organizations.
Since the headquarters of New York Times had moved to Manhattan, USA, Longacre Square was renamed Times Square.
NASA announced the selection of seven astronauts for a brand new space program, one of whom is an arcanist.
The novel, The Great Gatsby was officially published. Druvis III read it, but did not leave any comment.
A criminal gang composed entirely of arcanists. They used rapid cooling and <nobr>through-the</nobr>-wall arcane skills to steal a train in New York.
Soviet astronaut Gagarin went into space on Vostok 1 and circled the Earth once.
Unless there are special circumstances, Zeno Arms Academy always starts a new term on this day.
In 1900, the Eleventh World's Fair opened in Paris, and several arcanists were invited to attend.
SPDM had a conference on how to combine arcanum education with liberal studies.
The Laplace Scientific Computing Center starts its annual budget review on this day every year. The head of every lab will be busy in the following days.
J. P. Morgan was born. He would grow up to be a famous American financier who had a close relationship with the Pax House.
A French arcanist announced that they had created an extremely explosive potion. Considering its cost, however, many would stick with the nitroglycerin.
The U.S. announced it would go off the gold standard. The arcanum world in the US immediately stated it would not give up the use of its currency, the Sharpodonty.
An underground pub called "The Walden" opened for business. The owner provides his special <nobr>non-alcoholic</nobr> concoctions which tasted like alcohol.
The British Daily Mail published a photo of the Loch Ness Monster, which caused a sensation.
A French knight mistook A Knight as a normal armor and took it back to his residence.
Bette played a part with lines for the first time. Although the lines were only "Okay" and "Thank you," she believed it was a step to a new future.
Several arcanists in the Nile River Valley claimed to have experienced an unusual polar day, the cause of which was unknown.
Two biologists discovered the double helix of DNA together. By now, most of the  arcanists agree to the view that arcane skills are also inherited through DNA.
Medicine Pocket published a personal paper on the research of the Picrasma Tree in an internal journal of Laplace Scientific Computing Center, which provoked extensive discussion.
Erick did "well" in the exam by achieving 45 points out of 100.
Necrologist completed the commission of a mister in the tomb, which was to publish his poems and to donate the remuneration.
A Knight witnessed a war that took place in France. It nearly wiped France out of the map, but thankfully, a hero showed up.

<nobr>An-an</nobr> Lee was attacked by sea monkeys when she carried out an exorcism commission at some port. That battle showed her the Ghost Catcher also works on <nobr>non-supernatural</nobr> beings.
The Empire State Building was formally put into use. It was the tallest building in the world at the time.
The De Havilland Comet was first time in service. The <nobr>Long-distance</nobr> travel via an airplane thus became the reality.
13 arcanum species including Griffin were declared "Extinct" by Laplace Scientific Computing Center.
A French arcanist in the far east discovered a mysterious creature that was black and white.
Sotheby spent a large sum of money on three "Nightmares with a special skin color" in Kentucky. Actually they were just three maroon Thoroughbreds.
To promote the Paris Exposition, the Eiffel Tower was officially opened to the public.
A bank in Switzerland announced to provide deposit service in Sharpodonty.

Dream Talk

<size=40>Over</size> a thousand years ago, a traveling priestess brought back a pot of red rock powder for her tribe.
Staring down at it, she told a story.
REVERSE 1999
v1a5_df_sign_rockpaper_03
We have bestowed the warmth of the tribe and the stalwartness of family on the "Kangaroo." It is the way home.

<size=40>A</size> woman was separated from her tribe while hunting and couldn't find her way home. She wandered in the wilderness for seven days and seven nights until she was finally brought back home to her tribe on the back of a kangaroo.
Her survival was a miracle, and from that moment on, her people firmly believed that those tall, strong beasts were guides who would always carry them home. This belief dissolved into her bloodline, lasting thousands of years and giving this place the guardians of today.

<size=40>W</size>hen the world was first created, natural disasters were a common occurrence, and thus, the Malingee was born in the forests and wilderness. Giant rocks made up its body, its hulking joints grinding with every footstep. It lingered on the edges of the tribal grounds at night, afraid of the burning campfire.
The woman prepared to set off once again. This time, she would search for the eternal flame, for the glory of the tribe, having heard the legend of the <nobr>many-colored</nobr> lizard.
v1a5_df_sign_rock_01

<size=40>A</size>t that time, the world was devoid of color. The sun god sent a colorful lizard to the world, which cut itself open and gushed its colors upon the land, transforming the world into something entirely new. Its green blood spread into the forest, its blue eyes seeped into rivers and lakes, its yellow scales coated the mountains, and its purple bones crumbled into the valleys. As for its red heart, it landed in the center of the land, like a protruding belly button.
v1a5_df_sign_rockpaper_01
We bestow the dexterity of sport and the focus of perspicacity upon this colorful lizard with its joyful heart.
v1a5_df_sign_rock_02

<size=40>T</size>he woman passed her <nobr>coming-of</nobr>-age ceremony and became a priestess.
She hunted and killed a bison, pinned its skull to her waist, and then set off on a journey.
This skull called to her so that she never forgot to look up at the night sky. In the sky, a winding band of light shone. It was a fish. Its shadow fell on the ground so that she could tread on it and never get lost in the desert.
v1a5_df_sign_rockpaper_02
We bestow the brightness of life and the expansiveness of memory upon this lively fish, the guide of the starry sky.

<size=40>Through</size> forests, across lakes, over hills, and upon peaks, the woman searched. She found the red heart of the earth. It was a huge red rock.
The woman removed the bison's skull, upon which it rolled around in the soil and transformed back into a bison. There, they fought again, but this time not as enemies but as friends. Seeing such a scene, the heart of the colorful lizard began to beat again.

"<size=40>"I</size> love all that you are, and so I will bestow upon you an undying fire."
He promised the woman a stunning flame and asked her to pursue it for herself. "You will find it.
Go—find it. You know its heat, its form. It will burn in the same posture as you when you run. Remember to keep its call on your knees."

<size=40>T</size>hat's it, the heart of the colorful lizard said, I love everything so very much—the running and the flying dust. The way you stand shoulder to shoulder with your friends is so mesmerizing. I used to jump like that, but then my body took on this giant stony form.
The woman replied, "I am just as happy as you are. My heart is as passionate, brave, and generous as yours. Three hundred days from now, when the sun turns around the rainbow, I will lead my friends to see you again. Please prepare some land for us to run upon freely."

"<size=40>Indeed</size>, indeed," the lizard's heart said, "I have bestowed upon you the heart of hearts, the bones of bones. Bring all of the creatures best at running and swimming before me." A red rock then rolled down from the valley.

<size=40>S</size>o the woman, with her heart and bones, rode on a red clay cow and returned to her tribe.
By that time, she had grown old. Her relatives were no longer there, and the children no longer recognized her face.
She leapt from the back of the cow, and the red stone turned to dust. She put it in a bucket and threw it into the fire, then said that this was Malingee's Harvest, and that they were going to meet a great heart.

Trail ① Theater Impressions
*breath in* *breath out* <nobr>O-oh</nobr>, you're here? Not a good time. As you can see, my eyes are barely open.
*sighs* In the blink of an eye, my dream slips away like a deer into the deep of the forest.
Were you dreaming?
Heh, what kind of question is that? You make it sound like me dreaming is the most ridiculous thing in the world!
I have to remind you, except for some <nobr>out-dated</nobr> wisdom, there is nothing different between your head and mine, dearie.
What did you dream of?
I'm as curious about that as you are.
You could always allow me to return to my soft bed to try to summon that dream again. But even then, it likely won't be the same dream.
See, we seldom remember our dreams, and even what we don't forget can be hard to understand. And that's why we need a dream interpreter.
A doctor that values Shakespeare above his patients, and cigars above his own career—a doctor like Sigmund Freud.
He lures out forgotten memories from your past, through a technique called "free association." Through this, he can reveal what makes you who you are.
All you need to do is to lie on the sofa, and spill out your thoughts like old milk.

Once you do that, your mental health will surely improve. The sleepwalkers stop falling out of their beds, the hysterical go back to their sewing, with enough time maybe Nietzsche could write a comedy.
"But what about the medical journals?" You may ask. He must have released them. Otherwise, how could we prove the effectiveness of his treatments?
And he has. You can read them in journals, in the text books, and hear them in the chattering of medical students—
Your name will be blacked out on the pages by then, but your dreams will become the latest gossip on everyone's lips.
It's not good for the patients.
Oh my dear, all medicine has side effects. The best medicine is bitter to the taste.
It must be tolerated for the sake of the treatment. How else will these patients free themselves from their mental cages of unconscious desire and delusion?
It really is the smallest of prices—a mere coffee stain on your shirt, just telling a few people about an unlucky moment or two.
Besides, the patient does not give a name. The true protagonist remains a secret between you and the doctor.
Heh. Perhaps you're right. It's not the only way ...
What's the other, then?
Come, listen ... Do you hear that? That shrill, piercing sound of metal on the skull, the <nobr>blood-cuddling</nobr> screams ... Even the strongest soul would quake in fear.
But this is the other way. However, funny enough, some people prefer the pain. It ends faster than a hard talk with the doctor.
Look at this, dearie. This kind of hand mirror has become the latest fashion. Oh, it's a trifling thing, but people like me have to stay in the loop to make a living.
Come here. Gaze into the mirror, and fix your hat. What do you see? Do you like what you see?
I feel as if I can see all of Vienna.#I, I ... I!#It's broken.
A clever answer! I can tell you will fit right in here.

But there is still much left to see beyond the mirror. Oh. The young folk step to an <nobr>ever-changing</nobr> waltz. If you want to follow their trends, you'll need perfect timing to join the swirling dance.

Some have fallen behind. They lounge by the fountains of the park, bemoaning their lives and the price of rent. Come the next banquet and exhibition, they arrive wearing a new fine coat, but underneath their linens are ragged and old.
The mirror's reflection held a silver sheen once. Now it's tarnished at the edges.
Oh, look at our little artist in the mirror.
Something of a narcissist, then? No, I'm not laughing at you. In this place, valuing one's uniqueness, one's own voice is much to be desired.
You have to be loud enough, firm enough to show no fear, nor hesitation. So that at the end of the waltz, you will have the strength to break their instruments.
Is that so? Oh, has something gone wrong? Did an old lady like me waste her money?
Or, perhaps what it reflects is the "truth."
The mirror shows reality, nothing more, nothing less. So, it may be that there is nothing to see, or it may be something that can't be seen.
But things change, darling, especially in this city. Like an avalanche taking everything in its path, changing them irrecoverably and inevitably.
So next time when you look into a mirror like this, you may just see something else. Be patient.
So?
So, in the warmth of spring, the ice cracks deeper. One splinters into two, and each begins to splinter again.
They set up the mirror and lift the cloth exposing to light—the good, the bad, and what lies beyond them both.
Then the factions split and then split again. "Secessionists," by their nature, are not in the business of keeping things together. They won't stop the fractures—they can't.
In lifting the cloth and seeing their reflection, they scatter themselves like dandelion seeds in the wind.
Where are they going?

Oh, I don't know where, but I do know what they're doing. Some of them still paint with gold leaf, others believe they must depict what is real, some depict the ravings of their dreams, some seek to change the streets into works of art, and others drive out all meaning from their work.
The only time they ever reach an agreement is just before they lift the cloth from the mirror.
Before the Potemkin village with all its empty facades moves somewhere else, some of them might just achieve their ends.
To be like the golden cabbage sitting atop its dome over the Ring Road—to be recognized by everyone.
Let's start our conversation with a simple exercise. First, please repeat after me: Dittarsdorf.
After all the days you've spent in Vienna, you should be familiar with the name. Tell me, how do you feel about it?
Nothing worth mentioning.#Seems like it's a word as heavy as lead.
Nothing indeed. Well, you've become numb to it after hearing it so many times, on the street corners, in the cafes, every place you go.
You can't blame them for that. Most at least speak kindly of them, so long as you don't pick up on the venom hiding in their words.
These days, to be an opera singer is more glorious than any noble title; it supersedes them all! The Dittarsdorfs are the true nobles, the ones who can create art through "channeling."
Haha, you are making light of it again. But fair enough, you're new here, not as familiar with this name as those who live here, murmuring it in their dreams.

Most of the time, it swirls invisibly through the conversations on the street; other times, it is tangible in the signatures of the exhibits, seen in the performances and the metal badges clinging to collars ... and always in the boys and girls who inherit the Dittarsdorf talents.
And just like that, they are thrust into the role of the outstanding Dittarsdorfs, the lady songbird and the artistic painter.
In truth, I don't know much at all about these "Dittarsdorf."
Oh, of course. Well, then, high time to tell you about them.

Vienna, at present, is a splendid, crumbling house. Whenever the waltz starts playing, the roof trembles along with the music. While the dancing crowd—and funny that it is a crowd—none of them dare look up at it!

The people here live in identical, pretty, little houses, the social classes smoothed out like butter on a cake. Now, works of art become their icons, and in their madness, they scramble to make these beautiful, dazzling things.

The Dittarsdorfs, nobles who can perform channeling, are made to perform like dancing animals in a circus. Businessmen and nobles clamoring to sponsor their performances in order to glorify themselves.
The noble ladies prefer to curate the finest acts, highlighting their good taste and fashionability, while the lordlings seem to prefer new and hidden talents as some example of their virtue.

How, then, could a good singer ever miss a performance? But she must, to take her chance, seizing the lovely bird in her hand—that poor, noble little bird, because people said that she was born with madness.
And it is in this act of "fighting against her madness" that she proves herself proper among the noble ladies.
She knows better than anyone why a piece of art is valuable, and how to make it worth even more.
The Danube, a river born from dewdrops grown into a mighty course. She is a mother to many children, and all are eager to be fed.
Here is the empire founded by two of her strongest children—a rich and admirable duo.
There is an alluring charm to the music of Musikverein, captivating everyone who visits this place. I can talk about its art all day, and that's just the beginning!
There are 11 children in this empire. When bond together, they are invincible.
Their enemies will face catastrophe.
See, the flourishing cities, the cheering citizens, even the chirping birds are singing a song of a land of freedom.
Something's not right.#Hmm ... What a promising picture.
Heh heh ho. You're familiar with the devils in the detail.
Ah. You're just buying everything I'm selling. Be smart, my dear.
You'll see, if we dive deeper, you'll see something different.
You'll see charity dances raising funds for the poor. The icing on the cake for the philanthropist, they said, though no one knows where the money goes.
You'll see mice eating the bodies of the beggars, the arcanists being ousted from their arts, and poverty spreading its misery like an illness.
Except in the great duo, Austria and Hungary, in the vast and intimidating centers of power they've built together.
The other children, however, were shut out at the door. They may have their talents, but that alone cannot buy them a place at the table.
Bohemia, Moravia ... The empire has only the slightest sympathy to these forgotten children, nothing more than articles of fine words written in the newspapers.
How funny it is. To see these poor humans now sharing in the same fate as the arcanists.
Do you think they will choose to hold together, even if left outside of the negotiation table?
Cooperation is the only way they can survive.#People are stubborn.
That's no small task. A chain is only as strong as its weakest link. An <nobr>age-old</nobr> story.
Oh. So you're a pessimist. Then, I guess, you will enjoy the drama of this broken family.
The truth is, they will fight each other like rats in the barrel, until every one of them falls.
Crack, crack. Did you hear it? It's the fracturing of a great empire, like the breaking of spring ice.
In an army that speaks twenty different languages, who can a general trust to obey his commands?
Only those who speak the language he does.
You can already imagine it—a ridiculous beast with 11 limbs, each pulling in their own direction, limping across the battlefield until it gets shot ...
Luckily, that time hasn't come yet.
The crying of the children is still being drowned out by the music playing in the theater, and the beating hearts within the dancers' chests.
The wails of suffering are silent in the newspapers, and the world sees only the silvery mirage of freedom and prosperity.
Believing all these children can live in harmony.
But my darling, we know that the ice must break. It's as inevitable as the thaw of spring.
Ah ... A lovely day to rest at an outdoor cafe, isn't it, darling? Everyone working here is a capable server and knows how to address you properly with "my lady."
I'm here for one simple thing: information. With a careful ear to the <nobr>goings-on</nobr>, a shrewd businesswoman can gather all the latest news.
Oh, there she comes, that girl in green with the bouncing feathers in her hat. Don't worry. She can't hear us from here.
I know her.
Of course, you do. Isn't she our lively little cockatoo? She says she's a psychiatrist, but with all the work she does for the people, she's more like Vienna's own Robin Hood.
Look at those people around her, <nobr>tut-tut</nobr>. With their gold cufflinks and patched sleeves ... Very likely they're from Leopoldstadt.
You can hear them saying, "Our golden era is finally here! Forget all these melodramatic rumors!"
Leopoldstadt?
Maybe you know it by a different name? Perhaps you caught a glimpse of it under the list of exhibit sponsors?
Europe, at that time, welcomed people from all over the world; its culture and art held as their highest ideals; its institutions believed they held the keys to paradise.
They once believed that they were the lucky few. Blessed with the wisdom of a golden age, that's why they still linger here even after the smoke of war faded the glimmers of gold away.
It's not surprising to see our lady with them. See, she loves to seek these <nobr>well-hidden</nobr> things, and chirp along with the most overlooked voices.
But I feel sorry for her, because she herself overlooks some of these <nobr>teeny-tiny</nobr> things said at her own expense.
What things?
Words taken as jokes. Ignored because her wishes and anticipation outweigh their sting.

But while songs are floating in the wind, the clock keeps ticking, people in the cafe talk about the secessionists and the newest plays in the same breath ... No one cares about the rumors trafficked in the newspapers. They're only concerned with what is in front of their eyes ...
Still, the good doctor comes to share the pain of that melancholy lady, and then, next to the cafe, to encourage the lower class to persevere.
She says that every man is entitled to the same rights. She'll draw a circle around them all, like the Ring Road or the round mirrors in her clinic.
"The good times will come again," so say the coffee sippers. But you know, in the end, they'll be like the undissolved sugar at the bottom of the cup.
My dear, your coffee is getting cold.
Darling, did you hear that? The sound of a match scraping against the box, igniting in a dark, silent alley ... and then, "BOOM!"
War, like an unstoppable train, hurtles down the track with its passengers, vanishing in the thick, black smoke.
In the train, the elderly tremble in the corner, and the infants babble dreaming ...
Ah, but the only young man aboard is filling coal into the furnace. Meanwhile, another train is hurtling down the same track, puffing the same black smoke ...
Alas. The two trains are destined to collide, in "a war to end all wars."
Who are the passengers on the other train?
Pay close attention. You'll see the banner reaching out above their train, and the bloodstains on it.
Next, let's turn to where the train departed, to find the source of everything.
Rewind the clock to before the whistle blew, before the furnace ignited ...
And then, child, look somewhere far from here—in the Schönbrunn Palace, where the fine gentlemen of <nobr>Austria-Hungary</nobr> eagerly plan the extension of their national borders.
But the Habsburgs value their "honor" so much that first they must find themselves some excuse to cross that border.
Yet in another land, a humiliated people were gathering in secret. Their blood as hot as fire, ready to burn anyone and anywhere it was splattered.
Fate drove an <nobr>open-topped</nobr> car there, carrying an <nobr>ill-fated</nobr> couple. Their presence a crushing indignity that could not be endured.
An avenging bullet was sent to them as a gift from a <nobr>luck-struck</nobr> patriot.
In a moment, each party was granted their <nobr>long-sought</nobr> excuse. Boots had their excuse to kick down their doors, and guns their excuse to fire.
A yearning furnace at last had its reason to burn, to steam toward its final destination.
My dear, it's not a story of hatred or anger. The footprints were laid down before you ever stepped forward into them.
<nobr>Fresh-faced</nobr> boys traded books and toys for rifles, and poets were buried in trenches, musicians deafened by explosions and the howls of death.
But those <nobr>war-starters</nobr>? Those who doodled their ambitions on maps while supping their dessert, would lose nothing in their gamble.
The <nobr>dew-fed</nobr> river would still flow, and the facades of their great palaces would never be chipped or rocked by the guns they set off.
Nothing stains their hands, save the cream from their cakes.
Is there nothing we can do to stop all this?
Perhaps ... We wait. Wait for a pouring rain to douse the fires, a flood that might sweep the armies, wagered like betting chips, from their maps.
Then perhaps that car will turn, and the fated dead will come back to life—But you know that will not be how the story ends.
Hey, you! Yes, you, my hurried child, you rush through the street like a cyclone ... Where are you going?
I can't be late for the show!
A show, a show! So you came to Vienna for the love of stories. That's for sure.
Then this is just the right place for you. A place where the floors are decorated with gold, where music sings along with the stories ... Even a newcomer could be entranced here.
Oh, listen to me! You must not be a newcomer, but a true connoisseur! Well, before you leave, may I ask a simple question?
Which act in a show do you prefer?
Act One.#Act Three.#Act Five.#Every part of it.
Oh! Well begun is half done! You're always right to the point. We should know how a story starts and when we have stepped onto the path of fate.
Haha! The rising action! The most thrilling part, like biting into the filling of an apple strudel—you're about to have the sweetest part!

Yes, of course! The resolution, coming to its fated ending. We stand up and cheer, or stay in our seats and weep ... Our reward for not falling asleep during the intermission, worth every krone you've paid.
Haha, so greedy. It's a tough choice, isn't it? But you can't escape from making decisions.
Do you know which act I love the most? Not Act One, nor Three or Five ...
But Six. Oh! Act Six, my dear, that's the best part.

The part in which the king picks up his fallen head; the knight pulls out the sword in his chest; the bodies stand up, dust their clothes and come to the front of the stage, bow to the audience and receive their applause ...
That's not really a part of the performance ...
Yes, it is! My child, that is precisely when the real show begins.
I have a good script here. Let me put on my glasses ... Hmm ... Let's start from ... from Act Six.
The princess, a nightingale decorated with diamonds, an opera singer taking center stage, steps into a building of <nobr>gray-and</nobr>-white diamond patterns.
"And the curtain falls forever. The smile on her face seems too serene. She is still dreaming."
"Her madness keeps them all alert. But in the court, she seems so meek and mentally steady, like a docked boat on calm waters."
"Nodding elegantly to every gentleman she meets, she makes the shackle on her neck look like a piece of dazzling jewelry."
Next page ... oh.
What happened?
"In a transparent room, under an unyielding limelight, her dignity is stomped on, like a silk handkerchief thrown on the ground. They smash her crown, forcing her to pay for her madness."
Is she mad?
No ... not anymore.
"'Sleep, she said to me, sleep. If that's what she said, then I don't need to wake up.'"

"That's when the star falls into an <nobr>ever-lasting</nobr> dream. The blinding light becoming a spotlight on the stage; the empty room carrying the best reverberations. She has never been so calm. Everything beautiful in her is there forever, frozen in time."
I guess she went completely insane.
Or found eternal peace.
"Her world has become the performance. A show that never ends."
I'll say she's a great actress, isn't she?
But this is not a good story. I think it needs more context.
Hahaha, my dear. You are indeed a great connoisseur.
Only one act of a play can't tell a good story by itself.
Oh, forgive my ramblings. The golden curtain has risen.
Fix your collar, darling, and keep moving forward.

I never step forward.
In solitude, I never step forward.
I merely stay in place, swaying,
A wooden oar.
I never step forward.

The spine of a beast.

Vienna, the portrait of elegance and tranquility—a pearl set upon the banks of the Danube.

Life in the Midst

Of course, these houses can't compare to those at the Schwarzenbergplatz, where the bankers and the titled flock. And it's a fair distance from "Noble Boulevard." However, you can still live like nobility here, thanks to the neat and beautiful façade of the apartment buildings and the communal halls with their long spiral staircases. Once home, behind closed doors, it's all up to you.

    The neighborhood? There are plenty of parks and shops around—the vendors know what the citizens want and pay attention to. The clever ones might even drop a hint about a good play coming to the theater, with tickets they can get through a connection. If you need to rent a carriage, there are many choices here—just don't pick a house next to the carriage depot!

    Oh, and the clinics—we can't overlook those. If you're interested, I've heard there's a small clinic nearby, run by a young lady. She specializes in treating women for "hysteria"—you've heard of it, haven't you? Thanks to her, my café's doing a bit better. After all, the coachmen and servants waiting on their noblewomen need somewhere to pass the time and fill their bellies, do they not? You might want to take a look—you can't go wrong picking up a quaint little something! But not this book; it's a personal item—yes, the one belonging to the lady I just mentioned.

    If she were to run into you, she'd be delighted, I'm sure. After all, we businessfolk don't care much for "Freud."
Fine Times

No one openly says a bad word, as the days visibly stride forward and steps quicken, kicking up a golden breeze. Almost every moment brings new tidings, new footsteps rushing to Vienna, countless new creations, useful or not so useful, all pouring into this surging stream.

    News of airship trials has plagued the papers, and porcelain and glass paintings have become essential table decorations. In years past, the Viennese created tubed toothpaste, invented the pencil, learned how to utilize cocoa beans ... Life is getting better, art shines brighter, as if making up for what was never enjoyed before. Now, Vienna won't miss any single glint on the shining crest of the age.

    People have grown accustomed to this pace. They chase novelty but always look at the city with nostalgic, expectant, trusting eyes, never believing the worst could happen here. The most astonishing news in the papers only sparks ten minutes of discussion. Even the death of the Archduke merely prompts a confused, almost embarrassed smile from the gathered crowd. It is a sudden change, and thus, they resist it.

    No matter, his successor shall shoulder the responsibility! So ... let's keep dancing.

It could be a window, a ring, an umbrella, or a noose.

    We prefer the analogy of a ring; it suits the mood better. When they first proposed building this road, there were so many voices of dissent! And now? If one takes the time to examine the jewels set into the ring's edge, our opera house, the museums of natural history, the art galleries, the gardens, and the schools—all the things that push this city forward—are meticulously adorned along the ring's side.

    Whoever it may be, wherever they come from, if they wish to understand Vienna, the best way is to lead them around this road. Even if they seek something "different," it's just a matter of stepping out one more circle—Vienna's districts have their own meticulous divisions: the nobility occupies the inner city, merchants favor the areas near the ring road, and further out, the simple, hardworking folk.

    These layered circles also have their moments of convergence. The Viennese seize any opportunity to turn their lives into a celebration. Splendor, dignity, and grandeur are unquestionable truths. Those gazing up at the parade floats have never felt so close to that select few standing atop.

    You see, anyone can stand on the stage.
For Art's Sake

"Vienna" is undoubtedly the most treasured word of the times. Those young people who shouted throughout the long struggle, eager to tear off the old labels left upon them by the elder generations, are just as keen to possess this golden beacon.

    Among them, Theophil is notably adorned with trinkets, any few of which would clink at the tip of the tongue. A Viennese through and through—a medium—a noble—a painter! Sometimes a poet, depending on his mood. After all, when a creator's work can knock on the doors of Artistic Movements and Pan, what place is there he cannot go, what thing is there he cannot do?

    Theophil doesn't flaunt these titles—his companions do it for him, tirelessly straightening his crown at every meeting. Rumor has it Hermann corresponded with him, the "Science Club" threw invitations his way, the Neue Freie Presse published his critiques, and a carriage belonging to Theophil once stopped at 9 Eschenbach Street. No one knows better how to play with gold, and the rumors that spread in tandem point to the <nobr>ever-changing</nobr> companions by his side. In any case, long before he reached the legal age of adulthood, he had a reputation he could toss around at will.

    But he never wrote a play for his equally popular sister, nor painted her a lavishly decorated portrait. Only a small sketch lies in a corner of a drawer. It's the only one that depicts both Isolde and their mother. Theophil's talent was already evident then; he captured their unique expressions well.
Palatable Beverages

What makes this little shop so popular? Its fame even briefly surpassed that of Café Griensteidl, with its tiny storefront that fits only a handful of tables, its ordinary fried meat cutlets, and the most common, everyday coffee, it has created a small miracle.

    Running a café in Vienna is no easy task. The news racks must be filled daily with the latest papers, pressed flat with an iron. If one has connections and an eye for the popular, able to pick out newspapers that are in vogue, and displays a few publications that circulate secretly in closed circles, their wallet will surely swell. If one can advertise novel coffee recipes, recipes for secret family pastries, or perhaps encounter a rare guest—then a real opportunity has truly knocked!

    After all, the road where this shop is located is the inevitable route Kakania must take to return to her clinic. As long as she didn't intend to avoid someone by taking a detour but rather passed by as usual, with her friends for a visit. The swaying wooden sign of the café reminds her to pick up her letters and parcels. Thus, the two girls sit down at the table, and Isolde politely lifts the cup of coffee her companion has praised so highly.

    Many claim to have been there and speak of it as a conversation piece in other cafés, and so the news spread. The ordinary whipped <nobr>cream-topped</nobr> black coffee quickly earned a new nickname that consumed the streets of Vienna. The luck it allegedly carries is not important—it's the dramatic element of the story that is the key.

    No one can refuse a good play.
The Curtain Never Falls

Artistic investment requires not only vision but also an abundance of time. Without neither of the two, one must compensate with thrice the amount of bills and coins. Fortunately, what patrons understand best and can most readily provide is money itself. A perfect match! Vienna's painters, musicians, sculptors, and actors can now stride forward on their paths with vigor. Photographers, fashion designers, jewelers, and playwrights won't be left behind either. As long as you can sell talent, ho, readers and audiences will never complain about the crowd.

    This is especially true of drama. Performances on stage are exemplary, allowing one to clearly see how that distant social stratum lives—how they converse with elegance, mind their manners, and mask any unfortunate accents in their speech. For this reason, actors are like perfect little statues, drawing attention wherever they go. Even when the play ends, they still parade around the grand stage of life.

    People chase after the name "Isolde" with such fervor because she is that flawless statue, the most transparent, the most dazzling, capable of embodying countless possibilities—those written into the script. She is the city's treasure! With this pride, even a child who has never seen her perform would not speak a word against her.

    After all, who among us has not spent a great length of time with "Isolde," witnessing her grow from a child into a fine actress? How many know the name of her household pet, or the friends of her childhood? These tales are almost indistinguishable from folklore.

    By the time all of Vienna came to know her, she was already perfect.

Side by Side

Miners, covered in a layer of dust and wielding their picks, hurry over as others join them after washing off their bandages. In the square, some take shelter under the statue and read books, while children are led by loving hands through rows of coats and boots. A strong sense of camaraderie unites everyone in the square; they are all part of the same <nobr>tight-knit</nobr> community.

    The conversations begin and spread like a hurricane, sweeping from one end of the square to the other as everyone tries to engage with those around them. But then another voice joins in. The town's teacher has arrived, embodying the ideals we hold dear. She is like a character from a legend who has come to our town from a faraway place. Because of our strong will, even legends can become reality here. If the teacher had not said, "See you tomorrow!" this would have gone on all night.

    As a community, we each have a voice in shaping the future of our town. It's inspiring to see so many people come together to make a difference. There is a sense of pride that radiates from within, uniting us all towards a common goal.

    Oh, how powerful it is when we come together as one!
Vibrant Snowy Square

Take another good look at the square. It hasn't changed much—a polar bear stands in the center, outlined by a faint light, while children eagerly reach out to touch its paws. The snow dusts the bear's head, giving it a serene quality that contrasts with the lively setting. Flowers bloom amidst the white snow, covering most of the stones on the ground. The bear appears to be at peace against the mustard yellow background.

    This is an important place in Rayashki, as the town kitchen cannot accommodate such a large number of people. It is often used for public discussions and will continue to serve that purpose. Recently, it was decided to allow children to venture outside and explore the world beyond. The road leading there is bathed in sunlight, decorated with red ribbons that sway in the gentle breeze from the trees.

    People find familiar images here that evoke nostalgia and memories of past lives, yet those who come here rarely speak of their homeland. This is the true essence of Rayashki—everything they hoped to see in their homeland, but never did. It's like the distant horizon that Rusalka dreams of as she braves the icy waters, or the intricate illustrations created by traveling ley hunters, or even the homes of Foundation visitors who have long since disappeared. It's what previous generations promised the next: a glimpse of their idealized homeland.

   The more impossible an ideal seems, the stronger it becomes—unbreakable in its perceived perfection.

    Despite this, there is still so much to strive for and achieve in life.

To the town, she is a familiar figure. But to herself, everything is so drastically different.

She's used to walking in the snow. The poplar fluff floating through Moscow's streets reminds her of Rayashki; it's like snow, but it doesn't make her cheeks turn red or her hands and feet cold; it doesn't melt on the skin, nor can it hide anything. Canned goods, even sausages and fresh meat, are available in stores, and one doesn't have to count the days just to exchange for everyday items ... The first time she made soup in her new home, it felt surreal. Another vivid memory was when she got off the train, holding her child's hand in fear. Outside the small town, in Moscow, there were so many people, all seemingly full of hope. 

But she boarded the train back to Rayashki anyway.

Rayashki had changed, too. There were faces in the town she didn't recognize, and the statue in the center of the square had changed. The school was still the same, and the children played games in the small playground. The townspeople's greetings were a bit awkward; no one mentioned her hasty departure as if it was not important, as if anyone could leave at any time and also return whenever they wanted.

Snow fell on her hair and collar, turning her fingers and nose red—this was real snow.
Circle Dance

Snowmen of various sizes were arranged in a circle on the playground, and the children lovingly linked their twig arms together so that the snow friends were holding hands. Each child focused on decorating their little creation, staying close together, and when one arm brushed another's shoulder, there was a cheerful laugh. The little girl on the far left lowered her head, her braids curled up like haystacks in the sun. She carefully placed sunflower petals on her snowman's head. Nearby, two boys were trying to make their snowman's chubby body wider and sturdier so it would last longer and Ms. Vila could greet them more often. The little boy's snowman was a bear. It was only through his explanation that the head and paws of the arctic fox could be seen on its back. Foxes don't usually have long ears like rabbits, but he gave it those in order to hear his mother's footsteps, Vila's footsteps, and his friends' footsteps. Finally, he carefully placed the mined ore on the fox's chest, just as he wore the beautiful stone his father had left him. "Okay, my frosty comrades! You can all stay here and do the circle dance with Ms. Vila. Remember, no running around or making a ruckus; just listen to her instructions ..."

As for the people around her, most are still wearing their work clothes, with coal dust clinging to their collars and pant legs. This group of makeshift teachers and students shake hands, determined to spend time understanding a fading discipline. Those most dedicated to the work are also the most serious pragmatists. Is the study of ley lines omnipotent? No. But it may eventually bring about change.
