Disco Revival
Burn, Baby, Burn! Disco Revival!

By the late 1960s, people were desperate to escape from the chaos of rampant inflation, wars, and scandals like Watergate. With the lyrics "Don't rock the boat" from Rock the Boat as their mantra, they decided to step off the turbulent flagship and instead ride the carefree waves of disco.

In 1977, Saturday Night Fever hit the big screen, and it electrified the City of Tomorrow along the coast. Boys threw on bright floral shirts and pointed shoes, while girls dazzled in sparkly wrap dresses or bell-bottom pants with off-the-shoulder tops. Hand in hand, they flooded the streets, all heading for the nearest disco halls.

But in 1979, die-hard rock fans launched an open attack on disco culture, leading to a notorious event—Disco Demolition Night.

Firecrackers were tossed into crates filled with vinyl records, blowing them to pieces. This 98-cent "War on Disco" ended with a decisive victory for the traditionalists. Disco, which had ruled since the late '60s, quietly faded from the mainstream under the rise of a new wave music.

But now, as we enter the final decade of the 20th century, there's a growing feeling among die-hard fans—Disco, with its undeniable energy, is making an unexpected comeback.

Whether it's house, techno, or hip-hop, it's all just disco in a new form, with a new name and a new look, spinning once again under the disco ball.

We once approached it with hope, anticipation, and a bit of caution. But now, my friends, I can't wait any longer—I'm kicking off my shoes and heading straight for the dance floor.

The good stuff is back!
The Gray Area
From the Introduction of the Hongzhi Clinic Ledger

My name is Bruce Liu, an ordinary, unlicensed street doctor on Haight Street, hailing from an ancient Eastern land. If all goes well, I'll stay on this street until the day I can return home and reunite with my wife.

In the '80s, through skill, hard work, and sheer will to survive, we new immigrants managed to establish ourselves in this land. A few ambitious ones formed gangs, carving out new territories with nothing but our determination. They commanded respect from both sides of the law in San Francisco, but in doing so, they only deepened the poverty, isolation, and discrimination faced by the rest of our community.

As for me, a modest practitioner who played by the rules most of his life, I found myself learning the family traditions of the Italians, witnessing the extreme measures of the Brotherhood, offering good tea to corrupt cops collecting protection fees, and even picking shrapnel out of a tattooed kid's head. It made me realize—this wasn't the life I wanted.

I didn't choose Haight Street for any special reason, except that it reminded me of how people used to view Chinatown at the turn of the century—back when the elders referred to this vibrant city as "Dai Fau," or "Da Bu," meaning "The Great Port." Back then, the poor stood united and new immigrants had each other's backs. Oh, how I miss those days!

Another fellow on this street, Tang Ji, is a great example. He runs a decent restaurant here, looking after a group of "wayward" kids. One of them, a little guy named J, has become a regular of mine—first it was the back of his head, then his arm, and yesterday, his leg ... Don't get me started. Young hotheads think they're "superheroes," but in our culture, we call them "reckless fools."

Let me be clear: Bruce Liu isn't the kind of doctor you'd call a "benevolent healer." But if I'm going to keep running Hongzhi Clinic, I need to set some rules—no dealing with major troublemakers who cause harm to others, and no getting involved with gangs that send young men to their deaths for nothing.
The Mystery of Energy Healing
Unraveling the Enigma: A Revelation or a Hoax?

Note from the author: Due to anonymous complaints and external pressures, this article has been removed from the current issue.

Since the rise of the New Age movement, energy healing has become a hot topic. Despite my efforts in consulting experts and researching extensively, I still couldn't grasp the most fundamental, core question—what exactly is cosmic energy, and how does it heal us?

Therefore, I'd like to share three real-life experiences with you, dear readers.

The first time, I followed the guidelines of a popular bestseller and went to the outskirts of the city, to a valley during a full moon, where I meditated in what was supposed to be a "place of energy convergence." I almost got caught by a strange roadside shaman who tried to forcefully sell me meaningless talismans and bizarre witch doctor trinkets.

The second time, I was coerced into attending a two-week healing course on a method called "Ho'oponopono," a self-healing technique. The master claimed it could "erase the memory of the disease and deceive your symptoms ..." In the end, I gained nothing and couldn't even "erase" the painful memory of the exorbitant enrollment fee.

The third time, just as I was about to equate energy healing with mere quackery and gather evidence to conclusively label it a scam, I wandered into a tent at a market in the countryside.

A young dancer, without saying a word, was arranging a circle on the ground with candles, crystals, and some flowers and herbs. Just as I was about to leave, I heard a voice behind me: "You are lost."

"What do you mean?" I stopped in my tracks.

"Come here," she said, picking up a stone that glowed with a blue light, without further explanation.

I found myself irresistibly drawn to it, like someone who instinctively stops to gaze at the moon.

A faint vibration touched my sensitive nerves—not from the stone or anything visible, but from something far more distant, more vast, a resonance that was beyond description.

"You felt the vibrations. They're beautiful, aren't they?" Her voice seemed distant.

The heaviness and confusion in my heart began to dissipate, and a clearer understanding slowly took shape.

What is cosmic energy? It's not some miraculous force, but rather the most fundamental law of the universe—all things are made of particles, and all things vibrate.

How does it heal us? A true healer can harness the "vibrations" of cosmic energy to resonate with and enhance a person's inherent energy.

Finally, this article contains no suggestions or instructions. Consumers and healing enthusiasts are urged to consider carefully and discern wisely.

Thank you all for reading.

A Charming San Francisco
Charming San Francisco: Welcome and Farewell

If you've crossed the ocean to come here in this era, the first stop I recommend is the Transamerica Pyramid. From the highest point in San Francisco, you'll look down on a city that has withstood the test of time.

From the Gold Rush of the 19th century that brought people, energy, and endless possibilities to California, to the tech boom a century later in the vast Santa Clara Valley to the south, San Francisco has weathered the waves of history and still stands proudly on the West Coast.

This city, like a battle-hardened veteran, has survived countless trials—from the great San Andreas Fault earthquake of 1906 to the Loma Prieta quake of 1989, along with the ongoing power struggles and conflicts between law and order that have played out throughout its history.

Clearly, nothing can dampen this City of Tomorrow's passionate and singular pursuit of "Lady Liberty." Just as there are young people lining up all night at Ocean Beach to ride the Tilt-A-Whirl, there's also that ever-enduring golden ballroom, a relic that will never close.

Though there are the occasional unpleasant episodes, and you may feel a bit of a lull in the brief silence after the music stops, you know there's always somewhere to go on a lonely night, and this city will always welcome you.

On the other hand, it also reminds me of the funny, charming uncle from the movies. When the story reaches its climax and you're facing the choice between reality and dreams in the dark night of the soul, and everyone around you thinks you've lost it, he suddenly leans out from his worn, joke-filled couch and says, "Go for it, kid, I got your back."

You start to remember the toys he bought you as a child, the streets and bays he showed you, and how you once saw him as a comrade-in-arms, dreaming together of a great adventure in search of gold. Now, he's raising his hands to cheer you on, and throwing the biggest farewell party for your dream-chasing journey.

Friends, your best Uncle Francisco welcomes you, whether you're coming or going.

The Hitchhiker's Column

Since our last column, we've been inundated with letters, tapes, and voice recordings from our passionate readers. I must say, the impact of the "Piranhas in the Sewers" story exceeded my expectations. One anonymous reader compiled 23 different urban sewer predator legends she picked up during her travels and asked when I was going to write about "The Country Witch Who Turned Into a Hare." She fondly recalled how her grandmother's amusing witch stories, tinged with a touch of gentle fright, would lull her to sleep as a child.

I'd like to extend my heartfelt thanks to this reader—these contributions are invaluable to my writing, and I'll soon delve into these childhood tales. Stories of mysterious transformative arcane skills are truly captivating, and their prevalence might be more widespread than I initially thought.

As we continue with the last issue's theme, sewer legends intertwine with conspiracy theories. For example, in a tape sent in by a Mr. K from New York City, a relative of his staunchly believes that the government secretly hired a team to feed albino fish living in the sewers. In previous investigations, a teenager shared his thrilling experience—he encountered human-sized, upright-walking reptiles and rodents in the city sewers. These stories often end with the line, "The government knows they exist, but the higher-ups are keeping it all hush-hush ..." More radical speculators suggest that city sewers can easily be used as experimentation sites, with piranhas, alligators, giant snakes, and all manner of other dangerous creatures being secretly bred by the government or mysterious organizations for unknown purposes.

Leather-bound Diary

February 5th

Well, ain't that odd? Pierce came back early this morning, scared out of his mind. I had never seen the kid so freaked out. He sped through town and only slammed on the brakes when he got to the front door, as if something was chasing him. That nut almost ran over Marita's little bulldog!

Only God knows what he ran into.

February 15th

The birds were chirping the whole night long. I had never seen so many of them gathered together. Oh boy, they were so noisy; I barely slept a wink.

Ruth was scared, she thought it was some kind of omen. What a joke.

Those long-beaked birdies weren't afraid of shotguns, that's for sure. I fired a shot at them, but only a few got spooked enough to fly away.

Father Morgan suggested hiring a "bird control team"—if such a thing exists in the big city, that is. But I still think we should assemble all the gun users in the town and kill all those birds once and for all, rather than scare them off.

March 27th

Had a nightmare, a very vivid one, though I can't for the life of me remember what it was all about now.

Ruth woke up scared too; I comforted her. It was just a nightmare, nothing more.

March 30th

Pierce didn't come back from Houston, but the police sure did. They said Pierce's employer in Houston reported him missing, thinking he ran off with their money.

I wouldn't put it past that sly fox.

April 10th

All night long, the birds were making that racket again. When I pulled back the curtains in the morning, I thought I was still dreaming, but it was real. There were so many birds they were blocking out the sun.

It was like a waking nightmare.

April 12th

The birds scattered.

Everyone looked kind of strange. It had been ages since I saw Marita walking her dog, and Ruth started bawling over the most trivial things. It's unnerving.

April 17th

Johnny's back in town, looking like his soul got swallowed up by the devil. I saw him running, screaming like a madman, then he just collapsed on the lawn all of a sudden, crying and begging for something to spare him.

Father Morgan came, but he had this strange look about him.

I heard what Johnny was saying. He was mumbling on and on about a "motel."

May 13th

I talked to a realtor. Yeah, it's come to that—I'm finally thinking about moving.

Why? I don't know. I guess you could call it a ... gut feeling? Maybe my mind can be eased a bit somewhere new.

"Who's that? Close the door behind you, old sport ... Huh? Webber, why are you back here? Haven't you enlisted yet? Those vermin are bombing the town and all the farms every day—we're all counting on you ...
—An old man who calls the motel home

"Night after night, a scratching sound scrapes across the walls of the first floor... Could it be the clawing nails of decaying zombies, begging for sustenance? Hahaha... At least it's not the debt collectors."
—A guest on the run
Local tortilla chips/Cream cheese/Mexican burritos/Whole wheat tortillas/Salted oatmeal ...
—A dusty menu
"Relax, it's all fake. A Viking would never be scared of such a silly trick ... Quit pulling my blanket!"
—A jarl hiding under the covers

"First, gently tap with the back of the knife before cutting against the grain. That's the secret to properly handling meat... but this mediocre motel lacks any quality ingredients! Why on earth did they even hire me in the first place?!"
—An ex-chef
"Thirty-two bucks for a bottle of mineral water—talk about throwing your money down the drain. The thought of guzzling down that much cash every day makes my stomach churn ... Burp."
—An awakened cash register
"We've received a large number of complaints about extortionate prices at a motel in Austin ... but it's in the middle of nowhere. Do you even realize how much gas it'd take to get there?"
—A price control officer
"These charges are totally uncool, man! Every store should pay a welcoming fee to this legendary pirate captain, and provide me with all their services, free of charge!"
—A penniless hipster
"I penned my magnum opus in this motel room, a masterpiece collection of poetry, but those heartless critics tore it apart ...  Ah, is it already time to pay for another night here?!"
—A down-and-out poet
"I've always regretted not returning this poetry collection to that guest before he checked out, but thanks to this anthology, I've become a published writer and I'm doing quite well for myself now."
—A part-time maid
"Hey, stop reading that crappy article! Let's have a 50-mile race instead!"
—A texan biker
"If you add a dark reed pipe to the first-floor corridor, stepping on it will cause all the lights on the second floor to go out! This place is like a haunted Rube Goldberg machine!"
—A clever man with a questionable mind.
"Blonney, reckless and dumb, a typical Blondie. Always indulging herself in alcohol, beautiful clothes, and other vain pleasures."
—Movie, "A Nightmare at Green Lake"
"The pure entertainment brought by 'formulaic' approaches cannot be ignored. However, we must also consider the limitations they impose on the artistic integrity of cinema."
—A pretentious film critic
"Blonde girls, always standing out at school, always the talk of their classmates, known for throwing wild parties, drinking and smoking in their rooms ... Blonde girls are bad."
—A moody little girl
"Oh! What a captivating and endearing heroine!"
—A heckler upon the stage
"Mom told me that once I break out of my cocoon, I can go find her. Today is the 365th day since she left me."
—A blue cocoon
"Stay—we've got the comfiest bed, plenty of honey, and all the fruit you could ever desire. We can live together forever."
—An imaginary friend
"Some people spend their lives in a cocoon. When they finally break out, they may feel like a vulnerable prey, watched by circling vultures."
—Texas daily digest
"Follow the plan, just follow the plan ... One hour and five minutes to go."
—A rule-abiding worker
"Mom, look at the huge bubble I blew! Um, Mom? Why are you floating away from me?"
—A bubble-blowing child
"Parties are a scam—a tribute to rampant alcoholism and a complete nightmare for cleaners. Oh my God ... who threw up on the stereos again?!"
—A party venue cleaner

"We're all for people holding lawful parades in public places to voice legitimate demands. Just submit an application in advance, refrain from disturbing the peace, and never use arcane skills under any circumstances."
—A London cop

"Parties, as a form of entertainment, possess a certain duality. They often serve to relieve stress and have a regulatory role in society, but indulging in a life of constant partying can be a slippery slope—one party too many, and you may find yourself trapped in a vapid existence of empty pleasures."
—A red fruit at a party
"The fragments of the phenomenal world may seem insignificant, but they contribute to poor sanitation ... A schedule for cleaning the beach needs to be arranged."
—An Apeiron believer
"Hand, gun, handgun! Pick it up, squeeze the trigger. Bang, bang, bang! Hero, hero ... not enough bullets ..."
—Some Manus follower

Irrational numbers are a set of chaotic and disorderly numbers that must be disciplined by the pursuit of truth, in order to approach the realm of rational numbers. They should not distract the wise from their search for truth.
—The Corrector's notes
"Tools are neither good nor bad—they are the embodiment of human wisdom. As long as they are simple and efficient, they bring about order and facts."
—A focused researcher

"I've lost count of how many times I've told Mom—I hate math! All I want is to learn how to paint or play the piano, to be an artist. But she insists that I finish today's calculus homework before anything else."
—A sixth-grader
"I don't really get science and wrenches and what have you, but I do believe we should celebrate the beauty of peace and love. Sir, how would you like to buy a nice bouquet?"
—A florist
"Isn't math just brilliant? It allows us to build enormous jet rockets and launch them into the sky—into the vastness of the universe! Bang! Zoom! Whoosh!"
—An aspiring young astronaut
"I-I think that giving it your all is the very best you can do. So please ... don't give up too easily!"
—A steadfast scout
"Be it the Tower of Babel or the Leaning Tower of Pisa, towers are the product of our hard work, built one bucket of soil and one beam at a time ... and no one can argue otherwise!"
—A construction worker
"Rules are essential. Everyone should follow the rules, yes ... What? I can't smoke here? Well, I don't see no sign or anything!"
—An acclaimed educator
"Hi there, take a flyer, please. Huh? No, I don't know what's written on it, and I'm only paid 5 cents a day. So, you want a flyer or not?"
—A part-time flyer distributor
"You should do whatever you want, even if it's just running down the street! If you wanna do it, just do it!"
—An energetic girl
"What is art? Art is the expression of ideas, art is a party everyone can join! United, we must rise up and 'take over' public squares, streets, and even police stations!"
—A street artist
How can we elucidate the world of art to the masses? The answer is simple—it's impossible.
—"Art Daily"
"Art? Listen, kid, before you worry about that, make sure you fill your empty stomach. Art can wait."
—A street beggar
"I don't know all that much and I certainly don't understand art, but the guests who taught me to read seemed educated enough and treated us real good ... so I think art must be a good thing."
—A grateful girl
"Unexpected, romantic encounters? Don't get your hopes up. They're more likely to turn your best-laid plans into a mess and leave you with nothing but chaos."
—A night burglar

"Sure, gossips and secrets are intriguing, but don't be fooled by the glitz and glamor on the screen—behind it, it's not as thrilling as you might think ... I would rather have never been granted this 'blessing'!"
—From the other side of the screen
"Never take the bus. It follows a set route, you see, passing through pre-planned stops. Those eyes hiding in the grass will gobble you up the moment you get off!"
—A hallucinating traveler
"On March 11, a motel in Austin reportedly experienced a gas leak, leading to a fire that destroyed the building. Local police have launched an investigation into the matter."
—An explosive box

"Boletes, white mushrooms, milk caps ... there are so many kinds of mushrooms in the world waiting to be discovered. It could take you a lifetime to find them all, but unlike animals, mushrooms will always stay there, waiting for us."
—A mushroom gatherer
"Never stay out in the open wilderness. Never expose yourself. Never make a single sound ... The dense trees in the forest are your best protection and disguise."
—A forest hunter
"A bedtime story? Honestly, I-I'm not sure ... Before the story even begins, I always ... zzz ... zzz ..."
—A heavy sleeper
"N-No! I don't wanna sleep! I wanna hear more stories ... Why does Mommy always fall asleep first?"
—A little child

Under the Lone Star

People are born here. They die here.

Texas is one wide open space. The plains stretch on forever, offering up their thick black soil to the crops and their vast pastures to the cattle. The air is dry, and the days are long and hot. Summer storms and tornadoes are frequent visitors to the ranch—visitors who leave as quickly as they come. The people here create history and have established a proud way of life, regardless of the changes in the outside world.

They're independent, tough, and rugged. They're used to hard work, to gathering around the barbecue grill, to <nobr>hand-rolled</nobr> smokes, and shotguns. They're used to local radio news broadcasts on Friday mornings and "The Tonight Show" at eight in the evening. Highways and railways are the lifeblood of this Lone Star, pumping new trends into valleys and farms. But for those who listen to old country songs, they don't give a damn to disco, rock music, newfangled outfits, or catchy new slogans.

All these new things are annoying noise. They are completely meaningless and tasteless!

—She has always thought this way. She is a true, native Texan.

Always in Style

It has always existed.

From the haunted stables and outhouses of the Middle Ages to the <nobr>ghost-plagued</nobr> castles of Gothic literature, it constantly changed forms, waiting for more visitors—more nourishment. A ship then carried it across the ocean to the flourishing New World.

In this land, there was never a shortage of legends, both old and new. It became an abandoned manor or a cabin in the woods, joyfully devouring every visitor from the wilderness, along with their screams and cries.

The 20th century ushered in a new wave of stories. No one knew exactly where they came from—a friend of a friend, a transfer student, local oddities in the corners of newspaper. Their themes vary from cars, ovens, videotapes, sewers to cities and the impending new millennium. These tales gained their own names in modern culture: urban legends. In them, it sensed something familiar—the taste of fear and the need for fear.

And so, It quietly laid its foundations in the dim morning light, growing a simple wooden porch and a flickering sign, laying down its creaking stairs. At dawn, drivers on Route 77 suddenly noticed a motel that was a little out of date.

Now the motel needed a manager, of course.

Artificial Life

During the <nobr>mid-20th</nobr> century, advances in life sciences and biotechnology opened a new realm of possibilities. The <nobr>double-helix</nobr> was unraveled, revealing a previously hidden path—the code to deciphering life itself.

No one could resist clinging on to this hope, whether human or arcanist. The term "genetic engineering" emerged in 1973, as biologists wove and pruned the strands of DNA, allowing modified results to be inherited almost without fail. Suddenly, the challenges of the past in agriculture, medicine, and basic biological research were swept away by new solutions.

Naturally, attention returned to that classic academic subject: the mutual exclusivity of human and arcanist bloodlines. This time, at a research institute in Scotland, scientists chose to take the power of creating life into their own hands, attempting to realize a dream that never came true—to balance these two bloodlines at a 50:50 ratio in a single life form.

After going through 276 failures, the 277th experiment combined the genes of a female arcanist volunteer and a female human researcher. The embryo, formed in the lab, was then transferred to the uterus of a <nobr>Finn-Dorset</nobr> ewe.

A baby girl was born, with the eye color of her human mother, a skin tone similar to her arcanist mother, and unexpectedly—the head of a sheep, the third mother.

Her DNA ratio was a delicate balance of 60% Arcanist and 40% human. While it did not achieve the desired result, the method behind her birth was enough to attract the attention of countless academic and commercial organizations.

A new miracle of life at the end of the 20th century—that's what people called her.
Boundless Dreamland

Her slender limbs lack any real strength, and her development was much slower than that of her peers. On the other hand, she achieved far higher scores in intelligence test than children her age.

These two facts were not particularly surprising.

This combination of genes led to an <nobr>early-maturing</nobr> brain and incomplete physical development, a risk that was already known from the very beginning—she would experience a <nobr>much-longer-than-usual</nobr> childhood until her physical development stopped altogether.

She had ethic lessons and other academic courses tailored to her special condition. She lived in a clean, sterile room, accompanied by a portable music player.

The volunteer mother visited her regularly, the researcher mother measured her data and recorded her growth, and the ewe mother stayed by her side, lapping at her fleece and nursing her.

At night, she dreamt of a soft lawn she had only seen in books and videotapes, where her ewe mother waited for her, and they roamed through the clouds together.

Dolly, this is what grass tastes like.

Dolly, you're my sweet little lamb.

Dolly, this is simply wonderful. You must go to more places, see more lawns and more clouds, just like we saw in that dream.

The Traveler's Gift
"Self-Driving"

Using critters to propel cars? Quite an innovative idea.
Semmelweis is unconcerned with the jerky movements and swaying of the car; her main worry is that it is barreling directly towards her.
The driver gets out of the car to apologize to Semmelweis—although she fails to understand a single one of the strange words the gentleman utters.

The essence of gentlemanly conduct lies in sincerity—the more proper one's etiquette, the more sincere the apology. Hence, the gentleman shakily opens the trunk, lifts an item with the top of his head, and hands it to Semmelweis before offering to help open it.
Goldfinch Greenhouse

This delicate glass artefact boasts plants so lush that the wind carries a palpable green fragrance. Semmelweis is convinced she hears the faint sound of some string instrument, but all she sees is the greenhouse and the two birdcages positioned at its entrance, side by side.

Semmelweis remembers a tale she heard in Vienna. Right before goldfinches were used as currency, they were experts in finding paths through the arcane world. She reaches out, and the metallic finches in the cage chirp excitedly at her gesture.
Semmelweis gently wipes the dust from the nameplate. With a soft wave of arcane skill, a hook-shaped mechanism appears at the top of the birdcage. It is actually a cleverly disguised music box.
Echoes of the Era

They wave their hands in a flurry, overcome with emotion—Semmelweis has never heard such crude language before. To her, they lost all rationality long ago, which was their most prideful Artefact. Such perfect irony.
As the crowd disperses, Semmelweis notices several small objects on the ground. She crouches down to examine them in detail.

The dust disperses to reveal several critters gnawing on the debris, unwilling to leave. This time, they seem to converge at the same spot, chasing after each other. Semmelweis bends down once again, eager to uncover the truth.
A protester stops Semmelweis in her tracks, raising his hands and sobbing as he babbles incomprehensibly. A certain emotion shines in his eyes, as if he wishes to ask Semmelweis for something.
Wine to Drink, Tales to Tell

The tavern owner points Semmelweis down a path, and as she glances back, she discovers a hidden door. Descending the steps, her eyes widen at the sight of the owner's private collection. Each barrel seems to hold a story. As for which one will accompany her, that choice is purely down to her own whim.

The stench of alcohol fills the room—rich, bitter, and pungent. Not exactly pleasant, but not terrible either. If she indeed wishes to indulge in sensory pleasures, now is the perfect time—before the "Storm" swallows everything whole.
Semmelweis cannot decipher the exact content of the whispers in her mind, but her thoughts are unusually clear. She knows exactly what she needs—a drink.
Alcohol-induced hallucinations gradually pull her under with gentle hands. Semmelweis sees the tavern keeper smiling at her, as though inviting her to surrender to some eternal dream.

Semmelweis stumbles into a small room—silent, cool, and dimly lit, with no windows or adornments, like an abandoned and empty picture frame.
"Interested in the theater, are you, madam?"
A girl holding a rabbit doll stands in the center of the room, beckoning to her. Semmelweis cannot see her expression. The girl waves her finger, and a large door appears before her.

"It's a pleasure to see you again, madam. The play, prepared exclusively for you, is still underway. You will not be disappointed."
The girl stands in the same spot, beckoning to Semmelweis again. Once a play begins, it cannot easily be stopped. Semmelweis acknowledges her pure curiosity for the play, which has only reached its first act, and so she decides ...

"As you know, the second act is the climax of every play's story. Surely, you won't want to miss it, madam."
The girl beckons to Semmelweis again. She smiles, urging her to make a choice quickly—to take the stage again or to leave.
Semmelweis hears that voice in her head again, enticing her to make a choice—to venture completely into the darkness, or to continue toward the heavens, pursuing a light that might not exist.

"Congratulations, madam. You've already come this far, and soon you'll witness the conclusion of our play!"
The girl excitedly beckons to Semmelweis, this time handing her the rabbit doll.

"Since you've accepted my gift, we must let it tell our next story!"
The girl raises her skirt, twirls deftly, curtsies, and then exits. A breeze blows through the room, and Semmelweis detects what smells like benzoin.
Phantom in the Lake

A shadowy touch entwines Semmelweis, first like moonlight, then like a cold wind. It becomes heavier and stickier, mirroring the emotions that have been pent up in her heart for so long, drowning her like a swamp.
Suddenly, Semmelweis' eyes snap open and she finds herself floating in the water.

A shadowy touch engulfs Semmelweis, crawling over her skin and seeping into the depths of her consciousness. She descends with the raging torrent, through Vienna and brushing over the meadows at the foot of the mountains, until she reaches a small house hidden deep in the forest ahead.
Suddenly, Semmelweis' eyes snap open and she finds herself floating in the water.

A shadowy touch entwines Semmelweis. She feels a fatigue that seems to be emanating from deep within her tendons and bones. She hears the thud of her backpack hitting the ground, but is unable to lift even a single finger.
Just before collapsing onto the ground, Semmelweis suddenly opens her eyes and finds herself floating in the water.
Spiral Tower

Dozens of critters frantically and tirelessly slam their bodies against the door. On the other side, Semmelweis, after confirming the door is sturdy enough, finally has a moment to look around. From the magnificent spiral staircase above, she realizes she has hidden in a tower.

After dealing with the trouble, Semmelweis turns back vigilantly, staring at the malicious wands facing her. The young men point at Semmelweis's hand, trembling, "Don't ... don't you move!"
Semmelweis notices that the ends of their limbs and the shadows behind them are like rippling voids—unsuccessful disguises of Arcane Skill.

The tower returns to silence. Semmelweis continues climbing the stairs. As she nears the top, she hears the sound of intermittent gasps and panting. She discovers several young critters.
Owing to her previous experience, Semmelweis doubts these are real critters. Even though these little things are huddled together, whimpering, they don't seem to pose any threat.

Semmelweis sidesteps, narrowly avoiding the front of the car. As the vintage automobile speeds away, something tumbles from the trunk and lands at her feet—something that seems impossible to open by force.
But, of course, she has her ways. She retrieves a key from her satchel, feeling vaguely that this key has finally found its matching lock.

Semmelweis signals at that vintage car as she crosses the road, but it is already too late. The tires screech as the Critters bring the vehicle to a stop by the roadside. The pale-faced driver leans out of the window, taps his hat apologetically, and hands her a gift, muttering something confusing that Semmelweis assumes are apologies.

Semmelweis stands by the road, one arm extended. The car pulls up in front of her. The Critters disembark, tipping their hats apologetically and muttering strange words that Semmelweis assumes are apologies. Some even leap forward to kiss her fingertips. The most gallant of them offers his arm and escorts her into the car.
Accept their apology

All things considered, this might just be an ordinary jack-in-the-box.
The car speeds away, leaving a small item glinting in the dust. It might just be the final spark of this era.

The Critters jump out, maintaining their decorum despite the chaos. The most gallant pair rushes to either side of her, escorting her into the car and presenting a fragrant Sachertorte as a token of apology.

The gentleman twirls his mustache as he pulls a trinket from Semmelweis's bag. He fiddles with it for a moment, and returns her a marvelous Artefact.

Rhapsody of the Moon

[A Series of Dusks: Rhapsody of the Moon] is an expansion for [A Series of Dusks]. [Rhapsody of the Moon] builds on the base game mode, introducing new gameplay elements and increased difficulty levels, requiring you to take on an even more surreal and frenzied version of "Vienna." Suite of the Moon After loading up the new expansion, the "Suite of the Moon" feature becomes available. Before embarking on your exploration, you can visit the Suite of the Moon panel and choose from a variety of "Omen" modifiers. These modifiers add challenges to your gameplay, with each one increasing the current "Indulgence" value. The "Indulgence" value serves as an indicator for the difficulty level of your playthrough. Depending on this value, you may see changes in the appearance of the moon, with each moon phase representing a different difficulty bracket that adds even more dangerous effects to your playthrough. There are five difficulty brackets, or phases of the moon, determined by the current Indulgence value: [Misperception]: Low chance of increasing Stress at the start of the round. Very low chance of triggering Sudden Disaster. Clear Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +20%. [Illusory Sounds]: Low chance of increasing Stress at the start of the round. Low chance of triggering Sudden Disaster. Limited Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +20%. Enemy Control Resilience +20%. [Illusory Sight]: Moderate chance of increasing Stress at the start of the round. Moderate chance of triggering Sudden Disaster. Reduced Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +50%. Enemy Control Resilience +30%. [Illusory Touch]: High chance of increasing Stress at the start of the round. High chance of triggering Sudden Disaster. Majorly obstructed Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +100%. Enemy Control Resilience +50%. [Delirium]: High chance of significantly increasing Stress at the start of the round. Guaranteed to trigger Sudden Disaster. Severely obstructed Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +200%. Enemy Control Resistance +100%. Deployed characters get a decrease in Focus Chance. After completing an exploration, you will receive Shards of Shadow. These shards can be used to unlock new Catalyst incantations, Instinct buffs, or reset the cooldowns of certain Instinct buffs. If the Indulgence value is at 0, the Suite of the Moon will become inactive and no effects from Indulgence will impact you. You will also no longer be able to obtain Shards of Shadow. As the difficulty bracket of the Suite of the Moon increases, you'll be able to activate "Instinct" effects. By tapping on the broken mirror shards surrounding the image of the moon, a variety of Instincts can be chosen. The higher the difficulty bracket, the more Instincts can be activated, and the stronger their effects will be. After activating Instincts and clearing the second area, some of the Instincts will go into cooldown. Each time you clear the second area, or each area after that, these cooldowns are reduced by one round. Alternatively, you can use Shards of Shadow to instantly refresh the cooldowns. Stress in Battle After loading up the expansion, your characters will display a Stress meter while exploring. Actions taken during exploration will affect their Stress levels, which in turn will affect their behavior on the battlefield. When a character's Stress is low, they have a chance to trigger Vigilant Behavior based on their Afflatus. When a character's Stress is high, they have a chance to trigger Disorder Behavior based on their Afflatus. When a character's Stress reaches 50, they have either a low chance of triggering Focus Behavior, or a high chance of triggering Meltdown Behavior. Enemies also have Stress levels. The higher an enemy's stress, the more dangerous they become, forcing you to stay vigilant at all times. Core Content The core content is also updated—load up the new expansion to experience the following: New Catalysts: Two new Catalysts are added—the Silver Compass and the Rationality Loupe. New Path Nodes: Four new path nodes are added—Misty Domain, Into the Unknown, Perilous Encounter, and Treasure Trove. New Catalyst Incantations: Each Catalyst now has a new Catalyst incantation that can be unlocked by using Shards of Shadow. Some of these incantations can be cast by consuming Stimulus after completing certain path nodes. New Artefacts: Exciting new artefacts are added to the game. For more details, you will need to play through the new content yourself.

When an attack hits an enemy, inflict multiple types of effects from [Poison], [Burn], or [Bleed] on the target and on self. The more Medications within range, the more times these types of effects are inflicted on the enemy.
When an attack hits an enemy, inflict 1 type of effect from [Poison], [Burn], or [Bleed] on self.
Singed Mirror

When entering battle, for each Curio in the layout, all allies gain 1 stack of [Thorny].
After an ally attacks or is attacked, 50% chance to gain 1 stack of [Thorny].

When entering battle, for each Curio in the layout, all allies gain [Thorny].
After attacking or being attacked, chance to gain [Thorny].
If there are no Weapons in the layout, allies gain ATK +50%.
If there are no Weapons in the layout, allies gain a massive ATK boost.
Auto Read Write Drive
2 Energy to activate: ({count3*1}/2)
After losing enough [Dynamo], gain multiple random effects from [Collection of Attack Buffs].

For every 10 stacks of [Dynamo] lost on an ally, the ally gains 4 random effects from [Collection of Attack Buffs].
At the start of the round, for every 2 points of Energy, all deployed characters get Stress -{1+count2*1}, and the allies gain {1+count4*1} random effects from [Collection of Permanent Buffs].
At the start of the round, all allies get a decrease in Stress and gain multiple effects from [Collection of Permanent Buffs]. The more points of Energy, the better the effects.

When an ally triggers a Meltdown, other allies get Stress -5, and gain [Death Blossom] for self for 2 rounds.
When a character triggers a Meltdown, other allies get a decrease in Stress, and gain [Death Blossom] for self.

At the start of the round, all allies lose 30% current HP.

On battle completion, 66% chance to gain 15 Goldfinch Coins, 33% chance to apply Stress +3 on all deployed characters.
On battle completion, high chance to gain a small amount of Goldfinch Coins, low chance to increase Stress on all deployed characters.

On battle completion, 66% chance apply Stress -3 on all deployed characters, 33% chance to lose 15 Goldfinch Coins.
On battle completion, high chance to reduce Stress on all deployed characters, low chance to lose a small number of Goldfinch Coins.
A broken hourglass that cannot be turned over. Its base is inscribed with the words, "The explorer who forges ahead has dismantled the lowest rib of the starry sky and opened Its belly to millions."

A magazine brimming with Sharpodonties. In this tight space, the teeth on the coins gnaw at each other, creating an unbearable noise. Proof that there is truth in the expression "more money, more problems."

An effective life insurance policy with your name listed as the beneficiary. Although the exemptions and disclaimers seem to go on forever, as long as your goals align with the policy, enforcing these clauses won't be too difficult.
A replica of the Rosetta Stone. The three languages inscribed on it serve as a reminder that transient phenomena can never alter the essence of truth.

An effective property insurance policy with your name listed as the beneficiary. Although the exemptions and disclaimers seem to go on forever, as long as your goals align with the insurance, these clauses merely serve as a checklist for property preservation.

An invaluable treasure, with a faint song echoing within its shell. Crafted from gold and silver and inlaid with jewels, it was gifted to a pure maiden. But for her, gifts and rewards have never been necessary.
A locked nut, where the lock's significance outweighs its form. The seed's imprisonment began the moment it ripened but failed to descend into the soil.
A model ship gifted by an elderly gentleman. Even the fiercest storms and most colossal waves couldn't shake the mast of this vessel—just as nothing could rattle the gentleman's backbone.

A discarded compass. Initially, it exhibited only a minor deviation and still served as a reliable substitute for the North Star, but soon, a creeping moss overcame it, filling every crevice save for the needle.

A meticulously stuffed snake skin with dried petals and sharp thorns firmly embedded into its body. After changing hands several times, it started selecting more intelligent masters—for, upon holding it, only the wise would understand that it sees its master as an enemy.

An astonishingly effective beauty product that is still within the effective duration of its incantation. "The key to beauty lies within"—this tagline helped it win the hearts of more than half the ladies in town.
A smooth piece of amber that has swallowed a butterfly. Its wings are stuck together, still standing on its shriveled cocoon. Two simultaneous misfortunes befell this burgeoning life.
A fiercely burning mushroom. It tries to burn up everything that stands between it and survival, but there are far too many of these obstacles in its homeland.
When at a loss in battle, use your body heat to quickly incubate this egg. Yes, your enemies will ridicule you for doing so, but when the bird hatches, you will have the last laugh.
The left and right gloves have finally found each other. Overtaken by the joy of their reunion, they are now eager to share their luck with you.

A pipe that a drunken worker mistook for a plumbing part and fitted with a valve. Now, it is a phenomenal bestseller, allowing every gentleman to elegantly loosen the valve and take a deep puff—"I've never felt so full of life!"
A feather-light brooch. Its maker embedded its golden opening with tiny gems. Her movements were slow and gentle, like a devout believer returning a holy relic to its box.

This pendant of a rigid floating aircraft in flight is unsuitable for wearing. As a result, it has been hanging beneath the eaves for years, accumulating a wealth of flight experience in the local area. It is especially adept at dealing with afternoon air currents and avoiding the rain.
A hand that leads the lost back to a familiar road. They say that a man encountered it after being shipwrecked, and it led him straight across the channel. Since then, it has become a little rusty.
A custom and exquisitely made notebook from Hungary. Its cover has been worn over time. Inside are a variety of Ritual Disks, which have undoubtedly seen many battles.
A small box filled with replicas of the crests and seals of various reputable families. For those in the know, there are countless ways to maximize the value of this little box.

A projector presenting a pure and unreal dream. Through the lens, you glimpse her smiling between those doors at the edge of reality. The colors melt, merge, and surround you, lifting you higher and higher until you reach the final scene.

One of Laplace's great technological achievements, reconstructed by a boy genius. It is usually used to realize his whimsical ideas, but in special cases, it can also serve as a temporary lighting tool.

A forked weapon made from the antlers of two constantly fighting deer-shaped critters. Even after being made into a weapon, they haven't forgotten their intense rivalry—if one side hits the enemy in battle, the other side will risk breakage just to strike it itself.
If you encounter a lizard at a streetside café, don't worry—it probably belongs to a fashionable Viennese citizen who accidentally left it there. It won't pose any danger.
An arcanist once recorded the visions they observed in a realm and forged them into this armillary sphere. It was later used for astrology, divination, and even self-defense.

Go ahead and throw it at your enemies whenever you desire. The sharp thorns will make them run for their lives, and as the messenger of a certain explorer who forged ahead, its endless ramblings will probably annoy your enemies to death too.

Shimmerwings are completely invisible by the time they mature and are extremely difficult to catch without the use of optical arcane skills. In order to meet the unique preferences of Viennese nobles, they are sometimes colored with gold leaf.

This scarab lay dormant in an Egyptian elder's tomb for thousands of years. To this creature, the night is like sweet spring water. If you wear black clothes and pick it up, you will become its next master.
A group of tin soldiers ready to charge into battle. They train and rally, eager to contribute, united and brave, and terrified upon seeing the sacrifice of their allies.

Arcanists are occasionally known to make fake pendulums to sell to the uninformed—"Gaze at it, accept it, embrace it," they cry, "it will take you to the promised land!"—in reality, they are knick-knacks made from the byproducts of the materials that accidentally fall into their crucibles.
Artistic beauty aside, this delicate doll bestows the joy of completely removing one's inner defenses.
An artefact crafted from ancient agate. This vessel was born to hold all kinds of things, but all it truly holds is blood and mystery itself.
One of Laplace's many technological achievements. It teaches its user the virtues of patience—that one must bide one's time to enact the ultimate revenge.
Much older than the mute chainsaw. It is totally silent but generates a great number of sparks. Is this pure inspiration or the silent protest of the aged?
With arrows sharper than bone shards and venom more potent than any formula. It always produces some "special" surprises.
A scepter made of pure gold, symbolizing power, status, wealth, and abundance. No one knows about the red that has fused deep within it.

Recommended for use with a Silver Candelabra. It will draw in wandering spirits, attaching them to the exorcist's blade and making them the wielder's vassals. These spirits can do just about anything—provided they are willing to help you.
Dry a dragon claw bone in the sun for several days, coat it with beeswax, apply some herbal powder, and hey presto—you've got yourself a weapon that can pierce through anything.

Legend has it that whoever lifts this giant axe can bring "redemption" to the world. Throughout the ages, however, no one has ever been able to take on such a responsibility. Perhaps you will be the one.
It comes from a place farther than far, with a history longer than long. It will forever call, sing, and seek, until one day it is obliterated by time.
They only appear at night, silent and with deadly precision. When they go, they leave nothing but a faint, rusty smell behind. Then, the silence returns once again.
A cane made of pure gold, used to support the body, convey one's majesty, or perform arcane rituals ... and occasionally to knock some sense into an unmotivated youngster.
That little green parrot has used this to record many things—patient information, the latest psychotherapeutic procedures, and the stories only the two of them would discuss.
It bears an engraving of a short poem written by an arcanist. Read it aloud at your peril—after all, words are often sharper than a blade.
A glistening, clear purple liquid that allows one to see the light and peer into the darkness. It must be diluted to a specific ratio before consumption.
The fruits of the future bind you tightly, growing riper each day, their rich aroma endowing you with discerning eyes and a formidable constitution.
It has existed since this land was born. It is older than time and farther than the future. You know it. You have heard its legends, and now it finally embraces you.
More mucus, more bubbles—a single drop can spell your end. Read the safety precautions carefully before use.
Tinged with the glow of the full moon, it has become a light source unto itself, capable of awakening one from any dream, whatever it may be.

If you have a large bottle of benzoin on you, it goes without saying that you mustn't let your guard down. The more unstoppable you feel, the more cautious you should be, lest you return from your adventure with even graver injuries.

A support tool for Ritual Disks designed by Laplace's Arcane Skill Storage Department. It is used to forcibly overwrite disks with a specified incantation. Testing has shown that repeatedly writing the same incantation may enhance its strength. A small number have been distributed to be used as experimental items.
A disguised throwing bomb. Devised by a true collector to counteract the covetous nature of others. Although the acorn bomb's power is rather ordinary, it is enough to deter potential acorn thieves.

A golden cup favored by a certain noble when entertaining guests. Recently, there have been complaints of a suspicious taste residing within it. "It's sweet and fishy and sticks to your teeth and tongue. Wait, is this ..." Then he could say no more.

According to legend, those who wear these glasses can discern truth from falsehood, including the truths and fallacies of arcanum. In reality, they are just a pair of regular glasses burdened by their unwarranted fame.
A makeup box bearing traces of an incantation. It has been over-enchanted with expansion incantations, making it extremely jittery. It constantly opens and closes like a clam spitting mud into water.
A loud and flamboyant mask. Masks usually hide identities, but this one does something else: it makes the wearer unforgettable, even when hidden.

A medal cherished by generations of "true gentlemen." Normally, this medal would never leave the gentleman's side, allowing him to hold an unparalleled influence during his gatherings. "Bear this medal, and the whole world will know that you are a man of the finest quality!"
A number of buyers have found that this "big rabbit's foot" on a golden keychain does indeed bring good luck, earning it the moniker of "Super Rabbit Foot."
A pendant shaped like a hot air balloon, often mistaken for a lightbulb due to its inability to float. It is quite self-conscious of its merely symbolic role and seldom argues otherwise.
A noble girl's spotlight used to attract shimmerwings. Though they are not phototropic, shimmerwings flock to this special spotlight—even if it costs them their freedom.

One of Laplace's internal products, designed to be reliable, precise, and sustainable. It is mainly used for encrypted communication among field investigators. Due to cost constraints, there are no plans for mass production.
A typewriter used for storing incantations. Beware: Every word you type will come true. Push the wrong key, and a claw intended for your enemy might just strike you instead.
For centuries she has remained, ever contemplative, unchanging, and unceasing in her quest for progress.
A pirate bestowed her private stash upon it, along with the spirit of rock 'n' roll. Since then, it has performed night and day, seven days a week.

A locked golden box with an extraordinarily intricate keyhole—a keyhole into which no key fits unless its design is sufficiently artistic. Naturally, it has become a touchstone for the artists of the Vienna Secession.
You have obtained a scroll, its profound emotions palpable. Behold—it can probe the depths of your fears and bring you back to tranquility.

An old music box belonging to a stoic astrologer. It is so ancient that it can no longer produce a sound even remotely resembling music. She knows not its origin, just as she knows not why she cannot laugh or cry.
An outcast, ever defiant, never ceasing in its struggle. Now, its horn has been removed and presented to you, and its unyielding heart and blessings have been bestowed upon you.
A cluster of candle flames, new, dazzling, alive, and ... is there any need to say more? Its gloriousness is clear for all to see. As for what you can't see, your imagination will fill in the blanks.
A helmet passed down from a destitute composer. It is said to be destined for a spectral knight who floats above the ground. How ridiculous! Imagine a knight without a body!

A coffee pot belonging to a maid skilled with numbers. She claims the coffee brewed in this pot is more aromatic and refreshing. She also adds that, for her, no coffee is as stimulating as mathematics.
An invention born of an arcanist's whim. To maintain the balance of these scales, a goldfinch continuously regurgitates glittering coins at an incredible speed.
The goldfinch accepts your invitation, opening its sharp beak. It knows exactly what it can create and what it can destroy.

An elderberry-handled umbrella. It takes considerable effort to open, since the gem on the handle must believe you have exerted all your strength before it does so. The gem cannot tell how many people are holding the umbrella, however, so having a friend assist you is most efficient.
A golden curtain needle allegedly linked to a famous family murder case in Vienna. It ended up in the hands of a noble lady and potion enthusiast, and quickly became her new favorite item.

A gun used by the royal guard that doubles as an instrument. The designer's notes say: "Bring passion to where passion is needed most." To protect the instrument's tone and durability, the guards rarely load it with live ammunition.
You glimpse myriad emotions on the blade—love and hate, zeal and subtlety, repression and catharsis, a momentary tremor, an eternal passing. These always pierce the softest parts of us.

Invented by an arcane biologist in a moment of inspiration. To ensure the arrows hit their mark, he tied the "Super Rabbit Foot" to them. It might work or it might not—it all depends on whether the merchant's goods are genuine.
A liquid distilled from a throat-sealing poison. Handle with care and open cautiously—and be sure to consult a professional alchemist before use.
These reborn sprigs have finally taken root and sprouted. Now, she entrusts them to you, along with the countless possibilities they hold.
Pallid bones carrying all the fervor and hope of the ages. They look at you like a mother looks at her child. They will do anything to protect you.
Mucus, toxins, suspicious hues, trembling bubbles. Use this to turn absolutely any unfavorable battle to your advantage.

Grind, crush, and carefully measure the moonstone. 0.5—no, 0.8 ounces, not a mite more, not a mite less. Then add six drops of that 6 AM dew. Don't underestimate its efficacy. It is sure to make you feel happy and content.
A painkiller made of benzoin, only effective when you're not in too much pain. Don't even consider taking on more difficult tasks with only a small bottle of this stuff.

Thanks to the collaboration between the Laplace Universal Materials Enchantment Department and the Arcane Skills Storage Department, attaching Arcane Skills stored on floppy disks to items is now easier than ever.

An iteration of the One-day Winder. One wind will keep the doll moving for seven days. This model sparked protests from the Doll Rights Association. They claim that the doll's fatigue far outweighs the joy it provides.

The secret to maintaining a doll's vitality. This clockwork mechanism is blessed with arcanum—any doll can move for a full day with a single wind after acquiring such a component. "This design is a lot more convenient than just yelling at my kids to get up in the morning," one consumer remarked.

A velvet moose hand puppet. According to a criminal accused of committing multiple antique jewelry thefts, his motive was that the puppet wished to eat famous foods from history. All eleven stolen antique jewels have been recovered.

A flying squirrel hand puppet. While gliding, it accidentally spat up last night's dinner—it was a minor mishap, but the shiny stone it expelled caused quite a stir among the audience. The puppet was unfazed, however. It always knew that it had refined tastes.

A lighter waiting for a new owner. Its loose and warped windproof cover is like an old man's teeth, affecting its "expression" when lighting up. It still works, however. After all, it was found in a second-hand shop, not the trash.
A humming instrument made more portable with a string. Having spent many nights journeying the streets, the string is now old and frayed. Still, it's the loyal listener of all such instruments.
An instrument that can hum away at any time. Such instruments are not valuable, but an afternoon humming in the sun is worth a few coins, and a friend who nods along to the tune is worth a million.

A cicada wing ring inlaid with gems. The indigenous people who lived near the forest didn't show much interest in cicadas until an explorer seeking a guide offered this in exchange. His request was unusual—he wanted to go to the place where cicadas sang the loudest.

A cicada-shaped ring. Its owner tried to invent a code based on cicada songs, so he ventured alone into a forest where cicadas breed. When the end of summer came around, his friends ventured to the edge of the forest to find him and found this ring lying in the dirt.
A ticket to a masquerade ball. It can help you escape the inescapable, be it your appearance, wealth, or a persistent suitor, even if only for the duration of the ball.
Who calls your name in your dreams? Who sings you that lullaby? Baby, my baby, sleep well. Only now are you safe.

A spare item peeking out of a pocket. It holds a noble quality and a willingness to offer silent but appropriate help. Among intelligent beings, this relationship is known as "companionship." This is its goal.

The ultimate accessory for professional potion alchemists! Featuring more space, more versatile container slots, and a more comfortable fit, a famous London auction house has already bought 200 of these!
The antlers of the deer girl have finally taken root. You are amazed by the vitality within them—bright, light, and warm. You have never felt so safe.

A red dancing shoe that has lost its stage. Now, it imagines itself as a well-dressed noblewoman who is locked in a tower and unable to go out. This helps it escape most of the melancholy of widowhood.

A lone red dancing shoe. It has seen too many tears and too much bloodshed by its predecessors in the cobbler's shop. To prevent the same fate from befalling itself and its partner, it went to great lengths to ensure its partner perished in the fireplace before their first performance.
This curiosity not only helps arcanists find their way back to reality but also offers them additional blessings. Naturally, a small price must be paid to obtain it.
A gentle herb that enjoys secretly distinguishing between the types of incantations around it. Once it counts more than it can handle, it "whooshes" and grows all the thorns it can.
Pour hot tea into a cup, add three spoons of sugar, and one spoon of lukewarm milk. Oh, shall we discuss the latest poem published in Pan?

Once again, a reminder—the fairies and their scales are merely part of the product's creative concept. They are simulated using arcane projections and optical technology, and are capable of being mass produced. Of course, they protect more than just your teeth.

A spare item that unfolds like a blooming flower when taken out of your pocket. Its perfect form is proof of its friendship with its owner. It dutifully fulfills its role, longing to break its silence when it sees sauce dripping down its owner's chin.

A broken dragon toe. Modern scientific analysis shows that there is a large amount of scale debris accumulated in the cracks of the toe and that they both come from the same biological individual. It can therefore be inferred that the reason for its detachment from its owner is that the creature scratched too hard, causing it to break and fall off.
A thick black staff—though it is more like a wooden stick than a staff in size. Whenever you fail to cast an incantation, you can just throw it instead and do the same amount of damage.
Hush, be quiet—don't let your whispered breathing blow away this wandering light. When you face the darkness, you will need it.

Pour St. John's Wort oil into a glass vessel, pressurize it into a combustible canister, and ignite it with an open flame to create a terrifying yellowish-green spectacle. Those of sound mind should not attempt this procedure.
A delicate armband inlaid with blood-red gems, the ancient legacy of a fallen arcanist family. Its shining firelight dispels the gloom before you, illuminating it with the glow of faded glory.
A dull ring. The letters engraved upon it are full of scratches, symbolizing the fading of thoughts. Recite that nameless poem, for it will be your salvation.
Listen to that demonic sound that echoes in the depths of your mind—it's right. You believe it and resolutely step into the coffin.

A hammer-like pestle made of hard stone. It is used to pound the feathers and eggshells of fallen goldfinches, thus staining it an indelible gold. In ancient times, this gold was used for sacred murals.
A stone bucket often used to carry rare gifts. The bucket's holder doesn't care where they come from—they simply revel in the brief golden satisfaction.

A stone basin-like mortar. Countless goldfinch feathers have fallen into it, becoming golden dust after ceaseless pounding. If you get close to the golden bottom of this vessel, you can still hear the whispers of the birds that have been lost to it.

People often revere art and reject violence, but they are not so different. Sometimes art even relies on violence. Rather than discussing these things, why don't we guess whose gun will fire the next bullet?

A flail whose actual power does not match its appearance. The spikes cannot harm flesh, but they can make sentimental mortals experience heartbreak—like the eternal farewell of a loved one or lovers parting ways.
Originally designed as a medical tool for those plagued by hallucinations and narcolepsy. Once powered up, it is no longer just an ornament. What kind of madman would want to wear such a thing?

A yellowish tincture made by soaking oak processionary moth larvae in alcohol. It is said that the yellow saliva of a large arcane creature can stimulate the nerves and the mind. This is a herbal recreation of that substance. Clear-headed arcanists should avoid ingesting it.
For those accustomed to walking in the dark, this is better than nothing, but for those who are truly lost, it is a guiding beacon—no matter where it may lead you.

The carver of this cursed golden goblet turned into a golden snake the moment it was completed, and has been guarding it ever since. It always takes more than it gives, even knowing this will lead to its destruction.

Known to academics as "Dust Amber," this mineral is often found where carbuncles dwell. Someone once hoarded a large amount of it in their home, attempting to extract the dust buried within. But in the end, all they did was turn their home into a carbuncle nest.
This creation injures both your opponent and yourself. Simply wearing it is a grand act of determination. Who said that arcanists were weak? Now, take this!

According to an old urban legend, this painting is cursed. A wealthy man bought it for a large sum, then died that very night. On that same night, a boy who had never tasted the forbidden fruit of love met his destined one. The night was long, yet somehow still short.
A command banner woven with an arcane skill. It depicts a map pointing to safe passage. There is a small chance it will lead you down a dead end, but don't worry—it's just a flag, after all.
An automatically moving spherical compass—loyal, reliable, and best of all, free. No one cares how it works—just curb your curiosity and open it up.
Before aircraft were invented, cloud hunters drew maps on balloons and flew 800 kilograms of lightning over mountains. It was a game for the fearless.
No expertise needed—just hold, lift, and smash. It guides travelers in the fog and charts unknown paths. You'd better get used to this when you walk through the fog.
A country witch's favorite. Just add an ounce of mandrake to the pot, no more, no less, then boil the water and enjoy a carefree afternoon.
Priced at only a few Goldfinch Coins and sold by dubious shops claiming to sell genuine arcane items. "Good luck! If this one doesn't work, try another."
Priced at a few dozen Goldfinch Coins, it's currently sold in limited quantities at "Sea for Yourself," and comes with a free crystal spirit bead.

Since tangible keys can only open certain kinds of locks, one must seek the help of the intangible. The key's owner once pried open the doors of a tomb to try and coerce the spirits of the dead into doing devilish things. I hope you won't follow his path.
Placed in the trunk of an old abandoned car. Though locked, the state of the box suggests there is nothing of value inside.
Placed in the trunk of an old abandoned car. "Open it, and its contents will be yours to keep."
Placed in the trunk of an old abandoned car. What kind of person would leave their life's greatest treasure in a forgotten wreck?
No one cares how it works. Just inject a little fragrance and richness, and you will receive an unexpected joy ... probably.

A limited edition item from the "Sea for Yourself" store. It is rumored to have been stolen from the sacred flame of the Uluru Games during the event's heyday. Tempted and nourished by alcohol, the flame releases an intoxicating scent.
A handcrafted item overflowing with imagination. Just light the fuse and wait. It may not cause fatal damage, but it will certainly cause some trouble.
A dangerous attempt. Humans have long been fascinated by the abilities of arcanists and have tried many times to replicate them using human wisdom.

Newly sprouted branches tirelessly absorb nutrients until the land goes dry. Now, the remains of the young creatures that have died in the forest have become a slowly decomposing resting place for the branches to thrive on.
The ancient inscriptions on it can bring luck and protection, or plague and disease. The picker insists this is a curse tainted with venom.

A pure, black, limpid liquid with a strong bitter taste and a foul smell that matches its appearance. One often hears that "the best medicine is hard to swallow," but you're better off trusting your physiological instincts on this one.
This popular arcanist party drink doesn't rely on alcohol to evoke a primal frenzy but rather spreads honeyed joy with its thick, sweet, and sour taste. Drink up! Join the orange revelry!
A broken round mirror singed by flames and covered in deep crimson cracks. If you can't find answers in the dark, what exactly are you expecting?
An adaptive, walking floppy disk reader—a rare treasure coveted by arcanists the world over. The only drawback is that it may not be by your side when you need it.
Colorless thorns grow on vast verdant plains, drinking up all the land has to offer until the fields lose their color, and they become the only remaining feature.
A lantern with a brand new heart. Though flames tried to burn it to ashes, they ultimately became the fire that fuels its core. Even now, you can still feel its searing pulse at your fingertips.

To be free means to forget about the past and live in the moment. Life is filled with celebrations and moments of solitude, but they make it all worth living.
You've really got a helluva lotta land here, boss.
Folks used to fight tooth and nail for this land.
'Course not, my eyes don't look to the past.
It's just that the old folks I've met say so, and the stories tell it that way too. I reckon it'll be the same in the future.
But don't worry too much about all that. I'm right here.
I knew it. Happens all the time, right?
Kids are out playing hide and seek and don't come home for dinner. When you finally find 'em, there they are, drifting in the lake.

The desert?
The city?

Okay.

Highway of the Times
The History of Route 77

In the early 19th century, roads began to sprawl across America, born from a need to transport messages between states. Messages were carried by people, then by carriages, and then as the messages were carried by cars, the roads grew wider and wider. Soon, an entire system of roads covered the map.

A century later, this network had grown so large and so plentiful that they were given a new name—national highways. They were also assigned a number, like Route 1, or Route 101. But, this road, however? It refused a boring name like Route 71 or 73. Thus, Route 77 was born.

...

Call it the Great Southern Highway, the Main Street to Texas, whatever you like. The great race only happens here—from end to end, winner gets fifty dollars a mile! Let that cash prize slip through your fingers, and you'll regret it for the rest of your life, doomed to truck remorsefully along that some old road forever.

...

It may not compare to the interstate highways of today, but its charm remains. Take a stroll down this road and buy a commemorative medal, because nothing is more valuable than the joy of its memory.
Life Along Route 77
Unearthing Southern Life

What comes to mind when you think of the South? Probably the beating sun and the honest, hardworking people, right? How about shotguns and chainsaws? You need to stop watching so many movies. Chainsaws, at least, aren't a vital part of Southern life. Here are three points to remember if you want to avoid upsetting southerners:

- Many of them are hardworking and honest farmers—the salt of the earth. They're likely to work the fields their entire lives, come rain or shine. Their farms are their homes, and they're raised to be fiercely protective of them, so don't trespass. You wouldn't want someone to barge into your home, would you?

- They hold a deep connection to music, from country to bluegrass to heavy metal. Everything is welcome here, just take a look at Austin's South by Southwest music festival and you'll see it all. That being said, their standards can be quite high, and overly frivolous music might not be to their liking. For example, one should never claim that disco is true music in front of them—you wouldn't want to interrupt the flow of conversation with such a sensitive topic, would you?

- Living in vast, open spaces, "bigger is better" is the motto of the South. Big cars for long trips, huge roadside billboards to attract attention, wide hats and chunky boots to protect from the elements, and to show off a little, too. So remember, be generous. Don't say things like "just enough" or "too big." You wouldn't want to be seen as stingy, would you?

- And here's the most important point! Horror movies are all nonsense. The idea of Southern farm families being ignorant, conservative, bloodthirsty, and violent is a terrible stereotype. Never treat people based on things you've seen in the movies. You might regret it.

"That's right, the wife and I were on the road, staying at a motel along the highway," said the man in a grave tone.

"That day, I saw the strangest thing through the motel window. It was a little white sheep standing on two legs. I went out to say hello to it, and it replied! I thought it must've been a real smart sheep ..." added the melancholic woman.

This is a cautionary tale. Don't treat animals you find by the side of the road like pets—they might just be a person.
The Spirit of Expansion
Memoirs of an Old Man

I'm old. So old that my grandson might find me dead in bed tomorrow. Every day could be my last. That's why I've decided to write a few things down, so the priest and the kids will have something to say at my funeral.

There's nothing much exciting about being a ranch boy. I spent most of my days herding cattle and driving off cattle thieves. That's right, cowboys. But I can't quite seem to remember now. Did the name "cowboy" refer to the thieves or us ranchers? So if you're reading this and you can't figure out what I mean by "cowboy," let it be. I ain't even sure myself.

Things were different back then. There were no wide roads for people and cattle to walk on, no motor vehicles that could fit a whole bunch of cattle in them. We herded our cattle on horseback to rivers, markets, slaughterhouses, even to other states. We had to watch out for coyotes and bandits, too. But people didn't call us cowboys back then. What was it they called us? I just can't seem to recall.

It wasn't until later on that us farm boys became known as cowboys. The kids around the neighborhood used to ask me if I'd ever had a duel at high noon or tamed a wild horse. Maybe I was already going senile by then, because I had this vague feeling that I'd ridden a wild horse before and that I'd let a bullet fly under the noonday sun. But one thing's for certain: I never saw any gold. I'd hoped to collect at least a little and leave it to my kids, but I never found any to give.

Now they all call me "cowboy." Yep, "Old Cowboy Tommy," but I still feel like that might not be who I am. That's why I wrote all this. I hope that the real Old Tommy can exist somewhere in the world, at least for a short time.

The newer interstate highways may be faster and more convenient, but number 77's here to stay.
Land, new life, citizen welfare—this is the place to realize dreams and the road to freedom.
Ancient civilizations were built on the river; modern civilizations are built on the highway.
"So many cars come through here—we should really have a better road."
Last night, countless meteors streaked across the sky. They were all heading west.
Cars replaced feet, and we moved faster; now cars drive into restaurants, and we eat faster and pay faster.
"So many people are heading west to start a new life. We better keep up—I'm sure there's a huge market for our pants, cans, houses, and cars."
The winds show a new road to a distant journey and a chance to leave this barn and stable behind.
"After extensive testing, our cars' average speeds on this street always balance out to 77 mph. I think it must be fate."
Now there are two paying jobs, one heading south along this road and the other fixing it.
Businessmen will soon smell an opportunity in this deck of cards, and a huge card city will rise by the dam.
And then grab another handful and finally distribute it to the bad and the ugly.
Seven after seven, the cowboy spirit goes on.
That's how it was back then: what you wanted you couldn't get, and what you didn't want came in droves.
A straw hat, a guitar, and a mariachi. Hey! Friend! Sing a song for this hero's story!
He ran through the streets with gold in his hands, the dust behind him stirring the era.
In the cowboy bar, there's no water or milk, only throat-burning tequila.
Don't worry about the sign. Travelers are always looking for a place to stay at night.
The front desk's pastime when there are no guests. The pleasant hum of electricity never fails to inspire.
The broken doorbell isn't a problem—the screeching brakes will wake the maid.
Bad weather is great for a motel in need of guests. This is what hot towels were made for.
"The two of you seem pretty close. How long will you be staying? Just two hours, huh? Oh-ho-ho! Got it."
Age has its advantages. Some guests like places with no internet and no personal information checks.
They check in, and they check out. Watching the tire tracks build up is one of the maid's pleasures.
At first it was just a thin line, bringing good and bad news, but as the number of messages increased, the line widened into a road.
This road has taught many what fear is, like having a child with an empty stomach.
It's a well-known tale that milk spoils when something evil is near.
As long as you keep playing cards, this deck will be dealt to everyone, no exceptions.
Heavy traffic, narrow roads, heedless travelers, inevitable tragedy.
