You turn to unconventional methods to clear out the outpost, and your hard work yields rewards—you come across some usable alchemy materials.
Stay a while
A vagrant returns. He tells you about his begging exploits for the day and hopes you can help him out. Clearly, things didn't go well for him.
Have a try
"Test your aim; only $20 a round—no Cruzeiros ... and you have to use your own bullets." ... The shopkeeper's demeanor makes you want to shoot him instead.
The rainforest is never short of lurking threats. Fortunately, customers are often inclined to help the shopkeeper out of kindness. You use this as leverage to gather some intel.
You stand there, watching the hapless plump sheep miss their shots, all the while planning to fleece them in a bet.
Repair with alchemy
Your crucible can create many wonders, but precise mechanical parts aren't among them. Perhaps you've overestimated your cunning?
Repair with tools
You may excel at gambling and shooting, but fixing things has never been your forte—in fact, you're far better at breaking things.
Kick it
A swift kick does the trick—an impressive makeshift repair. Now you can move on.
The rainforest is a cornucopia of food. As a skilled hunter, you won't need to worry about going hungry.
Search for tools
A vehicle could save you precious time. Even finding a wheel would be better than trekking through the rainforest on foot.
Make supplies
You fire up the crucible and toss in everything you've got. You don't know what you'll need, but it never hurts to be overprepared.
You should rest first. The road ahead is still a long one.
Break in
Your special bullets melt all the lethal weapons inside. Your enemies have no choice but to surrender.
You resist the urge to break in and quietly leave. You don't like to waste your time on trifling matters.
Try them
Dull colors are edible, bright colors are poisonous—testing these old suppositions with your mouth was obviously an unwise choice.
Collect some
You are unwilling to take unnecessary risks outside the gambling table, so you let them become alchemy materials to be used in your crucible.
Agree to help
Your little creation saves the day. This is one incredibly lucky fellow, since your willingness to help is as unpredictable as a roll of the dice.
Stand by
The crocodile shows no interest in you, and you don't intend to disturb its happy hunting. Who knows, perhaps you'll come across some decent adventuring gear later.
Attempt to repair it
Clearly, repairing machinery is not where your strength lies, but tinkering with random things is something you can handle.
It's none of my business
You have no interest in the eccentric schemes of the computing center in the rainforest. You're more concerned with the cocoa beans that fill their machines.
Learn more
Watching your impressive marksmanship, the hunter's expression sours as he realizes his overconfidence may have been just a tad too much.
"You honestly think the things you caught while hunting are worth my time?" You scoff at the suggestion and leave.
Try to catch them
The tooth fairies are more agile than you thought. After a brief struggle, all you manage to snag is a small portion of the loot they stole. This entire escapade was barely worth it.
Rather than blindly attempting to capture them, perhaps you should try communicating with them amicably. Maybe they'll reveal the secrets of the rainforest to you.
Read it carefully
A gaggle of ferocious geese surrounds the pool, eyeing the delicious treasures in your pocket. Luckily, you came prepared.
Tear it apart
You will no longer allow the trivialities of the past to cloud your mind. There are more important matters to focus on right now.
Buy information
Being penniless is not something you want to grow accustomed to. Luckily, the other party is willing to accept your "junk" as payment.
Take special measures
You rarely play by the rules. "I'm not so good with words, so how about you talk to my gun?"
Since there's no chance of them to return to where they belong, it would be best to let them to rest here for now.
Store carefully
You don't know where they came from, but you can help return them to their rightful place.
"Buy" the goods
You leave something he may find of use, and in return, the supplies are yours to take. A few goods for a life is more than a fair deal.
Take a gamble
From a scientific standpoint, using poison to fight poison is not logical, but he has no choice but to try his luck.
Provide antidote
"You're a hell of a lot luckier than I am!" The thing that flew out of your crucible saves the smuggler's life. He wishes to thank you properly.
The car is miraculously fixed, but what else are you expecting? It still doesn't have a battery or gasoline. There's no way you can get it running.
Try starting it
After several attempts, you come to the conclusion that it would be better to take it apart and throw it into the crucible than cling on to any expectations of it actually working.
Give up
You'd rather take a risky bet at the gambling table than try to fix this.
Take care of it
The compressed food inside is by no means delicious, but it'll fill your belly. Besides, you're used to the taste.
Contact Zeno
You find the radio in the house and inform Zeno to send someone to retrieve the supplies. This took a little longer than you expected.
There's no need to feel bad about leaving them behind; they are not the primary focus of this journey after all.
Mess around with it
Thoughtless actions often lead to negative consequences, but fortunately luck is on your side. Good thing you have the other hand to help you remove the handcuffs.
Carry it with you
It's too heavy. You realize it was a mistake to try to catch fugitives with it, and abandon the idea. Fortunately, it's not too late.
Leave it be
It's much too heavy, and with its excessive size, it won't fit into your crucible. You decide to let it remain here forever.
Pick up the picture frame
It's a dusty family photo. What could have happened for them to leave without taking it with them?
Pick up the toy
Didn't you once have a stuffed animal like this? Was it a little crocodile or a little beaver? You know these are trivial memories of the past now.
Pick up the clock
The clock's hands are frozen at 2:18, capturing a moment in time forever. Perhaps it's waiting for its owner to return.
Do nothing
You don't want to disturb anything. For those caught in the "Storm," these remnants might one day become cherished memories.
All the eggs crash to the ground, and the hen leaves in despair. You find some useful items in the empty nest.
Prevent the tragedy
You stop the hen's madness. Even a trickster like you can't stand such an absurd scene.
Help him
You offer him a meal. After gobbling it down, the birdkeeper stands up, gives you a small token of thanks, and sets off to find his children.
Help him?
You hesitate, knowing how precious this freedom is. You once longed for it too.
Help enthusiastically
Tracing back your histories, you both work for the same goal or organization. You have no reason to turn down her request.
Coldly turn down
You have no fondness for those bureaucrats in plaid uniforms. At this moment, you have no intention or desire to lend her a hand.
Without breaking a sweat, you deal with the pests—along with the stench in the room.
The stench wafting from the door crack is suffocating. You curb your curiosity and move on.
You don't find anything useful and decide to leave.
Investigate carefully
Gathering evidence isn't your specialty, but you manage to do a sufficient job of it. In the end, you realize that it's just an unlucky soul who lost his life in some unfortunate accident.
How could anyone refuse such a warm invitation? Despite losing some time, you can't help but feel much cheerier.
You've never had much passion for music, so you offer her a small trinket as an apology and leave.
They're hard to turn down ...
Rather than leaving, you opt to buy some trinkets to reciprocate his kindness. It's been a while since you felt such warmth from strangers.
Decisively decline
Clearly, this is not the time for shopping or catching up.
Determine authenticity
This stack of useless papers and the false information they contain can't slow you down.
Accept without reservation
The Brotherhood's tricks successfully deceive you. It is not easy to find your way out of the favela, and it has already taken up a considerable amount of your time.
Visit the store
The food is by no means tasty, but it does help ease the hunger.
Past experience tells you this place isn't a good choice, and the empty seats confirm it.
Provide a recipe
Though the chef speaks highly of his dishes, you find their uniqueness a little hard to swallow. You generously offer a recipe of your own.
Loot thoroughly
You fail to find anything useful, but it was still quite an interesting experience.
Remain cautious
The charred remains of the house eventually collapse, but fortunately, no harm is done. The animals will have to find new homes.
Take a break
A rare scenic spot on your journey. How long has it been since you last had a proper rest?
Place a bet
Your participation elevates the intensity of the gambling. As expected, things devolve into a chaotic farce, but you walk away with significant gains.
Leave quietly.
Though you would like to join in, you have more important matters to attend to. See? Showing a little restraint now and then isn't so hard.
The gambling chips catch your attention and quickly make their way into your pocket. Just as you knew they would.
Talk to the children
You try to get information from the little scamps, but favela dwellers aren't the easiest folk to deal with. Fortunately, you know how to handle them.
Play with the children
What starts as a peaceful conversation turns into a "fierce battle." Luckily, you know how to handle the little rascals.
Negotiate with the children
The ringleader tries to extort you, but after seeing your "fireworks," they all flee in terror.
Make it stop
It's no more difficult to deal with them than any other thugs you've faced in the past.
Drive it away
Impatience overcomes you, and you fire a few shots to drive it away.
Trick it into coming down
A clever monkey never refuses a glass of delicious juice. Now you can make it pay.
Extend a warm welcome
You guide your two newly made friends, fending off hoodlums along the way. You even offer them some tasty delicacies from the area. This isn't like you at all!
Brush them off
After a brief exchange, you become impatient and leave without looking back.
Prepare and observe
As expected, their flashy outfits attract some unwanted attention. Fortunately, you were prepared for this and help chase away the uninvited intruders.
Escort to Zeno
Zeno's people take the child. You pray he makes better choices once he's calmed down.
Let go
The child's made-up story moves you, and you decide to let him go—who knows, maybe he is telling the truth.
Convey best wishes
The choice is his to make, and you must respect it. At least you can offer him a bit of help toward his journey.
Wander around
The favelas aren't all junk and despair; there are also certain sights worth seeing. You know this better than most.
Fill your belly
The roadside vendor's pot emits a tempting aroma. You know there's no guarantee it will live up to its promise, but you don't mind trying.
Talk to the residents
You know you're no different from any of them. Bullets, bets, and luck—that is all you can count on these days.
Have a rest.
You doze off in a corner. The people here never pay much attention to what others are doing, as long as they're not wearing anything valuable, that is.

Notes on a Weather Chart

- It is half past ten in the morning, yet even by the window, the page cannot be read without a lamp. I set the journal by the sill, lit the lamp, and returned to find it layered in fine coal ash.

- Best to refrain from keeping the windows open for now.

- On the Thames, visibility is so low that feeding the swans is a hopeless task. I hear their mournful calls but cannot see them. Their wings beat against the smog like warnings to retreat.

- Records suggest fogs like these are unusual for this season.

- Cases of tuberculosis are on the rise. While I have no firm statistics, the overcrowding in hospitals and sanatoriums tells its own story.

- By tea time, visibility's improved slightly. The bus lamps barely pierce the fog, their faint glow the only evidence of their passage.

- Not good. Now my chest is starting to burn too.

- At the hospital, there's talk of a "Black Fog" capable of flattening buildings. Supposedly, one hospital was claimed in such a disaster. A tiny tornado? No, didn't look like it. Either this is a macabre joke, or someone should call up an arcanist to investigate.

London Air Pollution Auto-Detect Cleaner Research Notes

Improved Suction Device - Third Test Unsuccessful again. Not surprising—a mere cleaning device cannot possibly hope to replace the role of the Fogwalker lineage. Amplifying the family's Arcane Skill may hold some promise, but ... we've only three weeks left. Truth is, my goal is not to solve the unsolvable mysteries of the industrial era—I simply need to ensure that breathable air is available to all for the event's duration. That means faster filtering, broader reach, larger capacity—just for a short period of time, not forever. Arcane Skill Boosting Device - Fourth Test I could be off the mark on this one. Boosting the potency of arcane skills showed very limited effects. This line of thought failed to meet expectations, miserably so. It was a bloody waste of time! Air Pollution Purifier - First Test Thanks to the St. Pavlov Foundation for their ritual inscription techniques, the device works! I was on the right track, somewhat. The Fogwalker's Arcane Skill may be irreplaceable, but this essentially doubles the number of hands we've got. By inscribing incantations onto a device like this, it's like having a duplicate of myself, working in tandem with me. Sadly, I'm not capable of supporting more than one of these, and the purification efficiency is still subpar ... Air Pollution Purifier MK. III - First Test A complete catastrophe! I'm a fool, an idiot, a nincompoop! Curse it, curse it! Advanced Air Pollution Purifier - Third Test What an astounding discovery by the Foundation! I've never heard of enchanting arcane skills onto everyday, ordinary items before; their developments in this area are revolutionary. Though I lack the expertise to perform true enchantment, following their instructions to combine specific tools has improved my Arcane Skill's integration into the device! And by integrating components of human technology ... I've achieved success! I shall name this creation the "London Air Pollution Auto-Detecting Purifier." London Air Pollution Auto-Detect Cleaner MK. III - Seventh Test Phenomenal! Maintaining the purification output puts an extraordinary strain on me, but at least it is sustainable for several hours. I pray that tomorrow's demonstration goes off without a hitch.
Unofficial Work Logs (Not Suitable for Formal Submission)

Note 1

It's hard to say which is more miserable—the pea soup in the air or the pea pudding on my table.

I didn't finish today's report concerning the Fogwalker. He wasn't in his office, and I only happened upon him while wandering the streets at dinnertime. Trying to find someone in the fog is the worst game of hide-and-seek imaginable. The Fogwalker is piecing together a device he claims to be some sort of smog filtration machine ... I hope he doesn't truly believe he can handle all this fog on his own.

Note 2

Almost had my leg smashed in by a car. An Uluru leaflet dive-bombed my face, and with the Foundation uniform on, I couldn't get cross about it and tear the thing up.

HQ sent new tasks. Annoying. Frankly, under these circumstances, it feels inevitable that the London qualifiers will be canceled.

Note 3

Never thought I'd be drafting up paperwork to get the qualifiers canceled so soon. I'm oddly excited about the whole thing.

Note 4

Yes, it's all so strange. Everything here contradicts what we've managed to preserve in our records. But so what, why couldn't it have just been recording errors, bad recording practices, or outright falsified data that were passed on to us?

Meanwhile, I'm choking on coal dust that is falling as heavy as snow and putting up with a colleague who keeps getting lost in the fog. A stellar job experience.

Note 5

It's done, though there's a heap of follow-up work ahead. Honestly, I'm hoping that magnificent contraption will actually succeed. That way all these decorations won't go to waste, the tourists and athletes won't have wasted their time, and I won't have wasted all my pre-drafted paperwork.

Subject: The "London Air Pollution Auto-detect Cleaner" Project: Progress and Future Collaboration To the Honorable Head of the Foundation's London Division, Allow me to extend our greetings on behalf of the London Atmospheric Clean-up Committee Office and present a thorough progress update on the "London Air Pollution Auto-detect Cleaner" initiative. ... Though the research has faced setbacks and failed to resolve the pressing issues of the Uluru qualifiers, we greatly appreciate the open-minded approach and collaborative spirit exhibited by your department. Without your material enchantment technologies and the protocols for incantation inscription, progress would have been far more limited. As indicated in earlier communications, we are committed to sharing the outcomes of this joint research endeavor in both mechanical engineering and arcanum studies. Although the device has not yet achieved its intended results, we will honor this commitment. As per standard collaboration practices with the Foundation, since your team provided only technical support while all material sourcing and manufacturing were conducted by us independently, the physical device will not be included in the shared materials. However, we will share its design concepts, manufacturing data, and complete test records. ... Please accept our heartfelt gratitude for your continued cooperation. Should you require clarification or wish to discuss this matter further, please do not hesitate to reach out. Yours sincerely, Arthur Fog London Atmospheric Clean-up Committee Office

Post-Qualifiers Prospects: Setting Out Beneath Clear Skies

Following the Uluru London Qualifiers, 32 athletes from Britain, competing in 18 different events, departed for Australia aboard an Imperial Airways flight this morning. The weather was exceptionally clear with fresh air and no visible smog. Imperial Airways personnel commented that it was "an exceedingly rare occurrence, an ideal omen for their momentous journey."

    Reports suggest that the rare clear skies may be related to the "Fog Monster Incident" during the qualifiers. Many claim that Willow's floor ritual routine banished both the fog and the phantom beast, while skeptics argue that the Witch staged the entire event, using a sinister spectacle to manipulate public sentiment. Others have even claimed to hold insider knowledge indicating this to be part of a century-long conspiracy orchestrated by the British government ...

    Whatever the truth of the matter, the Uluru qualifiers have brought tangible benefits to London. Hospital admissions for respiratory conditions have dropped by 60%, with many residents reporting easier breathing and air quality "reminiscent of centuries past."

Sometimes, it is not the outfit that defines the individual, but the individual that defines the outfit.

Its hem strategically conceals her legs from the side and rear, sparing her from unwanted attention.
A Custom Prosthesis

Built to suit the interviewee's body and habits, this prosthetic boasts flexible joints and an almost perfectly lifelike weight and appearance, making it a genuine work of art.
Nevertheless, the interviewee describes it as "an ugly, awkward fire poker."
Delayed Freedom, Belated Peace

The 1921 treaty marked the attainment of Ireland's long-sought independence. The shadows of conflict faded, and a compromise that most could live with was put forward. However, opinions remained divided.

While some believed the compromise to be just the first part of a larger plan, others considered it an outright betrayal of freedom. The debate over peace seemed to have no end in sight.

And so, the poor, innocent black swan, entrusting her faith to peace, danced gracefully that day.

Her misjudgment took everything from her—her family, her dreams, her home ...

Leaving only a stiff, clunky prosthetic as compensation.
The Power of Words

"Poor lass ... you're so young, and yet ... Be sure to come to me if you ever need anything, alright?"

The old woman across the street looks at everyone with pitying eyes, but after losing her son in the war, how could she spare any sympathy for anyone else?

"I'm not your daughter. Save your energy for yourself."

...

"Afternoon, miss, we live just down the street. We're getting married in a week—would you like to come?"

A new couple? Everyone else is struggling just to get by—and they're inviting a stranger to their wedding, of all things?

"A wedding? You'd be better off saving that money for your rent."

...

"Shh ... quiet, the witch is here—watch out or she'll put a curse on you."

"She curses anyone who gets too close to her—just look at Mrs. Kate and the Jameses!"

Utter foolishness, but it's not like I care—as long as they leave me alone.

"Your lives are already cursed with misery anyway, with or without me."
Second Place

Pandora Wilson: It's been a long time since you were out on the field. What's going through your mind right now?
Willow: Honestly, I am bored out of my mind.
Pandora Wilson: Oh, that's unexpected ... I thought you'd have deeper feelings than just boredom.
Willow: Were you expecting lofty dreams of glory? Or for me to speak of a burning desire for victory? Only a child would waste their thoughts on such trifles, and I curse anyone who gives a damn about them—may they never get what they want.
Pandora Wilson: I didn't mean to bring up any of those topics, but you make thought-provoking points all the same. So, what do you really care about when it comes to performing? 
Willow: There's a particular person I want to watch my performance.
Pandora Wilson: Would you care to tell us who that is?
Willow: Charlotte. Charlotte O'Hagan.
Pandora Wilson: So, this is about proving something to yourself? And to her?
Willow: Who knows? I just want to dedicate this dance to her, and wish her all the best of health.

Children and Young Persons

In a family of limited means, it makes perfect sense for children to assist with housework and lightening the load for the busy adults. When the household income falls short of supporting the entire family, children were often encouraged to do other work to supplement their parents' earnings.

However, after the Industrial Revolution took the children out of their homes and into the factories, problems began to surface.

This problem plagued Britain from the late 18th century and well into the 20th, only to be definitively resolved by the Children and Young Persons Act of 1933.

Yet, for some families, this resolution came at a price, how was the Grove family supposed to make ends meet when children were no longer allowed to work in factories?

"How about being a knocker-upper? You'll at least earn your lunch money that way."

"It's not a bad little job, runnin' around the city, meeting all kinds of people, and knockin' on their windows. It's better than polishin' shoes, anyway."
The Ultimate Answer

"You know what? You've actually got a very important job. Without you, how can people 'spect to get to work on time?"

She's at it again, same old nagging. Better get comfy.

"Sleeping in on workdays is bleedin' awful. You get the whip and a pay cut and all. No wages, no bread, and if you've got no bread, you'll starve, then you'll have to eat bugs and the like."

What's she even on about? She's doing my poor head in ...

"I know, love, you're all over the place with questions right now—why this, why that, why get up so early? Can't we have a cheeky lie-in? When all you get for your day's work is a measly loaf, you can't help but wonder why in God's name the bakery charges so much for it."

I get it now. She's the one who's confused.

"Sorry, can't say I know either. But I reckon there's an answer somewhere, right? If not, why do the grown-ups never ask?"

Sorry, little one. I see you're in a muddle, but there's not much I can do about that.

"So, you'll wake me up tomorrow too, right?"

The day's done, little one. Time to close your eyes.
"Night-night, Ollie. See ya tomorrow."

"Cluck, cluck."
The Secret of Flight

Pandora Wilson: Considering your age and your era, it's no small miracle that you've managed to retain such an unspoiled and innocent outlook on life.
Flutterpage: Mum and Dad keep bangin' on about it, tellin' me to grow up quicker, but I ain't quite figured that out yet—feels like I'm still just doing it one year at a time.
Pandora Wilson: I assume they're talking about growing up mentally, not physically.
Flutterpage: I reckon someone oughta put the secret to growin' up in the papers for the whole world to know.

Cavalry on the Waves

The early 20th century was an era of turmoil. As Australia continued to honor its cavalry's heroic deeds in the war, a thread of wool sailed across the Indian Ocean, passed the Cape of Good Hope, and crossed the Atlantic, bringing the legacy of pure Australian wool to a fedora hat in Great Britain.

His memory of the past is hazy, as a gentleman's hat can only observe the hats of others. But that particular day stands out vividly in his mind—a sea of fedoras and casquettes all around him, the rhythmic rise and fall of a clenched fist, and a white cloth overhead.

The white cloth then floated downward, gently resting on his head ... or more specifically, on the head of the gentleman wearing him.

"Our battle has only just begun!"

Indeed, it was in that moment that the words above made sense to him, and he realized—this is a battle, one that had just begun, and one that would never end.
A Faded Dream

Somewhere on this planet, there exists a beautiful land of red soil—a place teeming with life, where water flows, grass grows, and wool is plentiful. Yet, despite its tranquility, ambitious souls constantly eye the peaceful lives of its inhabitants.

That was until a courageous rider appeared—a brave member of the Rangers dedicated to restoring justice and equality to the people of the red land!

With the precision of an eagle and will of iron, he and his steed rode as one. He made his name known to all ...

"I am ... Brimley!"

...

"Now, I hope you all leave here today with no doubts in your hearts. This outcome is exactly what I had hoped for, both as a spokesperson and as a ranger."

Brimley concluded the press conference in record time, despite straying from the script. His opening words left a lasting impression on everyone present, including himself.
Once a Ranger, Always a Ranger

Brimley: It's truly an honor to be interviewed by UTTU today—not just as a spokesperson but also as a hat.
Pandora Wilson: And what a hat you are. Everyone knows how skillfully you handle the press, so I think I might actually manage to get a decent interview this time.
Brimley: Too right, you will. Keeping the populace pleased is part of a ranger's responsibility, after all.
Pandora Wilson: It's not rare to see people flip between different personalities when finding themselves in different situations, but you always seem to remain true to yourself.
Pandora Wilson: Do you cling on to your ranger identity, even when the job at hand doesn't call for it?
Brimley: Bloody oath! Whether I'm out there fighting for the underdog, staring down a bushfire, or scribbling away on the perfect speech—I'm a ranger, and I always will be!
Pandora Wilson: I'm glad you're finally speaking off-script. Now, let's get to the heart of who you are as a ranger—no holds barred.

Voyages of Volatility Gameplay Intro
Each rotation of Voyages of Volatility offers 3 selectable Myth Manifests to assist you in battle.
Challenge the 3 battles, and you can earn rewards once your total points reach the required milestones.
Each rotation of Voyages of Volatility offers 3 challenges, with points awarded for completing each challenge.
You have the option to adjust the challenge difficulty. Increasing the difficulty will make the battles harder, but you'll earn more points.
Characters and Myth Manifests deployed in a completed battle are considered locked-in, and cannot be used for any other remaining battles. Be strategic with your team choices!
Isle of Echoes Gameplay Intro
Myth Manifests are essentially powerful boss companions that aid you in battle.

To unlock a Myth Manifest, you must first defeat its first battle. The first trial battle unlocks the Myth Manifest for you to use, and subsequent trial battles will:
1. Grant stat boosts.
2. Unlock more passive skills.
3. Grant you Mind Map Fragments, which are basically "talent points" for you to assign on the Mind Map.
Depths of Myth Gameplay Intro

Depths of Myth is divided into multiple large zones, each of which is further divided into stages. Every 10 meters of depth marks a new stage within the zone, and the deeper you dive, the greater the rewards.
Euphotic Zone
Mesophotic Zone
Bathyal Zone
Abyssal Zone
Hadal Zone
Each Transition Zone has multiple trial battles for you to defeat. Only by completing them all can you break through the Transition Zone and venture further into the depths.
Characters and Myth Manifests deployed in a completed battle are considered locked-in, and cannot be used for any other remaining battles at that depth. Be strategic with your team choices!
By using Trance, you can earn rewards at a much faster rate.
Descending to different depth milestones in Depths of Myth will increase the amount of rewards earned through Trance.
Up to 4 Trance chances are replenished every Monday at 5 a.m., and a maximum of 8 Trance chances can be stored.
Mind Map Gameplay Intro
Here are the Mind Map Fragments you currently have. You can think of these fragments as "talent points."
You can reset your Mind Map at any time and get back all the Mind Map Fragments you have assigned.
Mind Map Fragments are used to activate nodes on the Mind Map. These nodes can be seen as "talents" that are carried by your Myth Manifest.

While machines have brought prosperity to the city, they have also brought smog.
So, you've got yourself a suitcase that can hold an entire army. You can change the scenery in here and even conjure up a few candy houses whenever you fancy? Not to shabby, I suppose.
But let's have a gander at who's living here ... A child, another child, there's ... a lunatic ... funny.
Right, let's be honest, now. It's not like any of this is really worth making a fuss over.
It's not like anyone else gives a damn, anyway. And as long as you're not bothered, it's nothing to lose sleep over.
I suppose I should take a leaf out of your book on this one.
Well, you certainly don't strike me as a witch.
No darkness, no indifference—you're young and responsible to a fault. You'd make for a terrible witch.
Oh, don't even bother trying to console me, I can't stand that sort of thing! It'll only make me say something even nastier.
Sometimes, in London, you'll see people takin' to the streets, all kinds of people shoutin' about how important it is for kids to be in school.
Did you ever go to school, Vertin? What do they make kids do there?
Skippin' ... I know all about that. Whenever I've got a question with no answer, I usually just fly off somewhere else for a bit.
Or I'd hide. Hidin' always does the trick. I can shove my head in the laundry basket, and the grown-ups'd think I'm just a heap of dirty clothes.
Your clothes are too tidy for that, so I s'pose it's not really an option ... but you could still give it a go—it's actually really comfy in the laundry basket.
I bet they've got a lot of really important jobs at school, ones that only little kids like us can do.
Probably as important as bein' a knocker-upper, right? Else, why would all them kids be so keen to go?
Me? I'm all grown up now! No school for me, that's what Dad says, anyway.
Crikey, you've got some top-notch rangers here. Wouldn't hurt to start a proper rangers' club, if you ask me.
I'd be top dog, of course, but who do you reckon should take number two? A true ranger's always up for a bit of advice on matters like this.
That "mighty king of wooden steeds," eh? You can't deny he's got one hell of an impressive mane, and those eyes—phwoar, true grit if I ever saw it.
Any ranger worth his salt would be chuffed to ride that one. On the other hand, the thing looks more like a steed than a rider, eh?
Ha! That young fella, he's got the makings of something great, no doubt!
The lad's got guts on that bike, I'll give him that, and he's certainly got the ranger tone down!
I'm teaching the lad everything I know.
You're not quite there yet, mate. You might not be a ranger, but you've definitely got what it takes to be the club's top sponsor—the big cheese who calls the shots!
Naturally, if you're keen on giving riding a go, I can show you how it's done.
The first step's easy, mate—all you've got to do is plop me on your head.
It seems like you're always at it, coming and going, and when you do return, you look like you've been to hell and back.
People like you don't last long in this world, you can mark my words.
What are you even trying to prove? That you're so courageous you don't even fear an early demise?
Don't be daft. A handful of years after you've kicked the bucket, not a single soul will remember you.
Or you could live like a spineless coward, endure all those sneers, and perhaps, one day, something good might come your way.
Has someone actually died here?
When death comes knocking, it'll be too late. So, make the most of the time you've got, while you still can.
(She follows you around, not a word spoken).
I haven't had any work to do since I got here, and it's left me with far too much time to spare.
From what I've gathered, the most popular job around here is bein' one of your lackeys, so I'm still learnin' the ropes.
No, you don't need to pay me—this job's interesting enough on its own.
(She spreads her arms, flaps them like wings, and takes off like a bird).
Blimey, the weather here is as temperamental as London's.
I reckon I spent too long under the Aussie sun ... nearly forgot what this kind of weather feels like!
That's right—London's fog, its streets, and all those old mates ... especially Fog. Before I even realized it, he'd become Old Fog, became a hero long before I had the chance.
Speaking of which, since I've got Oliver looking up to me in a way, maybe I should find a more subtle way to get him to call me "Uncle Brimley."
A real ranger never complains about the weather! Come rain or shine, it's all part of the ride, mate!
And don't forget about maintenance—when you're out riding in the rain, it's all about keeping your trusty mate polished and waxed.
*A lighthearted tune*
...? Hello? A flood of energy just obscured my vision. Is that you, right there?
*A serene tune*
So, you weren't trying to hide ... This energy—this *is* you, isn't it?
*A pressing tune*
No need to worry, I'll keep my distance ...
From right here ... I can finally see your true presence.
*A joyful tune*
*A concordant tune*
It's just like I've always said—those high-and-mighty suits? Can't trust 'em for a second.
They're totally out of touch with our struggles, our worries, and our dreams.
If we want a peaceful future, it's something we gotta create, with every step we take!
You're chasing big dreams, pal, and I've got your back on that.
A "pal" who's down to support the arts! Now that's a real pal! Ready to jump in with both feet and go all the way with me?
I was thinking of filling the Foundation brass's office with bubbles, just to shake things up a bit.
Dude ... Stir up the hornet's nest like that and everyone's gonna get stung. How about we go do something a little more practical?
You could lend a hand to A Knight with his armor, and hey, maybe pick up a bit of art along the way—the art of hammering steel.
Oh my ... Just what am I seeing right now?
Why in the world would you dress yourself like that?
You got it—everything I'm wearing is second-hand. Fashion doesn't come for free, Mr. Model.
Poverty is certainly no picnic ... it does limit one's wardrobe choices, but I'm not talking about managing your finances here.
A lack of confidence is far worse than poverty could ever be, my dear.
Be confident! You're pretty enough without all these gaudy embellishments of yours.
Especially those rhinestones ... Whatever compelled you to encrust every piece of jewelry you're wearing with those things?
Ain't you an adorable little puppy? Come here, darling. I've got a treat for you ...
Doggie
The puppy is very happy to play with you.
I always thought it'd be nice to have a little doggie around the motel, but not everyone's comfortable sharing their space with an animal.
The puppy feels your pain.
You know, darling, pets and children don't always mix well. A guest once confided in me that her child, in a fit of jealousy, placed their pet in the microwave just to get her attention.
I suppose there ain't no way to avoid these sorts of things from happening, is there?
<... It seems this horror story takes the idea of "hell is other people" and extends it to include pets.>
The puppy does not understand why you are trying to scare it.
Easy ... Quiet ...
What the hell are you doing over there?
N-Nothing! I just ... I saw you, ma'am, and ... I suppose ... it's just an old habit ...
I-I didn't steal anything! I'm just ... a little nervous, that's all ...
Ain't no need to fret, missy. We ain't living in those days where they'd string ya up for just lookin' the wrong way.
Ain't nobody around here gonna mess with you, and I can tell you ain't done nothin' wrong.
Y-Yes, that's right ... but ... please, allow me to stay away ...
Your gun ... it ... it makes my heart race with fear ...
Mr. Nick Bottom, I'm so glad you agreed to my interview request. Thank you!
No need for thanks! When I'm on stage, the spotlight never fazes me.
Now, there might've been a hint of a personal motive behind me scheduling this interview ...
So, if you don't mind me asking—what's it like to have a donkey's head?
It's brilliant! Vegetables taste more delicious than ever before, I'm always full of energy, and my mood's all the better for it!
What matters most is, with this mask on, she might still remember me from that day.
Mask?
Right, a mask just as lifelike as yours.
Hey! Poltergeist!
I-I don't have any spare change! Please leave me alone!
What are you talking about?
I was thinking of calling up Mesmer Jr. and Marcus to play a game of Perudo. You should join us.
I-I don't think so ... I'm not the best at games like that ...
Don't worry, it's easy. I'll show you how to play!
Can you at least ... give me some time to prepare ...?
I need to put on a new sheet, see if the snacks are still good ... and ... I need to mentally prepare myself for all this ...
So ... you go wherever you want, with people flocking to you and showering you with love and attention, and you don't even have to worry about being hunted down?
Maybe you could share your secret with me? That way, I won't have to starve.
Most people are wolves in sheep's clothing. They're all very dangerous, but it's simple enough getting through it all.
The first step is to play innocent, act weak, and get them to drop their guard.
Do I truly have to? I've done enough of that in my time ... Any other tips?
In that case ... just share your secrets with them, no matter how insignificant or grand. In exchange, take theirs, and make them forget yours.
Well, my master already destroyed my secret ... I don't need to beg for a contract anymore.
Well, it looks like you've got the hang of it, anyway.
What do you mean?
Nothing—just keep being yourself.
Sometimes, you just have to accept the fact that age catches up with you. Like recently, whenever it rains, my back and waist start acting up.
Regular care is the key to avoid rusting away. Someone makes sure to oil himself regularly, and that is why, even without legs, he is still quick on his feet. Ha-ha.
Hmm, guess I'm overdue for an oiling too ... Any recommendations?
Verily, to preserve a joyful heart is the most noble of self-maintenance practices. Pray, do you understand why one should heed the advice of the porcupine?
It is because they are always sharp and to the point.
*the delayed laughter of sudden realization*
*the satisfied laughter of having told a good joke*
So, that bottle of yours can just resize whatever's inside it?
So ... what you're telling me is that it's holding way more water than it looks?
Aye, the water in here's enough to float a proper ship, lass.
If I were you, I'd just fill that bottle with vodka.
Once, I just poured rum in here, and by thunder, it nearly had me capsized for good.
I took to mixing my rum with water after that. Rum's a fine thing, but overindulgence will have you sailing straight into a storm.
That's a shame. I just thought I'd found the perfect drinking buddy.
Well, who do we have here? I never thought I'd see the sacred flame of Uluru outside the stadium.
My, Charlotte, it's been a while, hasn't it? You've grown so much.
You still remember me? How flattering.
I have a good memory—children are always counting on me as a source of wisdom. Not to mention the fact that you're the youngest Floor Ritual champion in history.
Hah! And being the first disabled athlete makes me all the more memorable, doesn't it?
Disabled? Oh no, my child. The Uluru Games are for everyone.
It doesn't matter if you have four legs, three, or only one. Look at me—no legs whatsoever.
You look just like a little version of Mr. Fog.
I suppose calling me "Little Fog" wouldn't be entirely unwarranted ... Do you know my father?
I lent Mr. Fog a hand with his work—probably the most important work I've done, alongside wakin' folks up, that is.
What's wrong? You sound like you got a right bad toothache! Reckon you do? I could have a word with Ms. Tooth Fairy for you, she's brilliant at sortin' out tooth troubles.
No, I'm simply lamenting ... lamenting the fact that even a girl of your age must already concern herself with work.
*sigh* ... I'd wager the conscience of London's government was buried by coal ash long ago.
Mr. Brimley! Thanks a million for helping us with the journos last time!
A mere trifle, miss—hardly more effort than a quick flick of the brim.
Yay! I guess that makes us friends now, eh? Let's shake hands!
... This isn't very ranger-like of me, but I think I'll have to decline on this occasion ...
Oh, right, you have no hands! No worries, I'll go for your coat, or maybe the brim of your hat! You wouldn't get offended, would you?
Taking offense isn't the problem here ... It's just that, if I shook your hand, I could end up catching fire, and I'd prefer to avoid that, being as flammable as I am.
Reflecting what's around us won't help us learn the truth. We must cast our gaze further into the distance.
I couldn't agree more. It's important that we listen closely and broadcast voices from beyond.
Just as the speed of radio waves aligns with that of light, I believe we'll have many more topics to discuss.
By the way, Ms. Radio.
Yes?
Did you arrange for someone to give you a dusting today? I wonder if I could share that service ...?
Your Honor! My esteemed judge!
Should someone owe me coin, hindering my timely payment of the king's taxes, would you defend me, or would you side with our esteemed sovereign?
I shall ensure the debtor repays what they owe you in line with the law, then see to it that you pay your taxes as the law demands.
Ah, but what if he claims that if he pays me back, he won't have the coin to pay the sovereign's tax in due time? What shall we do then, Your Honor?
Let the sovereign wait.
Esteemed elfin, I offer you this coin—grant me the power to achieve world peace on my own terms.
If I could do that, I'd have made world peace happen all by myself by now! And do you really think world peace can be bought with just a coin?
Not just that! Are you planning to fix the world yourself, or are you hoping a wish can do it for you?!
S-Sorry, I guess I was just trying vent and let all that frustration out ...
The Flaming Boxer, The Ice Cream Debate, The Suitcase's Magical Voyage, The Warden's Childish Game ...
So many photos ... are you sure you want me to have them?
I capture these moments and share them with those who can't see such things with their own eyes ... people like you.
Thank you so much! I'll cherish these photos forever!
E-Excuse me, hello?
Aloha! Konnichiwa! Finally got a chance to use that nifty greeting I learned! Hah! What's on your mind, miss?
Oh ... You are from Hawaii, yes? I have always been interested in Hawaii ...
Glad to hear that! Hawaii is an amazing place—sunshine, beaches, and plenty of coconuts! You're always welcome to drop by!
But I don't have any family there, so I'm not sure if I can ...
Don't worry! We're all family—ohana! When you come, I'll show you around!
That sounds wonderful! I will send my photos over before I go! I wonder coffee shops are like in Hawaii ...?
Little lamb!
Oh, hello? Were you calling me just now?
Shh. Come over here, quick.
You must always be wary of wolves—they could be lurking in the shadows.
I appreciate your concern, but surely we must be safe here in the Wilderness, right?
Never let your guard down. One must stay alert.
You're really worked up about this. How about a piece of candy to help you relax? It's got a refreshing mint flavor.
... Okay.
Hello, Ms. Sonetto!
*suddenly stands upright* H-Hello.
Come play with us!
*slowly backing away* Forgive me, but I'm still on mission ...
It's alright, Lisa/Louise are good girls. We can wait for you.
After that, we can play forever, and ever, and ever ...
And ever!
I'm sorry, but I have to leave right now! *hurrying away*
You live on the other side of the screen?! How's that even possible?
Honestly, I'm just as mystified. This is my biggest secret, and it's still a mystery to me too.
That's incredible! Talk about being camera-ready, twenty-four-seven! Besides, you are hands down the most photogenic person I know!
I wish I could be more like you ...
Cheer up! From my perspective, you're the one living on the other side of the silver screen!
It's funny, isn't it? Our whole lives more or less revolve around being crammed into a tiny screen!
You've got the look of a real cowgirl about you—one fit to ride even my saddle!
Consider yourself lucky—not just anyone gets to ride the mighty king of wooden steeds!
Think I'll pass. Thanks anyway.
Why not? What's the matter? Don't you have confidence in your riding skills?
Hopping on you? I reckon that would make me seem a mite immature, don't you think?
So, what does the DUU-DUU-BELL-BOO eat once it's left the atmosphere?
Uhm ... Err ... I think ... if I remember correctly ... it's either grass or ... wait, no, wheat?
Grass in space? I didn't see any of that when I was up there.
You've been up in space?!
I ... W-What I meant was, I never saw anything like that in any of the documents!
I see ... well, a-actually, it's because they, uh, ruminate—yeah, you know, they chew their food again!
Sometimes, they'll touch down, eat way more than their body weight in wheat, and then zoom off again!
And that's where crop circles come from!
Good morning.
Indeed, the wind blows softly today, a most auspicious time to spread one's wings.
After this brief interaction, I am even more convinced of your literary prowess. I shall leave you to your peace for now, and return at another time.
"зима"
Chirp!
You're the one in charge of handling inheritances, huh?
That's me. Are there any "future matters" that require my attention?
Nothing too serious, just need a small favor.
If I kick the bucket before my pals, be sure to hand my stuff over to them.
What kind of "stuff" are we talking about?
I've got a whole stash of ice cream hidden in the freezer under the bed.
That's right.
Do you think I'm a witch?
I skipped whenever I could.
School's really boring.
Darley Clatter?
J?
How about me?
We all die someday.
I'm not ready to die just yet.
(Just act like you don't care).
Bad weather can make people nostalgic too.
All I can remember is the bad weather.

The path upward is blocked with a red marker. You'll have to take the path to the east. Drag Flutterpage along grid lines to move around.
There's a gray marker on the eastern path, signaling that it needs to be lit. Send your little bird to the lamp to <color=#cc492f>light the way forward</color>.
The little bird will stay on the streetlamp for a while. You'll have to <color=#cc492f>approach and retrieve it</color> before you can use it again.

We need to <color=#cc492f>check every landmark</color> to find your name, except for the streetlamps—you only need to visit those if you want to retrieve your little bird. Again, drag Flutterpage along grid lines to move around.
Looks like there's a bunch of paths that need illumination. We'll have to use our little bird to light them up, one at a time.

You can now access <color=#cc492f>Reveries in the Rain</color>, a system where you descend deeper into a sea of knowledge instead of climbing upward like in a traditional tower-climb.
This place is filled with forgotten knowledge and wisdom. Ideas from different eras and people intertwine here, some lost to the passage of time while others are yet to take form.

<color=#cc492f>Reveries in the Rain</color> is one of the gateways to the remnants of consciousness. Those seeking knowledge are drawn here through dreams, fantasies, hallucinations, and psychological struggles to gain insight on the secrets of arcanum and the mysteries of life.
Tap here to dive into the <color=#cc492f>Depths of Myth</color> and discover fascinating and innovative perspectives.
The boundless sea of myths churns, flooding the minds of the explorers with intriguing concepts. The further they delve, the more tempting ideas draw them in ...

Depths of Myth is divided into multiple large zones, each of which is further divided into stages. <color=#cc492f>Every 10 meters of depth marks a new stage within the zone</color>, and the deeper you dive, the greater the rewards.
Now that you're more familiar with this place, you should be able to uncover its secrets at a faster pace.
With the help of Trance, obtaining <color=#cc492f>Seeds of Inspiration</color> and <color=#cc492f>Sprouts of Fantasy</color> becomes a much easier task.
Descending to various stage milestones in the Depths of Myth will provide you with even better <color=#cc492f>Trance Rewards</color>.

Overthinking can be mentally exhausting, and your brain needs a break from time to time. Up to 4 <color=#cc492f>Trance chances</color> are replenished each week, and a maximum of 8 chances can be stored.

A new feature, Myth Manifests, is now available. These are powerful boss companions that can be summoned to fight alongside you in battle. They can act on their own and cannot be damaged or be affected by statuses.
Head to the <color=#cc492f>Isle of Echoes</color> to see the Myth Manifests, which are manifestations of all kinds of emotions that we must face, control, and use to our advantage.
This here is an overview of the <color=#cc492f>Myth Manifests</color> available in the current rotation. Some Myth Manifests are rotated out periodically, making room for new ones to interact with.

You can tap on "Advance" here and <color=#cc492f>defeat the first trial of each Myth Manifest to unlock them for you to use</color>. Each subsequent "Advance" trial you win here will level up your Myth Manifest and make it stronger in battle.

As you continue to win trials via the "Advance" option and <color=#cc492f>level up</color> your Myth Manifest, you will earn <color=#cc492f>Mind Map Fragments</color>. These fragments act as talent points that you can assign on the Mind Map as you see fit.
To get to the next zone, you must first traverse through a Transition Zone. Here, thoughts merge and blend together, creating dangerous undercurrents and eddies that can throw you off course.
Dive through the Transition Zone and defeat its trials to move on to <color=#cc492f>deeper depths</color>.

Each Transition Zone has <color=#cc492f>multiple trial battles</color> for you to overcome. Characters and Myth Manifests deployed in a completed trial battle are considered locked-in, suffer a <color=#cc492f>Disrupted</color> status during selection, and cannot be used for any other remaining challenges in the Transition Zone. Be strategic with your team choices!

Drifting on the currents of thought, the <color=#cc492f>Voyages of Volatility</color> manifest as fleeting vessels, constantly appearing and disappearing. Seize these passing ideas before they fade into the vast sea of consciousness.
<color=#cc492f>Voyages of Volatility</color> is now available, a system that offers challenging battles on a rotating schedule.

"Euphoria" is available for this character, a system that provides power boosts to earlier version characters. The following tutorial boxes will try to include some extra details, feel free to screenshot them for easy reference.
First, we need to unlock this character's "Incantation Cadence" just once, which is essentially a stat boost system with a Rank Up at every five Level Ups.
Each character can have one or multiple Epiphanies, and each Epiphany must be awakened once to unlock it. Tap the center to go awaken this character's Epiphanies.

An Epiphany requires materials to awaken, and is a collection of skill effects that boost the character's power. Most characters have only one Epiphany, but for those with multiple Epiphanies, the Epiphanies are displayed across different panels.
After awakening and equipping an Epiphany, the character gains a variety of enhancements to their skills.
Every time the character's Incantation Cadence gets a Rank Up after five Level Ups, the character's Epiphany becomes stronger, unlocking an additional skill effect.
Welcome to the Puppet Arena, where everyone can safely experience the ancient Uluru dueling games with puppet fighters and imitation artefacts.
Throughout the event, a variety of <color=#cc492f>rosters will be provided on a rotating basis</color>. Here are some of the new units introduced in this rotation.

The Puppet Arena refreshes its roster every <color=#cc492f>two weeks</color>, rotating in new combinations of <color=#cc492f>characters</color>, <color=#cc492f>artefacts</color>, and <color=#cc492f>arena modifiers</color> <color=#cc492f>for a period of time</color>.
In the Preparation Zone, you'll find <color=#cc492f>3 random lineups</color> to choose from when starting out. Pick one to be your starting roster.
In the Puppet Arena, you can form up to <color=#cc492f>3 teams</color>. The second and third teams will <color=#cc492f>unlock as you progress through the matches</color>.
You've added a puppet fighter to your team. Tap on the fighter to see the its details.

During battle, puppets will cast their available Arcane Skills at random. However, if you select <color=#cc492f>Prioritize!</color> for a particular skill, the puppet will focus on that skill during the battle.

You tap on an ally to check the Arcane Skills they're prioritizing. Also, keep in mind that each ally can equip <color=#cc492f>one</color> artefact; note that these imitation artefacts may have different effects compared to other game modes.
In an arena battle, puppets take actions in the order of their assigned slots on their team. In most cases, each puppet has one AP per round.
Your first opponent has been found. Teams with the <color=#cc492f>same number</color> will fight each other. In this case, your Team 01 will face your opponent's Team 01.
You have completed 3 matches. Here are some <color=#cc492f>arena modifiers</color> to choose from. Make sure to pick the one that benefits your teams the most.
After every <color=#cc492f>3 matches</color>, you have the opportunity to select an arena modifier. Pick wisely to help your teams advance in the Puppet Arena.
Tap here to look at all the arena modifiers you've picked so far.

If you're not sure whether one of your teams will beat its opposing team, you can <color=#cc492f>drag and move teams around</color> to change their <color=#cc492f>order of battle</color>. Adjusting your lineup right before combat is essential for success.

If you're confident, you can <color=#cc492f>stake</color> an extra participation chance for <color=#cc492f>more</color> Timeless Timber on a win. However, a loss will immediately cost you <color=#cc492f>2 participation chances</color>. Each participation chance is basically a "life" point—lose them all, and your run is over.

Congratulations on completing 9 matches! Next up is the Path of Peril, where your remaining participation chances will become <color=#cc492f>invalid</color>, and the entire run will <color=#cc492f>end immediately</color> after a single defeat.
Each participation chance is basically a "life" point—lose them all, and your run is over.
In Path of Peril, you can choose to stake the Puppet Hearts you've earned this run. For each match you win, your stake will be <color=#cc492f>doubled</color>.
However, if you lose, <color=#cc492f>you won't get any of your staked Puppet Hearts back</color>.
The Tiring Room is now open, where you can exchange Timeless Timber for various supplies. As the matches progress, the rarity of available supplies will <color=#cc492f>gradually increase</color>.
If the offered supplies don't meet your needs, you can <color=#cc492f>refresh</color> the stock for a small amount of Timeless Timber.
Here are the Timeless Timber and Puppet Hearts you've earned this run.
Timeless Timber is a currency that can be exchanged for a variety of supplies in the Puppet Arena.
Puppet Hearts are a testament to your battles in the arena. You can exchange them for various items at the <color=#cc492f>Heart Salvage</color>.

Once you're done with buying supplies, you can go back to tweaking your teams. Before heading into battle, simply tap the cart icon in the bottom left corner to <color=#cc492f>return at any time</color>.

Fly! Before it falls, catch the answer in your hand.

Smog and Pea Soup
"The Fog and Its Visitors"

During a certain period in history, the term "Big Smoke" became a "celebrated" moniker for London, drawing some curious travelers to its streets. However, from the 17th century to some time later, the essence of a visitor's experience in London hadn't changed much. Especially for those who chose to visit in winter, the dense fog often obscured the city's sights. By the 19th century, however, this fog had become an integral part of London's "charm," so much so that some curious visitors would feel their trip incomplete without a glimpse of the dense—and not always white—mist.

The shift in public perception, where disappointment gave way to "pleasant surprise" under the same foggy veil, was an intriguing one. This change was fueled, in no small part, by art: painters flocked to the city in winter to capture the fog-laden Thames, and novelists used the mysterious haze as the stage for detective dramas. As these works gained popularity, people naturally embraced the combination of fog, water, and the ancient cityscape, viewing the smog as an essential element of London's appeal.

For London residents, however, the smog was anything but romantic. This mix of stagnant water vapor and industrial pollutants became known as "pea soup" in the 19th century. Anyone breathing the air could tell that the name was far from complimentary. Yet, this wasn't enough to raise significant alarm—pollution alone wasn't enough to halt the relentless march of industrialization. It wasn't until London, the great coal-burning engine, was brought to a standstill by the Great Smog of 1952, choking the city for five days, that effective legislation began to take shape.

...

Today, as the "Storm" seems to hurl the world backward in time, I've had the privilege—or misfortune—to witness a yellow fog as thick as pea soup with my own eyes. It hovers among towering smokestacks, its texture, stench, and the reflexive gasp I stifled upon opening my window all testify to its harm. I recall reading a poet's description of it: "Like a secret something that adds beauty to everything."

What a strange, yet profoundly poetic, form of praise!

Now, before setting out on my field mission, I must hurry to claim a high-filtration mask—surely the only thing capable of making my journey remotely pleasant. Considering the absurd traffic accidents that occur in such fog, I might also need to fashion a reflective vest. A soft disk enchanted with an illumination arcane skill should also suffice. However, to penetrate this fog, the incantation will have to be exceptional in its potency.

I have no doubt that one or two researchers would eagerly pursue the challenge of developing such a device. Knowing them as I do, I'd bet all my personal files that were lost in the "Storm" on it, ha.
Sacred Flame Standardization
"Evolution of Uluru Traditions in the 20th Century"
Appendix: Character Research

"Standardization is a necessary process for sustainable development."

Though the chief overseer of the Foundation's Uluru Committee has never engraved this phrase onto her sleek walnut desk, anyone who has interacted with her knows it is her guiding principle.

With her approval, her assistant provided me with extensive materials. Since the Foundation officially took charge of the Uluru Games, this assistant has been by her side, driving and witnessing a series of transformative innovations.

"Without a doubt, for the wider Arcanist community, the Uluru Games are a glorious and ancient tradition. From bedtime stories for children to street games and even professional pursuits, they originate from Uluru, revolve around Uluru, and ultimately nurture Uluru in return. Fueled by people's spontaneous enthusiasm, the games have thrived to this day. Yet, the overseer was among the first to recognize the potential risks threatening its legacy."

The assistant recounted their initial encounter with the overseer: "In my youth, I witnessed a young participant nearly lose their life due to lack of safety regulations. I gathered similar cases and called for attention to fairness and safety in the games—and soon received a response: an invitation from the overseer to work together. I still remember her words during our first meeting: 'Competitive sports should be the seed of peace, not the breeding ground for danger'."

"It was only after working with her that I realized a standardized arena was merely the first step toward a renewed Uluru Games. Surely you remember the uproar when high-risk events were suspended for the first time? Critics lambasted the decision as destructive to Uluru's traditions. But amidst the storm of public opinion, the overseer remained steadfast, believing that only by ensuring the athletes' safety could the Uluru flame burn on.

"Please understand, the overseer has no intention of letting these traditional events disappear. Over recent years, several events have been reinstated with revised rules, and others are being revitalized with a combination of modern science and arcanum, transitioning into entertainment formats to preserve them. Our first experimental project, the Puppet Arena, was recently launched, and we eagerly await everyone's feedback."

At the end of our conversation, the assistant whispered, "She might appear stern and lacking in passion, but the overseer harbors a deeply held wish: that one day, 'arcanum will become a source of joy for all Arcanists'."
Secrets of the Stadium
"The Witch's Silhouette: Dances, Rituals, and More"

Dance is a ritual form understood by most Arcanists and even humankind at large. However, opinions differ on the source of its arcane power: "Anyone with a witch's lineage is born with it." "They use some ancestral salve, like a flying ointment." "Invisible demons guide them." "Surely they were kidnapped by fairies as children! My mother swears that's the story of every witch she's ever met."

To unravel this mystery, I joined the "Source" Arcanum Research Expedition and visited the hometown of Ms. Charlotte O'Hagan.

Surprisingly, the area still retains an Iron Age charm and simplicity. Fairies are openly visible and interact with humans, enlisting their help to build homes, wage battles, or play card games. In return, they offer magical treasures or sage advice. "We don't mind sharing our roof with mister spirit over there," said one family. "He knows how to keep meat fresh, so our herring always sells best on the street."

When asked about ritual dances, locals guided us to a clearing with massive stones arranged in a circular formation, complete with standing pillars and lintels—nearly identical to the setup in Ms. O'Hagan's training hall. "Usually, it happens on May Day or at the start of winter. Everyone holds ribbons or short sticks and dances in circles around the stones. Gradually, the numbers grow, but you can't tell who has joined—fairies and sprites like to disguise themselves and mingle!" One guide demonstrated some steps, claiming they were "taught to my great-great-grandfather by a fairy." Interestingly, parts of the dance mirrored Ms. O'Hagan's movements. However, all it did was attract a flock of birds.

Another villager shared a more modern adaptation: "Nowadays, most villages prefer to light two bonfires in the square. If you want protection, walk between them—the smoke and flames will ward off evil. For good fortune, you need to dance around them. Remember, clockwise only! Mischievous fairies might try to confuse you!"

...

At the end of our investigation, we sought Ms. O'Hagan's personal view on such floor rituals. Her response was succinct: "I have no stories to tell."

Cross Street Sightseers
"A Creased Letter Stained with Ash"

Dear Lily,

I'm sorry I haven't written to you in the past two weeks. The opening of the Uluru Fair has kept our family even busier than we expected. Athletes and tourists are everywhere now, filling Cross Street with a cacophony of accents. Aunt Martha says even pickpockets would be overwhelmed by the chaos here.

With the preliminaries officially underway, the shop will surely leave me with no free time at all. But I haven't forgotten our promise, and I'm sending you a local's guidebook to ensure you have a wonderful time at the fair—keep this letter with you, and you'll enjoy it to the fullest!

First, avoid vendors claiming they're officially registered with the fair's report list. This is a new fair for Uluru, and any claim of registration is bound to be false.

Second, always bring an umbrella in London, unless the Floor Ritual events manage to conjure up some rare sunshine. If you forget, look for Bernard's umbrella shop, near the florist with the antler decorations at the street corner. But here's the trick—look across from it! Down the alley, there's another umbrella shop. The prices differ by five fold, but the products are identical. In fact, both shops have the same owner!

When you reach Cross Street, you must try the "Fortune-Telling Ice Cream." The man's cart may not be the newest or most eye-catching, but wherever the Orbuculum on its handle goes, it draws a crowd. For just 2 extra pence, the vendor will predict your favorite flavor. If he gets it wrong, you'll get a free ice cream. It's the best deal ever! Too bad I've never managed to get a free one—he must either be a fortune-telling master or an ice cream genius, because I love every flavor he picks!

You mentioned wanting to buy a tea set in London. The porcelain shops on Cross Street aren't anything special, but I recommend a shop east of the square. Its sign reads "Herbal Specialties," but inside, it's filled with consigned tea sets. Mrs. Winston, a connoisseur of elegant tea sets, would surely be delighted to help you find a unique one.

Mom's calling for help, but I have to finish with this—Mom and I have reserved a great spot for you at the restaurant, complete with a bouquet. Guess what kind of flowers they are! I've also prepared mashed potatoes, pudding, and fish and chips for you. I can't wait for your arrival!

With love,

Monica

The long-extinguished sacred flame has once again been kindled in the ancient arena of the Uluru Games, bringing Australia's stories to a close. Mrs. Vincent's Afternoon Tea

I heard that Mr. Antonio has recently become enamored with a cruise ship orchestra—how curious. Oh, he's not some romantic artist, nor does he have a collection of fine treasures at home. He's an accountant—yes, the accountant for La Vie Française—a cautious, even slightly old-fashioned gentleman. Neither he nor his wife are particularly knowledgeable about music, and they seldom attend concerts.

Mr. Antonio gets seasick! He made quite a spectacle of himself on the ship ... Yes, he certainly lost his gentlemanly composure there, the orchestra on board completely captivated him. It was an exceptionally unique orchestra with a truly extraordinary musician ... That's how Mr. Antonio described it, darling. Hard to believe, isn't it? Who knows, maybe his seasickness was making him hallucinate?

In any case, Mr. and Mrs. Antonio have set sail again, on the "Dream Expedition." And Rusty's come back, hasn't he? That's a good boy, Rusty.
Days and Nights at Sea

The nights on deck are eerily quiet. Once the orchestra retires for the night, only the sea breeze, the melting ice, and the dizziness remain.

To endure such unbearable discomfort for the sake of these performances—this is not something he would have done in the past. On sleepless nights, with the wind howling across the deck, the preparations before the voyage now seemed trivial. He had practiced balancing on a waterbed, simulating the ship's motion, but never imagined he would still lose his balance on an actual ship.

He waits for the sunrise, for the final performance, for the return journey. Then, the days ashore will come—sitting in an office, counting coins that aren't his, staring at a life so predictable it seems to stretch to infinity.

The delayed sunrise at sea stirs unease, along with a faint curiosity—what would it be like if it delayed further, or if eternal darkness took its place?

Thankfully, the sun eventually rises.

I think it's better we part ways now. If we stand here hugging for too long, we might end up drawing a crowd.
Miss Barcarola, I'm sorry, but I'm afraid I can't allow this lady to board the ship.

Barcarola
All our guests have paid for their trip in full, and their professions and reasons for boarding fully comply with the ship's regulations.
Not everyone's profession meets the regulations. Let's take a look at Miss Regulus's self-introduction.
"An alchemist scholar from the renowned research institute, Laplace!"
"A true heir to the spirit of rock!"
And, "A pirate who once dominated all the radio frequencies along the River Thames!"

Miss Barcarola, you might not know this, but back in the '60s, there was a pirate rocker who went by the very same name. She broadcasted illegally on the Thames, took pleasure in antagonizing legal broadcasters and record labels, and was eventually shut down by the government.
Although the UK government's warrant against this pirate has been lifted, if this is the same person, inviting her aboard could affect the good reputation of the "Free Breeze."
I've met Miss Regulus myself, and there's no way she's the same person. She's far too young to have lived through the '60s.
She could be a copycat. What if she mimics her idol's outrageous actions on the high seas?
She wouldn't do such a thing!
I'm surprised you'd be so quick to defend her. Don't you know that those pirate rockers made a mockery of true musicians like you? Why are you standing up for her?
I've witnessed her passion for music firsthand, she's not mocking anyone. I'm not sure why she chose that name, but that's no reason to judge her so prematurely.
If you're still worried, Captain, I promise to keep an eye on her. I'll make sure she doesn't get up to any mischief in the broadcast room—or anything else you're concerned about.
If she does something that harms the good name of "Free Breeze," then you may throw me overboard along with her and my Crackling Box!

And there's no need to worry about the broadcast room, I'm sure it'll be just fine.

Let me guess—it's got stringent activation conditions, experimental results that are near impossible to replicate, and an unconventional method of operation?
Once activated, it detects environmental changes through gnosis, emitting screams at varying decibel levels to indicate different supernatural phenomena.

Our understanding of the "Storm" is still quite shallow.

Institutum Lorentz is offering a new perspective: the "Storm" is not a phenomenon, but the ebb and flow of chaotic, variable energy. Their concept of "pneuma" is indeed an appropriate way to understand it.
