Before the third, sixth, and seventh "Storms," Lorentz Butterfly predicted several potential "Storm Eye" locations, which emerged just as foretold.

With the assistance from the Field Agent Administration, I confirmed the status of the indicated areas. Although they didn't perfectly match the core regions of the "Storm," those coordinates did correspond to concurrent supernatural phenomena.
As researchers, we must recognize the value of building upon the work of those who came before us.
Yes, but for researchers, "didn't perfectly match" and "concurrent" don't constitute convincing enough reports.
If you want the data, the p-value is as low as 0.012, which means there's a significant correlation. The inputs and results can be verified, so the findings are reliable.
Oh, that's just great, fantastic.
Soon enough, the entire Institutum Lorentz will know—our IQ is reversing faster than time itself.
So much wood! Now we can finally fix Grandma Penu's roof, and she won't have to use clay pots to catch the rain anymore.
And Uncle Tarek's window—someone smashed it with a ball last time, and he complained so much he nearly threw his back out!
It was Kamuta! He's just too strong!
Ahem, Toa, let's go fix the houses together.
We could also make a nice chair as an apology to Uncle Tarek.
The coastline of Miti has shifted again; the waves are getting closer to our island.
If this continues, those of us living by the coast will have to think about moving.
Building new homes will take time, so we need to come up with solutions beforehand.
We could pile rocks and sand to build a breakwater; if the waves come in, it will give the people nearby time to react.
We can also place markers to remind them of the position of the high tide ... What's wrong, brother?
Nothing, just noticing the serious look on our young Nukutai chieftain's face. I'm wondering how she manages to be so smart and reliable all at once.
Well, now this smart and reliable chieftain has some orders. Kamuta, we need to act quickly!
Understood!
The warehouse has grown, but why not make it even bigger? We still have so much wood left.
If we made it a little larger, we could store enough berries and fish for years, and we'd only need to gather them every so often. That way, we'd save so much time for festivities!
You silly, fish and berries will spoil; you can't store them for that long.
I heard from the merchant ship that came last year that they have something called an "ice box" that keeps fish fresh for a long time. That's why they buy so much fish every time they come!
That sounds amazing! Maybe we could make one of those boxes too, but what exactly is "ice"?
I know this one! The elders said "ice" is a hard and cold form of water, slightly wet to the touch, and as solid as a rock!
Toa, you must have heard wrong. Water doesn't have a shape; how can it be as solid as a rock?
The elders really said that, you have to believe me!
Toa, guess what this is.
Um, a pit? A hole? Are we going to build an underground shelter?
This is my idea of how we can keep fish fresh for a long time without using "ice." If we don't want to stare at dead fish every day ...
We can bring in seawater to fill a pond and temporarily keep some fish in it. You know how interested the outsiders are in our fish.
But the sea is so big, and this pit is so small. It won't hold many fish, plus where are we going to find the small fish and shrimp to feed them?
Hmm... I was just going to discuss the details with my brother. We need to talk this over more carefully!
So, what do we do with this pit? Should we fill it back in?
How about we fill it with water? That way, we'll have somewhere to swim where we don't have to worry about the tides!
Fatutu, more oil has drifted over to Malaga. We've repaired the ship and are getting ready to clean up the oil.
The sea has gotten so dirty, and the beach now looks gray and dull.
Selone! Take this. I've infused these shells with arcane powers. String them together and surround Malaga with them ... this way, the oil will disperse.
You're amazing, Fatutu!
We had a great harvest in Vaipuna; our food reserves have nearly doubled.
But since we still haven't figured out how to get "ice," this food might not last till next year. I need to come up with more solutions ...
Fatutu, you've missed the simplest solution.
What is it?
We could throw a bonfire party tonight. After all, the best place to store food is in our stomachs.
Oh, right! We can cut the hala fruit into small pieces and roast them inside the fish. What do you think, brother? You're the best cook we've got!
Maybe we could try some new recipes tonight ...
Fatutu, what's this?
We've gathered so much wood this time! We've repaired the houses and chairs, and there's still some left, so I carved this giant wooden sand crab!
Shh, it's a surprise for my brother. He's been so busy; he needs something to help him relax ...
He's coming. Hide, hurry!
Many people will come for this trade season; we should send a few boats to guide them. As for the goods they need ...
We already have everything prepared! New warehouses, seawater ponds, and we've even repaired and repainted our canoes.
I've asked the shells, and they told me this trade season will be successful.
Even without asking the shells, I believe it will be a great success.
We've decorated the atoll with shells, prepared Sea Mother's Eyes for everyone, and marked the way for the guiding ships.
That should help them reach the island safely and return home safely.
The trade season has begun, and the ships have arrived!
What will they bring this time? I hope they have plenty of those food-filled tin cans for trade!
The captain from last time had a wooden box that could play songs. He said he'd bring a new one to trade next time ...
Is a singing box very precious to them? We could trade with them using the compassare talismans.
And the shell necklaces imbued with arcane powers, the protective dulse leaves, and the dried hala fruits!
Aren't you giving away a little too much there?
New warehouses, homes, breakwaters, seawater ponds, freshly painted dugout canoes—
And the repaired goalposts. Nukutaeao may be old, but our home thrives anew.
But I still worry about Miti's rising tides, even though the energy from the shells has become purer, and the trade season is going smoothly.
Don't worry, sister. You've already become a pillar of Nukutaeao, and everyone is proud of you.
Everyone should be proud of themselves. Watching the old houses being fixed up bit by bit, the granaries filling up ... Brother, I feel like I can do so much more for Nukutaeao.
Maybe, but not today. Today, you only need to rest. Come on, let's go home.
Brother said we shouldn't cut down all the trees at once, just like we shouldn't catch too many fish in one go.
We need to give them time to rest and regrow.
Yesterday, we saw a magnificent sunset.
The clouds and the sea seemed to be on fire; such a beautiful sky is a rare sight. I hope to see it again in my dreams ...
I don't want to be too hard on Fatutu, but sometimes ...
I should show her more care. Maybe a gift during the trade season would be a good start.
You know, outsiders don't always bring good things when they come to the island. They often leave behind troublesome clutter ...
But I think it's probably unintentional. Plus, with all the interesting things in those tin cans, its not so bad, really ...
There are evil wizards out there who curse people, making their heads feel fuzzy so they can't recognize their own family ...
You should wear a few molukka around your neck and keep some knitbone and dulse leaves in your pocket. That way, the evil wizards won't dare come near you!
The Nukutais have many arcane skills. We use them to soothe young plants, part the waves, and divert lightning ...

I've heard the outside world has strange arcane skills, and people who can't use any. How do they survive? Surely, there must be some arcane skill that allows them to live without using arcane skills!
We must treat the revelations from the shells with reverence. The energy of the Nukutai flows in harmony with our shells.
We live on the same island and sail on the same boats. The shells guide us in the direction of our lives, but they also need our protection. The Nukutais must hold their oars firmly.
Don't be fooled by Kamuta's appearance. We used to fight a lot when we were kids ...
He isn't that much older than me, so how did he grow so big all of a sudden?
Yesterday in the forest, a really big caterpillar landed on my arm.
It was heavy, squishy, and brightly colored. I wanted to bring it back with me, but my brother disagreed and gently placed it back on the tree trunk.
Our exploration of Vaipuna was a great success. We won't have to worry about supplies for quite a while.
Maybe we can spend an afternoon dyeing fabrics and making new clothes with Toa. I wonder if the juice from the red snappers will dye the fabric red.
Sometimes I wonder if I'm putting too much pressure on her ... After all, I wasn't any better than she is at her age.
Compared to Fatutu, Toa feels more like a child ...
Going out to sea during a storm is very dangerous but absolutely thrilling ... As long as the shells tell us everything will be fine, we'll be okay!
I did it only once ... and it was definitely the last time!
If our house gets damaged, we repair it, so that when the storm comes, it will shelter us.

We gather together, watching raindrops fall and the wind shake the tree leaves ... The storm always passes, the sun returns, and a circular rainbow appears in the sky, reflecting in the sea with our home at its center.
Will it rain or shine tomorrow? Why not ask the Spirit Shell?
I usually don't ask about the weather because I like it to be a surprise ... though sometimes it ends up being a shock.
Lately, it feels like Fatutu can see right through me ...
Is it that I can't hide my emotions? Or should I hide my shells ... No, that would make it too obvious.
I guess we Nukutais aren't very good at hiding things, are we?

Excerpt from "A History of Arcane Ethnicity"

...

Due to the reclusive nature of the Nukutais, our knowledge of this enigmatic people comes only from the sparse accounts of a few trading ships that had contact with them and the legends from neighboring societies.

...

In the folklore of coastal civilizations in the South Pacific, there are often tales of Shell People or Hermit Crab People. These beings, dressed in shells and living in the water, are depicted as otherworldly ocean emissaries or guardians. They offer advice and guidance to the protagonists in these stories or help those lost at sea.

...

With the Age of Exploration, the veil over these mysterious figures was lifted, and a small island named Nukutaeao, known for its production of mystical and esoteric crafts, became a topic of intrigue among adventurers in taverns. Consequently, the intrusion of explorers and trading ships seemed to weary the Nukutais, and records from that period show they gradually vanished from the pages of history. They employed some form of arcane skill to conceal the island's exact location, ensuring their homeland never appeared on any official map.

...

Today, with advancements in maritime technology and increasing global communication, it is only a matter of time before the island of the Nukutais is rediscovered. The author can only hope that this inevitable encounter will not bring undue harm to the Nukutais, wishing that they can integrate into the global community through peaceful and friendly exchanges. May the final chapter of this Age of Exploration conclude with harmony.

Fish Tank Brainstorm

"The topic of this brainstorming session is: How did this 'Pioneer' manage to cross the 'Storm' and continuously send information to the Earth's surface?" The ferrofluid flows freely in his glass tank.

"Is it possible that this is just a prank? Like a cipher game created by one of us, accompanied by fake photos and data ..." An indifferent researcher shrugs.

"Then go and write a detailed report on who you think is pulling the prank, one every week, until someone confesses to being behind it."

"That's an abuse of power!" The researcher, who intended to remain silent, slams the table. "Alright ... I have a thought. The 'Storm' rewinds people into disappearance, but some things that inherently exist longer might not be completely reversed. This 'Pioneer' could be some kind of man-made satellite that regularly sends data, and the 'Storm' rewinds it to an older version, but doesn't affect its operation."

"We've already experienced time periods as far back as the beginning of World War I; no man-made satellite should even exist at the time."

"I've got it! It's aliens! Aliens are crossing the 'Storm' and sending us some kind of signal! It's not surprising at all that they have technology immune to the 'Storm' among their advanced space tech, right?" A researcher with a fanciful imagination raises his hand.

"Damn it, we don't have time to verify baseless hypotheses such as these!"

"The man-made satellite theory might just be a reasonable hypothesis. Maybe the internal structure of the satellite just happened to form a knot-like structure? Many of the satellites launched by Laplace have adopted arcane techniques, theoretically capable of activating the immunity spell." The researcher, feigning seriousness, rests his chin on his hands.

"That's a good direction, but your reasoning is too idealistic. Let's proceed on the premise that there exists a satellite capable of gaining immunity to the 'Storm' and investigate further, regardless of the principle behind all this. Now, everyone, spread out and check every satellite in Laplace's history. If this hypothesis is confirmed, it could be another significant breakthrough in our 'Storm' research."

"Encyclopedia of Nautical Lore—Sea Monster Edition"

Serres Common Names: Pig-toothed Ray, Anchor Fish, Deep Bass Disc, Hammerhead Ray. Back home, we call this thing a Sea Bat. That's not right! Sea Bats are a different species and they definitely don't smash your portholes at night! Classification: Subclass: Aquatic Primal Critter, Order: Oceanic, Family: Ray-form, Genus: Flying Ray. In my opinion, it should be classified as a bird. Distinctive Features: Broad wings, long tail, a pair of clawed fins, and curved ivory-white fangs. Hey, I just thought of a business idea! Could we pass these fangs off as ivory? Serres typically live in groups and feed on large fish, seabirds, and drifting debris. While they may look similar to Olitiau, their behavior couldn't be more different. While Olitiaus are generally non-aggressive, Serres are known for their fondness for challenging creatures larger than themselves—including sperm whales, baleen whales, megalodon sharks, and passing ships. Sometimes, they even mistake protruding rocky outcrops and coral reefs for foes. When a Serres spots a ship, it leaps from the water, attacking the vessel with its sharp wings and calling upon its companions. They seem to have a competitive nature; each Serres strives to soar higher and leave deeper marks on its target. Stay away from the windows. You never know how deep their wings can slice. Despite their large numbers, Serres communicate through a single method: sound. They can produce a wide range of calls within the 10-180Hz frequency range, ideal for underwater communication, and they can sense each other's vibrations through their wing membranes. The best way to deal with Serres is to disrupt their hearing. Shouts, bangs, and music can confuse them, while enough volume can physically irritate their auditory systems, causing them to flee in discomfort. Now that's more like it! My former captain tried using anti-Olitiau measures against them, which is why he's my "former captain."

"We can't allow failure and betrayal to run rampant indefinitely, don't you agree, Ms. Grace?" The shadow of the serpent twists under the light, appearing several times larger than its true form.

"Yes," replies another shadow, trying to lower itself as much as possible.

"You quickly identified that the toy was a contract item used to control the succubus, which is impressive. It also shows you're different from Matheus and possess wisdom befitting an Apostle." The stirring rod clinked against the teacup, producing a melodic sound.

"I am sorry that others fell to Kimberly's betrayal; I did overestimate the potency of the contract item."

"If you'd shown less mercy to that succubus and given her stricter orders, this tragedy might have been averted. Likewise, if you had been more ruthless in Texas, you wouldn't have wasted so much time there and would not have lost the contract item in the chaos. Although, in the end, losing it was Igor and his subordinates' fault, not yours."

"Thank you for your guidance and understanding."

"Steel yourself, merciful little Grace. Showing compassion to a viper only gets you bitten. Remember this in your next mission."

"The Nukutais ... they will present us with their 'Spirit Shells.'"

"Your capabilities are undeniable. I still hold some faith in you." At last, a hot cup of tea is stirred into a cold one, and the serpent's shadow vanishes out the door without even flicking its tongue. "Oh, and I shouldn't need to remind you—any unforeseen events during the mission must be reported, especially anything related to Vertin. This is also according to Their guidance."

"...Yes, it's all for Their return."

Report on the "Free Breeze" Incident

According to the Timekeeper's statement provided to our personnel, the recent hijacking of the "Free Breeze" was orchestrated by Ms. Grace, a member of Manus Vindictae. Her involvement included the abduction of the Nukutais and persuading passengers to wear Manus Vindictae masks. Considering this, an upgrade in our risk assessment for Ms. Grace may be necessary, along with issuing a formal warrant for her arrest.

Additionally, with assistance from Regulus, a member of the Timekeeper's team, Researcher Ulrich of Laplace was able to complete his 'Artificial Storm' experiment on the "Free Breeze". Regulus's record was identified as an immune material, however its overall efficacy is weak, providing only a minor delay in the onset of Era Sickness, and critically lacks reproducibility; none of the copies of the records show the same level of efficacy. Regulus attributes this to her record's 'unique rock spirit,' claiming it possesses a soul that its imitations lack, this claim has not yet been rigorously assessed.

"Cruise's Sweetheart"

An outfit prepared for female musicians of the "Free Breeze" crew. Due to the outstanding solo performance of the interviewee, the crew prepared her a unique uniform befitting her role as the ship's music star.
"Crackling Box"

A composite instrument combining features of the violin, flute, euphonium, and other instruments through the "Astrictus" incantation. Known as "a most captivating gadget," "the eternal pearl of the 'Free Breeze'," and "the maestro of music" ... the interviewee used it for solos and gained numerous accolades.
It is rumored that this incantation originated from a renowned luthier family in Cremona, the birthplace of the violin. This background sheds light on the performer's extraordinary musical talents.
"Free Breeze" Hair Ornament

A souvenir in the shape of a ship's wheel, accentuated by silk ribbons in oceanic colors, given to every guest boarding the "Free Breeze."
The rules state that crew members should not ordinarily purchase or wear items intended for passengers. However, as part of a promotional stunt, the previous captain gifted this special item to the interviewee, in recognition of her role in the ship's publicity efforts.
Home, Music, Rebellion

Cremona is a world-famous haven for violins. Every day, its streets are filled with pilgrims who eagerly discuss music theory and gather to perform out of their deep devotion to artistry and craft of the violin.

Yes, the violin can be magnificent—until its sound saturates every day, every place, every room, and every dining table discussion. The child who once adored the violin began to lose her passion, her eyes drifting toward the broader world of musical instruments. However, to parents who were famed luthiers and players, anything else was only a distraction.

The family's arcane skill brought them accolades and opened doors with their innovations. But their rebellious child used that very skill to combine all the instruments she had secretly collected, creating something strange, beautiful and new. With this creation, she boarded a cruise ship bound for destinations unknown. Just like countless other children who ventured far from home, she left without looking back.

To this day, the girl from Cremona who boarded the "Free Breeze" continues to sail across the oceans of the world.

Instruments of the World
(WIP)

Bagpipe Musicians from Scotland define it as a reed aerophone, capable of producing a brilliant and resonant sound by inflating its bag. I think it's perfect for a grand, high-pitched entrance! However, its tone is rather pitched and can easily become monotonous. Irish Tin Whistle A six-holed flute with a fipple mouthpiece, known for its continuous sound that produces rich overtones. Its unique and complex timbre is fascinating. But it suffers from a limited range and volume, leaving it unsuitable for performances on a cruise ship. Euphonium A quintessential low-register instrument! It boasts an impressive lower range, and I adore its deep, mellow tone. Unfortunately, it can't reach higher notes, causing it to occasionally blend into the background during performances. Violin With its wide range and beautiful tone, the violin is a captivating instrument. Its rich variety of sound is delightful to all who hear it—unless, of course, you've been forced to play it since childhood. ...
Continuation of the Past

Barcarola: A talking mouth?! Where did you come from? I'd love to hear your story!
Pandora Wilson: I believe it would be best to keep our interview focused on you, Ms. Barcarola. You're the one that people want to know. 
Pandora Wilson: I was hoping you might share your experiences as a musician on the "Free Breeze."
Barcarola: Oh, right! Of course! Well, it was a wonderful experience. I still think of my time aboard fondly. During the day, I'd spend my time listening to our guests' stories, and if there happened to be a luncheon or tea party, then I would join them as we savored new dishes from around the world together.
Barcarola: And in the evenings, I would perform brand-new compositions based on their requests and experiences of the day, I admit I miss basking in their applause.
Pandora Wilson: That sounds absolutely sublime, what a shame that your ship is gone.
Barcarola: The "Free Breeze" may be gone but I'll never stop performing. In fact, we could even play together!
Pandora Wilson: I'm afraid I'm not much of a musician.
Barcarola: Don't worry, even the sound of a whistle or melodica can become part of a wonderful performance. I'll help you!
Pandora Wilson: I appreciate the encouragement, although I must insist against it.
Barcarola: ... Oh, scusami! I didn't mean to be too forward, I just love sharing music!

Nukutaeao Floral Accessory

Handcrafted accessories made from white hibiscus flowers indigenous to Nukutaeao. The Nukutais utilize a special technique to preserves these flowers, which has made them popular among visitors during their Merchants' Fair.
The flowers symbolize purity, resilience, and eternal life. However, the interviewee seems unaware of this symbolism.

A necklace crafted from various marine shells, each one intricately inscribed with hieroglyphics, except one, the furthest to the left.
The Nukutais consider these shells sacred, wearing them as amulets throughout their entire life. The inscriptions symbolize their emotional journey and most significant moments. Thus, the number and neatness of the inscriptions reflect the wearer's age, experiences, and soul.
Nukutaeao Totem

A mysterious totem inked on the interviewee's arm, which seems to lack deeper significance.
The Nukutais, skilled at living in harmony with nature on their secluded island, use stone powder as paint and their bodies as canvases to create unique designs.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean

The island was sinking.

Few noticed the dotted archipelago drifting in the South Pacific. As the merchant ships sailed away with the final tides before sunset, taking with them tropical fish and Nukutai handicrafts, they left behind an ever-submerging cemetery and a coastline battered repeatedly by storms. Nukutaeao is but a tiny dot in the ocean, a place that might be erased from the map with a swipe of a finger.

Masked figures reached out, stating, "We are born in the wrong era."

The tumultuous waves repeatedly affirmed their foresight. For the first time, those who lived their lives alongside shells argued intensely. The elders, shaking their heads, stubbornly ignored the signs, while the young discreetly covered the cracks in their shells, discussing an era-defining revenge and their planned escape.

The debate stretched until dawn. When the stars faded into the morning light, the new chieftain led what remained of their tribe from the vanishing island onto the "Free Breeze".

She said the Nukutais had no choice left.
The "Horrifying" Truth

"The world outside is filled with hate and war." The shells passed down from our ancestors tell us how frightening the world outside Nukutaeao is. Wicked witches hide in ancient caves, Nakarua serpents often conjure colossal waves on the seas, and roaring monsters and giant birds lurk on every island. Nukutaeao is peaceful and serene, while disputes are ever-present outside. "The outside world is full of cunning, evil people who will hurt others easily." What I've seen on the "Free Breeze" is quite different. People sing and dance, and they're masters of fascinating performances. The brave sit on small boats drifting with the waves, spreading "peace and love." Every night, under the watch of the Southern Cross, the passengers sleep peacefully. They seem no different from us. "We are born in the wrong era." The outside world isn't as bad as we heard, and people aren't as evil as we imagined ... Are these people truly the right targets for our vendetta?
Primal and Civilized

Pandora Wilson: You are certain to be the subject of great curiosity in agreeing to this interview. So little is known about your homeland.
Fatutu: There's a reason for that, the "Veil of Nothingness" cast by our ancestors, it hid Nukutaeao from the outside world.
Pandora Wilson: So, prior to now, you never had any contact with the outside world?
Fatutu: No, we did, our people would periodically welcome traders to our land and invited guests to come and experience our island.
Pandora Wilson: That does make me curious, what kind of goods do you have to trade?
Fatutu: Pickled red snapper, sundried hala fruit ... Oh, and we use a special technique to preserve hibiscus flowers, the accessories we make from them are always very popular.
Pandora Wilson: Considering all that happened, I'm surprised that you seem so positive about the "outside world."
Fatutu: ... We Nukutais have always been hospitable. Even aboard that cruise ship ...
Fatutu: Ah, but I noticed that the guests on that ship seemed to love and yearn for the sea. That's quite different from our people. I wonder why they don't miss their homes and friends?
Pandora Wilson: Perhaps it's because they don't have a home like yours.
Navy Tricorne Hat

A tri-cornered hat with feathers that tremble slightly, as if harboring a mysterious will of its own.
It appeared on an ordinary morning, bringing the interviewee a distant call, an unexpected voyage, and an extended duty.
"Bloom of the End"

A piece of dead coral, heavy on the shoulder, like the fingers and bones of the departed. The interviewee explains that at its core, it is a flower, its life is marked by transformation and sedimentation until it reaches its final form—a bloom that will never wither.
And so, she continues to cherish it, holding it delicately.
"Lifetime"

A fossilized turbo, with distant wind sounds and untold whispers filling its shell.
"It was salvaged from a deep sea trench, murmuring love, regret, and wishes. Until these whispers cease, I shall keep sailing."
"A Fragment of Inspiration"

A thin, transparent piece of silken fabric with a pearly sheen, complementing the colorful glaze of the shells. 
After observing the entire process of customizing a performance gown, the interviewee kept this small remnant, believing it to hold some fleeting inspiration, far too precious to be discarded.
"Touch of the Star"

A silver-plated brooch, reflecting the fabric's hue of the evening dress, shimmering like water ripples in the mist.
Sea stars are flexible and simple creatures that perceive everything through their bodies without relying on eyesight.
Much like the owner of this accessory.

"Blessing of Thetis"
Censer

A handheld censer filled with hot coals and frankincense, provided by Eurybia, the sponsor of the "Midnight Smoke Show." It's used to present incense to the guests.
"It's one of our best brand events from our 'Ocean' series. Through her performance, our fashion philosophy of 'spirituality and self' has been perfectly embodied."
Critter Fur Shawl

A custom fur shawl made primarily from the winter fur of domesticated critters, hand-trimmed and collected by the lady herself. It also incorporates spider silk, synthetic fibers, and ornate feathers left by Dodoughs in the wilderness. No animals or critters were harmed in the manufacturing process.

Pet Accessory
(A pair)

Accessories produced by Ms. NewBabel's Critter Center for formal pet occasions.
Although popular belief holds that the critters' compliance is due to arcane incantations, the designer asserts that the comfortable, lightweight materials and the love in their hearts are what truly make the difference.
Art Nouveau Fishtail Skirt

A cherished evening dress worn by the interviewee on significant occasions. She spent her first earnings on this gown to step onto bigger and further stages. Now, she takes it out of her wardrobe once again.
Red Rain Boots

Red seafarer rain boots issued to the crew of the cruise ship.
Made from PVC with steel-plated soles, they protect the little sailor against punctures and erosion as she rushes across the deck, continuing the hunt in the post-storm sea breeze.
"Umbrella"

A slender shotgun disguised within a meticulously folded umbrella, all in an effort to avoid alarming passengers.
Until the trigger is pulled, few would ever imagine a hunter's silver bullet to fly out instead of an umbrella cover.
Last Resort

Silver bullets specially constructed to be fired underwater.
The interviewee indicates a knot on the carrying strap: "The previous one had been worn while crossing the atoll. Now, it is kept as a memento."
White Parrot Feather

Parrots are often held to be divine messengers, capable of conversing with both humans and gods through their gift of speech. However, the stylist adorned the interviewee with the feathers not as a testament to her skills but to endow this elegant attire with a touch of passion and courage.
Eastern Sandalwood Fan

An imported fan made from sandalwood with ribs carved in Baroque patterns adorned by the thinnest silk, favored by Europeans.
When unfurled, it gently wafts out a delightful fragrance capable of soothing guests, lifting their spirits, and helping them find "peaceful awareness."
"Fluttering Wing"

A brooch of metal and glass, shaped like wings, taken from a dusty box and polished anew.
The hostess of the salon acts like your closest friend while maintaining the perfect distance, much like this brooch, just above the heart, but never piercing the skin.

A month and a half into the Battle of Verdun, an internal meeting was held at the Pax House.
Blonney invited Poltergeist to star in her new film. Timidly, Poltergeist arrived on set, draped in two oversized bedsheets.
To prevent Cristallo's asthma from flaring up, The Fool carefully restrained the hilarity of his every joke.
Fatutu and Leilani engaged in a serious debate over whether to smash the coconut with a stone, or to smash a stone with the coconut.
The Coleman Laboratory published its 13th paper of the year, describing the successful development of a deep-sea pressure protection ritual.
Erick laughed off Tooth Fairy's advice to brush her teeth before bed. A month later, she paid a painful price for it.
Many sought wisdom from 6, but he never gave straightforward answers. Yet, somehow, everyone left feeling as though they had gained invaluable insight.
In celebration of Paul Robeson's birthday, Ol' Man River resonated from at least three places in the suitcase today.
In 1972, the Pax Security Council witnessed the signing of the Biological Weapons Convention.

As an assistant at Laplace, Dora managed a wide range of tasks: coordination, calculations, project management, experimental design ... When surrounded by exceptional geniuses, she became the one to fill in the gaps.
While talking to Eagle about their future dreams, Lopera gave the young scout a hearty pat on the back for encouragement.
Though the grown-ups couldn't stop her, Ezra successfully prevented Balloon Party from launching the suitcase into the sky with a bunch of balloons.
In 1900, the Paris Exposition was held, inspiring the idea of journeying around the globe in hot air balloons.
In 1896, the first modern Olympic Games concluded in Athens, Greece. Meanwhile, registration for that year's Uluru Games began.
In 1788, the French naturalist Georges Buffon passed away, and Laplace respectfully adorned all 36 volumes of Histoire Naturelle in its main hall.

The provocative letter from the Lorentz Butterfly was delivered while Medicine Pocket was on duty, and the whole of Laplace was filled with the letter's distorted cries as it was mangled beyond recognition.
In 1993, the St. Pavlov Foundation's final effort to peacefully resolve the Waco standoff failed.
The Vienna branch of the St. Pavlov Foundation replenished its staff with new permanent additions.
An-an Lee generously treated Twins Sleep to two large bars of milk chocolate, then casually shrugged at Sonetto standing next to them.
In 1816, British novelist Charlotte Brontë was born.
aliEn T cleverly answers Flutterpage's question with a fairy tale from his own world: "Yes, there are 'winds' in outer space—they are greetings from distant stars."
Charlie rehearsed Hamlet in the suitcase, playing the role of Hamlet herself, with Sweetheart as Ophelia and A Knight as, quite literally, a suit of armor.
SPDM completed the third revision of A Brief Introduction to Strategy.
Mondlicht kept a wary distance from some of the unusual-looking arcanists in the suitcase, such as Rabies, Nick Bottom, and ONiON.
Liang Yue tried to tell the suitcase residents that just because you're Chinese, it doesn't automagically mean you know Kung Fu, just look at Madam Z!
Loggerhead hosted a screening of Noire's film Where Shadows Walk in the suitcase. When the lights came back on, Jiu Niangzi was found peacefully asleep in her chair.
37 helped Windsong fine-tune her Ley Calibrator, enhancing the instrument's measurement precision even further.
Mr. Duncan once sought advice from Necrologist on how to arrange for his legacy to be passed on.
Brimley and APPLe jointly graced the cover of a renowned arcanist fashion magazine, praised for their distinctive and attention-grabbing combination.
Medicine Pocket had long obsessed over getting their hands on Semmelweis's blood, convinced that it would reveal answers to the Infected's transformation.
J and Pavia got into a fistfight over something minor. The next day, they drank excessively together and became fast friends.

In 1998, Le Chemin de Sèvres was stolen from the Louvre. The Foundation conducted an extensive investigation using arcanum techniques, only to find that the theft was executed with nothing but a razor. This greatly piqued Melania's interest.

As the headmaster of Zeno Arms Academy read the rules for the mid-term assessment, Lilya couldn't help but burst into laughter. The following year, the updated rules officially prohibited laughter during the headmaster's speeches.
Out of curiosity, Kakania tried to use Door as a medium for her arcane skills. This almost led to the most devastating disaster in the suitcase's history.
Yenisei spent three whole days sorting out the bills sent to Sotheby.
In 1840, Russian composer Pyotr Tchaikovsky was born. Зима greatly enjoys his symphonies.
Ms. Moissan experimented with twenty-four different braided hairstyles on Lorelei while she sang.
Bette played a supporting role in Noire's new film, and her brilliant death scene stole the show.
Under the eager gaze of the children in the suitcase, their eyes sparkling with anticipation, Argus relented and showed off her riding skills on Darley Clatter.

X, fascinated by Sputnik's scientific potential, invited her to join his latest project. However, when the fifth strange gadget X created jumped on one of Sputnik's antennas, she stormed off and filed a complaint to Laplace.
In 1820, Florence Nightingale was born. Known as the "Lady with the Lamp," she is widely revered as the founder of modern nursing.
In 1981, Pope John Paul II was seriously wounded in an assassination attempt.
While riding with Lilya on her broomstick, Click discovered an exhilarating new perspective for photography—from a height of over 10,000 meters.
A laboratory technician position at Laplace was posted, and the institute received over three hundred resumes from doctorate holders in just one day.

Constantine and Lucy's annual chess match ended in a draw, marking Lucy's first draw after losing in the tournament for two consecutive years. The following year, Constantine decided not to participate again.
"Who is the Most Energy-Efficient Awakened in Laplace?" was the topic of intense debate on Laplace's internal forums for an entire week.
In 1804, Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French.
Eternity explains her marketing strategies to Ms. NewBabel, who responds favorably but abruptly ends the conversation with disinterest when Eternity starts promoting her Obedience Microphone.
After tuning Voyager's violin, Barcarola is treated to a rendition of Santa Lucia as a delightful reward.
Claude Smith, Headmaster of Zeno Arms Academy, addresses the new recruits and rallies them for the challenges ahead.
Willow was brought by Ulu to meet the other athletes, but she had to repeatedly interrupt Ulu's praise and introductions.
In 1915, Italy declared war on Austria-Hungary.
John Titor makes a post to celebrate the birthday of the TRADIC.
Kakania and Mercuria engage in a conversation about the idea of "healing," but Kakania struggles to comprehend what Mercuria is conveying.
In 1976, Martin Heidegger passed away on this day, inspiring Pickles and 6 to immerse themselves in a discussion about existentialism.
To help Mesmer Jr. overcome her fear of strange and eccentric arcanists, her colleagues in the suitcase arrange her a meeting with Barbara.
Eternity convinced her client to pay an exorbitant price for her Shoes of Youth, only to have Tennant swindle all of the client's money before the contract could be signed.
In 1953, New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary and his guide, Tenzing Norgay, reached the top of Everest.
X has finished his new invention, the Transoceanic Pigeon Mail Catapult, except it doesn't actually involve pigeons or catapults.
Sophia finally grasped the reasoning behind a theory 37 proposed three months ago.
Shamane gives Avgust some personally made milk candies in exchange for his sunflower seeds.
In 1953, the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II took place on this day, giving Oliver Fog a day off.

The rule "Do NOT press red buttons recklessly" was removed from the Laplace Safety Manual and replaced with "Do NOT designate red buttons as danger buttons! Do NOT designate red buttons as danger buttons!"
La Source loudly declares that she is not a child.
After a series of stringent security checks, Diggers is finally allowed to host an art exhibit in the Wilderness.
In 1799, Russian poet Alexander Pushkin was born.
After hearing the story of White Rum and Captain Anne, Regulus is filled with longing for her ship, APPLe, which is lost to her forever.
Approximately 42% of this year's SPDM graduates were employed at the Foundation headquarters, a figure nearly identical to last year's.
Pioneer accepts an offer to model for a luxury brand, but he disagrees with their jewelry's taste and quality, leading to a heated exchange.
In 1907, the Lumière brothers introduced the Autochrome Lumière, the first color process to be put into commercial production.
In 1903, King Alexander I and Queen Draga of the Kingdom of Serbia were tragically killed in an assassination.
In 1985, Chinese mathematician Hua Luogeng died on this day. 37 has read his An Introduction to Number Theory, and provided proofs related to error terms in her own way.
J and Desert Flannel share their taste in fashion and discover common interests, which shocks Pioneer to no end.
The Laplace Rehabilitation Center increased its fire management budget once again in response to the rising number of accidental explosions.
Mr. Duncan and X invent an underwater bicycle, featuring waterwheels instead of standard wheels.
Bunny Bunny made a Border Collie plushie from Pickles's fur she collected over the months. Pickles does NOT know what to feel about that.
Regulus starts a rule reciting competition between Liang Yue and Sonetto. After an hour of listening to their voices, she falls asleep and slips into a nightmare.
When Baby Blue sees Barbara, she mistakenly believes she still hasn't awakened from her dream.
Tuesday promised room service breakfast to anyone who could withstand her horror story challenge, and so Tuesday's Horror Club was formed yesterday—only to fall apart today.
To shake off the nightmares of their last terror-filled evening, the former members of Tuesday's Horror Club decide to attend a tea party hosted by Sotheby and Satsuki.
Nick Bottom founded a philosophy club with three other members—Aleph, Merlin, and The Idealist.
In 1978, Charon, one of Pluto's natural satellites, was discovered.
In 1912, Alan Turing, the father of theoretical computer science, was born on this day. That same year, numerous hypotheses about man-made Awakened beings were proposed within the arcanist community.
The SPDM is considering replacing their tear gas grenades with chili-flavored foam kangaroo extinguishers.
In 1946, the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development became operational on this day.
A young Druvis III once considered signing up for the forest off-trail challenge at the Uluru Games. However, before the application could be mailed, a great fire turned everything to ashes.

In 1925, German physicist Werner Heisenberg published On the Quantum-Theoretical Reinterpretation of Kinematical and Mechanical Relationships on this day, laying the foundation for Lorentz's research on Chaos Energy.
In 1963, Argentine novelist Julio Cortázar published his masterpiece Hopscotch on this day.
Barbara undergoes her yearly physical check-up at Laplace. As expected, her vital signs are as stable as they can be.
Зима and Recoleta exchanged insights on literary writing, and rewrote one of Зима's poems together.

Fugue of Reflections

"Fugue of Reflections" is the latest expansion for "A Series of Dusks." This expansion adds a new ending to the base game and introduces character-exclusive artefacts known as [Acoustica]. More characters will rise to prominence in the pre-Storm Vienna. New Ending You don't need to have the expansion loaded up to experience the new ending, but you do need to have completed the [A Wish Granted] ending. Explore Vienna to see how to unlock the new conclusion. [Acoustica] Artefacts With the expansion loaded up, you can acquire [Acoustica] artefacts during exploration. These artefacts represent exclusive power ups for certain characters, and require the character to be in specific party positions to activate their effects. You can enhance Acoustica artefacts by meeting certain conditions. By meeting all enhancement requirements, an Acoustica artefact becomes [Fully Enhanced]. Based on how many fully enhanced artefacts are in your layout, additional [Harmonia] buff effects can be triggered, further strengthening your team. Completing the final path node of the Ring Road and defeating the [Impending Crisis] battle guarantees you one [Acoustica] artefact, prioritizing those exclusive to your current companion. You may also find Acoustica artefacts during exploration. A portable 6x24 brass scouting telescope. While scouts use it to calculate direction, elevation, and distance, in Vienna, it's more commonly found in the hands of theatergoers in the back rows.
The moment it is picked up, the sound around the ears subtly shifts, transforming into a violin melody from the stars, echoing within a haunting illusion.
This flame burns vigorously, illuminating fists, sheaths, and arrow feathers; this flame is humble and kind, never scorching the hand that holds it.
It has transcribed the works of masters, excerpted the inspirations of pioneers, and refined a nameless yet earnest poem.
A thin and tough piece of leather. With determination and a gentle touch, it can tame any critter into a state of obedience.
A crudely crafted stainless steel container, seemingly imbued with a specific arcane skill. It continuously dispenses a rich, aromatic, and versatile organic solvent in an unceasing flow.
A green silk ribbon, cool and soothing to the touch. Its original owner placed it here to provide comfort and guidance to those in need.

An intriguing device distributed by avant-garde artists at the theater entrance. Close your right eye to experience intense emotions, and your left eye to feel peace and tranquility. It is said, "If you observe with both eyes, you will uncover the hidden drama behind the stage."

A set of lead-acid batteries, a quintessential human invention: heavy and clunky, yet capable of providing stable and considerable energy. To many, using a box to light a bulb seems no less mysterious than arcanum.
A bamboo ladle from a foreign land. Note that despite its similar appearance, its function is not to strike enemies but to scoop fine wine.
A skeleton, a skull. It could be that of a lamb, a sacrificial offering laid upon the altar, or a tempter of darkness and decay.
A sealed, opaque container is a splendid riddle. Whether you succeed or fail, you will always gain a pill, a chance and opportunity, and a feeling of anticipation.
The combination of toughness and softness, an object of graceful motion. Dancers use it to sketch rainbows for the gods, and the gods reward them with applause and glory.
There might be a thousand ways to fold a paper bird, but only the style taught by childhood friends can carry wishes high into the sky.
A freshly composed, unperformed piece of music, imbued with the hopes, sorrows, and longings of its creator. One corner, once soaked and now dried, bears tiny crystallized grains of salt.
As long as you wear it, you can swagger onto any theater stage, and perhaps even earn some unexpected and anticipated applause.
Another form of music. Classical, lyrical jazz, or rock? Only the vibrating stylus of a record player can truly understand.
Grow, be incinerated, and then grow again. The oak etches the ebb and flow of arcane energy into its rings, just as life captures each twilight intertwined with joy and sorrow.
A bright and proud crystal orb. The user will soon notice that uttering the phrase "Who is the most powerful crystal orb?" significantly raises the accuracy of the divination.
Both a clever enigma and a subtle truth. Some are captivated by it for life, while others take one glance and flee in terror.
An incredibly advanced mode of transportation, a toy for the daring. Riding it across cobblestone streets, all worries vanish, leaving only a heart-pounding, exhilarating thrill.
A cable with plugs, transmitting electricity, signals, and perhaps secrets—some from this era, and others not.
This mirror can no longer accurately reflect the viewer's face, yet it was picked up and carefully preserved. Sometimes, it is the brokenness itself that carries meaning.
A peculiarly shaped shoulder bag, filled with seawater-soaked treasures. These rust- and salt-covered items might fetch a handsome price at an auction—if you have a silver tongue.
A precise liquid measuring instrument. Holding it makes you feel like a doctor, an alchemist, or a cutting-edge scientist ... the kind of person who's both cool and knowledgeable.
Go ahead and place your bets. You know, even if you lose everything, you can always bounce back, because this is the last chip you carry around your neck.
Meticulously prepared with the freshest, most precious ingredients, and catalyzed by whimsical ideas. Take a sip, it definitely does not taste like Dr. Papper.
Remember to feed it with ample food and proper respect, and maybe one day it will offer you some friendly advice.
A seemingly not-so-smart smart translator. It's slow to react to German, French, and Italian on the street but responds enthusiastically to "woof" and "howl."
A freshly picked rose, with both a blossom and a bud on the same stem. It wasn't forgotten here, but is waiting for someone.

This is a rest site in your long journey, and a home you never dreamt to find.
In the Suitcase, you can meet people from all corners of the world. Their words, actions, and experiences each have a unique rhythm.
Just like how the world has countless different instruments: hurdy-gurdies, ouds, bagpipes, launeddas ...
When these unique instruments come together, they create ever-changing new melodies.
Yes ... Take, for example, the cello, saxophone, and harp. Each has its own charm when played solo.
Of course, the violin isn't bad either. Its wide range and beautiful tone make it a natural favorite ...
But I prefer playing ensembles, Like the performances on "Free Breeze," where the waves and the wind join in, now that is music that's truly irreplaceable!
Yeah, exactly. We could also hold a concert in the Suitcase together!
Will everyone come? Bring your instruments, a hand drum, a maraca, even a leaf ...
It's a bit like Nukutaeao here; we're surrounded by water, though there, the sea breeze blows, and the surface of the water often mists over.
At dusk, we would kick cocoball on the beach together. Fishing boats would dock, and the sun would set and rise.
There are many strange rooms here. Sometimes, I forget where I've been.
I want to ask them for directions, but many people don't seem to care where they are ...
There are many other things as well ... but I'm sure I'll find a way to deal with them!
Yes, strangers often come by, wandering like me, looking around, sometimes getting lost.
But back during the trade seasons, we entertained many guests as well. I imagine it was a bit like when we first met.
Just like back then, we can trade things we need and help each other out. After all, we're now living on the same land.
The wilderness is peaceful. Every now and then, we need to let our ears and hearts rest—but just for a little while!
It's also a place for solitary thinking, just like that old church in Cremona.
Wandering through familiar places, that's something I used to do too.
The same instruments, the same performances, everyone saying the same things ... None of it was bad, really, but I couldn't stay trapped there any longer.
So I took my "Crackling Box" and wandered, eventually finding my way here.
Well, I'm constantly thinking of new compositions and performances, imagining sounds and instruments I've yet to see.
Would you be interested in listening to a new composition if I were to create one? You'd be the first to hear it!
Perhaps we could invite more people, sit in a circle, and have a small outdoor concert!
I tried writing in the sand by the water's edge, matching the words on the shells with the new ones I've learned.
The shells' language is simple. I can feel their thoughts, but describing them is tricky, hmm ...
Only the Nukutai can understand these words, as these shells record all of our emotions and experiences.
If you'd like, I could try teaching them to you.
My shell is doing perfectly well. It's amazing how much it can record for us; we never need to worry about forgetting anything.
Of course, the shell will also help record things about you, like how you invited us here.
And your concern for the shell—you've made it so happy.
Playing solo has its charm, too.
By ensemble, you mean performing together?
How are you settling in here?
Is it a lot different from the island?
I walk around here pretty often.
What do you think about?
These words are incomprehensible to me.
How's your shell doing?

Interim Report: Besides the Eclipse

The moth-attraction experiment mainly induced strong homesickness. To end my uncontrollable crying and depressive symptoms, this phototaxis research will be temporarily concluded. I will start compiling the summary report as usual.
Nukutaeao? The island swallowed up by the sea? I read about it in the newspaper. How is that linked to our fate? Oh, right, that was something from the "past." So, now that island should still exist.

I remember ... it was in a tucked away in the corner of the newspaper, a dilapidated wooden boat carrying "the last of the Nukutais." It was only mentioned once, followed by bold headlines of new maritime discoveries. Hey, a bunch of arcanists suddenly appearing out of nowhere—who else but us would care?

Humans are insatiable; you hide to avoid conflict with them, yet they see it as the natural order of things. All of this is for the sake of those new arcanists. The sooner we can make their island well known, the sooner they'll learn of humanity's malice, and we can avoid the worst case scenario.

Lady Grace, elegant and merciful Lady Grace, such benevolence should not be bestowed upon humans for mere show. Those human boiler operators, along with their captain who shields them, should be sent to the depths of the sea, to mark the beginning of our new kin's journey. A transaction? They don't deserve it. Well then! It's time to set sail! Load another shovel of coal into the boiler!

The sound of shattering, followed by scolding from above—new materials are needed. The heart is too soft, the spine lacks strength, and the skull is unstable. There must be a perfect material capable of holding a life through its entire lifetime ...

The clangor of drills, the new collaborators are too noisy, interrupting my meditations. They haven't even undergone the trials; why allow them to roam freely... Is there no peace even at the world's end? Hopefully, Lord Forget Me Not will stand firm against their leader.

The gulls are calling, but there's no sound of boats cutting through the waves. Perhaps the promised ship won't come after all. I had been pessimistic, but it's still disheartening not to have more compatriots join us. I hope Lady Grace, at least, brought back sufficient supplies.

Silence. Not even a whisper of wind. What else can I do? Since Lady Grace brought back some shells, why don't I ... Teeth? Yes, teeth might work. Strong, enduring. If my life ends here, my teeth might ...

Lord Forget Me Not seemed to have said something to Ms. Grace. It's unusual to see a hint of anxiety in her usually serene smile, but I'm sure I didn't misread it. Ms. Grace, the graceful and composed Ms. Grace ... Have you made some mistakes as well?

Why am I guarding the cold storage? Everyone else is guarding the engine room or the lower cabins. How could the cold storage be of use in our future tasks?

What's that? It's for storing Ms. Grace's collection?

Oh, that makes sense. May she be in good spirits.

Welcome to the cold storage, new friend. Sorry, but the ice cream has been moved out. You can take a rest here for now. Ms. Grace in her wisdom wants to document everyone's past, even the most foolish stories. Perhaps it's just her love for collecting, I can't say for sure. Nonetheless, it means everyone has the opportunity to be remembered. Isn't that marvelous?

I once had the privilege of seeing Ms. Grace's collection. Every piece is a work of art, meticulously preserved and each with its own story. Yes, Ms. Grace remembers them all, even those who would have been forgotten by society. So, wipe away that frown. Once we reach land, she will remember us and carry us forward on our path of devotion.

What is a home really? The land? The house? Or the people around you? It's a complicated question, but if I had to choose, I'd pick the people. You can find a new land, your house can be rebuilt, but every shell's pattern is unique. Wherever they go, I will follow.

Home? Home is full of suffering. I might as well set it ablaze. Is it my fault I was born an arcanist? Take me anywhere, it's better than staying here in misery. Even if I fall to my death on the way, at least it's my choice.

Home no longer exists. Only by staying close to my loved ones can I gain some warmth. My future is filled with suffering, and my shell will bear many scars. When I die, my legacy will be a tale of sorrow. How will my descendants learn about happiness from such memories? Please, take us back to the past. Let the children experience happiness at least once, so they won't lose their way.

Filthy, filthy. I'm at the doorstep of home but can't open the door. My hands are covered in blood. Touching the doorknob will anger my mother. Please, give me a small basin of water so I can wash my hands clean and step over the threshold with a smile.

Manus Vindictae has leveraged the information gathered from crossing the "Storm" to present Ms. Grace as a prophet, thereby earning the trust of the Nukutai people in this era. According to internal records, the Nukutais, displaced by rising sea levels, were meant to be contacted and properly resettled by our branch. It may be time to reconsider our strategy of passively awaiting era events to unfold, to avoid such incidents in the future.

From birth, the Nukutais will receive a shell which, through special arcanum rituals, records their entire emotional journey. This is how they described it during previous consultations. They take pride in passing on shells filled with beautiful memories to their descendants. In essence, the Nukutais' "Spirit Shells" carry an arcanist's lifetime of emotional fluctuations, making them excellent carriers of arcane energy, and a prime target for Manus Vindictae.

Ms. Grace, who carried out Manus Vindictae's plan to win over the Nukutais, is suspected of being directly under the command of Mr. Forget Me Not and linked to the earlier incident involving the transfer of Ms. Kimberly's contract item. Given her numerous malicious actions in the "Free Breeze" incident, which had a profound impact on all parties involved, it is recommended that she be added to the wanted list.

The exact goal of Manus Vindictae remains unclear, but since Ms. Grace took over "Free Breeze," there have been multiple unusual sailing records. Based on the findings from this research, it is suspected that Manus Vindictae is stationed in a region even further south. Australia has already undergone comprehensive checks during the Uluru Games. It is now recommended that subsequent searches focus on South America and South Africa, particularly in regions like Chile, Argentina, and the Republic of South Africa.

Listen up, rookie. Since I'm your instructor, I need to make sure you don't embarrass me out there.
Poitier
Did you review the basic operational guidelines for Los Angeles Arcane Affairs Officers before taking this job?
Yes! First, all police operations must remain within Los Angeles's administrative jurisdiction.

Second, we must develop practical and cohesive plans, procedures, and strategies to reduce arcanum-related crimes and behaviors, improve the quality of life for citizens, and maintain harmonious relations between humans and arcanists ...

Administrative Procedure 311-09: In civil disputes involving arcanum, mediation should be prioritized to minimize the impact of arcanum-related factors, provide citizens with professional guidance, and avoid actions that could escalate conflicts.
… Oh, great, a model student response.
Administrative Procedure 320-05: In criminal cases involving arcanum, Arcane Affairs Officers in the vicinity should provide assistance whenever possible, minimizing harm to citizens …
With that painfully by-the-book response, you might as well join Internal Affairs. Heard they love that kind of stuff.
Let's keep it simple, remember—big or small, whenever arcanum is involved, it's up to us, the "arcane cops," to handle it.
But don't worry too much; more often than not, the small stuff outweighs the big stuff.
Understood, Instructor Poitier. Should I recite the rest?
The rest? Nah, you sound like you've got that covered—
On the topic of injury and death compensation ...
Alright, alright, rookie, that's enough!
Rookie, where's your chameleon comms? Lost it?
I think I still have it ... look, right here. It's just gone into camouflage.
Maybe Qiangliang showing up scared it into hiding.
Qiangliang? That electric tiger of yours? The one that lives in your phone?
This old brick phone was the relic I used during my first summoning of Qiangliang. It became the token of our bond.
When I use this phone to call Qiangliang, it will answer.
Wild! It's like something straight out of those TV shows.
But using a phone for rituals? I thought rituals from your side of the world would be more …
... Traditional? Like those dancing shadow puppets you've got?
That's an excellent guess. Previous generations of summoners in my family did use shadow puppetry to call Qiangliang. But that was centuries ago.
Oh? So, does that make you a once-in-a-century kind of genius?
… Not really. I was just lucky that the phone is a more convenient method than shadow puppetry.
There it is—you're still humble as ever, princess.
Can you summon Qiangliang again? I owe it a thank you for the help earlier.
I wouldn't recommend it. Calling Qiangliang without a good reason might make it angry, and …
And?
The calls are really expensive.
Great. We've hit a dead end. Just what exactly did we miss?
Maybe we should go over the items in Loggerhead's bag again.
Loggerhead … seriously? She packed all these film reels, but somehow missed the most important one!
Look at this. Was she planning to open a video store? So many movie reels!
Hey, Liang, these ones are in Chinese, right?
… Yes, ma'am. That's The Qimen Fighters. Here's Ms. Vampire, and Troubled Lunatics.
Classic Hong Kong films, but it's unclear if these were Loggerhead's collection, or gifts from Director Noire.
Good grief. Do we need to watch all of these? We don't have that kind of time.
No, I don't think so. These are just regular film reels, and their stories aren't related to our investigation.
Ha! I almost forgot you used to sneak around and watch movies behind your parents' backs. Your knowledge is broader than I thought.
So, other than C07, which one here's your favorite?
Our time is running out.
Ugh, dull as ever. I knew it.
But … if we wrap this up quick, you should watch Ms. Vampire. It's a hallmark of Hong Kong arcanum films.
Oh? I'll remember that.
We've gone through the bag, but the missing reel isn't here.
Perhaps it's time for us to try something else.
Yeah, let's hear what our big-shot director has to say.
So, what happened next? After I passed out, how'd you manage to drive off the Nightpiercer?
… We didn't drive her off. She left when she heard the sirens from the reinforcements you called.
Chief Elden arrived. Director Noire used arcane skills to control her puppets and guide them to you. That allowed the medics to reach you and Ms. Scott in time to get you to the hospital.
Sounds like we owe her a big thank you.
… Sorry, Miss Poitier. I couldn't stop Ms. Qi Xing. She took the Reunion of the Three Swallows …
This is all my fault.
Don't beat yourself up, kid. No one expected the Nightpiercer to show up like that.
How are Scott and Pug Dog holding up?
Pug Dog's been caught and is in custody. Ms. Scott is stable after emergency treatment, but she hasn't regained consciousness just yet.

Doctors believe her coma, like those other victims, was caused by Reunion of the Three Swallows. The department has officers guarding her, but until the case is solved, we can't expect her to provide any useful information.
As for Director Noire … Sorry, I should've informed you earlier. She's the one who tipped me off about the illegal arcane artifact deal.
Though she participated in the deal, her honesty, cooperation, and her lawyer's efforts convinced the department not to pursue her case further.
Tch, typical of Hollywood. A director can go from criminal to collaborator with just a few words.
We should talk to her again—about Ms. Qi Xing and about that reel … Maybe there's more she hasn't told us.
You know, I've shared so many of my stories with you. Why don't you tell me some of yours?
Directors are always on the lookout for good material. I'm curious about your past.
They say you're a once-in-a-generation talent, the one who summoned Qiangliang—the Xiandao Beast that hadn't answered the Liang family's call in 300 years.
… That was all just a misunderstanding.
The day I summoned Qiangliang, I learned its name and glimpsed its memories.
Centuries ago, Qiangliang was gravely injured during its last summoning and has been recovering ever since. That's why it hasn't answered the Liang family's calls.
I just happened to summon it when it was finally healed. My family thought Qiangliang chose me, so they placed high expectations on me.
… But I'm no chosen one. I was just lucky.
Does your family know about this?
No, I never told them.
… I did not want to disappoint them.
"That morning, we lay amidst the ruins, and sis handed me a bottle of beer. Suddenly, I understood—I already had the whole world. I just hadn't bothered to look."
Qi Xing
… You're right. If we cut out the chaotic, corrupted footage, this could be a great film.
That line—it's so Teresa. A house can be rebuilt, and the gaps between friends can be mended. She always loved life.
It's hard to believe, especially after seeing this. A Teresa like this would never have taken her own life.
... You're right.
Miss Vigil, thank you. Her creation being restored to its original form is something I'm truly grateful for. And it's all thanks to you and your team.
About Qiangliang … I'm more sorry than you can imagine. This wasn't my intention, but ultimately, my selfish behavior caused this to happen.
If there's anything I can do to make amends …
There's no need to feel guilty, Miss Qi Xing. Purging the ghost plague is part of Qiangliang's and my duty.
I know that you really liked those movies … I must have really let you down, eh, kid?
… I won't lie. I was a little disappointed.
But it doesn't matter, C07 is still my favorite character, and that will never change.
... Thank you.
Wait a moment, Qi Xing. Before you and the officers leave, Miss Liang and I need to confirm one last thing.
There's something in your testimony that's been eating at me. Don't get me wrong, I'm not saying that you're lying. The Vigil's interrogation experts confirmed that much.

But even you probably noticed—the sequence of events that led you to become the "Nightpiercer;" you stole the reel, and caused the incident in Chinatown, but your motives seem … inconsistent. I feel like I'm missing a piece to this puzzle.
It's almost like the memory gaps affecting Loggerhead. But your expertise in arcane skills surpasses hers. Perhaps you can recall something.
I'm sorry. I really don't remember …

I only recall how it all began. I got word that Reunion of the Three Swallows had found its way out of Foundation storage and into the black market. I even got into the secret auction for it through some intermediaries but, unfortunately, I didn't have the dough.
So I asked myself, who else out there could be as fixated on that reel as me? The answer to that was obvious.
It's me.
That's right. You're a public figure. Following you to Los Angeles wasn't difficult. I tracked down your intermediary, Pug Dog, and for a bit of cash, I got the time and location of your deal.
I see. So, the "friendly advice" Pug Dog gave me back then was about you. What a guy—zero professional ethics.
That night, my only objective was to take the reel from you. The question of who stole it from the Foundation wasn't something I even bothered to think about. But …
At the very last moment, a sliver of sense kicked in. It was a close call, but I managed to hold myself back. I think there was a moment when I really intended to kill that poor staffer, Miss Scott.
… But I don't understand why I felt that way. You know the rest.
The player that placed us here …

Reconstructing Idealized Memories

Although I don't usually keep a journal, I had to record today's encounter—I met the great Miss Matilda Bouanich!

I still remember that summer. My mother lectured me for an hour before we left and then another hour during our journey. I thought I was following her instructions perfectly: I was dressed perfectly neat; my greetings were memorized word-for-word. But the moment I met the Bouanichs, I froze solid, too nervous to say anything. Even adults can get stage fright, so how was it fair to give her own daughter the cold shoulder for it? A smile or a pat on the back from mother was all I needed to finish my greeting without fumbling.

Thank goodness for Lady Beryl. She saw what happened, and her gracious words salvaged the situation. I didn't disappoint my mother after that. I'm sure of it because the rest of my memories of that visit were pleasant—Lady Beryl's warm smile and Matilda's energetic chatter. Matilda could be as noisy as she liked and still win her mother's approval, how I envied that so much.

But Lady Beryl … for some reason, I can't remember what she looked like. Now I understand Latham's frustration. Being Matilda's mother, I could imagine a matured, refined version of Matilda—minus the childish energy and, oh right, without the hooked nose, that's my mother's trait.

This letter was tucked inside a folder of interrogation records, it appears to have been exchanged silently between two Vigiles agents during an interrogation. The two distinct handwritings reflect their unspoken dialogue:

"She's tight-lipped about it."

"But she seems unaware that we've already figured out everything."

"Fascinating, like a mouse in a lab experiment—arrogant yet clueless."

"There's still one thing left to figure out: how exactly did she learn to crack the anti-theft arcane seal?"

"All her lies and disguises fall apart under scrutiny, but she hasn't given up a single clue about this. Even our artificial somnambulism couldn't uncover anything …"

"Could it just be sheer dumb luck?"

"Disappointing. I've taught you better—never rely on million-to-one coincidences. Always consider the more plausible scenario."

"You mean … she's being controlled by someone else? And they've erased her memory, so she can't betray them?"

"Exactly. That slippery merchant gave up Scott, but there's no way a minor employee could pull off something like this. Rejoice, we've hooked a big fish."

"So … we're letting her go?"

"Yes, but not without loosening her strings first."

"Understood. I'll notify Mr. Pedra. I trust he'll ensure Miss Scott feels completely at ease after some … subtle adjustments."

"Good. You're a reliable assistant, Billy."

The second writer seemed about to reply but left only a hesitant pen stroke.

The Last Fangxiangshi

On the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month, under the turning stars at year's end, a ritual must be performed to banish plague spirits, ensuring the renewal of life. Officials gathered in the palace, guards lined the stairs, and peasants, merchants, and craftsmen presented offerings. Even passing sages paused in reverence.

"Let Zhenzi prepare. Commence the banishment."

The eunuch recited incantations, and the Zhenzi responded in unison. Under watchful eyes, the Fangxiangshi brandished shield and spear, performing a solemn dance to summon the Xiandao Beast and dispel all evil spirits. 

This year, however, something was different. Though the chief minister declared the ceremony complete, the Xiandao Beast lingered. The Fangxiangshi, clad in black and red robes, now bore white hair and furrowed brows.

The beasts growled lowly by his side as he spoke: "The lineage of the Fangxiangshi ends with me. You must carry on the duty."

The Zhenzi exchanged astonished glances, realizing their leader had entrusted them with the mantle.

Qiangliang let out a low growl. On this day, the chief minister and each of the Zhenzi took on a new surname, pledging to defend the people in the name of their respective Xiandao Beast.

The New Waves

A New Wave!

In the 1970s, Hong Kong drew nourishment from a booming economy. Meanwhile, the term "New Wave" was no longer novel in Paris but became a rallying cry for inspiration on this distant shore.

No one knows exactly how this movement started. While the streets buzzed with the influence of Shaw Brothers' dramatic, operatic martial arts films, a new generation of creators began to focus on a different side of the city. Lugging heavy 16mm film cameras through neon-lit streets, they captured gritty yet striking imagery.

They wanted more people to see their films! They yearned for bolder content on the silver screen! Their passion fueled their creativity, blending violence, folklore, and arcanum into stories filled with romance, absurdity, and tragedy. Their works captured the clash between people and their times, leaving an enduring cultural legacy.

Amid this wave, the film Muddle emerged, marking a significant milestone for its creator.
News Scrapbook

Detective C07 Shatters Box Office Records! The holiday movie season has ended, with Detective C07 dominating the cinemas with its thrilling fights and comedic moments. This outcome was a forgone conclusion for the C07 series, but the film's ending has sparked heated debates. It's reported that lead actress Qi Xing is scheduled to appear at the upcoming film festival in a week, sharing behind-the-scenes stories with her fans. —Silver Screen New Weekly: Lunar New Year Edition Hero Films Without Heroes By Anonymous Years ago, when C07 first premiered, we were thrilled to see that heroes didn't have to be glorified, untouchable elites. Heroes could also be cheeky and humorous, like a friend who loves to show off. But as the series continued, with larger budgets and grander productions, its original spirit seemed to fade away. Watching the latest installment of Detective C07, all I felt was disappointment. Is this still the Detective C07 that championed justice? Is this still the same filmmaker who gave us Muddle? —World Film Review New Art Trio's Midnight Clash: What's Keeping Ms. He Pleading? Late last night, reports surfaced of a heated argument at the home of New Art Company screenwriter He Rijun. At around 2 a.m., cameras captured Ms. Noire and Ms. Qi Xing leaving together, their expressions suggesting the disagreement was far from resolved. By 8 a.m., Ms. Qi Xing announced she would not attend next week's film festival. Following this, director Noire declared that there would be no further installments for Detective C07. Though no official explanation was given, the incident undoubtedly signals a major shift for New Art Company. Stay tuned for updates. —Harbor Daily

The specific technology Laplace used to achieve this function has been buried within the vast "memories" of the interviewee. After searching fruitlessly for an hour, they declared it to be classified.

The Beginning of All Stories

In the 1820s, people discovered the phenomenon of persistence of vision, making horses endlessly gallop on spinning strips of narrow paper.

In the 1870s, twelve cameras were aligned to capture exposure in one-thousandth of a second, stitching photographs into moving images.

By the 1880s, numerous inventors using varying methods but identical ingenuity created the tools of cinema. Paper reels, mirrors, lamps, hand-drawn frames at sixteen per second, and supple celluloid film … Audiences handed over their nickels in exchange for comedic tales told through fragmented scenes.

Inventions continued. Twenty-second clips became three-minute shorts, and shorts turned into longer films. What came next? Athletes, trains, dogs, or the sea? Eager eyes watched intently, unaware that a small piece inside the projector had awakened.

Gears pulled perforations, and film glided smoothly through her body, narrating an endless silver-screen world. Alongside the people ahead of the projector, she too marveled and anticipated each frame and every scene.

Brewing Coffee: A sudden warmth, a daze, an urge to sing. That feeling is surprisingly similar in humans. So you swallowed the keychain and then went looking for it everywhere?! Cheeseburger: Sticky, noisy, energizing, dizzying. This is one of the best items on the Foundation's cafeteria menu! Pandora Wilson: Hello, Ms. Loggerhead. Loggerhead: Hello! Sorry, I don't remember your name. If you'd like, just hang tight while I project my memory reel from the past three days ... Pandora Wilson: No worries, this is our first meeting. Pandora Wilson: As an awakened born within a projector, you must have witnessed countless great films. What are your favorite ones? Loggerhead: Oh, it would definitely be a black-and-white silent film! Love Lock

Silver Waist Charm
Jade and silver beads form a shimmering web that sways with every step and passing breeze. It gathers the worldly loves and hates of each believer, as well as their briefest glimpses of fear.
The Three Poisons

A jade-green vial brimming with life, with lush willow branches and nectar sweet as honey. "Why mind the trivial details of appearances? For now, just savor its sweetness," the interviewee urged. "Come, don't be afraid, it's well-behaved."
Raven Wing Crown

A wing-shaped headpiece crafted from feathers, thorns, and wrought iron, adorned with neatly arranged raven feathers, glowing in deep blue and purple hues. Alongside her cherished staff, it will witness prosperity returning to the forest.
Spiral Thorn Wand

A black wooden staff spiraling upward with hawthorn thorns entwined around it.

"Insight and Revelation"

Crows perch on thorny branches, neither arriving nor leaving.

A "Small" Purse

No one knows what the interviewee's purse contains.
"The world is filled with countless stages, each performing countless dramas. Surely, you can see this purse couldn't possibly hold all the stories I've seen."
"Inside and Out of the Play"
