The moment armies start to march, the world stands still.
You fight or fall back, charge forward, or run. Those are the only rules on the battlefield.
I don't see a start time on this report, nor does it state the reason for or the demands of this war.
That's because the war hasn't started yet.#Because this is a war waged with paper and pens.
That's what you think. The scars left on the land may be the most obvious form of destruction, but the true devastation of war is one that develops gradually in the souls of people.
Ah, a literary war. Indeed, the violence enacted upon words is often just as devastating as an order on a battlefield.
Words must fulfill their duties to their creators, just as soldiers must answer to their commanders.
I still don't see how this relates to what's happening now.
You don't? Hmm. The young writers have been exiled—sent down a path with no signs to follow and no destination.
In dark days of bloody conflict, soldiers often find comfort in scriptures and verses—or in letters from their loved ones.
They hold those words close—a fragile piece of home—a brief solace from the roaring of the battlefield.
But, as they fall one by one, they learn the bitter truth. No destiny awaits them but death, that bitter homesickness still weighing heavy in their hearts.
I hope they can at least find some peace in their dreams.
In dreams? Maybe. Walking the streets of your hometown, spending a lazy afternoon at the writing desk—dreams can take you anywhere.
But live there too long, and the lines between fiction and reality will blur, and soon you'll never wake up again.
Soldiers crawl through trenches, roll in the mud, and charge to their deaths again and again ...
... while words are forever trapped within the confines of poetry, made to live, die, and live again under the golden prophecy ...
Ugh. I can't stand the way poets talk.
Let's take a step back—pull you out of that whirlwind of passion and dreams.
If you want to make the best call, you need to zero in on what really matters. So, what's your take on that big speech?
The Latin American Boom.
A sudden explosion that shook Latin American literary circles about 30 years ago. It was destructive—but also gave rise to new life.
Lucky for us, we don't have to worry about shell shock in the literary world.
You don't strike me as someone who knows about literature.
It's not about knowing literature. Any soldier with a little experience can deliver a status report. Alright, eyes on the map.
As we speak, ships are lined up on the Spanish coast—but this time, they're poised to make a new kind of discovery, if you can call it that.
And here are our new "Columbuses," heading to the docks to embark on their journey.
Who are these new "Columbuses"?
Carmen and Carlos, the driving force behind this literary feast between Spain and Latin America.
Carmen, with an eye for opportunity and a mind for business, sought out the continent's literary gems and secured generous publishing deals for them.
Carlos, with his deep understanding of market dynamics, brought these works to the eyes of the European public.
Then? A golden era began. It all kicked off with a scandal at a military academy, and soon the entire world was captivated by the story of a baby with a pig's tail from a faraway land.
But we mustn't forget the writers themselves. Fuentes, a towering figure of the Spanish-speaking world, and Cortázar, the writer ever seeing through the eyes of a child.
And of course, Mario and Gabo—key players in this literary revolution—will forever be etched in the annals of history.
They corresponded regularly, always expressing deep admiration for each other's work. In fact, one even wrote a doctoral thesis on the other.
Ah, friendship.
That must have been a proud time for them.
It was.
But no matter how explosive the boom was, it couldn't escape its fleeting nature.
With the second imprisonment and self-criticism of a Cuban poet, in came an inexplicable right hook, and bang!—silence.
The military junta had gripped the poets' throats. The verse of the pioneers was cut off, their voices no longer heard.
The bond between two generations was broken, and for the younger of the two, the silence was intolerable.
They looked for a new theme, a new idea, a new voice—a new method to speak on their disappointment, their horror, and their anger.
And they became the new guerrillas.
Few soldiers would appreciate the idea of taking orders from an accursed die. A skilled commander would never rely on luck to make decisions.
On the battlefield, the distance for every maneuver should be clear and precise—not two numbers with a "d" in the middle—unless you're looking to invite a mutiny.
That said, if a die with such power were placed in a soldier's hand ...
I'm pretty sure they'd roll it and let it decide their destiny.
Luck won't always be on your side.
Exactly. There's no good luck without bad luck—just as a coin must have two sides. Luck essentially defines one's entire life.
And whether it's make or break, life or death, the die will keep on rolling.
Of course, dice aren't the only tools used to "play" with fate—coins, lotteries, even shells on the beach can all serve the same purpose.
Thanks to the randomness of fate, a Babylonian may rise to be a proconsul one day and fall into slavery the next.
Some tragedies could have been avoided.
Well, that's where historians come in.
With a little creative editing of the history books, even the random rolls of a die can suddenly make sense.
What were once "avoidable tragedies" are rebranded as "reasonable incidents" or even "desirable outcomes."
At least the roll of a die is impartial.
Hmph, you're starting to sound like a gambler.
But even gamblers, after hitting a hot streak—or a losing spell—start to convince themselves that they've figured out the grand pattern behind games of chance.
It isn't just gamblers, either. Witches tried to influence fate through rituals and charms. Ancient mathematicians calculated probabilities on paper. Some even wrote books on game theory.
Meanwhile, others suspected there were cheaters among them.
I just hope these high rollers unite to confront the demon who holds the laws of the universe—the past, present, and future—in its claws and give it a "Well done!" and a slap in the face.
You're talking in circles today.
Haven't I always? It's just that today, the die rolled a peculiar number.
But all things considered, I prefer the other kind of commander.
The die is cast. But regardless of what number has been rolled, it's time to cross the river.
Ahem ... Take a deep breath, soldier; the smoke's cleared now. This story—this "battle"—will soon come to an end.
A writer has departed from her domain, leaving her creations scattered behind her, like blood-soaked bandages and fragmented skulls in the trenches.
What a garbled mess.
I don't understand it at all.#I think I understand.
Glad we're on the same page. Thank heavens my commander wasn't some kind of littérateur; else I'd have been blown to bits before I could decipher their poetic orders.

*whistle* How wonderful for you. You know what? You should be the leader of the Literature Encryption Communication Team. Just arm yourself with a dictionary, and even enemies with .45 Maxim machine guns won't stand a chance against you.
Because the poetry you recite will surely blow their minds before their bullets pierce yours.
You've developed a sense of humor.

Well, it's all thanks to a certain writer, the embodiment of the wandering poet and traveler from Santiago to Buenos Aires. She impressed me with her precious experience as a cafe dishwasher and campground caretaker.
What really rekindled my sense of humor was her seriousness about her literary pursuits. You'd understand what I mean if you'd ever heard a cheesy joke at a comrade's graveside.
Drawing strength from her wanderings and rebellious exploits, she attempted to change society, wielding the sword of literature as a revolutionary intellectual and a leader of thought.
Some would hail her as a battle angel of Latin America, with words as piercing as bullets and poems as powerful as tactical bombers.
I doubt literature has such a profound impact.#I believe in the power of literature.
Many share your doubt, myself included.
You stand firm in your beliefs, huh? Well, maybe that's a good thing. A commander has to trust their soldiers, or they'll be forced to surrender before long.
Here, come closer. Let me tell you a secret ...
Many—if not all—people foolishly think it's the executioner who drops the guillotine blade, the powder that fires the bullet.

While they're half right, they're substantially inaccurate. The craters on the battlefield aren't the result of bombs, but of clashing ideologies—a trigger pulled long before the powder ever ignited in the barrel.
As for literature ...
Well, it's probably best not to buy too much into the Latin American Boom. Forget about the status report from earlier.
That said, at least there's one thing that's certain:
Books can bite back—and they'll leave scars.
Look, it's sinking. Corpses float on the planks, and the fleeing prisoners are swimming toward the shore. Time to abandon ship.
What ship?
One that was exiled to a desolate corner of the ocean by the resplendent civilized world.
It's both a prison and a sanitarium. Are any of your friends aboard? If so, you might find the following report a little offensive.
"Dregs of society" ... "Human scum" ... These are the terms used to describe its eccentric passengers.
To be fair, they do lack discipline and independence.
But that may well be a response to the heavy pain they've endured.
Some theorists suggest that they're innocent victims, trapped in the confines between rationality and irrationality, defined and redefined by historians as they please.
But let's ditch the theories and simplify things: the moment the shackle called "madness" was fastened around their necks—whether they were truly mentally ill or not—their lives were forever scarred.
And now, the mad passengers are storming the shore.
A favorable outcome.#They're spreading their disease.
I suppose it is. You can see the joy in their faces, even in the footprints they leave behind as they hop across the beach.
Yes, freedom is favorable, indeed. The freedom to squander our lives, to trample on the dignity of others, the freedom to embrace absurdity and meaninglessness.
But one can gain immunity through controlled infection—the disease can become its own vaccine.
Just beware of the ignorant commander who deifies a wandering lunatic in pursuit of a little knowledge.
Let's dig deeper—scavenge through the messy battlefield for dog tags—were these people born mad?
After watching the inhabitants of this earth tear each other apart in one war after another, I've concluded this: only knowledge drives people to madness; ignorance does not.
Madness is a side effect of the sedative that is "knowledge." As long as those on land continue to consume it, this ship will never be short on recruits.
This is a war between madness and civilization. Both sides have leveled accusations, spilled blood, and pummeled each other ...
... and soon, everyone will have leapt into the trenches and beaten and been beaten to a bloody pulp. Only a few can escape this fate.
Like who?
Check your six.
The one leaning against the sunken ship, showing no signs of struggle or sorrow—García.
The seawater has flooded his windpipe and reddened his eyes, yet there he is, staring blankly at the shore ...
He's in his home base. He holds no hope for forgiveness from his enemies—not in the slightest. He's a one-man army, fighting only for himself. Alone.
Now, do a 360 and look again—he's been utterly defeated.

Even though they refuse to discuss the outside world, spending even a few days inside the prison makes clear that the reason they are here is precisely what they avoid speaking about.

Ushuaia is a cold town on the tip of Argentina's southernmost territory. The polar night, the frozen sea, the proximity to Antarctica, the endless winter—it all makes the place seem buried by time and forgotten. It possesses all the necessary qualities of a prison, making it an ideal place to send arcanist suspects diagnosed with mental illness, a place to be forgotten.

Setting aside the true definition of madness and their status as prisoners, what I see in this prison are former poets, writers, and social activists. In their era, some spoke of poetry—then disappeared from society for owning a book by Jean-Paul Sartre. Some incited grassroots rebellion against hierarchical structures—only to be exiled. They were repeatedly questioned, "Why do you read these books? Why do you write these poems?" They were branded "thought organizers" and eventually sent here to partake in an experiment conducted under the names of Foucault and psychoanalysis. It is nearly impossible to determine whether their "madness" was defined by society because they resisted order, or if it was induced through relentless electric shocks and torture. Or perhaps all of these reasons are one and the same. This reason is often avoided, sanitized, or ignored—because deep down, we all know how deeply it is woven into the fabric of all our lives.

...

At first, they said nothing, but this very act of deliberate avoidance was what truly conveyed their grief and fear.

When they speak of "Manus Vindictae," their tone is always light, often laced with jokes—colorful descriptions like "a greasy-headed musician smearing tiles like a drunk Edward Goya" frequently crop up in their poetry. Even though I have never "seen" such a scene myself, I can still grasp their attitude toward Manus Vindictae—it was an oppression surpassing even their past sufferings. Yet, subconsciously, they "ignored" this similarity—perhaps out of denial, or perhaps because this prison had already taught them to obey, also subconsciously.

But as far as I know, Manus Vindictae did bring their terror here. Those masks drove arcanists to insanity and caused unbearable suffering, as if they were caught in an inescapable snare. After prolonged torment, they lost the ability to utter even a single phrase of their own language, reduced to slaves of this underground faction—left with only a singular thought, their souls having left the empty husk of their former selves.

And as for humans—it seems they were driven to death en masse. At night, they were not allowed prolonged sleep, woken by their companions every hour to sit beneath the watchtower and chant prayers. And by dawn, high-intensity training and interrogations that did not require or expect any answers would begin again ... The purpose of Manus Vindictae is buried beneath these cruel methods, as clear as the deepest crevasse in the ice field—it is nothing but destruction. They seek to "completely destroy" humanity.

In 1935, Professor António from Portugal became intrigued by a medical study documenting how gorillas became docile after the removal of their frontal lobes. Inspired by this, he successfully performed the world's first human frontal lobotomy, known as leukotomy. The surgery was remarkably successful, paving the way for significant breakthroughs in research. In 1949, Professor António was awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine for his work.

Through continuous practice and refinement, he and others eventually improved and perfected the procedure, even developing a specialized leukotome. However, the surgical technique required a high level of expertise, and as a result, it was never widely adopted.

In 1945, American doctor Walter Freeman modified the procedure, which became infamously known as the "ice pick lobotomy." The technique involved rendering patients unconscious with electroshock or anesthesia, and then hammering a steel pick—roughly the thickness of a chopstick—through the upper part of the eye socket into the brain. The pick was then manually rotated to destroy the frontal lobe.

In 1950, following strong recommendations from psychiatric pathologist Vasily Gayanovsky, the Soviet government became the first to announce a complete ban on frontal lobotomies. Over the next two decades, most countries, including the United States, followed suit and passed laws prohibiting the procedure.

"Irrational Blockade Therapy"

This should not be considered a set of tools but rather a precise solution, essential for removing lesions, correcting disorder, and restoring order. Additionally, the interviewee emphasizes that they have no intention of assigning these objects any emotions, names, or symbolic meanings.
A set of silent witnesses. They have observed the precision of each incision, the force of each suture, and the timing of each operation. *Also from the interviewee*.

"Rope of Sand, Universe of Infinity"

The accessory's shape derives from the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, while the book "with infinite pages" was said to be found by chance in the eighth underground floor of a national library housing 950,000 volumes.
Despite this introduction by the interviewee, the author maintains that it was merely an old book taken from a street stall.
Potion

One evening in 1996, in Stockholm, a well-known local alchemist and arcanist received an unusual visitor.

The guest was a 17-year-old human boy. A pure-blooded human—such visitors were rare for an alchemist, as the field of alchemy was dominated by arcanists with innate talent and access to resources. Few humans ever sought their counsel.

But soon, the alchemist realized that this taciturn young man was a prodigy beyond comprehension. He came in search of knowledge, but after a night of conversation, the alchemist knew the boy would leave disappointed.

The alchemist wished to help the boy, but in this world, there was no answer to his question. What he sought was too vast, too ambitious—a pursuit destined to become a lifelong curse.

The alchemist wanted to free the boy from this curse, or perhaps—to help him find the answer. An answer everyone desires, including the alchemist.

Alchemy is a science of the body. The alchemist gave the boy a formula for a potion, one that would free him from the limitations of human physiology, allowing him to reach the peak of rationality and perception. He would never again forget anything—not one detail, nor any speck of knowledge or trivia. He could absorb endless expanses of alchemical wisdom and more ...

The boy left, overjoyed. He did not yet know that this potion formula would soon become a curse that would haunt him for the rest of his days.
Symbolism

A small, unnoticed crack The Idealist: The moment that rusty six-centimeter iron nail was so crudely driven into the wall, it created a fracture in the plaster—growing each day in subtle, irreversible decay. Every minute fissure, every delicate break, is so beautiful, so sorrowful. This is the origin of my epic poem. I've named it A History of Eternity. The Forgotten Vienna Years, page 102, line 16, second word Zahir: Idée fixe. This word has taken deep root in my mind ... No, it is not just a concept—it is something more tangible, softer, impenetrable ... An unbreakable spiderweb, a mesh veiling both my eyes and the pathways of my brain ... Whenever I seek out all the possible meanings contained within philosophical concepts, this word urges me beyond the concept itself. A state of trance ... December 12, 1990, 2:08:34 PM, the shadow cast on the third window of the Central Tower Merlin: Summer sunlight. The warmest moment in Ushuaia of the year 1990. It traces patterns along the edges of the window, like a decipherable genealogy of psychoanalysis. I sense an omen, a connection with the entire power structure of Comala. They are one and the same. I should adjust the summer window's orientation accordingly.

Pandora Wilson: Hello, Mr. Aleph.
Pandora Wilson: I've leaned on some highly secretive sources to get in contact with you. I've heard that you've served as an advisor to quite a few people. Whether it's Manus Vindictae, Lorentz, Laplace, or even ordinary Arcanists ... do you truly answer all of their questions?
Aleph: Yes. Just as I am doing now.
Pandora Wilson: Ha, I see. May I ask how you ensure that your answers are always correct?
Aleph: In truth, I cannot guarantee that. I extract all of my knowledge from the books, history, and disciplines I am familiar with, but that does not mean any of it is necessarily correct, authoritative, or representative of any truth. It is merely an answer.
Pandora Wilson: So, you mean that your answers do not contain your personal emotions or judgments?
Aleph: I cannot be certain. But "personal emotions and judgments" ... that is a vague concept. These memories are a part of me—do they also define my "personality"?
Pandora Wilson: There will always be those who take your answers as absolute truth.
Aleph: My apologies. In the future, I will make sure to inform them of these disclaimers before answering their questions.

A cloak embroidered with a Spanish poem about time, ashes, gravestones, flowers, eternity, death, and miracles. *Per the interviewee's strong request, all imagery has been preserved*
Out of curiosity, we asked about the origins of the garment and poem. "It was simply a miracle—an incomprehensible, fleeting miracle that happened in the cycles of everyday life."
—Clearly, expecting a straightforward answer from a writer was wishful thinking.
"Heart of Visceral Realism"

Visceral Realism: Glory in Failure

In 1975, at the Gandhi Bookstore in Mexico City, three unknown young poets founded the "Visceral Realism" poetry movement. They disrupted formal poetry readings, took part in youth resistance, and declared: "The important thing is not to write poetry, but to live as a poet." 

Misunderstood, lonely, poor, and failed—thus was born a poet's glory. 

Every postwar Latin American youth was swept into the movement. They were lost idealists, convinced that their struggle could transform this land, could change the world. But their generation's ideals quickly collapsed. In the end, the poet left for Europe, exiled and disillusioned.

The legend of resistance continues in the poet's novels. He wrote about his past wanderings, about his lifelong journey across Latin America, about the unfinished quests of poets, and the ideals shattered by the violence of reality ... the absurd, brave, glorious, and failed poets.

Let me tell you how a story should be written: stories should be written in threes, and if possible, in tens! The Rise and Fall of Sanity A tale set in a desert town, revolving around the ancient tradition known as "The Die of Babylon" ... There's no way to write the ending. Something's off—what could possibly be missing from this story? Ruinas Gloriosas y Directrices de Metáforas A trilogy belonging to two protagonists, an epic journey beginning with their return home. Through countless revisions, nearly every part of their adventures had multiple versions. In the end, they all became part of this work. The manuscript is complete, but for certain reasons, it was never submitted or published. The Final Days of Chac Mool Amid the Mexican Muralist Movement, a young muralist unexpectedly uncovers a secret hidden within his friend's work ... It's on hold. I need to return to Mexico City. To stand once more before those great murals, only then will I know how to finish it!

A Viennese noble wielding a conch is recklessly flinging coins at passersby. The people hit by the money scramble away in panic—no one dares pick up the coins from the ground.

It seems the panicked citizen has mistaken the conch in Semmelweis's hand. Their expression is that of a drowning person clinging to a reed.

"Look at the foolish choice you've made. The troops have surrounded the area. Are you really going to risk your life under cannon fire for a stranger's property? You know the reward isn't worth the risk."

[A Series of Dusks: Rhapsody of the Moon] is an expansion for [A Series of Dusks]. [Rhapsody of the Moon] builds on the base game mode, introducing new gameplay elements and increased difficulty levels, requiring you to take on an even more surreal and frenzied version of "Vienna." Suite of the Moon After loading up the new expansion, the "Suite of the Moon" feature becomes available. Before embarking on your exploration, you can visit the Suite of the Moon panel and choose from a variety of "Omen" modifiers. These modifiers add challenges to your gameplay, with each one increasing the current "Indulgence" value. The "Indulgence" value serves as an indicator for the difficulty level of your playthrough. Depending on this value, you may see changes in the appearance of the moon, with each moon phase representing a different difficulty bracket that adds even more dangerous effects to your playthrough. There are five difficulty brackets, or phases of the moon, determined by the current Indulgence value: [Misperception]: Low chance of increasing Stress at the start of the round. Very low chance of triggering Sudden Disaster. Clear Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +20%. [Illusory Sounds]: Low chance of increasing Stress at the start of the round. Low chance of triggering Sudden Disaster. Limited Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +20%. Enemy Control Resilience +20%. [Illusory Sight]: Moderate chance of increasing Stress at the start of the round. Moderate chance of triggering Sudden Disaster. Reduced Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +50%. Enemy Control Resilience +30%. [Illusory Touch]: High chance of increasing Stress at the start of the round. High chance of triggering Sudden Disaster. Majorly obstructed Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +100%. Enemy Control Resilience +50%. [Delirium]: High chance of significantly increasing Stress at the start of the round. Guaranteed to trigger Sudden Disaster. Severely obstructed Vision. Shard of Shadow gain +200%. Enemy Control Resistance +100%. Deployed characters get a decrease in Focus Chance. After completing an exploration, you will receive Shards of Shadow. These shards can be used to unlock new Catalyst incantations, Instinct buffs, or reset the cooldowns of certain Instinct buffs. If the Indulgence value is at 0, the Suite of the Moon will become inactive and no effects from Indulgence will impact you. You will also no longer be able to obtain Shards of Shadow. As the difficulty bracket of the Suite of the Moon increases, you'll be able to activate "Instinct" effects. By tapping on the broken mirror shards surrounding the image of the moon, a variety of Instincts can be chosen. The higher the difficulty bracket, the more Instincts can be activated, and the stronger their effects will be. After activating Instincts and clearing the second area, some of the Instincts will go into cooldown. Each time you clear the second area, or each area after that, these cooldowns are reduced by one round. Alternatively, you can use Shards of Shadow to instantly refresh the cooldowns. Stress in Battle After loading up the expansion, your characters will display a Stress meter while exploring. Actions taken during exploration will affect their Stress levels, which in turn will affect their behavior on the battlefield. When a character's Stress is low, they have a chance to trigger Vigilant Behavior based on their Afflatus. When a character's Stress is high, they have a chance to trigger Disorder Behavior based on their Afflatus. When a character's Stress reaches 50, they have either a low chance of triggering Focus Behavior, or a high chance of triggering Meltdown Behavior. Enemies also have Stress levels. The higher an enemy's stress, the more dangerous they become, forcing you to stay vigilant at all times. Core Content The core content is also updated—load up the new expansion to experience the following: New Catalysts: Two new Catalysts are added—the Silver Compass and the Rationality Loupe. New Path Nodes: Four new path nodes are added—Misty Domain, Into the Unknown, Perilous Encounter, and Treasure Trove. New Catalyst Incantations: Each Catalyst now has a new Catalyst incantation that can be unlocked by using Shards of Shadow. Some of these incantations can be cast by consuming Stimulus after completing certain path nodes. New Artefacts: Exciting new artefacts are added to the game. For more details, you will need to play through the new content yourself.

"Fugue of Reflections" is the latest expansion for "A Series of Dusks." This expansion adds a new ending to the base game and introduces character-exclusive artefacts known as [Acoustica]. More characters will rise to prominence in the pre-Storm Vienna. New Ending You don't need to have the expansion loaded up to experience the new ending, but you do need to have completed the [A Wish Granted] ending. Explore Vienna to see how to unlock the new conclusion. [Acoustica] Artefacts With the expansion loaded up, you can acquire [Acoustica] artefacts during exploration. These artefacts represent exclusive power ups for certain characters, and require the character to be in specific party positions to activate their effects. You can enhance Acoustica artefacts by meeting certain conditions. By meeting all enhancement requirements, an Acoustica artefact becomes [Fully Enhanced]. Based on how many fully enhanced artefacts are in your layout, additional [Harmonia] buff effects can be triggered, further strengthening your team. Completing the final path node of the Ring Road and defeating the [Impending Crisis] battle guarantees you one [Acoustica] artefact, prioritizing those exclusive to your current companion. You may also find Acoustica artefacts during exploration. [Current Characters with Acoustica Artefacts]: A Knight, Eagle, Voyager, Spathodea, Sonetto, Ms. NewBabel, Lilya, Lorelei, An-an Lee, Lucy, Jiu Niangzi, Anjo Nala, Lopera, Willow, Flutterpage, Barcarola, Charlie, Regulus, Druvis III, Matilda, 37, J, TTT, Semmelweis, Eternity, Medicine Pocket, Centurion, Sotheby, Melania, and Pickles. Tougher Battles With the expansion loaded up, enemy stats are increased. During an [Impending Crisis] and the final battle, you will also gain three powerful special incantations. Once used up, however, the enemies will become significantly stronger. Base Content The base content has also been updated with the following: New Path Node: The [Tuning Hall] path node has been added. New Combat Mechanics: Some battles can now include extra detrimental incantations that are added to your hand during combat. New Artefacts: [Acoustica] artefacts and [Fabled] quality artefacts have been added. More content awaits your discovery.

"The Effervescent Silence" is the final expansion of A Series of Dusks. The Effervescent Silence builds upon the base game mode by introducing new endings alongside the "Decisions" and "Tolls" mechanics, which require Timekeepers to make meaningful choices when selecting an area. Additionally, a new type of artifact, "Counteractive," has been added to counterbalance the effects of Tolls. New Ending Accessing the new ending does not require installing the expansion, but players must complete the ending "Wish Granted" first. The method to unlock it is left for Timekeepers to discover. Craftmaster's Favors With the update, Craftmaster's Favors will be introduced and do not require the expansion to be installed. At the end of an exploration, depending on the number of cleared areas (1/2/3/4/5), 2/3/4/6/8 Craftmaster's Favors will be automatically consumed, granting the same number of Keepsakes. "Decisions" and "Tolls" With the expansion installed, area selection will show Decision Effects and Toll artifacts. Each Decision Effect applies only to its respective area and disappears once you leave. Upon entering an area, Timekeepers must select and obtain one of three pre-revealed Toll artefacts and bear its Toll. Upon leaving the area, one of the remaining two Toll artefacts must also be chosen and obtained. Multiple Toll effects will continue to accumulate, even if they are the same effect. By toggling the Toll display option in the top right, Timekeepers can switch between viewing an artefact's base effects and the details of the Tolls. When making a Decision selection, Timekeepers may refresh once to reroll the available Decision effect and the Toll artefacts. While selecting a Toll artefact, refresh attempts can be used to change the artefact's Toll effect—but not the artefact itself. Fewer Path Nodes When the expansion is installed, certain areas will feature fewer path nodes, reducing the number of battle encounters. New Artefacts The expansion introduces Counteractive artefacts, which can be obtained during a playthrough. Additionally, more characters will receive their own Acoustica artefacts. For more information related to Acoustica artefacts, install the Fugue of Reflections expansion to explore their full potential. A set of sharp instruments, neatly wrapped in pristine white cloth. They pierce skulls, carve thoughts, and elevate the craft into an art form.
A lone chess piece among many, existing within the realm of imagination. While others drift and linger, this one leaps from its story, eager to charge into the next era.

Compact, convenient, and reliable—ever since its invention, these have been the hallmarks of its design. Arcanum managed to reach the finish line before human technology even took off. If only every user could control electricity, things would be much easier.
A well-worn clapperboard. With each retake, the title and scene numbers grow more scribbled, yet the sturdy wooden board remains dutiful and unchanged—Clap!
An invitation to a psychology salon from a spirited young scholar. A trembling quill seeks kindred minds, and the envelope carries her boundless insight and enthusiasm.
A humble set of painting tools. The colors are limited—perfect for children, or rather, for the future stars in the art world.
A handcrafted pendulum— a small echo of a budding artistic movement. A skilled user can sense its energy: fluid and unbound, like new branches stretching with life and potential.
A tool for straightening teeth—delicate, precise, and unyielding. With gentle force, it guides enamel and bone into perfect alignment over time.
A theater ticket to an enchanting performance of Tosca. The theater depends on its actors, and the actors on their craft—but no matter what, her portrayal of Tosca remains unmatched.
A clean, delicate, and immaculate headscarf. At this point, its symbolic value surpasses its practical use. Put it on—after all, who would suspect a maid?
Ice crystals, honeycombs, aromatic hydrocarbons—within finite geometry lies infinite meaning. Symmetry and balance are virtues, worthy of admiration and preservation.

A finely calibrated instrument designed to measure solar azimuth, first motion, and magnetic flux density—all to vectorize and analyze the fluctuations of a specific target's arcane fluctuations. Or, in simpler terms, it's a handy tool for gauging "ley energy."
A wooden model canoe, a crafted souvenir from across the ocean. Poets let their thoughts drift upon it—some glimpse rustic simplicity, others sense a deep yearning for home.
A peacock feather, one of the hundred eyes gifted by Hera. Handle it with care, for a tool of keen insight can just as easily become a blinding curse.

The gates stand open, the clock has stopped, and the tower's guardian is gone. And so, this journal becomes the object of greatest intrigue—clues within may reconstruct the truth, or weave an entirely new tale.
A simple, hand-stitched doll, found in street stalls and nestled by children's pillows. It has slowly learned to blink, to speak, to live—within the imagination of a child.
A practical reference book—sourced from mushrooms, shaped like mushrooms, and all about mushrooms. Warning: be mindful of hidden toxins while reading.
An instrument, a collectible. Priceless yet not for sale; ancient yet unverifiable; melodious yet now silent.

An instrument from an ancient civilization across the globe, yet favored by naturalist enthusiasts on Vienna's streets. A gentle tap lets it harmonize with birdsong and rustling leaves, composing a symphony of the wild.
The starry sky—the meeting place of reason and emotion. Amid endless revolutions, humans and arcanists converse, science and arcane skill complementing one another. She believes in it wholeheartedly.
Following the North Atlantic Drift, it merged into the waves of the river. The bottle's journey may rival the tale contained within.
A black veil, concealing grief and long-held wishes. In solemn silence, even tears become unnecessary.
A common flower—an unassuming yet passionate soul. In this era, silence and caution are virtues, but for a small bloom, such concerns are distant.
So much spinning, colliding, interlocking—given how busy they all are, does it even matter whether the result is tea or coffee?
It always aspired to be a solid, elegant shield, but alas, it was born too small and delicate. If the moment is right, perhaps it can bravely block a bullet aimed at your heart.
The street magician insists he never broke his promise—a king on a card is still a king. He suggests the Carbuncle seek out the rest of the deck to gather his own subjects.
A folded note, a piece of evidence, or a dose of poison? Choose freely what secret you wish to entrust—an ornate exterior always makes the best disguise.

It often tells the other pieces in the box about its origins—a suit of tiny armor with a soft body, its enamel glistening under the ocean's waves. If given another chance, it would still choose to be a shield.
Tick-tock, tick-tock. Over and over again, unwavering and constant. It does not bow to the chaos of the world, nor to the pressures of time.

Thanks to the legacy of this legendary arcanist, pointed hats and robes once became a fashion trend in the arcanum world. Even after styles changed, many still firmly believe that wearing his likeness enhances their incantations.
A cursed pencil tip—snapping at the worst possible moment. Some mysterious force compels you to keep it. "You never know when it might come in handy."
Excellent! A small, practical tool—who knows how many pencil tips await it? Use with care—pencils break more often than they sharpen.

When wielding a heart as tough and spiked as this, be sure to take care. No matter the reason, do not let its madness stain you.

A delicate conch shell, identical to the one held by that young girl. She once vowed to sing for every wave and every note—this is one of the ways she keeps her promise.

Roaring through endless white days, then falling silent in sleepless nights.
An unfamiliar world, capable of raising previously unexamined propositions and opening up new perspectives on the universe.
But … does it still matter?
"Transcendentality" … or perhaps … this pursuit that exhausts all things …
It is everything in the universe, the sum of all inquiries. It is truth, an existence beyond words.
It … cannot be reached, cannot be touched.
Shadows in the mind, phantoms that linger day and night.
They argue endlessly, filling every corner of my mind with the chaos of reality.
They just won't let me stop and think …
Vertin, please, find me a job here!
Anything—cleaner, bookkeeper, critter breeder in a factory … even a deckhand!
Oh, and if it's paid daily, even better—I swear I'm not implying you'd delay my wages.
Hmm? Well, of course, writing doesn't exactly put food on the table, does it?
Otherwise, I'd starve to death before I even finished my novel, haha …
But don't worry about me. I'm used to this kind of life. I'll manage just fine!
I understand now, Vertin.
You're trying to offer me a stable environment where I can write without worry, aren't you?
Indeed, as long as one lives, new and interesting things will always arise …
You never ask me questions, and you never waver.
You're always like this—no doubts, no hesitation, moving forward with absolute conviction.
What binds the prisoner, why the forest lies in shadow, who dwells beneath the mask …
No, these questions are meaningless. They are not yours to ask.
Only you may ask what's in your heart—I need not say a word.
Do you seek nothing? Is everything already meaningless to you?
No, you are not omniscient, but you accept your ignorance and pursue answers regardless.
That is why you are so different from everyone else. That … is good.
Perfect, Vertin. You came just in time!
I was just writing the opening scene of a character based on you. Your arrival is sure to inspire me even further!
"Vertin stood before me. With the entire Wilderness contained in this little suitcase, our meeting was bound to happen sooner or later. And so, the story began … "
Yes! This is exactly the scene I need!
… "Vertin brushed past me, walking toward the stone steps, passing through the pure white door, leaving the Wilderness behind. I had missed the perfect beginning."
The path of literature is always guided by eurekas and chances … Whatever the case, your arrival has given me new thoughts. Thank you, Vertin!
What exactly is "Transcendentality"?
Who are you talking to?
You don't need to do this.
What questions should I ask?
I have nothing to ask.
This is exactly why I'm here.
I was just passing by.

Roll the die one last time!
No longer heavy, no longer absurd—
Look, it gleams in the dunes of night.
Mental Cage

Complicated, endless, bewildering.
Reality, memory, illusion.
The existence of nonexistence.
Aleph.
Merlin, the Idealist.
Zahir, Paracelsus.
In the cell, in the mirror, in the chambers of the mind.
Off the Scene

Makeup removed, costume shed, the camera left behind.
The setting sun quietly mocks the endless rewrites in the margins.
How is one meant to act out the rest of their life?
A monologue, laced with irony.

I've adapted Ruinas Gloriosas y Directrices de Metáforas into an entirely new tabletop RPG—no need to understand it fully, you and your companions in the suitcase can all join in. Wait, Vertin, why the grimace?
Remember, each player takes their turn in a clockwise fashion. If you wish to share secrets, you may pass notes to one another.

The first time I encountered tabletop games was at a poetry reading. The professor was reciting a long, tedious narrative poem when a friend, whose name I no longer remember, leaned over and asked, "What's your character's stats?"
No, Vertin. Don't talk to me right now ... it's your turn. Stay in character and focus!
Shall we continue the last game? Don't worry, I've saved our progress. We can call Joshua and Jennifer over and start anytime!
Give me the right number of tokens, please. But … are you sure you want to buy this now? Oh, nothing, it's totally up to you!
"The cowboy says to the coachman: 'If we follow those cattle, maybe we'll find the shadows we lost.' " So, what's your next move? Will you follow them?
We've been through this loop a few times now. Is there anything you'd like to describe? How exactly are you taking the item? What's going through your character's mind?

"The fog ahead thickens, and even the whistling can't help them orient themselves. In the distance, the vague outline of an ancient temple emerges." We've now arrived at Templo de la Metáfora. Stay quiet, and watch out for monsters and traps.

Clear goals, well-placed monsters and traps, scaling rewards, distinct character setups, and a rule system that allows for every possibility … I made sure that Ruinas Gloriosas y Directrices de Metáforas was simple enough. So, what exactly makes it so hard to understand?
"The wind carries a whisper like an ancient poem through the fog." How do you plan to investigate that old stone platform?
Of course, I won't just tell you outright—it's all part of the metaphor. The clues are hidden in the previous lines. Think carefully …

"The old man's eyes light up with joy. 'My god, it's you! You've finally arrived—the ones who set everything in motion. I've waited for you for an entire century!'" Now, to touch the core of Templo de la Metáfora, you must solve a riddle.
This is a great treasure discovered in the "Laberinto de Símbolos." Its greatness lies in the fact that it is a part of us—a fragment, a symbol.
Congratulations! You've obtained your own "Golden Fleece." Relax, it's just a metaphor—it's got nothing to do with Jason or Medea.

A perfect rabbit—it has self-awareness, its actions are unpredictable, and the results it brings always weave a story.
Hmm? I think … this is the essence of Visceral Realism …
This item is incredibly rare, a gift left to you by the Gaucho Rider of 1975, a legendary cowboy from Sonora. Make good use of it.
Thank goodness, we've finally gotten past the cowboy and coachman bit ... Ahem. Now, quick, come with me—our grand adventure carries on!
This tale isn't solely about the cowboy and the coachman—it's about us as well. Honestly, is that so difficult to grasp?
Okay, the temple chapter is finished, but the story is far from finished.
I didn't expect you to loot the place clean. From what I saw, it was like putting sugar cubes next to an anthill.
You've taken every last item from the stone platform. This might be a bit of a spoiler, but you won't be able to collect anything else for now.
Well… that's certainly one way to go about adventuring … But you really should think about the hints I gave you, Vertin!
Actually, these items aren't part of the metaphor—okay, I did say, "everything is part of the metaphor," but these items really aren't!
I'm beginning to wonder … if exchanging items is what excites you most about the game?
Hey, I get that spending all your indicators at once is a common rookie mistake, but as the game master, I strongly suggest saving a few for the next part!
Excellent work! You now have all the essential items with you!

Hang on … I think you're misunderstanding something, Vertin. Ruinas Gloriosas y Directrices de Metáforas is not a game focused on base-building and combat … You don't need to set up fortifications in the village!
Another night passes, and now every villager is armed with a brand-new weapon and ten bottles of healing potion. The village walls have also been raised to ten meters tall …

First Day on the Job

A month ago, I graduated from Leningrad University and was assigned to work at the Plesetsk Cosmodrome. This launch base is a major joint project between the government and Laplace, and today is my first day on the job. I made sure to put on a brand-new pair of leather shoes and even ironed my suit. The building is magnificent, and the lab is fully equipped with all the latest technology—far more than I ever expected in my scientific career. My team leader, Andreas, seems to be a kind man. He told me there aren't too many rules here—just remember to wear your gear during safety inspections.

The base has pretty good meal subsidies, generous leave policies, and even holiday bonuses. Our whole team gets together to drink vodka every Friday night! If we're lucky, they'll even invite a nearby circus to come and perform ... Honestly, it's nothing like what I had imagined, but all the more reason to do my best to get the job done.
Houseplant Tending

Once winter sets in, the nights here become unbearably long. Back in Leningrad, I used to keep a few potted plants indoors to help lift my spirits. But here, my only option is to try my luck with the neighboring botany team. They're running a preliminary experiment to observe how plants grow in zero gravity by culturing sunflower explants.

I "bribed" Alyosha with a few bottles to look after a potted sunflower I picked out. He also promised to, if their experiment succeeds, hand it over for me to bring back to my dorm.

[Crossed out] My sunflower has turned completely moldy! Alyosha said he doesn't know why and that he'll start over with a new batch. He must've secretly used the clean bench for some other experiment and contaminated these materials! What an idiot!

[Crossed out] Another Foundation branch staff member is coming to the base. I heard he enjoys tinkering with little gadgets. Hopefully, he knows a thing or two about growing plants—then he can have my vodka instead.
An Unfunded Pursuit

I ran into a problem at work—a matrix calculation I've been stuck on for two full days. Andreas suggested I ask the materials team leader next door for help. He said she's brilliant at math and once helped the propulsion team optimize their advanced model—something they'd been struggling with for three months.

According to Andreas, she's the only one on her team. A rather unusual organizational structure. I've also heard her research is ... extraordinary, so extraordinary that it has no staff, no recognition, and, most importantly, no funding. Yet it sounds like she's willingly wasting her time there.

Well, I suppose there will always be people who waste their time on unfunded, seemingly pointless research. I remember hearing about this even back in university—like the one studying the flight dynamics of oak processionary moths, or the one trying to ignite a lamp kilometers away using optical arcane skills. Researchers like that usually end up obscure and unknown for their entire lives.

In any case, I plan to ask for her help tomorrow. Still, I admit, I really hope I don't end up in such a miserable situation.
Aurora Observation

Today I overheard the geography team talking about anomalies they've discovered in magnetospheric activity. I've always had terrible luck with auroras—I seem to miss them every time. Turns out there really is something unusual going on. Hopefully, they'll get to the bottom of it soon and give us a proper aurora forecast.

But they've barely started—the first step is placing observation instruments, and even that is still in its early stages. At least they've brought in a ley line researcher to help set things up. Poor girl's not even stationed at the base …

If I really want to see the aurora, I'd better just spend more time outside and hope for the best. After all, increasing the sample size is a key part of any research—I refuse to believe my luck can stay this bad forever!

Who knows, maybe I'll even run into that ley line researcher, Windsong. If she's willing to share a bit of her data with me ...
Unending Song

Someone forgot to turn off their record player. There's been faint music echoing through the lab hallways all morning—indistinct and constant like bees hovering near your ears. After a while I finally managed to catch the lyrics:

"The stars shine bright across the night,
I ask the void, what's past the light?

A voice calls out, my heart beats fast:
Will you stay still or rise at last?

I'll pack my things without delay,
And chase the stars that guide my way."

...

My team leader lost his patience before I did. He stormed out of the lab, searched around, and finally shut off that damn thing off. Thank goodness. Silence at last.

Anonymous Letter

Since Warden Tartuffe's transfer, the authorities never contacted Comala Prison again. And ever since Manus Vindictae's involvement, operations here have temporarily been placed under Merlin's supervision. Welcome to Comala Prison. For any inquiries, please leave a letter in the mailbox at the entrance or call the number listed below.
Interim Report: Beyond the Boundaries

This moth-luring experiment was a complete success, with no significant psychological abnormalities observed. It's presumed that I've grown accustomed to this work environment. I will now proceed with the usual summary report.

This is Murphy's, and this is Bugsy's. Take them, and don't forget to thank Henry. He chose to wear the mask so you could have these pills and food to keep your free literature alive. Praise be to his selfless commitment.

When you see one human, there's likely forty more beyond your sight. I know, I know, they're all the property of the Administrators, and we have a deal with them—no slaughter without cause in prison. But isn't our hatred for humanity reason enough? Is it not?

Good morning, Murphy, Bugsy. You two know the rules better than I do. Henry's traded goods are running out. Who's next to wear the mask? Poetry isn't going to fill our stomachs. Does no one really want to follow in Henry's footsteps?
Ah, time to say goodbye. Why are so few of you willing to come? Since when did you all become so opinionated? Fine, an extra participant in the ritual is always welcome. Follow me.

I get it now. From today onward, I am Manus Vindictae, not the Order of Enlightenment. Names don't matter, but when do I get to operate outside? Zeno's forces are still enforcing martial law? Why me? I haven't even done anything to provoke them!

And now you're telling me the Zeno faction in Brazil is on our side? They almost killed me back there! Just who are we, what are we supposed to be doing? Until I get some real answers, I refuse to—what? A cruise trip? Fine, fine, I'll put up with this a little longer.

The lead, she's up there socializing in the banquet hall, while I'm shoveling coal in the boiler room?! This isn't the cruise experience I signed up for! I can't balance a pilgrimage and shovel coal at the same time like the others!

Following this endless pilgrimage, I have finally reached the world's end. Sigh, maybe the real treasure was the hardships we faced along the way. Now, my journey ends in this prison—entering this cage is my escape from the world's cage ... Wait, what!? Now we have to go even farther south?!
"Yes, the prison we're heading to is fascinating—a place where no one is truly themselves. As for the warden ... I know him well. You can stay as long as you like; I assure you, he won't interfere."
"There's nothing more to be done. Just let things take their course. This display cabinet … I'll keep it for myself."

"You lost Ms. Urd? What a disappointment. You want me to give you a chance to 'make it right'? No, we don't tolerate failure here. You will get nothing but punishment. Meanwhile, I will search for Ms. Urd myself."

"Thank you for your concern, but I'm fine. It's just a minor side effect from the arcane skill. And here we are—watch your step. The path ahead is treacherous. We're about to climb a mountain that isn't known to anyone"

Regarding your question—whether I have contacts within the Foundation or Laplace. I do answer some researchers' inquiries from time to time. No need to speculate, Ms. Grace. This does not count as espionage.
Regrettably, I'm not the warden of this prison. If you want to know more about Manus Vindictae's past, perhaps Merlin can tell you.

No need for irrelevant questions. I'm sure you've already pieced together a rough idea of who I am. Years ago, I crossed paths with Mr. Forget Me Not during a brief stint researching the Fountain of Youth. That's all there is to it.

Ms. Urd has left. As per our discussion, Merlin did not stop her and even managed to hide her movements from Manus Vindictae. But ultimately, she made her own decision—to head for Antarctica and seek her own fate. This is something neither of us can change for it may be the will of fate itself.

I have a grim suspicion—Urd may have chosen to side with Manus Vindictae. According to the moth's intel, she went to Antarctica of her own accord to join them. At the very least, it seems she's come to some kind of understanding with them.

There's no doubt that Manus Vindictae's headquarters is in Antarctica. That would explain why, even after dismantling so many of their hideouts, we've failed to make a real dent in their numbers. It's reasonable to assume they have some way of withstanding the "Storm," which only functions in Antarctica—and their deployment there likely exceeds anything we previously estimated.
The movements of the Zeno rebels remain unclear. Unless they have taken no action after defecting, they must be preparing for a large-scale military operation.

This experiment showed significant noise and signs of possible self-dialogue, limiting the amount of usable data. Preliminary speculation points to an anomaly in the moth's condition—or perhaps an undetected issue with my own health. Regardless, I request that this situation be reported to the appropriate authorities.

Sylvie is doing well. Maxime and Alexandre always help her think in parallel, and Monique, as usual, keeps things under control at critical moments. And me? I didn't just hibernate. The local literature has filled the gaps in my collection that Sylvie once ruthlessly discarded.

The Melusines were deeply moved by these authors' vivid portrayals of suffering and death, yet even within the darkest themes, the authors' exploration of new paths brimmed with vitality, dreams, and a defiant sense of romanticism.

Whenever I read the literature to her, her memories become unusually vivid, and she recalls one line in particular with striking clarity from Pasternak's February: "The truest verses arise by chance, tempered in the fire of pain."

Of course, there's no way to verify this and Sylvie would never admit it, but I believe she's the most romantic in our family. Or maybe the second-most. After me. I wish you were part of the Dubois family too. That way, you'll truly understand what Sylvie's memories feel like when she sees a shooting star.

I truly hope we can talk about all of this someday. Maybe after Sylvie's little challenge is complete, you could visit Plesetsk. I promise Sylvie and I will both be warmly waiting to welcome you.

Your dear friend,

Estelle

I didn't know this table was their turf! They're still biting me! Hey, who's playing music at a time like this?! Somebody, help!

...

As many of you have read in academic journals, the theoretical feasibility of teleportation incantations is not determined by distance.

However, the farther the distance, the more interference factors there are, and to this day, we still don't know exactly why. Thus, long-distance teleportation has always been considered the realm of pure fantasy.

However, during the extreme conditions just before the "Storm," we gathered a vast amount of arcane energy fluctuation data from outer space to the Earth's surface.

After repeated cross-analysis, we finally discovered a stable arcanum waveform capable of anchoring teleportation incantations. My teammate, she gave it a misleading name—"Pulsar Waveform." I suppose that was her way of being poetic or something.

...

Yes, I hear some of you murmuring that this is purely experimental, lacking theoretical proof and impossible to replicate. That's true. But the fact is, over the past few weeks, we've tested it repeatedly. As long as you simulate this waveform near the destination and there's enough arcane energy, you can achieve teleportation with up to 95% accuracy.

...

That's all I wanted to share today. I believe that one day in the distant future, with a complete theoretical framework, teleportation could become a field that outpaces aerospace itself. But even now, what we've uncovered is a stable, practical technology—perfect for food delivery.

Binary Dust

Look closely—this is the 20th century!

It burst through the door before anyone could react, rushing in at full speed. Humanity barely had time to take to the skies before it was already reaching for the surface of the moon.

Silicon chips began to gleam across new fields, gradually revealing an extraordinary vision. Screens and data streams built a new world shaped by new desires, like an ouroboros shedding its skin.

The LSCC maintained its cutting-edge spirit. Employees turned offices into gaming arcades; bookshelves were crammed with the Global Catalog, Tumbling Stone, and neatly printed cognitive enhancement research papers.

Laboratories in Palo Alto were lit all night, bright enough to dull the stars overhead. What did it matter? Compared to those great advances of the era, everything else was just dust in the wind.

In a small apartment, nine pairs of eyes fixated on the scrolling numbers. The machines, the theories, the roaring processors, and glowing monitors never commented on themselves, nor did they incite any religious awe. When parents spoke about personal computers, they praised them for making communication easier, weaving the world closer together.

Yes, this was the reality she and her siblings chose to pursue.

Higher than the White Birch

This is the vibrant eighties.

New things are everywhere. Volga drivers roll down their windows to grab a Pepsi from roadside vendors. A little bear plush sits quietly on a shop counter, watching the crowds wave their goodbyes. Inside the circus tents, the shows go on as scheduled. Troupe members deliver just the right amount of thrill and excitement to the audience, then relieve the lingering tension with hot meals after the curtain falls. She rests safely inside this eggshell of a world—beyond it, chaos and the human condition churn.

Her troupe loves to share stories with her during their breaks. Night school classmates eagerly bring her news and gossip. Myths, legends, and ongoing events in the real world tangle together like the warm, rough knots in a bear cub's fur. Not every story actually happens, but every single one overflows with hope for the future, enough to make you forget the frostbite in your fingers, the endless lines, the long journeys and exhaustion.

There is an ideal here. A yearning for a steadier, safer life. If you can reach the cosmos, what pain or death could ever defeat you?

That's why she keeps stepping onto the narrow wire again and again, chasing a higher vantage point.

Higher than that taut wire. Higher than the waving flags.

High enough to look down on this glass sphere of a world—until everything on the ground blurs together, and nothing seems separate anymore.

If the snow mound can collapse once, then it can collapse again. And again.

Change and upheaval teach people to keep their distance from unreadable prophecies, only to push them further into the current. A few manage to keep hold of the reins of their horses, tempering their lives for the sake of another unreadable, elusive word: freedom.

To the children struggling to get by, the wild hares darting through the woods mattered more than the occasional news from town. Back then, "a life adrift" was just a phrase, it carried no weight and held no meaning for them. There were so many languages and words to name the world before them, yet not a single one could describe the world as it was. Long before they could make sense of what was unfolding around them, he and his siblings had already seen how the fire came to an end.

"What do you see, Lyonya?" his brother asks, mimicking ataman-like solemnity. He sets down his knife and buries the half-carved wood in the snow, staring into the distance.

The eyes of the birch trees gazed back in silence. The snow reflected the blinding light of the sun.

"Nothing. Just snow."

It was just an endless, eternal field of snow.

So here you are, calling out to the cosmos, hoping the vast unknown will serve up an answer unbounded by gravity.
To the naked eye, the water in the Wilderness looks very clean. However, there is no evidence that it is suitable for sustaining life ...
Vertin, have you ever observed signs of fish in the rivers and lakes around here?
Just Abang Akus? Ha, never mind—as if a snake could make hors d'oeuvres out of something that size.
You know, Vertin, one of us has been thinking about catching some fish in the Wilderness for a snack.
… If there were any. So there's no need for you to worry. Now, it's just me watching over my own little fish, making sure they don't get snatched up.
Hear that? If even Vertin hasn't seen them, they're probably not in the area.
That's right, it turns out one of us decided that lake fish might make for a tasty treat, and by the time I realized it, he'd already been sneaking out for several nights ...
All's well that ends well, I suppose. You can stop fretting over fish that may not exist, and I can stop losing sleep over him sneaking off.
I've been observing these critters … Have you noticed? They're constantly picking out friends for themselves.
They're quite amiable when with their chosen friends, but a few of the Carbuncles can't help but start brawling the moment they see each other.
No ... that's not it. This is simply a matter of personal interest.
These critters always remind me of the little creatures I once cared for … especially when they dart after specks of dust in those little clusters of theirs. Such carefree little things.
I was just wanting to confirm ... does Ms. NewBabel need any help? I might be able to lend a hand.
I'm flattered, but ... who could possibly manage a thing like that out here in the Wilderness?
I've only managed to recognize a handful, so I'm tracing their paths and studying which companions they choose.
It reminds me of how I learned about the stars as a child. You need to start off with the ones that stand out most, and soon the whole constellation begins to take shape ...
A touch of patience is all they ask ... and all they ever really need.
I've noticed the snow in the suitcase vanishes quicker than one might expect. It melts right along with the ever-changing weather.
The weather here is wildly unpredictable, yet strangely, I've never come across a single tale or rumor about weather phenomena inside a suitcase.
Because this kind of uncertainty and change often serves as fertile ground for myths and legends, people will go to great lengths to find patterns in what otherwise defies understanding.
Storytelling is our oldest method of making sense of the unknown, and the simplest ...
And I've certainly crossed paths with my fair share of storytellers here, in this suitcase of yours.
Now that's not really something I'm good at. As you know, I just have a knack for collecting stories.
How about a change of topic? I was wondering ... do you know how Han Zhang's been lately?
This episode of Approaching Arcanum is almost at an end, and as tradition dictates, no show is complete without ...
A lucky audience member! Hey there, Vertin!

Oh, right … we haven't technically built up any traditions yet. After all, this is our very first episode, so calling it a "tradition" is a bit premature. We'll need some empirical evidence before we can make that claim!
Stick around for the next show, and the one after that, and soon enough, talking about "tradition" and saying "as tradition dictates" will become a tradition in itself.
Yes, this is the part where we introduce you to our listeners ... and offer our sincerest thanks.
Although this wasn't the smoothest of shows, and in the end, we only managed to air it over the radio, you've stuck with us through thick and thin.
So we came to one conclusion—that if anyone deserves the title of our inaugural lucky audience member, it's most certainly you!
Timekeeper, I've heard the students at the SPDM hardly ever get to see the outside world before graduation.
Was it the same for you?

Does that mean you've never been to a circus before? Did you ever sneak out after school with your classmates, just to squeeze into a big top tent like sardines, passing around a single piece of chocolate ...?

Not that I ever had any experience like that, I only meant that I think most schoolchildren share a moment like that at some point. I used to see kids just like that ... before I became part of the show myself.
From then on, I was in the spotlight. There's no time to watch from the crowd when you're preparing for a performance. I had a job to do, and I had to do it right.
I heard about it from a Laplace researcher, and it made me wonder ... perhaps you've never seen a circus performance before?

I used to think circus performances were quite common, and that laughter and gasps were a regular part of the shows. But it turns out that, in different times and places, things aren't always like that.

That's why I'm preparing a performance here in the Wilderness. It won't be very polished, and it certainly won't be as good as the shows we used to put on, but I want to relive a piece of the past that once brought joy to so many people ...
I want to share that joy once more. Will you come to see it?
Ah, perfect timing. I believe you may have dropped this.
It rolled into the little space between the sofa and the rug. I just happened to catch sight of it.
Happy to help. Your suitcase is such a peaceful little haven, and in my experience, people are more likely to misplace things in the places they feel most at home.
I wouldn't really call it wisdom or anything like that, just a personal feeling. There aren't many places in the world where you can truly feel at ease, but your suitcase is definitely one of them.
That wasn't my intention, but thank you for your generosity.
I don't usually treat lost items as collectibles. I wouldn't want my storeroom looking like a lost-and-found. Kidding, of course.
I've seen Abang Akus.
Not that I've seen.
So you've taken on one of Ms. NewBabel's requests?
You mean you can tell every Carbuncle apart?
Why do you say that?
Why don't you cook up a story.
Tradition?
Lucky audience member?
Yes.
Why do you ask?
Thanks, I was just looking for this.
It's all yours.

Expedition Team Log

Day One For polar explorers, the romance lies in challenging the last great unknown. McMurdo Sound, on the northwest edge of the Ross Ice Shelf—this is the heart and launch point of Antarctic expeditions. Yes, we've arrived. Day Three At Mack's shout, we all stepped out of camp and saw auroras in broad daylight. Even in the coldest place on Earth, it was a rare and beautiful sight … but no, something about it felt wrong. Day Seven We've lost two members … We still don't know what happened. The sun is gone from the sky, though it should still be daytime. … Something is wrong with this place. Day Twelve? It's fine. We're close to the coast. Any passing ship will see us … and my distress signal. Day ……………… Do not seek the truth. Do not go deeper into Antarctica. Do not proceed!
Antarctica Survival and Food Guide

Available Equipment for Polar Environments Due to Antarctica's harsh climate and extreme conditions, standard expedition tools, such as compasses, are often ineffective. Prior to landing, ensure essential specialized equipment is prepared, including diesel generators, snowmobiles, and radio transmitters. Conduct a complete inventory check in advance. Food Storage Recommendations For portability and preservation, canned food is ideal. Beef broth with turnips and potatoes is recommended for quick nutrition. A small reserve of Neptune chocolate is also advised for emergencies. Contingency Measures for Extreme Scenarios A form of "black algae" has been observed spreading within the Antarctic Circle. This pseudo-algal organism appears to be a hybrid of ancient microbial strains and unidentified bio-fibers. Preliminary analysis confirms it is non-toxic. In worst-case scenarios, it may be consumed for sustenance. ※No guarantees are made regarding its effects.
Endgame Solver

Simone: Madam Lucy, are you preparing for the chess exhibition match with the vice president? Lucy: Your inference is correct, Simone. Given my unsatisfactory results in the past two events, I find it necessary to further improve my calculation speed and explore a wider range of possible board states. Simone: I do not know much about chess, but I've heard that brute-forcing through opening moves isn't a practical way to play. Lucy: Perhaps. But every player must learn to solve the endgame puzzles laid by their predecessors more efficiently. When searching for the right path, systematically going through all possibilities is still the best approach. Simone: But this is just an exhibition match. The data loss from earlier is still affecting you—you shouldn't push yourself so hard over it. Lucy: You misunderstand, Simone. I am not a professional chess player—the notion of winning or losing this match holds little significance for me. The same goes for the vice president. The victory or defeat she truly cares about lies beyond the chessboard. Lucy: I am simply preparing for this match sincerely, following human social conventions. As for the vice president—she is a player who truly desires victory. I suspect it is that very desire that sharpens her skill. But unfortunately, when it comes to the one "match" she truly cares about, I have already stepped away from the table.
Tracking Igor

We've lost track of Igor and his forces, but it's confirmed they've reached the interior of Antarctica.

Based on the final intelligence reports we received, their likely encampment is far from the Ross Sea landing site—hardly an ideal position for an ambush or interception. From both a terrain and a strategic standpoint, it seems more like a location chosen for a swift retreat.

Currently, we have no way of discerning Admiral Igor's true intentions. For now, however, it's clear that his forces will not pose the primary threat when the Zeno Expeditionary Force launches its assault on Antarctica.
The Mother Spirit

The "Mother Spirit" is a deity worshipped by certain communities within the Arctic Circle. According to legend, after she casts endless sunlight over the North Pole, she falls into slumber at the edge of the Antarctic, awaiting her next awakening—a cycle that brings eternal day to the north once more. In regions where this myth is told, the "Reindeer Festival" emerged. During the festival, youths compete in reindeer handling, and the year's champion becomes the Mother Spirit's chosen, marking the occasion by sounding the great drum in praise of the sun, raising the proudest banner, and declaring a victory that flutters in the wind. It is said that a lost child who passes through the Mother Spirit's body glimpses her soul and receives a piece of "good news" powerful enough to change the course of their life. ■ Preliminary assessment: This is most likely a fabricated local myth with no credible value for further reference.

Hissabeth's new fascination with the Spinning Wheel showed progress today, as she managed to stay conscious in the lake for 17 seconds before falling asleep.

As Isolde sang alone in her room, a voice outside her window began to harmonize with hers.

After treating her last patient, the exhausted Mesmer Jr., who had been struggling with insomnia, finally fell asleep while counting sheep.

Mr. Karson and Sotheby used to share food with the neighborhood too!
If only we met in a normal era ... This APPLe misses the dinner we had before the "Storm."
Wow, a committee of 40 ... They could throw a big party after every meeting!

And the Doge, the host of the party, could have as much cake as he wanted because his guests would throw it at him.
Is it just me or this villa actually smells nostalgic?
Nostalgic? What do you mean? Like the smell of a wine cellar? Mr. Karson wouldn't let me go there when we lived in the mansion.
Yes, you've got it precisely. It's a smell that feels both ... sweet and sad.
This APPLe must pay respect to whoever runs charity organizations like this. They've given the orphans a place to go.
Many of my friends, who come from different eras, grew up in orphanages, but thanks to their teachers, they are not any less virtuous than others.
They are the embodiment of people's kindness.
It's just like an artery ...
Pumping "blood" to the heart of the kingdom.
I like this bridge! It feels like a secret tunnel that allows me to sneak away from Mr. Karson.
Dead or alive, people always want a nice place to rest in.
What? You mean people rest in these stone boxes?
That's a really thick blanket they cover on themselves!
Wow! A gathering of Auto Islands! Are Typhon and Jupiter here?
Well ... I don't think the people here are as friendly as you think, Ms. Sotheby.
I see! The evil Jupiter must have lurked somewhere nearby!
But there's no need to worry! Typhon will keep us safe!
Hmm ...?
What's wrong, Mr. X?
We made a mistake in the experiment: one of the observers has gone on a different time track than the others'.
That sounds horrible ... Will it cause any danger?
Well, if you see the observers as marbles rolling in a run race, this one is setting off from a much further place ...
But still it will reach the same destination as others' in the end, so the situation is still under control. No need to worry about its influence on reality.
It's just that she'll have to spend years living alone before the others arrive.
Is there anything we can do for her? This is not part of the plan, after all ...
We have an emergency to deal with before that. Observer No.4's data is "corrupted," but he's still connected to the stage.
Going astray is like a good trip compared to this.
No.4? Is that ... Mr. APPLe?
Don't move, Mr. Leonardo. There's a Nightmare lying on your shoulder. It's dangerous ...
Nonsense. I didn't hire any model called Nightmare ...
Leonardo
I must be mistaken then. That could be an underdeveloped Succarath. Look, it's greeting me ...
You two can barely stand. I suggest we wait for the illusion to wear off before we go.
La Volpe
Greetings, Mr. Fox. Allow me to introduce you to this Succarath. Unlike the ones in stories, it's actually very friendly!
Look. It's won't get mad even if you pull its tail like this.
I can't breathe ... *cough* Are you sure it's not mad?
... Let's take some more rest. Emm, Ms. Sotheby, do you mind letting go of Leonardo's mantle?
This APPLe can't believe he just watched The Bacchae in the Theater of Dionysos ... This will be a day to remember.
The performance was intoxicating; I could almost smell wine in the air ...
Wait ... *sniff* That's the smell of wine for real ...
Hmm? The offering is talking ... I-I must be experiencing the ecstasy of the god!
Female Believer
