Did you miss the Dionysia parade? Too bad, my friend ... Then you should at least try the wine I made!
Thank you, but ... Uhm!
How's that? Haha! Have as much as you want! We shall be enlightened by Dionysos through his grace ...
Oh ...
This feels good ... I-I think I get it now ...
That's right! Step out of yourself and get closer to the god. That's "ecstasy" ...
Step out of myself? Indeed, this APPLe feels ... *burp* so free ...
Where are you going? Oh, you must be stepping out of yourself to meet Dionysos, haha! So long, my friend! So long!
So, this is the "perfect plan" that you promised would work?
Alexios
Even a moron could find such an obvious clue! Thanks to you, they were drawn to the temple, and I could only talk trash and left like an idiot!
It-It was an accident, Deimos ...
Cultists
Only few should have noticed the ribbons. Besides, they didn't find out our plan ...
An accident? You mean my sword could cut off Kassandra's head if nothing went wrong in your stupid plan?
You'd better give me a reason not to cut off yours "accidentally"!
P-Please spare me! In fact, we have a backup plan for this situation ...
We've hung the ribbons in many other temples. I'm sure the message will be conveyed anyhow ...
And you'll have a second chance!
Kassandra, I might have found some other relevant symbols here.
Hmm? I must have missed them. Show me.
Kassandra
Here. A large triangle consisting of smaller ones. It was carved by this woman.
I've seen this before—no need to worry about it. She must be one of those geeks who study Pythagoreanism. They are simply into ...
Mathematics, right?
Do they name themselves with numbers?
Haha, looks like you know them well. What else do you see?
Gold leaf with strange symbols on it.
Life, the truth, Orpheus ... Hmm ...
I think they have something to do with a certain cult; it is said they could communicate with the dead through gold leaf like this. Did you hear anything when you touched it?
No.
I guess so. Only one tenth of the rumors we hear is true, in my experience ... So, no more symbols?
That's all.
Good.
Personally speaking, the building is now regarded with far more importance than it was originally intended to have.
What is rare is dear, you know. Like my exclusive radio show, if you didn't follow, it's gone for good! It will only worth more and more!
Time will tell the value of great deeds!
Meetings? Ugh, so boring and a waste of this terrific stage!
Look how perfect it could fit for a rock live show! If I got to hold one here, I assure you all the pains and trouble will be blown away!
Actually, Captain ... I think they still need SOME time to fully understand the art form of rock music.
Captain, this is the place where they collect their shipwreck trophies ...
Hey, I'm thinking ... any chance they can salvage those records that went under with APPLe I?
I'm afraid not, given it's not their trophy ...
Not even if we pay them 100 bottles of Dr. Papper? I mean, it could work if they also drink Dr. Papper on Dionysia.
Such a majestic temple… Perhaps it suggests that Apollo held a role just as vital as Dionysos in the lives of the Athenians.
Well, now I'm starting to miss that grape hair boy. Who would have thought it?
He must have more shared topics with them than we do.
Oh yes, that "thunder guy"! I know him. He's the one controlling the lightning in the sky and light up the earth, or at least that's what I've been told.
Of course they'll build a temple for him. I mean, imagine how dazzling his light effect could be! It's a must-have in any great parties!
That's not entirely wrong, but ... I have to remind you that this "lightning technician" is also known for having a thunderous temper.
Temple of Hera, the queen of Olympian gods ... It surly has its unique charm. Look at these delicate and exquisite sculptures on the pillars, depicting only the mortal women in the Heraia ...
... rather than the gods or the king.
Great minds think alike! I can see how they agree that all the great singers are from grassroots.
It's a sorrowful story. After all the utmost effort the artist had spent, he never lived to see the praise he deserved ...
Oh ... Let's salute "Phidias"! With our utmost respect!
We shall always remember him, just as we will always remember APPLe—only the greatest ship ever!
People are forgetful. If you ask this APPLe, even if the relics of the Akropolis still stand today, history could easily be interpreted differently from how it is now.
The fallen columns might have been the result of an accident; the red brick ruins could be the execution ground for heroic sacrifice.
Oh, I got what you mean! Like how people often mishear lyrics and come up with something that makes no sense at all!
I can't make heads or tails of it ... Ezio, I'm afraid I'll be needing those keen, all-seeing eyes of yours.
Leave it to me.
Hmm, haven't I seen this symbol somewhere before ...?
It's exactly like those on the frescos! This is getting interesting ... Quick, let's see what's on the next page!
Hooray! I can't wait anymore!
One moment.
Aha! There you are!
The strokes and colors look familiar ... Now, whose style could this possibly be?
Do you see these lines? Objects can be made to look larger or smaller depending on where they are on the line. Using them, we can create a convincing sense of depth!
Wow!
Now, try extending them and see what happens!
Exactly. These are orthogonals or perspective lines—These lines spring from the vanishing point.
There are many other orthogonals on the painting. Try looking for the rest!
Tell me what you need. I can see the lines, plain as day.
Ezio, could you mark the orthogonals for us?
Keep extending them back until they converge once more at the "vanishing point"—where everything disappears.
So now we have four vanishing points.
The next step is to connect the vanishing points in pairs to form two lines.
The point where the two lines intersect on the blank wall is ...
"Under the Waning Glow"!
And that's the very answer we've been looking for.
Ah ... the sole point of convergence. What's our next move?
Hmm ... Ms. Vertin did say something about placing this APPLe at the vanishing point, didn't she?
That is correct.

An Unfinished Letter

There hasn't been much progress these last few days, but I studied the cipher again and decided that light was the answer—it was the only thing that could cause a reaction on the frescos. I'm going to re-design the experiment, but I need some inspiration. Could you collect more information about the frescos for me? Their locations, contents, number—anything will do. And I have some bad news: you are not the only one who wants me to crack the puzzle. Right before I wrote this letter, I managed to escape from a group of Templars. I'll set off for Florence in days, and ... (The letter abruptly stops here, as if someone interrupted the writer)
The "Golden Apple"

Ezio,
We are still looking for information about the "Golden Apple," as what we have cannot confirm its connection with the Piece of Eden. Word is that it has something to do with the secret chamber that used to house the Compliners. Whatever it is, it has drawn a lot of attention and you should be prepared for trouble.
And there's one more thing you should know: we've heard the apple snore like a human several times, which is unbelievable. Some said the Piece of Eden came alive over the past few years, but I highly doubt it.
Finally, we couldn't find Leonardo in Milan and I think he's in trouble. I'll keep you posted.

Niccolò Machiavelli
Diary with Paint on It

March ■■ Good heavens! I never thought linear perspective would be so hard to learn. I asked plenty of dumb questions, but Uccello answered all of them patiently and kept encouraging me. Father said I needed more practice too. March ■■ The lords kept throwing out new ideas, but Uccello always managed to talk them down. The fresco is getting more and more lively and artistic ... It is an honor to witness the birth of a masterpiece. March ■■ Following Uccello's advice, everyone tried that magical paint, including the most stubborn ones among us. I hope these days never end. April ■■ We are being dismissed. My skills have improved over these last few days. Uccello generously shared his paint with us before he left. The story is coming to an end. We have to leave the painting unfinished ... I've put away the paint, but its odor remains in my mind.
The Book Merchant's Notebook

[Southeast Corner of the Room] Piles of a sand-quicklime mixture, a bit of carbon dust, several nails and punched paintings. Just some leftover materials they didn't use. Worthless to me. [East of the Room] Two carving knives, several brushes, and a piece of glass. Nothing worth taking. The glass looks like some kind of lens. Dried Paint They didn't seal the paint can with beeswax! What a waste ... A dozen letters and several intact paintings. Finally, something worth taking. I can make a new manuscript and name it Mystery of the Frescos or Wonders of Florence ... No, I need a more eye-catching title. [North of the Room] Scaffoldings. Collapsed. Messy carvings: a group of dancing human symbols, their meaning is unclear. Is this a signature? I bet the scaffoldings were broken by the ones who were fighting.

Dear Uccello, It's been too long since we parted. I heard you went back to Pratovecchio. Is it still as beautiful as you said it was? I still remember what it looked like in your painting—a sea of olive and fig trees. Those days we spent together were just like a dream. I've always wanted to pick up the brush once again, but my life is already occupied by meaningless housework ... They said I didn't have much time left. (Blurred) But I came back without letting anyone know. When I left a new signature at the corner, I found that our friends had done the same thing. Lippi, Giovanni ... What about you? I'm never sure since you've always been so unpredictable. How are you doing? Hopefully, you're still drawing. In fact, I know you are. Bianca

Origin of the Oracle

"Decades ago, a small group of people gathered around a theory. They believed it could be used to control the space. To them, the world moved between two forces: order and chaos."

But some among them fell too deeply into chaos. From that descent, the Cult of Kosmos was born.

Wearing masks, black robes, and the image of a serpent that devours all, they made no effort to hide their ambition and greed. They claimed to desire order, but sought to build it through war—an order that served only themselves. And so, the Greek world was plunged into endless conflict.

To prolong the war, they orchestrated an event in 446 BCE. Within the smoke-filled temple of Delphi, a trembling, feverish female voice delivered a sentence upon a newborn boy:
"To prevent Sparta's fall, the child must fall first."
Bound by the divine will of the oracle, the Spartan Gerousia left the family no choice. One rainy night, the infant was cast from Mount Taygetos.

Though he survived the fall, his descent through life never stopped. As if swallowed by the serpent itself, he no longer belonged to his family—or to any place under the Sun.

Florence Never Fades

Like many who live through great eras of history, the people of Renaissance Florence rarely grasped the weight of the age they inhabited.

They were preoccupied with the price of wool, the exchange of florins, and adding the last brushstroke to a mysterious smile. Unknowingly, they shaped a new reality—one where an ancient idea bloomed once more from the shadows: that mankind is born free.

This idea, a fragile spark at first, inspired countless souls to rise in its name. It carried the ancient struggle into the modern world, tinting the war between Assassins and Templars with a vivid shade of Florentine red.
At the heart of this conflict stood the Auditore family. One generation. Two. Three? Only their successors know the final count.

But whatever the number, the world remains in balance.
After centuries of bloodshed, the sun over Florence still shines with the same generosity, warming saints and sinners alike. This city, instinctively tilting her left cheek toward tradition, can't help but glance to the right, gazing toward a brilliant, uncharted future.

Spartan Inheritance

In 480 BCE, King Xerxes I of Persia led a massive invasion into Greece. At the narrow pass of Thermopylae, King Leonidas of Sparta and his 298 Spartan warriors—joined by a handful of soldiers from other city-states—used the terrain to hold back an army that outnumbered them many times over.
Leonidas and his men fought fiercely for three days, withstanding wave after wave of Persian assault, until they were finally overwhelmed and fell where they stood.

The war has long since passed, and the legend now rests in the verses of wandering epics. And the hero's broken spear, preserved through bloodlines, lives on in its passing.

Decades later, in Lakonia—briefly spared from the tides of war—a descendant of Leonidas was born and raised. A spirited girl, trained in Spartan discipline by her father, a respected general of the polis. Her mother had bestowed upon her that legendary broken spear, forging in the child both the art and spirit of Sparta.
But one rainy night, to the sound of her mother's wails, that very father cast his daughter from the cliffs.

Perhaps it was Tyche's mercy. The fall did not deliver her to the underworld, but instead marked the beginning of something else—a legend. She stood, lifted her eyes, and there it was: the broken spear that had fallen with her, resting quietly under the moonlight.

And so, it finally met the moment to fight for its master again.
A Song Drifting Through Athens

The following passage was recorded by Vertin and others, attributed to an Athenian bard. According to the bard, it tells the tale of a mercenary known only as "The Eagle Bearer":

Tell me, Muse, of the legendary mercenary,
The western wind that swept across the wine-dark sea, ever wandering,
Who met many people and city-states, their cunning and guile,
And through the vast oceans and the forests of the gods,
Endured endless suffering in body and spirit,
Seeking kin, seeking home.
Goddess, daughter of Zeus, sing us her tale.

She once walked the soil of Phokis, where Apollo's priestess
Altered her prophecy for her.
When the west wind reached Attika,
The Athenians welcomed her with joyous feasts.
Winged words carried her to Lakonia,
Where she stood before the king of Lakedaimon,
And her arrival forced him to face a dark fate.
As he turned to flee, a spear pierced his chest.
The king collapsed, his armor clattering against the stone.

Time flowed on, and the end came as it does for all.
By the will of the gods, she found her way home,
Returned to Sparta, though peace still eluded her.
When she was back in her mother's arms, the gods rejoiced,
All but one—the distant god of fear,
Son of Ares—held fast to his spite
Against god-like Kassandra,
Until she stood once again before the cliff where it all began.

Assassins can move between rooftops and the ground without using a ladder.
Most enemies cannot move between these two terrains at all, while some can by using a ladder.
Each tile can hold up to 4 enemies.

Towers are located in the middle of 4 tiles. Assassins can climb them at the cost of AP to enter the Stealth status, gaining immunity to enemies' search.
Enemies cannot climb towers.
Haystacks and Rooftop Gardens are hiding spots open to Assassins in the Stealth status. They also provide immunity to enemies' search.
If there are enemies in an alert tile, Assassins entering this tile will be Exposed.
Assassins cannot use Assassin Skills in water tiles.
New enemies are spawned from the spawn spots every round. Their number will further increase when the alarm sounds.
Assassins must enter the area or use a skill to learn information about it.

If an Assassin is Exposed during an enemy round, the alarm will sound, increasing enemies' Detection and causing the spawn spot to spawn more enemies.
An active alarm will reset as long as no Assassins are exposed in 2 consecutive rounds.
When on a tower, tap on the adjacent Haystacks to perform the Leap of Faith, which allows Assassins to move there without consuming AP.
Assassins automatically enter the Stealth status when in an enemy-free tile. While in this status, they can perform Assassination to kill enemies.

When detected during an enemy search, Assassins enter the Exposed status, drawing enemies to move towards them.
Enemies attack Exposed Assassins in their round.

When changing from the Exposed status to the Stealth status, Assassins leave a trace on their current tile, towards which enemies will continue to move.
The trace only disappears when any enemy reaches it or 2 rounds after it is generated.
When in the Stealth status, Assassins can perform Assassination against enemies in the same tile, killing them directly.
When in the Stealth status and on a tower/rooftop, Assassins can perform Air Assassination against enemies in the adjacent tiles, killing them and moving to that tile simultaneously.

When Assassins attack an enemy, they have to fight all the enemies in that tile.
When in the Stealth status, Assassins' attack automatically becomes Ambush, which increases their Critical DMG in battle.

When there are multiple Assassins in the same tile, they can launch a Joint Attack, which starts a battle involving all the Assassins and enemies in that tile.
When in the Stealth status, Assassins' Joint Attack automatically becomes Joint Ambush, which increases their Critical DMG in battle.
When in a hiding spot, Assassins can perform Hidden Assassination against enemies in the same tile, killing them without leaving a body and obtaining their items directly.

When an Assassin's HP goes to 0, they enter the Downed status and cannot conduct any operations.
Other Assassins can use items or skills to heal them.

Enemies become bodies after being killed. Assassins can hide them when there are no enemies around, after which they may obtain items.
When an enemy moves to a tile with bodies in it, the alarm sounds.
One incident is triggered at the start of each round, causing a variety of impacts and deciding enemies' movement direction if no Assassins are being Exposed.
When no Assassins are being Exposed, enemies move in the direction decided by the incident of the round; otherwise, they move towards Exposed Assassins.

Enemies start a search when Assassins move to their tiles or when they move to Assassins' tiles.
When there are multiple enemies, each of them starts an independent search. Assassins become Exposed if detected.
When exposed Assassins move away from enemy tiles, half of the tile's enemies will chase them to the current tile if possible.
In an enemy round, enemies start a battle involving all the enemies and all the Exposed Assassins in the same tile if there are any.
Enemies in the Stationed status stay where they are.
A monster generated by the Interferometer's errors. Has high Detection yet low combat power.
Axemen cannot climb onto rooftops, but they are very good at fighting and it's extremely hard to kill them with Throwing Knives. Try to avoid them.
A monster generated by the Interferometer's errors. Can move between rooftops and the ground without using a ladder.
A monster generated by the Interferometer's errors. Can move 2 tiles per round.
Archers deals (Max HP x25%) DMG to random Exposed Assassins in the adjacent tiles before they move.
A monster generated by the Interferometer's errors. When in water tiles, it gains a significant stats boost.
The Commander spawns an extra soldier during the spawn phrase every round.
A monster generated by the Interferometer's errors. Immune to items and Assassin Skills, it can only be defeated in battle.

Detection Guide
While not detected, any attack against the enemy can trigger Assassination.
Enemies' Detection level goes up every round, taking less DMG.
Enemies with Shields cannot trigger Assassination. You can break their Shields to reset their Detection level to 0.

After that, the enemy round starts. They may spawn new enemies, move, or attack.
After the enemy round ends, your round starts again, recovering all Assassins' AP.

Enemies attack Exposed Assassins in the same tile.

In this status, they can perform Assassination to kill enemies.

"You're inside the Wilderness, a place where you can relive a person's memories of Florence."
Vertin, so this is your dwelling?
... A drifting plain at sea, with supplies from unknown sources, ample and well-hidden.
In short—a fine hideout. It wouldn't lose to Florence or Venice.
Florence ... bright, enchanting, my eternal home. Precisely why drawing too close to it in heart invites calamity.
Perhaps ... once all is resolved, you'll no longer fear the shadows clinging to those—or where—you love.
Ah ... there's no Carnival here.
But more importantly—no old friends.
They were my best allies and my greatest mentors ... I do miss them now, truly.
An ocean full of mist ... and buildings I can't begin to understand.
Who's hiding behind the rocks? Vertin? Or Alexios?
Good. As the host, maybe you'll do me a favor.
... This place could use more haystacks. Especially under buildings tall enough to poke Zeus in the eye.
For the sake of all misthios' professional longevity, I suggest you add some.
Don't bother lying.
The moment I saw you—and you didn't try to stab me—I knew exactly who you were.
Timekeeper ...? Sounds like a god's name.
To me, nothing shows mortal arrogance more than taking divine titles—unless you've earned them.
Don't you dare compare me to mortal fools like you or that brazen misthios with the broken spear.
I alone am worthy of the name "Deimos."
Because I AM Deimos.
... Why not? Heh, how typical among the ignorant. Once you have claimed a name, you have to embody it.
Reaching above your station, refusing to bow to us ...
That is your gravest mistake—you mortals, forever blind to your own insignificance.
This place is free of conspiracies, violence, and oppression.
Even just for a while, I can stop being an Assassin.
Our goal here has been achieved.
Quitting is not an option for Assassins. It's like a mark burned onto our bodies ... and our souls.
I am and always will be an Assassin, but sometimes, I can use a break like this.
Such a peaceful moment under the sun ... It reminds me of the old days in Florence when everything had yet to happen.
I believe you understand that feeling, Vertin.
Vertin, you said you were interested in the mercenary lifestyle, huh?
Are you ready for "Kassandra's Morning"?
Get up early before sunrise, arm yourself, and wait for your creditors at the door.
Then you can choose to pay the debts or kick their ass.
Well, I always go with the latter.
Good. I'll send Ikaros to wake you up tomorrow.
Make sure to train your arms and legs in advance. Maybe then you'll be useful when a debt collector comes knocking at my door.
Save your strength and get some rest. Don't over sleep.
Get out of my face.
If you're here to negotiate on her behalf, you have my answer.
You know who I'm talking about—the mercenary with a broken spear, my "sister."
Leave her before you regret it ... You stand no chance against me.
You're a smart woman and I'm willing to bet you know who would win in a contest between us. Make the right choice.
There is only one way to survive, and that is ...
Apparently, you need someone to tell you what to do ...
Someone who deserves your loyalty.
I hope you have enough sense to make the right decision.
How does it compare to Florence?
How does it compare to Venice?
It's me.
It's Alexios.
A god like you?
Why not?
Are you going to quit?
What's that?
Sounds fun. Count me in.
What do you mean "her"?
I'm only here for a chat, and I speak for myself.

Power transfer secured. Only a few more steps to go.
Well, Ms. Moissan always told me not to celebrate too quickly.
I'm winning, mia signorina.
Please go home and continue with your Latin lesson.
My potion is not working. Did I make it wrong ...?
Oh no! My "War Machine"! It broke down!
This devil twirls about like a fly! Get it!
Of course I do! This APPLe won't go down without a fight!

May ... the Father of Understanding guide ... us.
Don't fall for his tricks ... Ezio.
Heh ... This world has fallen to sin. Only the Templars have the strength to put it in order!
We are the instruments of this world's salvation!

Ahh ... We've gone so far astray from the light ...
Don't let your guard down. He likely still has something up his sleeve ...
They are led to destruction by their delusions! Brought to catastrophe by their ignorance.
They ... MUST PERISH!
How ... How could this be ...

The suffering I've gone through empowers me ... Gives me enough strength to return the pain to you, to everyone that wronged me.

Behold, this worn yet even glow of memory,
Plunging with a "plunk" through the crimson clouds.
The evening bell summons recollections from the grave,
Turning to white doves—weightless now, no longer burning.
And I wait, for its tireless, infinite returns.

Circling, wings spread toward rosy-fingered dawn,
Striding, leaping, sailing to the wine-dark sea.
Clutch the helm, raise your voice in song,
Till sirens climb your blade,
Summoning the first dream that stings you.

Ezio Auditore I

Thank you for the data, Vertin. Ahem, let's start the update right away. Now, about our new friend ... —X Ezio Auditore was born in 1459. In a diary entry from 1474, Maria Auditore, one of the greatest Florentine chroniclers and Ezio's mother, describes her son as "competitive, stubborn and loud mouthed, but so passionate that it is impossible to fault him for anything." His official records completely disappeared in 1476, as if he had never existed. In the same year, Uberto Alberti, Florence's Gonfaloniere, accused the Auditore family of treason against the city and sentenced them to death. Ezio's father and brothers, Giovanni Auditore, Federico Auditore, and Petruccio Auditore were thus executed in public at Piazza della Signoria.
Ezio Auditore II

1476 Ezio's family were arrested when he was out on an errand. In an attempt to stop their execution upon his return, he screamed that Uberto Alberti was a liar—the Gonfaloniere possessed the documents that could prove the Auditores' innocence, yet he denied any knowledge of such evidence. Ezio's vain attempt exposed himself; he barely escaped with the help of Giovanni's friend. Afterwards, he started to learn the skills required for being an Assassin. To fix the Hidden Blade which he inherited from Giovanni, Ezio was directed to Leonardo da Vinci, starting a friendship that would endure for the rest of their lives. With his Hidden Blade repaired, Ezio conducted the first assassination in his life: he sneaked into the courtyard of the Basilica di Santa Croce and stabbed Uberto Alberti through his chest. "The Auditore are not dead! I'm still here! Me! Ezio! Ezio Auditore!"
Ezio Auditore III

1476 After Uberto's assassination, Ezio became the most wanted man in Florence. He left the city with his mother and sister and found shelter at his uncle Mario's villa in Monteriggioni. Mario informed Ezio of the Assassins' existence, yet the young man refused to embrace his heritage. His top priority was to protect the family he had left and seek vengeance. 1478 During his hunt after the Pazzi family, Ezio gained information on a conspiracy against the Medici. He protected Lorenzo de' Medici from the public assassination at the Florence Cathedral. Palazzo della Signoria

Arnolfo di Cambio designed the Palazzo della Signoria (also known as the Palazzo Vecchio) in 1299, for the rulers of Florence, the Signoria. The Signoria was made up of nine members (or Priori) selected by the city's guilds and a Gonfaloniere of Justice. Interesting fact: The tower in front is off-center because it was incorporated into the Palazzo from an earlier structure. It contains two small cells, one of which was used to imprison Cosimo de' Medici. Besides, the Piazza della Signoria in front of the Palazzo Vecchio used to be an execution ground. A Knight: An execution ground right next to the center of power ... Someone believes some of those who sat on the throne were merely cowards.
Florence Cathedral

One of Italy's largest churches and the largest landmark in Florence, Santa Maria del Fiore is considered by many to be the first masterpiece of Renaissance architecture. Although the church was designed by Arnolfo di Cambio in 1296, the dome was not started until the 15th Century. None of the architects at that time had any idea how to construct such an enormous structure, since the use of buttresses was forbidden in Florence and mortar took several days to set. But all was not lost. In an amazing comeback story, Filippo Brunelleschi, an architect who had been defeated in an earlier bid to design the Baptistery doors, won the competition to build the dome. He beat out Lorenzo Ghiberti, the same artist he had lost to before. Brunelleschi invented machines to hoist the bricks needed for the dome up to the workers and was able to construct the entire dome without using centring. X: Respect to Brunelleschi and his inventions! I think I'm inspired by his story. Since we already have machines that lift things up, why not invent something completely different? For example, a machine that drops things down.
Auditore Palace

Completed in 1473, the Palazzo Auditore is notable for its rusticated stonework and Roman pilasters. Giovanni Auditore designed the palazzo himself, based on initial sketches by Leone Battista Alberti. Once built, the palazzo became a fixture of the Santa Maria Novella district. Lorenzo de'Medici mentioned in a letter addressed to Giovanni, dated 1474, that he admired the façade's lack of "ostentation." An-an Lee: So cool, so fancy! Leonardo's Workshop

Leonardo da Vinci opened his own studio after completing his apprenticeship to Verrocchio, one of the most successful Florentine artists of the day. Between 1476 and 1481, Leonardo probably continued to collaborate with Verrocchio, although no one is quite sure what he was working on. In 1481, he was given his first commission by the monks of San Donate a Scopeto, to paint The Adoration of the Magi. In true da Vinci style, he began the painting, but never finished it. Santa Trinita

Constructed over an existing church in 1258, Santa Trinita (Holy Trinity) is known for its Sassetti chapel, which is decorated with frescos of the life of Saint Francis by Domenico Ghirlandaio, a painter most famous for his brief role as one of Michelangelo's teachers. Santa Trinita was the mother church of the Vallumbrosan order of monks, a very serious group that strictly enforced both poverty and silence, for life. 37: I don't think they knew anything about their numbers, but they still remind me of my friends on the island ...
Ospedale degli Innocenti

Designed by Filippo Brunelleschi and opened in 1445, the Ospedale degli Innocenti (Hospital of the Innocents) was an orphanage for unwanted babies. Babies were typically abandoned in a basin in the front, although later transactions were facilitated by the introduction of a rotating horizontal wheel which moved infants into the building without the parent being seen. Many a mother abandoned her baby in order to be hired by the Ospedale as a wet nurse, so she could be paid to feed her own child. X: Life was a bit boring growing up in the orphanage. Basilica di San Lorenzo

The Church in which all the Medici went to die, San Lorenzo claims to be the oldest in Florence. It was consecrated in 393, while still outside the city walls. Michelangelo designed the inner façade, while Filippo Brunelleschi, the creator of Santa Maria del Fiore's dome, designed the layout. He died before the church was finished and several of his designs were subsequently modified. Containing nearly fifty tombs, the Medici crypt was intended to house the Holy Sepulchre containing the body of Christ at its centre. However, attempts to buy it and, then, to steal it from Jerusalem failed. Necrologist: These stone coffins speak with the utmost courtesy. People's habits are indeed hidden within their souls.
Palazzo Ducale

The Palazzo Ducale was constructed from 1309-1424, in the Gothic style, as the residence for the Doge. The Doge was the highest ranking elder in Venice and served in his position for life. In 1172, the selection of the Doge became entrusted to a committee of 40 (the Forty), whose members were chosen by the Venetian Great Council. Venice liked to think of itself as a Republic, meaning that the people could participate in the government. When the Doge took office he was introduced to the people with the words: "This is the Doge, if it please you." In fact, members of the Great Council were appointed by the forty, which in turn chose the Forty. Candidates for the Great Council were selected from a small pool containing only noble families and although the Doge could nominate anyone to the Council, the Forty and the Council itself had to approve the nomination. Druvis III: They built a club which they claimed to be open for everyone, yet left a barking dog to guard the door.
Scuola Grande di San Marco

The Scuola Grande di San Marco was one of the six large charitable organizations founded in Venice to help citizens afford food, dowries, processions, marriages, burials and anything else they might need. Notably, membership was open to any citizen of Venice, not just the elite. Citizenship status was conferred on third generation Venetians or those who had paid taxes for fifteen years. The façade of the building, which was built in 1260, was destroyed in a 1485 fire, causing it to be rebuilt in its current, opulent Byzantine form. Desert Flannel: Strewth! Free food and supplies? Ponte Vecchio

This famous bridge spans the Arno at it narrowest point. The original version was presumably constructed by the Romans, but the first written records only appear in 996. Two previous incarnations of the bridge were swept away in floods before the present structure was built in 1345. A tower was built at the southeast corner to defend it. The bridge consists of three segmental arches. It has always had shops lining the central passageway, a feature which seems extraordinary now, but was common during the Renaissance. In 1549, the Medici family purchased the Palazzo Pitti and rebuilt the bridge. The new design included a secret tunnel through which the Medicis could travel between the Palazzo Pitti and the Palazzo della Signoria without being spotted. Lilya: Secret tunnel? Hah. Arsenale di Venezia

First built as a naval depot for private ships, the Arsenal was rebuilt and enlarged in 1320. From that point on, it was used by the Venetian state to construct and maintain its ships. Famously, at the peak of production, shipbuilders were able to produce an entire ship in a day. The impressive front gate (the Porta Magna) went up in 1460, in the Classical revivalist style. Fogwalker: Produce an entire ship in a day? That workload could've taken much more time. Would the workers be allowed to rest in the next few days?
Torre dell'Orologio

Constructed in the late 15th century as a display of Venice's wealth, the Torre dell'Orologio displays the time of the day, the current phase of the moon, and the dominant sign of the Zodiac. According to legend, the designers of the clock face were blinded once their work was complete, so they could never duplicate it elsewhere. The designers lived inside the clock tower for the rest of their lives to maintain it. The Torre dell'Orologio ended up serving one very important practical purpose; it was used by sailors in the nearby harbor to time their departures with the tide. The illegitimate son of a notary and a peasant woman, Leonardo da Vinci was raised in Tuscany. At age 14, he was apprenticed to a Florentine painter, Verrocchio, who taught him chemistry, drafting, painting, sculpting and modelling. When he was 20, Leonardo established his own workshop, and then travelled across Italy, eventually painting his masterpieces "The Last Supper" in 1498 and "The Mona Lisa" in 1503-1507. During his travels, Leonardo studied the world with unquenchable curiosity. He created designs for a helicopter, tank, solar power and a calculator, among others. Despite this epic list of accomplishments, Leonardo was hounded by his patrons for his chronic procrastination. Carnival of Venice

The world-famous Carnival of Venice began in 1296, as a public holiday on the day before Lent. Doctors

Diagrams of the human body and the printing press influenced Renaissance medicine greatly, which had in turn been influenced by Arabic medicine during the Middle Ages. By the 15th Century, science had already begun its slow climb toward becoming more relevant than spirituality in the field of healthcare. However, many people clung to old ways, visiting local mystics instead of doctors. After the plague ravaged Europe in 1350, many doctors dressed in special plague gear to treat patients. To prevent contamination, they wore a cape coated in wax, and a primitive gas mask in the shape of a beak. Blacksmiths

Every Renaissance community needed a blacksmith. Swords, locks, pans, knives, nails and armor were all made from metal and all needed to be shaped. In addition, architectural ironwork flourished during the Renaissance as blacksmiths began to apply their practical craft towards making art. Bandits

The countryside during the Renaissance was filled with bandits, causing most travellers to move in armed groups called caravans. Anxious voyagers usually sewed valuables and gold into the soles of their shoes or the lining of their jackets. Guides called Vetturini were sometimes hired to help plot the route of the caravans and book rooms at local inns, but those carriers were often working with the bandits. Art Merchants

The shops of Renaissance artists were usually small, and dealt mainly in religious decorations for churches or homes. Artists were treated as craftsmen, just like carpenters and blacksmiths. The production of art was usually cooperative. The head of the shop was the master, who received commissions and oversaw the assembly of the painting. He was expected to be a businessman and turn a profit, usually creating copies of whatever religious paintings were in vogue at the time. Melania: Painters became merchants in the end ... Home to the Forgotten

The dome of Santa Maria del Fiore was designed by the famous architect, Filippo Brunelleschi, yet built by a group of ordinary workers whom no one remembers. During the construction, they were required to bring their lunch to the site and finish it where they worked, since it was dangerous to descend and climb the scaffoldings. In 1426, Brunelleschi opened taverns within the dome with kitchens and wine, allowing the workers to eat without leaving their work—even though the project they were working on was bound to go down in history, they cared more about the food on the table and the money in their pockets. Parthenon

The Parthenon is one of the most well-known buildings in the world, and an enduring symbol of Ancient Greek civilization. While it is located on the Akropolis, the building is not a traditional temple. It was built by the sculptor Phidias and the architects Kallikrates and Iktinos as a great monument to the glory of the city of Athens. That glory is evident in its many carvings. One of the most carved monuments in Greek architecture, the Parthenon's decorations depict several mythological scenes. These include the birth of Athena, her fight against Poseidon for the patronage of Athens, the gods' battle with the giants and the procession of the Great Panathenaia. Pnyx

The Athenian assembly was known as the ekklesia. It met at the Pnyx forty times a year to discuss various civic matters, and each session usually lasted a few hours. The word pnyx is believed to mean something close to "packed together." This was probably a reference to the fact that during meetings of the ekklesia, the location would be filled to its capacity, with citizens packed in practically shoulder-to-shoulder. All male citizens were allowed to directly participate in the democratic process. Those over twenty years old had the right to speak and vote, while those over thirty could be elected to the higher position of magistrate. In total, there were approximately 30,000 citizens in Athens in the classical period. To draft and adopt decrees, 6,000 of them had to attend the meeting. Poltergeist: "Packed together"?! Athenian Portico

Next to the Naxian Sphinx stood a simple structure to display offerings from the Athenians, most of which were spoils of war. In particular, these offerings—called "ex-votos"—were prows of sunken Persian ships. The Athenians built the portico after their naval victory over the Persians in 478 BCE. This building showcases Athens's dominance as a naval power. Its location suggests that the Athenians attributed their victories to divine favor. Archaeological findings also reveal that each ship's prow underwent a ritual purification before it was permitted to be displayed as a war trophy. Jessica: "Ex-votos"? I get it. Theater of Delphi

The theater of Delphi was situated above the Temple of Apollo. It offered an expansive view of sanctuary and the valley below, and could accommodate around 5,000 spectators in its seats. The theater hosted different artistic contests, especially during competitions like the Pythian Games. These contests included plays, poetry readings, and musical performances, and were held not only for the audience, but also for Apollo, the god of arts—among other things. Diggers: It melts my heart! At last we arrive at the Temple of Apollo, where the Oracle relayed her prophecies. Atop its imposing columns, the structure's pediments displayed famous mythological scenes sculpted by the renowned Greek artist Antenor. Temple of Athena Chalkioikos

According to Pausanias, the two most important Spartan temples were the temple of Artemis Orthia, and the temple of Athena Chalkioikos. Pausanias describes the building of the sanctuary of Athena Chalkioikos in great detail. It was located on the Akropolis of Sparta, west of the agora. Its construction was started by the mythical king of Sparta, Tyndareos, but was completed by the Spartan sculptor Gitiadas in the 6th century BCE. The epithet Chalkioikos (house from bronze) was attached to this temple due to the bronze and copper decorations on its walls. These embossed sheets depicted mythological scenes like Herakles's labors, achievements of the sons of Tyndareos, the legend of Perseus and Medusa, and the birth of Athena. The bronze decorations and the bronze statue of Athena were the works of Gitiadas, who also composed a hymn to the goddess. Akropolis of Sparta

The Akropolis of Sparta consisted of several buildings that date from different chronological periods – from the Archaic to the Byzantine era. At the top of the Akropolis was the sanctuary of Athena Chalkioikos, dated to the 6th century BCE. It was originally a sanctuary of Pitane, as confirmed by archaeological discoveries dating as early as the Mycenaean period. Near the sanctuary of Athena was the ancient theater of Sparta. It is based on a structure dated to the Roman period. The theater probably had a wooden stage; a fact supported by several inscriptions from the 2nd century CE. Excavations next to the theater also revealed connected shops. The Akropolis of Sparta also held visible traces of the Skias, the semi-circular building of the archaic-classical periods—but with visible repairs from the Roman period. Pickles: Woof ... Woof? Woof.
Temple of Zeus

The Olympic Games were dedicated to Zeus, and all the ceremonies and events were hosted in his honor. It's no surprise that the largest temple in the sanctuary was the Temple of Zeus. While most temples were restricted to priests, the Temple of Zeus welcomed all who visited Olympia. This openness was most likely meant to show off the gold and ivory statue of Zeus that stood within the temple's walls. The building also featured art depicting both versions of the Olympic festival's founding myth. The eastern pediment showed a scene from the legendary race between Pelops and Oinomaos. The temple's metopes, meanwhile, showed the twelve labors of Herakles, the other mythical founder of the games. Heraion

The Heraion was a temple dedicated to Hera. It is one of the oldest temples in the sanctuary, dating back to approximately 590 BCE. The structure included columns painted with images of women who won the Heraia, an athletic competition made up of running events. Every four years, sixteen women were chosen to make a veil dedicated to Hera. These women also organized the competition, though they did not compete in it. The Heraia was unique for its focus on female athletes, in contrast to the male-exclusive Olympic Games. Workshop of Phidias

This workshop was built for the renowned sculptor Phidias after his work on the Akropolis of Athens. In 435 BCE, Phidias came to Olympia to begin working on the great chryselephantine statue of Zeus. He died five years later, shortly after completing his masterpiece. This grand statue would become one of the seven wonders of the ancient world. Phidias's workshop was located right next to the Temple of Zeus. Its structure has been well preserved, mostly owing to its conversion to a church in the 5th century CE. Archaeologists have also discovered lots of ancient materials in the surrounding area, such as casting molds and sculpting tools. The most famous artifact, however, is a cup bearing an inscription that aggressively states: "I belong to Phidias!" Hissabeth: I should label my sandwich before putting it in the fridge. Theater of Dionysos

The Theater of Dionysos as it exists today dates back to the 4th century BCE, when the statesman Lykourgos reorganized the sanctuary. lt features a circular orchestra, with a stone skene—or stage—in front of it. However, archaeologists believe that the original shape of the orchestra was a square. In the Hellenistic period, 67 marble thrones reserved for city officials were added around the orchestra. At the center of this row was a seat meant for the priest of Dionysos. During the Roman period, a new stage was built in honor of both the god and the emperor Nero, and extra seats of honor were added around the edge of the orchestra. Located in Ithaka, Odysseus' Palace is said to be the personal residence of Odysseus, the hero in Homer's epic poem Odyssey. Behind the Propylaea was the giant bronze statue of Athena Promachos, or "Athena who fights on the front lines." That name was reflected in the spear and shield the statue held in its hands. Dionysia and Drama Competitions

The Great Dionysia was supervised by the head magistrate known as the archon, who was assisted by twelve other magistrates. Among his duties, the archon picked choregoi—rich Athenian citizens responsible for providing the budget for rehearsals and performances. Two days before the Dionysia, a ceremony called the proagon took place where playwrights introduced their work. The Dionysia finally began in earnest with a procession to the god's temple, followed by sacrifices and a symposium. The next two days centered on dithyramb contests, while the final four days were dedicated to drama competitions. The contests' outcomes were decided by ten judges, who were appointed at random by the archon. The judges placed their votes in an urn, and five of the votes were randomly picked to determine the winner. The Fool: The most important part of a tragedy is the curtain call—the king who just shed blood opens his eyes again, the princess who committed suicide rises once more ... Their bows towards the supreme leader make the tragedies complete!
Odysseus and the Sirens

The sirens were beautiful but deadly creatures that lived on a rocky island. Their song was so enchanting, sailors who heard their singing fell to the rocks. Sirens were half-women, half-birds—or at least, that was how they were represented in Greek art. They were usually depicted played musical instruments, such as harps. In "The Odyssey," Odysseus was very curious to listen to them, so Circe the witch told him how he could enjoy their song without danger. Odysseus had his sailors plug their ears with beeswax and tie him to the pole of his ship. When they passed near the sirens, Odysseus was mesmerized by the song. He begged his sailors to release him, but they couldn't hear him. This trick saved his life and the lives of his companions. Lorelei: The sirens ... They were expecting listeners who understood them, don't you think? But the side effect of their voices is too strong ... Hmm, maybe they should just sing to the conchs.
Pythian Oracle

Prophecies were given in the most restricted part of the temple, the adyton, by a chaste woman known as the Pythia. Before delivering prophecies, she first purified herself with water, then burned laurel leaves and barley flour to begin the ritual. Finally, while seated on a tripod surrounded by offerings, the Pythia delivered Apollo's messages. Her words were often strange and indecipherable, and required further interpretation by the temple's priests. Despite much research, the exact causes of the Oracle's behavior while prophesying are debated to this day. Mercuria: Burning laurel leaves ... Its smell remains the same after thousands of years, and it will never change, like the laws of the universe.
Two Kings

Sparta's political system differed from most of Greece's. One of its most distinctive features was that it was ruled by two kings. These kings belonged to two separate dynasties: the Eurypontids and the Agiads, both of which were said to be descended from Herakles. Both kings shared equal powers, and disputes between them required the intervention of special magistrates known as ephors. However, if one of the kings were more charismatic or experienced, they could influence the weaker king's choices. Isolde: Heh-heh ... One kingdom with two kings. How curious, just like one body with two heads. If either of them had a knife ...
Pentathlon

The pentathlon took place at the stadium on the second day. As its name implies, it was made up of five events: discus throwing, javelin throwing, jumping, racing, and wrestling. There are several differences between the ancient version of events and their contemporary counterparts. For example, ancient long jumpers held weights in their hands to give them momentum to launch, since there was no run-up before the jump. Similarly, if an athlete won the first three events, they were immediately declared the winner, instead of being judged by their overall performance in all five events. Running events worked the same as they do today—with the notable exception of all the athletes being nude. As for wrestling, competitors were not divided by weight class as they are today, but instead by age. The winner was the first to throw his opponent to the ground three times. X: Update suspended. It's time for some eye, finger, and hip exercises!
Scytale

In the field of cryptography, the scytale is a device used for transposition ciphers. It involves wrapping a strip of parchment around a cylindrical rod, with the message written across the surface. This method was reportedly employed by the ancient Greeks—especially the Spartans—for secure communication during military operations. This device can carry secret information stably at a low cost, yet its disadvantage is also obvious: anyone can decrypt as long as they have heard of this encryption method. X: This is inspiring ... I wonder if it's possible to invent a new kind of scytale which only those who have never heard of it can decrypt ...

Priestess in Distress

"Lysimachus, where are you? For the love of Athena, I told you not to provoke those dangerous men ..." The anxious priestess looked around, her eyes pleading for help.
"Eagle Bearer, Lysimachus has gone missing for two days. Find her I beg you, and bring her back safely."
Eerily Quiet

Lysimachus's house looks ordinary and quiet.
Perhaps a little too quiet—an uneasy feeling lingers in the air.

The back door was wide open, and the interior was in disarray.
The intruders didn't seem to loot the place; the floor was marked with signs of struggle and dragging.
In the corner by the doorframe, a few dark snake scales lay scattered.
Threatening Letter

"Stop your rituals. Your fake god deserves no offerings. Stop now, or you will lose more."
The handwriting is barely legible, and at the end of the letter, a poorly-done snake pattern is drawn.
A Sword Quest

"No warrior can say no to a finely forged sword, and there's one that cuts through iron like butter—a sword perfect for you."
The bard tries to pique Kassandra's interest.
"Do you know the sword's origin? The gods used it to uphold justice. It was once hidden in Athenian ruins but has since gone missing. If you want to find the sword, search the bandit camp on the city outskirts ..."
Droll Drunkard

"When he tantalizes our hearts, *hic* it's through ... getting drunk! He shows me the art of ... dancing!"
A heavily drunk man staggers through the street, leaving chaos wherever he goes.
"Someone help stop him; the Dionysia hasn't even started yet! Hey, put that jar down! Stop smashing things!"
Villager's Prayer

"O mighty Zeus, barbaric bandits are terrorizing our village, please grant us a worthy warrior to wipe out these thugs at their hideout in the Melissani Cave!"
Did Zeus hear our plea?  Does he care about us? No one knows. Either way, fate has brought you here.
A Blacksmith's Invitation

"More and more wolves have been appearing on the mountain lately, and people are too afraid to go mine iron."
The old blacksmith speaks with worry, sighing and pounding his hands nonstop.
"What use is a blacksmith without iron ore? I beg you—please deal with those wolves on Mount Ainos."
Transport to Nowhere

A merchant caravan is in an uproar; Kassandra decides to see what is going on.
"I shouldn't have put my faith in your petty vineyard. If the goods don't arrive soon, we're leaving!"
"Listen, the transport team is supposed to arrive this morning. I worry they might've run into trouble on the road."
Kassandra asks about the transport route and departure time, her expression growing serious. "I'm afraid things aren't looking good."
On the Clifftop
Following the trade route, Kassandra reaches a clifftop where the hoofprints and wheel tracks are in complete disarray.
Wrecked Wagon

Looking down the cliff, Kassandra notices that the wagon has shattered into pieces, and all the cargo was stolen.
"With so many heavy crates, the bandits couldn't have gone far."
The Victims
Kassandra spots the bodies of several merchants. It appears they had tried to hide from the bandits but were shot down by arrows.
Panic and Chaos

The bandits tried to cover their tracks, but with so many people involved, plenty of clues remained.
The scattered footprints appear again to the west, and Kassandra heads in that direction.
Medicinal Supplies

The temple healer tends to the wounded soldiers. Stone statues stand solemnly around them, and the injured dare not groan too loudly.
"You see, there are many wounded here, and we've gone through the antler powder far too quickly. If you're familiar with Mount Parnassos, could you help me find some deer antlers?"
Stolen Sapphire

"Misthios, the sapphire worshiped in the temple has been stolen! The gods will surely take out their anger on us!"
The priest's anger flares up, eager to personally thrash the thief.
"I heard thieves like to hide in caves, and there are some abandoned caves west of the temple. Maybe you can find them there."
Strange Statue
Just as she was about to leave, the statue at the end of the cave caught Kassandra's attention. An inconspicuous hexagonal groove is hidden beneath the statue's chest.
Hidden Door
Upon inserting the sapphire, the statue slowly moves aside, showing a narrow tunnel behind.

At the end of the tunnel, Kassandra discovers the long-forgotten treasure. Could it be that the sapphire's original purpose was to open the secret chamber? Then who was the first person to place the treasure here ...
Boar Bounty
The town's bulletin board displays the latest bounty: a wild boar is injuring people, and sharp spears can't penetrate its hide. Brave warriors are needed to take it down—quickly!
Absent Soldiers

"Demaratos hasn't reported yet, which is unusual—Spartan soldiers never forget their assembly time."
The sergeant's face is stern. He clearly trusts his men deeply and is now greatly worried.
"Something must have happened ... but I can't leave the camp now. Could you help me find Demaratos?"
Secluded Path

Tracing the road from the assembly point, Kassandra arrives at the path Demaratos might have taken.
It is a secluded area, overgrown with trees and bushes—an ideal spot for an ambush.
Broken Spear
Sure enough, in the bushes, Kassandra discovers a broken spear. She senses the presence of a fight.
Trail of Bloodstains

Following the trail of bloodstains and footprints, Kassandra reaches a hilltop, where a makeshift bandit camp comes into view.
The bandits are scrambling to try on the stolen Spartan armor, while the poor young victim lies tossed aside.
Expose the Cheater

"I know you're an excellent athlete, and if I'm not mistaken, you're quite skilled with a javelin too?"
Kassandra nods, as this is nothing unfamiliar to a seasoned warrior.
"Then please take a look. I suspect the opponent's javelin is rigged. And cheating is not allowed in Olympia."
Rigged Javelin

The suspected athlete appears calm, but Kassandra notices something off—the javelin, though well disguised, has a different weight distribution and is made of non-standard materials.
In other words, it's a custom-made javelin designed for cheating in competition.
Subbed In

"The athlete suddenly fell ill?" The judge, upon hearing the news, scans the surroundings and locks eyes with Kassandra.
"You look fit and agile—if you step into the arena, the crowd is bound to give you the warmest of welcomes. Care to give it a try?"
Mysterious Symbols

While admiring the Heraion, Kassandra discovers a string of unfamiliar symbols on a hidden pedestal slab.
"Maybe the scytale can be used here too?"
Code Breaking

"Olive tree ... southeast ... Olympia ..."
Does this point to the location of some treasure? Or perhaps a trap set to catch those sniffing for sensitive information?
Beneath the Olive Tree
There seems to be something hidden among the roots of the stunted olive tree.
Built to the glory of Athens's protector, the Parthenon housed the gold and ivory statue of Athena made by Phidias. Made of Pentelic marble, the structure held the city's and Delian League's riches.
Situated on a hill, this was where Athenians gathered for assemblies. Decrees were ratified, budgets voted on, and administration members appointed. It was where citizens could have a voice.
This building was constructed against the polygonal wall that supported the terrace of the temple of Apollo and was used for setting up ex-votos, mostly spoils of war.
The theater of Delphi was situated above the Temple of Apollo. It offered an expansive view of sanctuary and the valley below, and could accommodate around 5,000 spectators in its seats.
This was built inside the god's sanctuary and introduced Greek theater to the heart of the city. The great works of Euripides, Aischylos, Sophokles, and Aristophanes were performed there.
Behind the Propylaea was the giant bronze statue of Athena Promachos, or "Athena who fights on the front lines."

The Dionysia began in earnest with a procession to the god's temple, followed by sacrifices and a symposium. The next two days centered on dithyramb contests, while the final four days were dedicated to drama competitions.
Spartans used a cipher to communicate during military operations. They wrote on leather strips, which were wrapped around a wooden stick.
431 BCE, Kassandra and Herodotus arrived in Athens. Herodotus told Kassandra to attend Perikles's symposium to tell him about the Cult of Kosmos.
The sirens were beautiful but deadly creatures that lived on a rocky island. Their song was so enchanting, sailors who heard their singing fell to the rocks.
Odysseus, the most illustrious of all Greek heroes, was among the chiefs who set out for Troy. He returned to Ithaka and reclaimed his palace twenty years later.

451 BCE, Kassandra was brought to the beaches of Kephallonia by a raging storm. There, she was found by a local merchant Markos, who offered her a piece of bread in exchange for her help in the future.
431 BCE, Kassandra disguised herself as a cult member and infiltrated the Sanctuary of Delphi. In there, she realized that Deimos was her lost brother Alexios.
Prophecies were given in the most restricted part of the temple, the adyton, by a chaste woman known as the Pythia.
The Panhellenic Sanctuary of Delphi was renowned for the Oracle of Apollo, and considered the center of the world in ancient Greece.
429-426 BCE, Kassandra publicly unveiled Pausanias the cultist King, forcing him to be ousted.
451 BCE, the priest of Sparta was about to drop Alexios off Mount Taygetos when Kassandra attempted to save her brother. Unfortunately, she pushed the priest and Alexios to their apparent deaths.
Sparta's political system differed from most of Greece's. One of its most distinctive features was that it was ruled by two kings.
The temple of Athena on the akropolis was one of Sparta's most important monuments. The bronze sheets that decorated its interior gave birth to the name Chalkioikos.
The Akropolis of Sparta consisted of several buildings that date from different chronological periods – from the Archaic to the Byzantine era.
428 BCE, Kassandra competed in the pankration final, fought the champion Dorieus and won the competition for Sparta.

A siren is calling out by the roadside, but all passersby cover their ears to avoid her.
Exotic Siren
Please! Hear my words! I am looking for a warrior who is brave enough to challenge the stormy sea!
At last, a kind and brave woman. People here tend to see Rusalki as sea monsters. It's hard to find someone who'll listen.
Long story short, a sea monster—your people seem to call it Skylla—has come to this coastline. Someone must drive it away, or the harbor will be flooded.
If you're willing to help, go find Ms. Lorelei by the shore. She's holding Skylla back and waiting for a brave soul like you.
At last, a curious woman. People here tend to see Rusalki as sea monsters. It's hard to find someone who'll listen.
Altruistic Siren
Skylla, Skylla, go back to your strait. Your friend Charybdis isn't here; there's no one to play your whirlpool games with.
A siren by the shore is singing toward a whirlpool just a stone's throw away, unaware that she herself has become a threat to passing ships—fortunately, none are nearby.
No need to keep singing. I'm here to help.
Oh, you've come, just as the little seashell's message foretold.

Skylla has been waiting a long time too. She's particularly playful and quite mischievous, trying to keep six friends all to herself ... But her selfishness will only make her friends sad, and that's not good.
This place is too big, and my song can't reach her. Could you go tell her that for the sake of her health, she really shouldn't eat too much?
You did it! The people here don't have to fear the flooding anymore.
Beating Skylla with a siren's help—that's a first for me.
Our unity gave us great strength! My dear friend, I'll tell my comrades of your brave deed!
Quirky Mercenary
Hey, you look like a fellow mercenary to me—and not a bad one. Got a job for you, interested?

Yeah well, maybe Athenians are polite and all, but what's that to me? I'm not from Athens. And Athenian gangs are dumber than my pal Andrea—it took me quite some time to teach them what a fun gang is like.
But some people just don't appreciate my effort, especially that "Indigen"—what a lousy code name!
The job I've got for you is to take him out.
Hiring a merc costs money. But no one's hiring me right now, and this job doesn't suit my tastes.
So I need someone else to go take out this 'Indigen' guy. Thinks his cult name can protect him. But he's really pissed me off.
Looks like you've got a score to settle with those fanatics as well. Then I'll take it as a yes. Follow me.
He's just an buffoon. I'm not paying much for a buffoon. This fake bead pulled from a goat's backside is the best I can offer. If you're in, come with me.
Good job. Now, take your payment, and don't come looking for me again.
Exotic Bard
First I was dragged around in a suitcase, and now I've reached the end of Odysseus's epic adventure.
We help shape this story from afar without realizing it, and in turn, it shapes us.
Hard to guess what comes next, isn't it, heroine?
A misthios with a mysterious past, a lost brother turned rival, and enemies lurking in the shadows ... Maybe once you meet your wise mentor, you'll finally see where this adventure leads.
But it's too soon to talk about endings. Let's start with the beginning—how about taking out some bandits?
These savage thugs have taken over Odysseus's palace. You can tell the author had no intention of bringing them back again—perfect for highlighting the protagonist's courage early in the story.
Oh, I'm no philosopher—I'm a writer. I live for storytelling, and I always hunger for inspiration.
Odysseus's palace must be a wellspring of inspiration. I'm curious what I could create there, but a gang of bandits has taken it over. It's now harder to get in than a prison.
Maybe you could help me deal with them? I think this is the natural course of our meeting here.

Look at this one—after you took him down, a letter fell from his body. The letter shows that he was part of some dark, secret cult. Your story is connected to a grander one, naturally and yet with surprising coincidence.
Your poems sound strange to me, but for a bard, you're awfully good with a sword.
My pen is my sword. As long as I keep writing, my blade stays sharp.
It's okay if you don't understand my story now. But once you see my swordplay, you'll understand my literature someday.
Exotic Scholar
An eagle bearer ... you must be the helpful mercenary Vila spoke of, says a foreigner exuding the aura of an Athenian philosopher, clutching a strange device in her hand.
Vila ...? Am I supposed to know her?
Of course. You've met her—a Rusalka—er, I mean a mermaid, or a siren. Not exactly common around here, I imagine.
I thought all her friends would be sirens too.

Well, true friendship transcends race, but let's not dwell on that. Do you have a moment? Like Vila, I'm in need of some ... martial support. It's a matter of great importance—my academic research depends on it.
I guess you could say that. My research is being hindered by a creature born of ley energy. If you can eliminate it, I'll share the minerals I've gathered during my studies.
Really? I knew it—the study of ley lines is bound to find its audience, somewhere, sometime.
But this isn't the moment for academic lectures—we're on the clock.
My colleague is monitoring the creature on-site. She'll explain everything to you. Though I should warn you, her appearance isn't ... well received in these parts. Try not to be alarmed.
A Gorgon speaks to you casually, with a cheerful smile—her "hair" even adds commentary.
Friendly Gorgon
So you're the helper Windsong found?
Snake I
She looks reliable.
Snake II
Will she attack us like the other hunters?
That foreigner might be a witch.
Or perhaps a goddess to guide you on your journey. Your local myths are full of such things, aren't they?
Unless I'm some kind of a demigod.
Why not? I know you folks think Gorgons are dangerous creatures, but I have at least forty-seven ways to prove I'm friendly—and technically, I'm only distantly related to Gorgons ...
The energetic Gorgon certainly makes a case for her amicable nature.
The Gorgon raises both hands high.
Easy, easy ... See? We can talk, right? I'm not some rampaging monster. Let's work this out peacefully, okay?
No tricks, Gorgon.
Honestly, to me, Gorgon's just a distant classification. We may look alike, but—anyway, let's talk about the job.

Thank the Aegean for its pleasant climate—I've got so much energy to burn when it comes to research. But a terrifying legendary creature—one of the Gigantes—has taken root near my ley energy research field.
My petrification arcane skill isn't effective against creatures made of ley energy. So I need someone who can fight it. Though it's powerful, I have faith in your capabilities.
I'm not sure I can live up to Herakles' legacy, but I'll take the job.
Thank you! Here's your reward. Say—got time to grab a bite after this? I'd love to try some Athenian food. You must have recommendations!
Don't bother. The entire city's vendors would turn their backs on you ...
Mathematician
Huh? Why can't I go in? Isn't this a place for seeking truth?
If that Pythia only accepts oracles blindly without proper verification and discussion, how can she be sure her theories are correct?
Oh hello, dear integer, you look like a marvelous number—do you know how to get into this temple?
Integer? Umm ... what does that mean?
Everyone has their own soul number. Yours is clearly an integer, with lots of 3s and 2s as factors.
So, do you have a way to get into the temple?
Sneaking in? That's a great idea. It's not my strong suit, but it shouldn't violate the Scripture in any way.
Oh, I have an idea—you can go in and debate the Pythia on my behalf. I'll write a letter for you; the Pythia will definitely understand it, unless she's a terribly irrational number.
Hmm ... looks like I'll have to try other methods. Maybe I can find some flaws in the temple's spatial geometry.
You can then go verify the flaws I find—if you're interested, that is. Don't forget to take the letter.
You sneak into the Temple and leave the Mathematician's letter on Pythian's desk. You also confirm that she's a Cultist after reading the other letters on the desk.
Wow, you came back so quickly—has the Pythia given you an answer?
What? Oh ... then I should look for someone else to discuss with. Thank you for your help.
Hmm ... looks like she couldn't solve the problem. I should go check elsewhere. Thank you for your help.
Beautiful Actress
Excuse me, are you Kassandra the Eagle Bearer?
To think my reputation has reached the theatre of Delphi.
It would seem so. I haven't been here long, but many guests mentioned a mercenary traveling with an eagle.
There are also occasional rumors that you're searching for a secret organization called the Cult of Kosmos.
Haha, you're probably right, but when you first show people your sincerity, they can't wait to return it ...
The chatter after plays can last quite long; sometimes it even spills shocking news. I've long since learned how to get used to it.

A guest claiming to be a Cultist invited me to join. He spoke of the Cult's 'great cause' and grumbled about your interference. Out of courtesy, I took his address—you might be interested in meeting that chatty guest?
Why would you help me?
I just want to make sure I get to further enjoy my peaceful holiday here, Ms. Kassandra. Besides, his behavior reminded me of the despicable paparazzi back home.
Thank you so much, Ms. Kassandra. I'll spread word of your deeds among the guests—I'm sure that'll help keep other Cultists away.
Hey, we meet again. Are you also traveling the phenomenal world in search of the truth?
I guess you could say that. I've gathered a lot of clues along the way, but I haven't found the final answer yet.
Have you tried setting the clues up as a system? The phenomenal world can be very deceptive—formulas can help us see the truth more clearly.
I always thought math was just for counting chickens or something like that.
Nah-uh. Everything is numbers, and everything can be solved. Let me show you—give me a look at your clues.

My blades will be at your service.

This creature seems to be some kind of evil consciousness given form. Its origin may not be what I expected, but its danger is beyond doubt. Please be careful.
Thank you for your help, Ms. Kassandra. Without you, this would've been a brutal fight for me.

What do I do, what do I do ...

Should I go to the guards? But some of them might be working with them secretly ... Announce it in public? No, it won't work ... Ask the Timekeeper for help? But she's on vacation—it'd be rude to burden her with work at a time like this. Who can I even talk to ...
All your worries ... you just said it out loud.
Wh-What?! I'm sorry, I didn't mean to! Could you pretend you didn't hear that ...?
A misthios ... maybe I could hire you with the money I've saved? No, I haven't even explained the request, you couldn't possibly give a price ...
Really? Then can I ask for your opinion? But you really mustn't tell anyone else. This could be dangerous ...

So here it is ... I discovered that a seemingly ordinary citizen is actually a member of the evil cult that secretly manipulates the entire Greece. He's planning to use the sports games to carry out their plot. My arcane skill doesn't lie, but I have no solid proof ...

Firenze Contracts
Rise as shadows with blades thirsting for the freedom of all.
Choose a [Weapon] and [Route] based on the enemy's [Weapon] and [Route] to complete assassination missions.
Firenze Contracts Rules

Choose your [Weapon] and [Route] to counter enemy's [Weapon] and [Route] to complete assassination mission.

Both sides need to play 1 [Weapon] card and 1 [Route] card each round.

After cards are played, resolve [Weapon] cards and [Route] cards separately based on cards' strength and weakness.

There are 3 types of [Weapon]: Medium Sword, Blunt Weapon, Short Blade and 3 types of [Route]: On the streets, Marketplace, and Fortifications. Each has 1 stronger card and a weaker card.

Strength & Weakness Relation:
[Route]: On the Streets cards are STRONGER than Fortification cards.

There are chances for special weapons to be available in a round.
O brave sailors, though the waves rise—hoist the sails and set forth to meet them! For over the horizon lies glory to claim and treasure to be taken.
Select a destination, assemble your fleet, roll the dice and roll high to win.
[Voyage by Sea] Rules

New [Destinations] will be generated every day. Roll high to to explore the [Destination].

After selecting a [Destination], select from three ships (repeated ships allowed) to build your [Fleet]. Each ship has an independent dice array.

After you have chosen your fleet, the system will roll the dice arrays 3 times according to your selection. You succeed if the sum of your dice rolls meet or exceed the required points.

Calling the Timekeeper, this is Ulrich ... Damn it, the Foundation's communications are barely getting through.
What's up? Lost contact with yer pals?
Lieutenant Moldir's intel about the ritual is critical. I have to report it to the Timekeeper as soon as possible.
But the blizzard's too heavy, and the mountain's too tall. We need to find a location suitable for our shortwave radio ...
No sweat, partner! Just leave it to me! So what kinda spot we lookin' for?
Electromagnetic waves get absorbed and reflected by terrain. Direct waves give off stronger signals than reflected or diffracted ones.
So the fewer the obstacles between us and the Timekeeper's team, the more likely we are to make contact.
Of course, the state of the ionosphere still affects a few ... Sergeant Fairchild? Are you listening?
... Huh? 'Course I am! Bright-eyed and bushy-tailed as ever. So, ya need a clear spot facin' the city ruins, right?
Then you folks do yer thing, and I'll scout on up ahead. Keep yer peepers open for my markers!
Well? Yer radio workin'?
No response, but there are no issues with the signal. The Timekeeper must be busy.
Dontcha worry! It's all clear ahead. Ya can holler for yer pals any time ya like!
I'll admit that you've got a knack for science. If we make it back alive, I wonder if you would consider joining the Laplace Scientific Computing Center?
I'm certain my colleagues would have no issue in accommodating another unusual arcanist.
Shucks, I'm flattered! I'd be keen for a visit, but I'm afraid I done already sworn my loyalty to Lieutenant Moldir!
Gonna scout on ahead now. Save yer lecture for later! Keep movin' and try not to let yer brain freeze through!

Dontcha stop now! It's dangerous here. We gotta keep movin'.

I need to establish communications. This intel must reach the Timekeeper—now!
