Office, St. Pavlov Foundation
On the other side, a long interrogation is finally coming to a close.
An unexpected visitor arrives as a letter is slipped into the room.
Foundation Staff Member
"Sorry for the interruption, but I have news for Ms. Lopera."
A Foundation staff member steps into the room and hands an envelope to Lopera.
She opens it and pulls out the contents in full view of everyone. No one stops her.
"Eastern Front. Igor."
She reads in silence; her ever-easy smile falls away into frustration.
She scans the page again and again, as if searching for another name.
"We thought it best to share this with you."
"We haven't received any intelligence on former Lieutenant Moldir."
"That doesn't surprise me."
"If she's still alive, if she's somewhere out there, I just hope she doesn't come to regret her choices."
"Sounds like she did some work for us in Antarctica."
"Is that so?"
"If there's any news of her, I want to know first."
"We'll do what we can."
The blinds of the interrogation room are pulled open, and the dazzling light of day floods in.
On this late-fall afternoon, the sunlight slants into the cold, bare room.
Lopera stands by the window, lifting a hand to shield her eyes as she squints toward the world outside.
"You said earlier that the 'Storm' has changed the era again."
"Yes. We're back in 1920, 71 years before the last reversion."
"Only for some reason the Great War isn't over; the timeline as we once knew it has changed."
War goes on.
Lopera doesn't say anything further, her face tangled with emotion as she looks out toward an unreachable horizon.
In the daylight, somewhere far across the world, the woman she worries for rides beneath the mountains, holding her reins in a firm grip.
"Fall in!"
The lieutenant's command cuts through the air. At the valley's edge, her soldiers wait, fully armed.
The troop falls into formation, silently waiting for whatever order comes next.
"Forward!"

A Name Etched in the Wall

The children of soldiers who retired in 1945 grew up in the afterglow of the Great Patriotic War. They donned their uniforms, entered the military academy, and became the celebrated "next generation."

As the shadow of the Cold War descended, the academy's progressive education shook these young inheritors—they would no longer fight for hollow concepts like territory, but pursue something far grander: the "Vision of Balance."

A young man named Igor rose above his peers. His name began appearing in military briefings: commanding cross-border operations, quelling rebellions, directly overseeing high-level missions such as containing arcanists ... The years carved scars and wrinkles into his face like knife marks, yet his gaze grew ever colder, like the dark current beneath a frozen river. He had nearly forgotten—both the ideals the Great Patriotic War had etched into his heart and the myth of peace and order.

Until that day, when he studied the "invitation" on his desk—a yellowed, timeworn envelope bearing the seal of Zeno's Tortoise. The Zeno Military Academy, an international institution capable of maintaining peace, a center of order dedicated to the true "Vision of Balance."

He walked alone into that imposing building. Inside the Hall of Merit, countless names—some strange, some familiar—were carved into the towering walls. He recalled the fierce ambition of his youth: to carve the name his father gave him onto those stone walls, to stand alongside history.
A Notebook Hidden in His Pocket

Page 1: Special Purpose The commander in chief gifted me a notebook. He hoped I would inherit his habit: recording every challenge from my subordinates. They bring vigilance and wisdom, making the troops more loyal and brave. Page 17: A Record of Failure Captain Chris pleaded with me to order the flank's retreat. The supply line had been cut—sooner or later, they'd all freeze to death in those mountains. I began to waver: "Hold for twelve more hours and reinforcements will arrive ..." He roared: "But twelve hours means hundreds of lives!!" It was a hard call, but I agreed to the retreat. *Note: The flank was lost. Ten times as many soldiers died as a result. Mercy destroyed that battle. Page 38: Reflections on Sacrifice The medical team sent to assist was trapped in the city—an obvious trap. As commander, I could not afford to be foolish. I rejected all objections and pleas, ordering a full-speed retreat and abandoning the rescue. We won the battle, but the logistics chief refused to attend the victory celebration. I realized then that my troops would likely lose considerable medical support going forward. *Note: An overcorrection born of shortsightedness. I still paid the price for my own foolishness. Page 69: Disagreement with the Chief of Staff Clearly, morale was low. We needed a chance to breathe. I refused to execute high command's order to hold our position. Chief of staff Krutov strongly disagreed, protesting with barely concealed sarcasm. I told him: leak word of our retreat, then blanket the withdrawal route with artillery fire. Retreat was seen as "cowardly failure" at the time, but later proved an effective tactic for buying time to prepare our counteroffensive—we successfully lured the enemy deep and struck back. *Note: Preserving morale is vital, but feigning weakness is an even greater skill.
The Leader

Pandora Wilson: Sorry for the wait, Mr. Igor. Our preparations took longer than usual because we rarely interview someone with a ... delicate identity like yours.
Igor: That is understandable. I take no offense.
Pandora Wilson: First question—and forgive the indelicacy—why did you agree to an unofficial interview from a magazine?
Igor: I did my research on you—independent principles, wide-ranging topics, and no record of manipulating public opinion.
Pandora Wilson: But surely we're not the only publication like that.
Igor: An old friend of mine often submits to you. I have read a few issues of UTTU myself in my spare time.
Pandora Wilson: ... Oh? We're honored. Was there anything in particular that appealed to you?

Igor: It seems you have answered the first question for me.
Pandora Wilson: *chuckle* You're more talkative than I imagined, and more dominant. This has given us some unexpected material.
Pandora Wilson: Now, let's move to our main topic—your past with the St. Pavlov Foundation ...

Foundation Medical Kit

A cleverly designed portable medical kit. The interviewee demonstrated its quick-access features and explained her unique system for organizing medicines. She added that in emergencies where a full medical case isn't practical, this kit represents the bare minimum for travel.
"The Knight's Helping Hands"

A pair of knight's gauntlets bestowed upon the interviewee by the Hochland Order. Forged from finely polished wrought iron with classical, restrained lines. Their surface still bears the warmth of careful upkeep and the marks of time. In our view, gauntlets used for rescue and aid embody the truest expression of chivalry.
Trench Raider Club

A solid, heavy trench weapon. Unlike any other melee weapon we've documented, the interviewee has melted away what should have been its most lethal edge. As an "unqualified weapon," its smooth surface conveys a restrained, tranquil beauty.
The Nightwatch at Dawn

With the end of the Crusades, Europe's knightly class embarked on a long journey from the classical world toward modernity. By the late 19th century, when the embers of faith still flickered, even the Hochland Order could not remain untouched.

The Order's revival also occurred in that final century before belief faded entirely. A red-haired girl trained in the stone halls of the monastery. She polished her longsword after morning prayer and studied ancient maxims—until war came.

In that catastrophe known as "modern warfare," knights stood numb upon scorched earth. Every ancient creed crumbled under the thunder of artillery. Industrialized war had no room for knightly glory—before roaring guns, creeping poison gas, and endless trench warfare, mercy, protection, and sacrifice all seemed small and laughable.

She saw it all. She saw the Order's members began to accept that the age had turned. They no longer believed themselves saints from legend, but ordinary people holding fast to old oaths. She saw that this long night devouring humanity had never belonged to ancient knights, and had never promised glory to those who kept watch.

It was on that day she laid down her arms.
War Report: The Miracle of the Knight in White

To investigate the rumors, I crossed half of Europe to Montpaix in eastern France. Some call her a miracle; others describe it as some arcane practice of classical medicine. To me, it seems more like hope born from the desperation of the wounded.

Thanks to my profession, I was able to meet the "Knight in White" herself—Marsha Rosenhart. She sat calmly at the edge of a bed in the makeshift tent. Sunlight filtered through canvas onto her shoulders.

"A technician happened to notice my use of painkillers and reported it out of concern," she said evenly. "The Logistics Committee worried I was overworking myself and decided I needed a temporary rest."

"Is it true? Why do you rely on medication?" I asked directly.

"My arcane skill can absorb pain, but not eliminate it. Without painkillers, I'd never sleep through the night." She answered without hesitation.

An unexpected answer—one that also solved the mystery behind her miraculous treatment.

"Why push yourself this far?" I asked, knowing my readers would ask the same question.

"I am a knight," she said, her voice firm. "To be a knight means enduring and protecting. Those are vows I must uphold."

Dear readers, I've always prided myself on objectivity and restraint in my reporting.

Yet beyond the miracles she performs on broken bodies, perhaps there truly is another kind of miracle dwelling within the heart of Marsha Rosenhart.
The Meaning of Pain

Pandora Wilson: I imagine many readers will be astonished by your experiences—absorbing pain from so many different people, in so many different degrees. Would you say those experiences made you who you are today?
Marsha: I'm not sure ... The way I see it, pain doesn't make people stronger. It's just that in learning how not to break, you slowly become someone different.
Pandora Wilson: You mean suffering itself has no meaning?
Marsha: I haven't thought that deeply about it. Suffering is just suffering—there's nothing special about it. Like ... someone who's never been through war can still understand how precious life is.
Pandora Wilson: Oh? Excellent. Let me try to distill your point: you believe that pain itself has no inherent value—what matters is the spirit and resilience people show when confronting it. Is that right?
Marsha: ... Hm?
Pandora Wilson: Thank you for sharing. This has been a reflective and inspiring interview.
Tailor-Made Cavalier Hat

A folded-brim cavalier hat. Its upturned brim is designed to avoid interfering with the steel winged headpiece the wearer has on her head. The interviewee seems particularly fond of the tall, pointy decorations, wearing them even at the risk of piercing through the hat's crown.
Ceremonious Cape

A magnificent, dignified cape—not designed for ambush or combat, yet one that allows the interviewee to move freely through palace halls. "The deep jewel tone is solemn without being dreary. The embroidery balances classical motifs with Art Nouveau styling. The tassels must be short enough, and the fabric needs to be stiff and well-tailored so it won't interfere with shouldering and aiming a rifle." The interviewee clearly possesses considerable expertise in costume design, which deepens our curiosity about her professional background.
"Ode to Peace"

A smokeless rifle with finely engraved detailing, meticulously maintained inside and out. The rifling bears not a speck of grime, guaranteeing each bullet departs at peak velocity to pierce cleanly through the skull of any who would shatter the peace. Peace, of course, is forged by weapons—it always has been.
"Soaring Over the Steppe"

A silver circlet. It remains attached to her no matter how she moves, as if it were a part of her body. The engraved patterns likely originate from the steppe of her homeland. She once mentioned: "When something moves me, it must be connected to a place I've lived."
"Stainless Heart"

A set of repair tools. When the writer arrived, the interviewee was polishing them. Judging from their gentle gleam, they must see frequent use.
While demonstrating them for us, her clothing accidentally knocked one tool loose. Clearly, with her military background, she has yet to adapt to such decorative attire.
"A Reminder of Home"

A handcrafted medal remade into a brooch. The emblem is etched with traces of windblown sand, in stark contrast with the silk ribbon beneath.
When we brought it up, the interviewee's gaze turned firm—"It's just an old thing." The writer understood the subject was closed.
"Acceptable Blood Loss"

An "unusual" syringe.
Its casing is cast from lightweight alloy. The interviewee prepares the solution—a mixture of mercury, sulfur, and small amounts of purified chemical extracts.
The writer noticed a tube connected to the rear of the syringe. When asked about its purpose, they explained: the formula requires their blood as a base. They have conducted this experiment hundreds of times already.
"Golden Touch"

A gauntlet cast from base metal alloys. Intricate mechanisms are embedded within, capable of responding to heart rate and skin temperature.
This gauntlet once caused an accident—the spare metal on the laboratory bench instantly liquefied.
"Need to adjust the sulfur ratio—more than the mercury, less than the salt. Lower body temperature below normal readings. Then it will be perfect," the interviewee wrote.
"Insight from the Hanging One"

Multiple badges pinned to the interviewee's waist and chest, engraved with different arcane symbols representing enlightenment and ...
"No one cares what those things actually mean," the interviewee cut in. "But they've got a nice bite to them. Want to try?"
Since the badges' material remains unverified, the writer strongly advises readers against imitating this peculiar habit ...
Morning Tea Set

A tea set for beverages and desserts. These pieces arrived at the castle across different eras. A century ago, the old master favored the silver teapot, while his great-granddaughter treasured the porcelain teacups. Now they are all lifted gently by a steady hand, producing melodious, layered chimes as they're set down—bringing delicacies and attentive care to every guest.
Emblem of Glory

A brilliant gold medal adorned with rubies and pearls. Not something you'd expect on an ordinary waitress. Is this impressive medal a royal commendation, or a secret gift from someone powerful? The interviewee offered no explanation, and faced with such a bright smile, we found ourselves unable to press further.
Night Watch

A ring of keys and a slumbering teddy bear, guardians of the castle's order and peace around the clock. When young guests fear the shadows that fall at night, the interviewee leaves the bear as a companion. "It's enormously strong and can chase away all the bad people. It has a brave heart, too."

He carries so much—sins, betrayals, and the names of fallen comrades.
Where the Banner Points
The living and the dead charge together beneath an invisible banner.
They walk through fire to wipe away the dust that dims their glory.
And This I Swear
She sacrifices herself to fulfill the true meaning of ancient oaths.
By Reflections Witnessed
The bell's toll echoes, a silent reflection in the mirrored hall, announcing the beginning of a new day.

Now she stands outside a historic venue, dressed in crisp formal attire.
The Palace of Versailles, once the crown jewel of monarchy, drew countless admirers in its time. But now, its beauty goes largely unnoticed. People gather here for one reason only—the possibility of peace at last.
She is neither invited delegate nor palace servant. Drawing on years of battlefield experience, this sniper has infiltrated the magnificent palace. Her mission is clear and unwavering—eliminate any potential threats and ensure this conference, which holds the fate of millions in the balance, proceeds without incident.
Inside the mirrored hall, pens hover over paper, and the treaty awaits signatures—though it is far from fair. Born of competing interests, it inevitably carries traces of hypocrisy and deception. Yet it has halted the war, however briefly, and nudged the world one step closer to something resembling order.
She believes true peace will come eventually. It will live in endless laughter and fill every ordinary moment.
Idyll of the Luberon
Perhaps this moment of tranquility is what she's been yearning for.

In Provence's summer, lavender blooms into a purple sea.
Not far from the lavender fields stands Gordes Castle. Built in the 11th century, the fortress remains formidable even now, offering shelter to those displaced by war.
Moldir and her siblings have come here. After leaving the battlefield behind, they've finally crossed through the smoke and seen the world as it truly is. The shrieking in the air no longer comes from bombs, but from fireworks bursting overhead.
Yet war's shadow still clings to them. When you've grown accustomed to something, it's hard to simply walk away. Every night, Moldir inspects the castle grounds to ensure it can withstand any attack.
Again and again. Endlessly.
Forever Is Too Short
Those creatures who once gently licked our hands have given their lives so that we may make ours eternal.

Inside the dim laboratory, Medicine Pocket records vital signs and physiological data—monitored by the machine, the agony of blood boiling from alchemical practice is converted into measurable data. This agony has value—before long, it will serve a greater purpose.
Intermittent stabs of pain spread through their nerves. In a daze, they see that little kennel again. It was a sunny afternoon. The dogs left their metal cages for the first time, sniffing curiously at the grass before them. Behind their ears, light blue identification codes remained. They were the survivors.
Not far from the lawn, in the backyard, tiny graves dot the ground. Even now, the researcher can still recall how those experimental dogs watched people with their glassy eyes. Those wet licks and soft touches—all of it now sealed inside a single pill.
In 1935, the Monument to the Unknown Dog was erected at the Institute of Experimental Medicine in Leningrad. Every step forward of the human civilization carries the weight of these little lives.
Service Fit for Royalty
The sun is shining; time to start the day's work.

Bunny Bunny's Schedule 7:00 AM Prepare breakfast—a large serving of bacon and eggs with a cup of butter coffee. Remember to bring the guest in the guest room his meal! He just broke through the blockade yesterday to get here. He's carrying important documents—supposedly vital to the safety of more than 30 big shots ... I need to help him make sure those files don't fall into Manus Vindictae's hands. 11:00 AM Provide lunch for the visitors. These visitors are up to no good—they're looking for someone. I know exactly who! Good thing I hid the guest beforehand ... But they trashed all the rooms I'd just tidied! 2:00 PM Help the butler move today's supplies. Not heavy at all! Apparently these supplies were seized from Manus Vindictae. No wonder the crates feel slimy—how filthy. Don't they practice personal hygiene? 9:00 PM Get ready for bed, but remember to bring the master some late-night snacks. The visitors from this afternoon planted bugs inside the lamp! How sneaky!

Quiet has returned within the crumbling fences. Neither the herdsmen nor the herd looked back toward their homes.
... Coffee itself isn't rare. Making it well—that takes skill.
Brew it too long and it turns bitter and harsh. Too short, and it's bland as snowmelt.
It reminds me of wartime. The days when we would lap up fallen snow just to quench our thirst.
I suppose so.
People who leave the battlefield—if their minds aren't filled with new things ...
What they see when they close their eyes is only guns, blood-smeared faces, and campfires flickering in the night.
Not entirely. Too much coffee makes people more awake.
In the end, I always find myself holding a cup, inviting whoever's still here to share a drink ...
So, want one?
Of course.
This teacup was a gift from an orange-haired girl with a blue ribbon.
She told me that every afternoon, she'd gather her friends for tea parties out on the plains.
Perhaps someday I'll join those children at their tea parties ...
Bringing my jar of fireflies.
The weather here is always changing.
Just now it was clear—suddenly storm clouds are gathering and the wind's picking up.
Could you give me a hand? Please take that kettle of hot water to the lounge.
Oh, you can smell it?
Recently, Ms. NewBabel asked me to help care for the "overly energetic" sleepless Critters out on the plains.
So I added some sage to the Drowsy Sheep Tincture.
Thank you. You've been a great help.
But please, keep the kettle away from the Teakettlers.
Otherwise they get too excited and start spraying steam everywhere, like a pot boiling over.
Ms. NewBabel always says perhaps I'm a natural-born Critter tamer ... because I can sense shifts in their emotions faster than anyone else.
The communication device is the most honest thing on the battlefield.
It never pretends to be brave, never lies. It simply relays what it knows, faithfully.
This is a song Moldir used to love playing on the dombra.
"Oh golden summer, you've lingered too long."
"We lift our cups to the dwindling days. "
... I can't quite remember the rest.
... I did.
Back then, my comrades always asked me to keep the beat for them.
They kept singing even when snowflakes landed on their faces—
"My heart that yearns for home."
"Will be carried by ravens back to the steppes."
The air is always freshest after it rains.
Like earth, dew, and grass mixed with a hint of benzoin.
That silver-haired girl who loves meditation gave some to me recently.
It helps ease the pain of the wounded.
But at night, when I'm alone with all kinds of pain ...
I use it to help me sleep sometimes.
Muddy puddles in the trenches, bloodstains, mangled bodies, and those who collect them.
But there's more than that.
Rain passing through forests, drumming on armor with a crisp sound.
Horses resting under trees, nuzzling me gently. Makes me very nostalgic.
Are you learning how to make coffee?
To forget?
Can I have a cup?
Smells like medicine.
Need more boiling water?
I hear ... a song? The melody sounds sad.
I hear ... a song? Did you used to sing?
Benzoin?
Does the rain remind you of anything?

Clue Summary Mr. Creius' letter mentions there's information on Urd hidden in Bereggrad on the Eastern Front, which is also where Lilya lost contact with the Foundation. To investigate Urd's whereabouts and ensure Lilya's safety, Team Timekeeper must head to the Eastern Front.

Clue One: Mr. Creius arranges for Ms. Marsha to meet Team Timekeeper in Tamarovka. The Timekeeper confirms that Lilya is safe and receives assistance from Vice Admiral Burakov, the commander of the Zeno Cavalry Corps on the Eastern Front.
Clue Two: Igor has critical intelligence regarding Urd. He will share it if the Timekeeper and the Cavalry Corps agree to work with his Gryphon Legion to confront Krutov's army together.
Clue Three: In the Amber Room, the Timekeeper finds some information that is hard to understand. It seems she wants to go back there after the war ends ...

Clue Four: The Timekeeper does not uncover more details about Urd or the vessel ensoulment experiments in the Amber Room, but she and Igor reach a mutual understanding. She believes that as long as their goals align ... or do not conflict, she can trust him.

Clue Summary A former Zeno admiral, Igor defected during the São Paulo incident, taking his forces to join Manus Vindictae. After the Antarctic incident, he separated from Manus Vindictae, causing a split with his close ally Krutov, who continues to work with the Manus. Igor proposes forming a cooperative alliance with the Timekeeper and Vice Admiral Burakov to stop Krutov's forces.

Clue One: Throughout their conflicts with Krutov's army, the Cavalry Corps remains on the defensive. Blinded by his hatred, Ptolemy worsens the situation. Igor, however, sees something on the battlefield that gives him a slight advantage.

Clue Two: Using intelligence obtained at the cost of Gryphon soldiers' lives, Igor learns about Krutov's movements. Igor uses his arcane skill to teleport himself and his soldiers into the heart of the enemy formation, confronting Krutov's army directly in a final battle.

Clue Three: After the final battle, Igor and the Timekeeper seem to return to the Amber Room in secret. According to the Timekeeper, Igor hopes to establish further cooperation with her and has shared crucial intelligence about Krutov.

Clue Summary Ms. Marsha was once a knight of the Hochland Order and later became a medic for the Foundation, moving from battlefield to battlefield. After the battles on the Western Front ended, she joined "XII" Squad under Mr. Creius. She is currently escorting willing fighters to the Don River region to support the Eastern Front. Under Commander Ivan's direction, Ms. Marsha stations her team in Tamarovka, where she unexpectedly finds Merel, who has deserted her squad.

Clue One: Before the siege begins, soldiers from Krutov's army infiltrate Bereggrad to seize supplies. Ms. Marsha rushes to the hospital to protect the children inside, but she encounters an enemy assault and sustains serious injuries.

Clue Two: After the situation on the Eastern Front calms down, Ms. Marsha receives a message from "XII" Squad. She learns that Mr. Creius has already made thorough preparations for Merel, and now her job is to escort her back to the Foundation.

Clue Summary Lilya follows Admiral Somme's orders and heads alone to the Eastern Front on a mission. She discovers some possible traces of the Zeno rebels. However, due to a suspected equipment malfunction, she loses contact with the Foundation before she can relay any specific details.
Clue One: While on the Eastern Front, Lilya follows the Zeno Cavalry Corps under Vice Admiral Burakov's command. After delivering her intelligence, she remains on standby at the camp.

Clue Two: When the Timekeeper arrives on the Eastern Front, she makes contact with Lilya and brings good news: the Foundation has formed the new Flying Witches, who will soon arrive on the Eastern Front.
Clue Three: Lilya temporarily leads the newly formed Flying Witches. She gets a new Su-02ве, allowing her to carry out missions while her old Red-38 is out of commission.

Clue Four: The rites set up by Manus Vindictae in the Don River basin are the main cause of the Golden Famine. After forming a tentative alliance, Igor provides the coordinates of these rites. Lilya leads the Flying Witches to locate and destroy them.
Clue Five: After the final battle, Lilya considers executing Igor herself but is persuaded by his confession, deciding to give him another "chance."

Clue Summary Vice Admiral Ivan Ivanovich Burakov, commander of the Zeno Cavalry, comes from the Don River basin. With the region suffering from the Golden Famine, he leads the Cavalry Corps to protect local residents from bandits. Vice Admiral Burakov was once one of Igor's subordinates and has some understanding of his arcane skill. Based on Lilya's report, he suspects that the "bandits" might actually be Igor's rebels.

Clue One: Vice Admiral Burakov is surprised by the personnel and intelligence the Timekeeper brings but seems somewhat disappointed to learn she is not there to investigate the Golden Famine. Nevertheless, he promises to assist with the Timekeeper's operations.

Clue Two: During negotiations with Igor, Vice Admiral Burakov discovers that the bandits are not just Zeno rebels but Krutov's army working with Manus Vindictae. He recognizes the value of Igor's proposed alliance but still feels hesitant about dealing with this former-colleague-turned-traitor.

Clue Three: To ensure peace in the Don River region, Vice Admiral Burakov decides to cooperate with Igor to jointly counter Krutov's army. This decision goes against orders from the Zeno Command Center, and he is prepared to face a military tribunal for it.
Clue Four: With the Gryphon Legion's assistance, the Cavalry Corps achieves victory on the Eastern Front. As a result, Vice Admiral Burakov begins to let go of some of his suspicions toward Igor.

Clue Summary Colonel Sabina Sternova, chief of staff of the Zeno Cavalry Corps, is known for her military acumen and unwavering loyalty to Vice Admiral Burakov. She previously submitted reports to the Foundation regarding the famine issue in the Don River basin, but no significant progress has been made. Colonel Sternova infers from Lilya's report that the weapons used by the bandits are not something they can acquire independently, strongly indicating Manus Vindictae's support.
Clue One: After the war, Colonel Sternova plans to leave the Don with the Cavalry Corps for the next battlefield.

Clue Summary Sergey is a soldier locally recruited by the Zeno Cavalry. He comes from a village in the Don River basin with a long family history of military service. After unusual climate conditions cause crop failures, he joins the Zeno Cavalry to hunt down local bandits. He has an optimistic nature.

Clue One: After the city's disturbances are quelled, Sergey's squad begins pursuing a patrol team from Krutov's army but falls into an ambush set by a Manus ritualist, resulting in the capture of the entire squad.
Clue Two: Sergey lives through the final battle. He later decides to follow Igor and joins the Gryphon Legion.

Clue Summary Moldir is Igor's adopted daughter and Lopera's older sister. Like Ptolemy, she is loyal to her father, but she is much calmer and has a better understanding of long-term consequences. During the Antarctic incident, she successfully escaped and returned to Igor's forces. During the war on the Eastern Front, Moldir is carrying out missions in other regions on Igor's orders.

Clue Summary Ptolemy is Igor's adopted son. He believes that his father's actions are justified and works tirelessly to achieve Igor's goals. In the outskirts of Bereggrad, he acts as Igor's messenger, delivering messages to the Timekeeper and Vice Admiral Burakov.

Clue One: During a past assassination attempt, Ptolemy lost his left eye while protecting Krutov. When he learns the truth behind the attack, he becomes blinded by revenge, leading to poor judgment in battle.

Clue Summary Mr. Creius previously served as a liaison for the Foundation's military department and is now the captain of the newly formed "XII" Squad. His accomplishments on the Western Front earned him more support within the Hawks. Madam Z deduces that this is a key reason he could obtain intelligence about Urd. Mr. Creius shares the intelligence he has with the Timekeeper to facilitate cooperation between them.

Clue One: For some reason, after the Western Front battles ended, "Blackbird" Merel deserted the "XII" Squad and did not return to the Foundation. Mr. Creius knows she fears him and is avoiding her former squadmates.
Clue Two: Upon learning of Merel's desertion, Mr. Creius forges a "secret order" assigning her to the Eastern Front to investigate the Golden Famine, preparing for her eventual return to the squad.

Clue Summary According to information sent by Ms. Marsha, "XII" Squad's "Blackbird" Merel left her squad during the war on the Western Front and subsequently disappeared. Perhaps her experiences in Antarctica made her desperate to escape the war. Merel meets Mr. Charon on the Western Front. To evade the Foundation's search, she travels with him as his companion.
Clue One: While escaping from Perevoznaya, Merel accidentally falls into a river. After Sergey fishes her out of the Don, she stays temporarily at the Cavalry camp.
Clue Two: Later, Merel follows the Cavalry Corps to Tamarovka, where Ms. Marsha, also a member of "XII" Squad, discovers her. Merel can get help from her, if she does not run again.
Clue Three: Hearing the "secret order" from the "XII" Squad, Merel realizes she will not face punishment from the Foundation but will still have to rejoin her old unit.
Clue Summary A ritualist of Manus Vindictae commands Manus soldiers and manages prisoners of war within Krutov's army. Her true name and genuine purpose for cooperating with Krutov remain unknown.

Clue Summary Mr. Charon is an Awakened who works as a gravedigger on the Western Front, putting fallen comrades to rest. After the war on the Western Front, he travels with Merel and his beloved horse Andreas.
Clue One: After becoming separated from Merel in Perevoznaya, Mr. Charon is captured by Krutov's army.
Clue Two: Before the war starts, Mr. Charon endures horrific torture at the hands of Krutov's soldiers. His bound and mangled body is sent to Bereggrad as a declaration of war.
Clue Three: Thanks to the efforts of Ms. Marsha and Merel, Mr. Charon recovers. He is currently recuperating in Bereggrad.
Clue Four: After the war, Mr. Charon bids farewell to Ms. Marsha and Merel, then continues on his journey with Andreas.

Clue Summary Mr. Irinei fights to increase the Hawks' influence within the Foundation. He firmly believes that establishing a Foundation army is essential to overcoming the unfavorable situation caused by Manus Vindictae and regaining the initiative. The Doves disagree with the Hawks' radical approach, leading to two opposing voices within the Foundation. They work together on the surface, but each side acts for its own goals in secret.

Clue Summary Madam Z has helped the Timekeeper many times, making her one of the few Foundation officials to earn the Timekeeper's trust. Madam Z doubts Mr. Creius's reasons for reaching out to the Timekeeper. She fears the Hawks plan to pull the Timekeeper to their side, or even force her hand. Nevertheless, she trusts the Timekeeper's judgment and approves her mission.

Clue Summary Krutov was once a subordinate under Igor. By working with Manus Vindictae, he has built his army's power in the Don River basin and become a local warlord. Interested in his arcane skill, Krutov wants Charon to serve his army.
Clue One: The main reason Krutov and Igor split was a difference in their ideologies. Krutov despises Igor and wants to destroy the Gryphon Legion in Bereggrad.

Clue Two: Before the battle begins, Krutov tortures Charon and sends his mutilated body to Bereggrad, using his deathly aura to injure the Cavalry Corps' morale. Krutov wants to kill Igor and prove his worth to Manus Vindictae.

Clue Three: Even while he served under Igor, Krutov had big ambitions. He once staged an assassination attempt on the Gryphon Legion to achieve his own goals, making him an enemy of Ptolemy as a result.

Clue Four: On the final battlefield, Krutov undergoes the mask trial, covering the whole field in a harsh winter. However, under the assault from Lilya and the others, Krutov is ultimately defeated. He uses the Manus ritualist's rite to escape Tamarovka, vanishing without a trace.
