On this day in history, Ms. Matilda Bouanich, who is "destined for greatness," was born in Paris.|The one birthday invitation which Matilda was worried about among all the others was sent back again. "Sorry, the recipient is on a field mission."|There is always only one candle on Matilda's birthday cake, which means "Matilda is always No. 1!"|Matilda rose early, chose her outfit with care, and went over every meticulous detail of her birthday party, not for the least reason that—according to her divination—Maman would be there too.|To make her party the best it could be, Matilda had secretly prepared a small gift for each of her friends. "Don't be so surprised; this is precisely what is expected of a Bouanich!"

Bette will get to play her own stand-in today. No script, no style limit, no cuts, just one theme: happy birthday.|Bette was flattered and almost fainted when she heard that Sweetheart the star and Charlie the troupe leader would show up at her birthday party as surprise guests.|Although the heroine fumbled her lines, it was a great show for a birthday party.|When Bette learned she could play the lead in a short film written by Recoleta and directed by Noire, she dove straight into the script to the point that she forgot to even eat her birthday cake.|Bette received the "Best Actress" trophy, presented by the children in the Suitcase. She held up the cardboard trophy and spent three minutes putting together a speech—containing a total of twelve thank-yous.

When asked about memories of his birthdays, Click recalled all the dangerous escapes during the war, which he didn't feel like talking about.|Click decided to open up a birthday-themed section in his personal photography collection, and the first photo he added was the one he took with birthday party guests.|The moment the "cake bomb" passed over Click's body and hit an unfortunate guest in the face, Click immediately raised the camera in his hand.|After having celebrated so many birthdays, Click had enough film to last him years. When someone offered him a new camera as a gift, though, he just hugged his old friend close and shook his head.|After his friends took turns trying to convince him, Click finally handed over his camera with a shy smile, letting everyone take a birthday photo with him.

Sotheby gave Mr. Duncan a ridiculously extravagant birthday gift: a life-sized German Shepherd statue made of pure gold. Mr. Duncan was overjoyed but ultimately politely declined the gift.|Following the design provided by X, Mr. Duncan assembled a decorative drink-pourer from scrap materials. He enjoyed this unique birthday gift.|After declining another one of Sotheby's expensive gifts, Mr. Duncan decided to piece together a Typhon doll for her using scrap materials. He hoped it would bring her a more simple kind of happiness.|Watching the guests bring gifts to Mr. Duncan at his birthday party, Kuku the German Shepherd—not quite sure what was happening—placed his favorite toy in Mr. Duncan's hands.|At this year's birthday party, the little band in the Suitcase played an energetic samba for Mr. Duncan. He barely heard the opening notes before grabbing his flute and joining in, playing and dancing at the same time.

This was not the day written in the notebook—the day when Paul's friends would visit. This was the day Charon woke up on the battlefield. On the day marked in the notebook, Paul wandered along lakes and through woods with nets, returning at nightfall to present captured butterflies beneath the glow of firelight and a mother's proud smile. Charon had never shared the day of his awakening; to him, it was neither birth nor death and held no meaning worth celebrating.|When Sonetto handed him the standard personnel form, Charon completed it meticulously, without considering what would come next. The significance only struck him when the Chief Assistant accidentally dropped a party cracker, and Bunny Bunny began laying out cake, beer, and steak before him.|Though familiar with how the Suitcase residents celebrate birthdays, Charon remained motionless before the cake, unable to grasp why his existence deserved any celebration. Yet the long-closed poppy buds growing on his chest quietly unfurled their petals.|Once everyone figured out that Charon had no need nor interest in food, his birthday spread was replaced with more practical gifts. That said, when Regulus walked in with a bag of fertilizer, Bunny Bunny still threw her out of the room.|After Charon received his third shovel, everyone started giving their gifts to the quiet black horse instead. This year, Andreas received a brand-new set of tack.

In the dry summer of 1459, in a noble residence in Florence, Italy, a banker rushes in, cradling his newborn son. Without pause, he utters the words that will shape the boy's life: "You are an Auditore. You are a warrior. So fight."|On his birthday, his companions in the Suitcase prepare gifts for the Master Assassin. As he marvels at the many unfamiliar trinkets, Ezio discovers a crude mechanical bird, clearly inspired by Da Vinci's designs. "Charming," he thinks, gently rubbing it with his calloused thumb.|While pursuing his quest for vengeance, Ezio never had time to celebrate his birthday. But when Florence held their annual parade in honor of St. John the Baptist, he would muse, "That perhaps sharing a birthday with a man of vision isn't so bad." Back then, he hadn't realized the meaning it would carry.|Urged on by the children, Ezio put on a show: 45 birthday balloons taken out in less than a minute, ending with a smooth sidestep as confetti exploded from the last.|Ezio preferred the rich wine of this era over his birthday cake, surprisingly soft as it was. When the night fell silent, he quietly poured a glass and placed it before the few keepsakes of his father and brothers he had left.
Random waterspouts appear in this terrain.

About a dozen years ago, Alien T spent the last birthday on his mother planet before he left. |Apparently, Alien T missed the lovely little birthday parties his family would throw for him, but this one prepared by the long-limbers on the Blue Planet was better than expected! |Alien T proposed that they should prepare a gift for the cow, too... No, not the cow, but the DUU-DUU-BELL-BOO. |DUU-DUU-BELL-BOO spent the entire day inside aliEn T. Maybe there was a birthday party in there. Maybe even presents. |For his birthday, the Laplace staff have built a 1:1 scale lamp modeled after aliEn T. He appreciates the gesture, and the new method of disguise.

Most girls born on a summer day tend to love summer. Unfortunately, her drowning also happened on a summer day. |When people in the suitcase were discussing the theme for Poltergeist's birthday party, she drew everyone's attention by making noises and shouting "No beach party!" |Poltergeist had been nervous until her birthday finally arrived. Fortunately, she didn't grow another tentacle, probably because her age remained the same. |Poltergeist hid herself away all day today. She wanted to spend it alone—whether in self-reflection or as punishment for all the paranormal phenomena she'd caused. |At this year's party theme discussion, Poltergeist mustered the courage to suggest a beach party, even bringing a light blue sheet for the occasion.

Her routine life often made Kaalaa Baunaa forget special days. After an unexpected round of birthday wishes, she found herself wondering whether to add her birthday to the list of "necessary things." |Kaalaa Baunaa discovered by chance that the astrolabe showed her luck reaching its annual peak on this day. |Kaalaa Baunaa's birthday gifts included complete outfits, and new spectacle frames. She had no idea what to do with any of them. |Kaalaa Baunaa politely declined all suggestions of a lively celebration, instead choosing to pass the day quietly and inviting her friends to spend the evening stargazing. |Kaalaa Baunaa almost missed today after staying up too late the night before watching the stars. Fortunately, her friends waited until night to deliver her birthday cake.

On this day, Pioneer walked by the storefront where he was born, a window made of the most typical type of glass in this era. |The gift box revealed a brand-new pair of hands, flexible and elastic, but lacking the strength to hold anything. After switching to these hands, Pioneer found it difficult to pick up anything heavier than a teacup. J thoughtfully provided a bottle of nail polish. |Pioneer practiced his thank-you speech in advance for receiving blessings. Thanks to the arcane skill of "ventriloquism," he imitated thank-you phrases in various languages and accents, even preparing a crisp birdsong for his beloved pet animal friend. |For today's special event, Pioneer has blended in among the department store's mannequins to play a little game of hide-and-seek with everyone. |To celebrate his birthday, Pioneer has invited some graffiti artists to give him a full street art transformation.

The researchers and volunteers threw a small birthday party for Barbara, gifting her items allowed in the sterile room. She later drifted into a deep sleep, soothed by the gentle bleating of mother sheep and dreaming of lush green pastures. |Barbara spends her birthday looking for stories. After having a cup of coffee at the motel, she pens a well-crafted article and jots down a small number in the corner of her notebook. |Bunny Bunny makes Barbara a cake on her birthday. Upon lifting the box's lid, Barbara finds it difficult to mask her surprise—it looks white, fluffy, and sweet, just like the clouds in her dream. |After all her hard work, Barbara has won Employee of the Month at the UTTU office, presented by the editor-in-chief herself. Nothing makes for a better birthday gift than that. |At Baby Blue's suggestion, Barbara threw a dream-sharing party today. She collected a number of vivid and fascinating dream stories, and everyone who attended got a sound sleep.

On her birthday, Flutterpage finds a box waiting for her—a gift that Willow sent half a month earlier, just to be sure it would arrive on time. Now a fortnight after being sent, the cake finally arrives. Fortunately, it has been dosed with a preservation potion so that Flutterpage will be spared of any digestive complications. |For the first time, Flutterpage celebrates her special day away from her family at the SPDM. Despite being surrounded by new friends, she couldn't help but shed a few tears in secret. |Eagle walks with Flutterpage through the Wilderness for what seems like an eternity, finally finding the gift she has hidden for her in a sheltered nook between some dead wood and jagged rocks. |Flutterpage takes on a part-time job she's never tried before, proof that she's grown up a little bit more. |With Recoleta's help, Flutterpage noted down all sorts of questions from children and compiled them into a book titled What Kids Want to Know. She brought in Eagle and some others to help, too, hoping to use her birthday to finally get some answers from the grown-ups.

Recoleta huddled against the wall, using the steam from a cup of cheap mate to shield her from the cold and the shopkeeper's gaze. She spent hours making the last edits to her manuscript, wished for a smooth submission, then downed the cold tea in one gulp. |Recoleta and Marcus had an engaging discussion on how months and climate are perceived differently. The conversation ended abruptly when inspiration struck—Recoleta hunched over her desk to write, and Marcus quietly left the room. |Ms. Moissan assisted Recoleta in connecting with a printing house. That day, with everyone's help, she sold 81 copies of her self-printed collection. It wasn't a huge number, but it broke her personal record—enough to warrant a celebratory meal shared with friends. |Recoleta earnestly invited everyone to a tabletop game adapted from her novel today—a mystery adventure of dreams, the Suitcase, and time travel that has left every participant utterly befuddled. They haven't even managed to make it halfway through. |Recoleta finds that the bookstore she often used to visit is holding a commemorative event. She settles into the corner of the store and quietly reads "her own" story one more time.

"A child is born on a day in which their mother suffers. We must never forget that day." Cheng Heguang consulted many arcanists skilled in calculation inside the Suitcase before finally recording his birthday according to the standard calendar. |Cheng Heguang prepared longevity noodles meticulously, the rich, savory broth cutting perfectly through the cake's sweet aftertaste. He gave every guest the same instruction: never bite the noodles in half. |Cheng Heguang still follows the ancient lunar calendar, celebrating a second birthday each year. After that date, many receive fish he caught himself—a hometown tradition symbolizing abundance and prosperity for the year ahead. |When Cheng Heguang learned there were more guests than expected, he headed straight out and returned with enough fish to fill the table, making sure everyone had enough to enjoy. |Cheng Heguang initially planned for everyone to experience an Eastern birthday tradition, but with so many young companions in the Suitcase, he tucks away his treasured wine and reaches for the juice instead.

On July 24, Pavia was born in Rome, Italy. No one knows exactly when Pavia was born in Piedmont.|The most exuberant part of the day for Pavia is dessert - he'll knock back a 10-inch, 3-pound black truffle ice cream cake all on his own.|Pavia doesn't need so-called "friends" to celebrate his birthday with. He has his "best pals" - just like in that dark basement.|In the heavy air after a long rain, Pavia finishes the day's missions, steps into a random bar, and downs a liqueur on the rocks.|Pavia sees nothing special about today. He scarfs down a cream cake loaded with sugar and a few scoops of ice cream, then drifts into a dreamless sleep in the company of his "pack."

"Ladies and gentlemen, great offer of Neo-Science Exorcism Office, 12% off only on my birthday!"|On this night, An-an Lee posted a post on her blog "Nai Mang Dik Si" to complain about the bad margarine which Kowloon Bakery used in her cake. The post then received a lot of likes and comments that say "Happy birthday!"|Compared to those expensive and meaningless gifts, the gadgets from flea markets are more to An-an's liking.|An-an Lee is rewatching two classic horror movies with her friends in the Suitcase. It's a good thing they have cake and chocolate to keep their energy up during this four-hour movie marathon.|A big job came in to the Neo-Science Exorcism Office last night. An-an Lee wiped the sweat from her forehead, pulled the well-fed Lily onto her back, and rushed out the door—only to realize midnight had already passed.

On her birthday, Blonney loves to invite her entire class to her home for an all-night slumber party, playing the part of the classic social butterfly in every high school movie.|Blonney fantasizes about staging a "Birthday Night Scare" during the party, but the poor acting skills of her "homicidal maniac" only end up leaving her friends in stitches.|Blonney once spent an utterly unremarkable birthday at Green Lake Campsite—nothing but a cake and a birthday card. Oddly enough, she remembers that day fondly.|The "Lil' Scarface" series launched a new blind box set, and Blonney collected all of them—including the secret one—on her birthday.|Blonney's friends have made her a cake decorated with berries, pink syrup, and plenty of strawberry jam. She takes a knife and cuts the first slice.

"I thought it was just a normal day, like any other day. Same morning, same noon, same night," she said with some surprise.|"Now that time is flowing out of order, in which calendar are you looking for July 27th?" That's what she said.|"It's an interesting custom to celebrate a birth with a cream-covered circle and a shortened line to represent age! Oh! So I should blow them out?" She looked curious.|"I know—the day has come again. So when the numbers representing time turn from '23:59:59' to '00:00:00,' you'll be celebrating for me!" she exclaims proudly.|"If I move the ice cream just slightly, the center of the dodecagram will align perfectly with the golden ratio of this line," she says as she shifts the plate.

That day, Getian watched as the scholar entered the city to take his exams, wiped his sweat with a cloth, leafed through books in the shadow of his hat, and then Getian completely forgot about the rest of what happened. The only thing he was sure of was that it was an extremely hot day.|Entering the door to a meeting, Getian habitually stretches out his wings—the air stirs, and a congratulatory letter written in an ancient script slowly unfolds. He is startled, but not angry.|The new scholar tree in the wilderness is the work of Druvis III. Under the tree, Getian tightens his wings and tries to tell bone-related anecdotes to blend in with the group. This is clearly unnecessary, as he is already the center of the birthday celebration.|Confetti and glitter have found their way onto Getian's wings. Having grown familiar with these celebrations, he holds back the urge to preen his feathers.|On one birthday, Getian received a record player and a vinyl record. After several attempts to get it working, rock music exploded from it like a shaken soda. His nerves didn't recover for months.

Eagle was born in Washington, D.C., USA. When she came into this world, her father was serving in the military.|The organization does not celebrate birthdays for boy and girl scouts, but luckily, Eagle receives a small cake from the Institutum on this day.|Every year on this day, Eagle shows up at the Arlington Cemetery. She wishes her father could watch her grow up, like all regular fathers do.|On her first birthday at Laplace, Eagle is surprised to receive special birthday badges from every department. It doesn't take her long to figure out they all came from Ms. Marguerite's arcane printer.|While opening her birthday presents, Eagle finds an unsigned copy of The Spy's Handbook. She spends the rest of the day reading through it carefully.|Eagle spends three hours searching the Arlington National Cemetery of this era, but finds nothing. She returns to the hotel and quietly reports her growth over the last year to a faded sash.

You run your hand over the desk in the study room.
It always feels familiar.

The books here are new.
That smell of fresh paper hangs in the air.

There seem to be faint traces of arcane energy here.
Maybe the exit is close.

The shelves hold books from many different fields.
Some have gathered a little dust.
Manus Believer
Stop!
I order you to answer my question.
Where is the one who gave you your orders?
(This way ...?)
(These believers aren't smart enough to describe the location in words ...)
Leave.
Where are you headed in such a rush?
Ustrina
Haven't you heard the commotion on the higher floors? I do not intend to allow that scheming brute Krutov to take all the glory this day.
Taira
There is no glory to be found in this battle. It is only a means to an end. The Guiding One wishes to speak to someone within the Foundation.
Don't you understand? She has come to the Foundation in person. How could it possibly be just a social call?
We have a chance to destroy the Foundation completely; why should we not seize it?
Now, of all times? This attack is rushed.
Arcanists are dying en masse. That is not our goal.
Staying hidden, biding our time in the shadows—that's what suits us. Like it always has.
This is why I'd rather deal with simpletons like Krutov. He'll soon get what he deserves, of course.
The Guiding One has never objected to the idea of us going to the Foundation with Her.
Nor has She agreed.
I don't think attacking the Foundation or destroying a shelter for arcanist children will bring any outcome that truly benefits us.
I can move again! Has Arcana left?
I think so, though I feel nothing.
"Razor" Captain
The hallway has taken heavy damage. Nautika, can you still take off?
Ms. Nautika, please take me with you. There must be something I can help with.
Alright, everyone on my back and hold tight. We're flying up to join our other allies!
Hey, good to see you all here! In the mood for some rock music?
Captain, I'm afraid this is no time for that.
The enemy is retreating, but there are still remaining Manus Vindictae forces inside the building. We can't afford to let our guard down.
I can use these trees to evacuate people, but someone needs to take out the remaining enemies.
Leave it to me and "Razor" Captain! We'll sweep them out floor by floor!
Yeah, this Rockin' Pirate will make sure to kick those black-robed freaks out!
I'll help too!
Whoa, nice move with your tail, Nautika! You sure you don't want some rock music to go with that?
Ms. Recoleta, watch out!
Thank you! Perfect shot. You kept the collection safe!
The Manus are almost wiped out! Go aid allies in need!
Roger that, boss! I'll go help out the ladies!
Oh, don't worry about me—my tail is strong enough to protect everyone!
Your Honor? I rarely see you outside the Court. It seems this disaster at Headquarters has meant changes for all of us ...
The jury has reached a preliminary verdict on your case. But that doesn't mean I intend to give up my "inquiries" outside the Committee.

Pity. I was rather hoping this was a purely social call. Ever since the trial was recessed, I‘ve been wondering—have you decided to let me off this time, or are you simply gathering more evidence against me?
... Let's pick up where we left off. You confessed to "sending a subordinate to use a tracking serum on a member of your own squad."
In past cases, given the exigencies of war, leniency has been shown to commanders for similar lapses in judgment—but what I'm more curious about is the source of this "tracking serum."
I believe I made everything perfectly clear to the Committee. It was a "positioning test sample" from the Medical Department's warehouse. An independent report has already confirmed it was harmless.

I've reviewed that "report"—the one unauthorized by the Foundation's medical institution. So allow me to correct the record: it was a "positioning test sample lacking official safety clearance from Headquarters."
In other words, the serum's origin is unknown—and that's the real question. Where exactly did you obtain this "tracking serum?"
Your Honor, "documentation and judgment" may be within your authority, but "speaking or remaining silent" is still my right.
... Are you threatening a Special Tribunal Officer?
You misunderstand me. I'm simply saying I can't answer that question. Perhaps you can ask me again at the next "trial"—

I have a document here proving that in October 1920, following the tenth "Storm," you dispatched Yermolai to the Don River region to investigate a classified research project long since abandoned by the Foundation.
I don't like to presume, but I get the feeling that it isn't the "tracking serum" that you're actually after. It's the investigation itself.

You sent Yermolai to Bereggrad to investigate the vessel ensoulment experiments—yet he returned with the "tracking serum" and administered it to Merel immediately, without keeping any record. I assure you, that falls well outside the operational mandate of the "XII" Squad.
... The White Stone House sees further than I expected.
Back on topic—what were your findings regarding the vessel ensoulment experiments?
None. Yermolai never located the "Amber Room." He only found a leftover vial of the "tracking serum" in a separate hidden warehouse in Bereggrad.
The "tracking serum" is indeed related to cross-era dye marking—a product of the vessel ensoulment experiments. In the past, researchers used it to track subjects reversed by the "Storm."
And you simply administered it to a member of your own squad? Did you give no thought to any potential consequences when you issued that order?
My only concern was achieving the objective. If there's a cost to pay for it, I will—and clearly, your decision to meet me in private suggests the price is negotiable.
I'm still thinking about Platonic solids.
Oh, here we go again. Philosophy's too deep for me.
Grundriss
It's actually pretty simple ... Plato believed that everything we see is just a "shadow." Their real "essence" is hidden from us.
Like ... you see a circle drawn on the ground, and no matter how you look at it, it's never quite perfect, right?
Of course. No one can draw a perfect circle.
In your mind, what would a "perfect circle" look like?
Hmm ... smooth edges, perfect, symmetrical?
Exactly. This "perfect circle" in your mind is what Plato calls a "Form."
I don't really understand. What does that have to do with the buildings here ...?
You may have already noticed that the buildings in Nowa Miedź are covered in triangles, squares, pentagons ...
They remind me of the prototypes of those Forms Plato listed in Timaeus.
That's not unusual—aren't most modern buildings made up of geometric shapes? Straight lines, squares, triangles, they're everywhere.
No, it's not the same. The geometric layout here doesn't simply seem to be pursuing any clear function—
They exist in a more ... natural way. Maybe it's a kind of design language. A language of materials ...
I need to understand it ... understand it again.
Everything has to start over from the beginning.
Looks like we all agree that repairing the dome is an experiment worth the risk. But how long will it take? A year? A month? A week?
Kenna
I'm sorry I can't really give you an accurate time.
That's exactly what worries me, and yet ...
We've worked together for years. I've always trusted your professional judgment and instincts.
The New Office Construction Project has a firm deadline. The Committee naturally wants it completed as soon as possible, which means resources will flow to the alternative with better potential.
If you can prove this building's worth in the short term, I'd be glad to persuade the other Committee members on your behalf.
But before that, you need to deal with some basic, practical problems first ...
I understand. I need to finish the survey first. Structure, materials ... every detail matters.
After the "temporal anomaly," the dome might not be the only risk in a partially collapsed building. Cracks in the walls, foundation instability from water damage ... I need to sort all of that out.
But if a building that survived the "temporal anomaly" only had a few issues like these to fix, the Committee wouldn't have hesitated.
So please, give me ... two weeks. I need two weeks to finish the on-site survey, then I'll deliver a practical phased timeline and risk contingency plan.
No. I'll buy you more time.
Cheers! To your health, to Olga's stock, uh, and—
Jasio
To ample budgets! Return flights and ... quality construction!
Well said! To quality ... oh, it's you.
Everyone's drinking today, aren't they? We've got good wine here, and I won't let Cornerstone drink alone ... *burp*
Is the bar spinning?
That just means you haven't had enough yet, miss. Another round! To the ceiling, the bar, and the table!
To the table! ... Ugh, I'll regret this tomorrow.
No regrets, miss. See? I never regret anything.
When I wrote that poem ... when I got the rejection letters ... when Kamila left me ... See? No regrets!
Even when Kamila took our little Lena away, I didn't ... not one tear, I promise you that!
Little Lena?
My daughter. My brilliant daughter, black hair just like her mother's ... They went to West Germany ... My Lena used to write to me all the time.
Have I ever shown you her letters?
*burp*—oh, no. I've never seen you sober before ...
Those letters, in her pretty little handwriting: "Take care of yourself, Dad" ... No, now that's all that's left. Just the letters.
It's all gone. After the rain ... all I have left are her letters ...
It took everything—Lena, Kamila, and tomorrow ... Cheers to our vanishing tomorrow!
Cheers ... Cheers ...
We've had a lot of debriefings lately. It's rare for someone to come back on time as you did.
Foundation Officer
I'm just used to getting the job done and getting out.
Your old boss got reassigned again.
I know. I paid her a visit.
Did she say anything?
She said history doesn't reward loyalty, but it can inspire victory. And ... she told me not to end up like her.
She's the one who got you into the Foundation. That's a strange thing to say if she wants you to look back.
I don't understand what you mean.
... Too many people in the Foundation are in a rush to pick sides lately.
I've heard—the Hawks and the Doves. Both sides seem to make good points.
That's right. But when the wall comes down, no one wants to admit they were the first brick to give way. We're not picking a side yet.
Understood. I'll stay with you for now.
Alright, let's get to business. Headquarters is concerned about this "ghost." Any updates?
Based on the data from the Clappy Jelly ... the whole building's energy seems to be linked to her.
Could she be related to these stones that are immune to the anomaly?
Nothing's for certain. But it's highly likely she shares the same origin as those stones—wherever the stones are, she is close behind.
Anything else? We'd appreciate any details you can offer.
There was a moment when I picked up a rise in her energy on the Clappy Jelly while people were singing.
You can speak more plainly.
Her existence might be tied to that rhyme ... that's just my theory. The current data can't confirm it yet.
Fascinating ...

Such a lovely day, isn't it?
These noisy children are soon going to be locked behind the school gate, and I will say goodbye to you.
This war will be over as long as I close my eyes. It has lasted far too long.
Finally ...
What are you doing standing around? Aren't you heading to school? Go on then. Children your age are SUPPOSED to be learning and playing.
I graduated long ago.#I'll miss you.
College then. Get yourself a doctorate at least.
Haven't you realized how precious peace is after coming back from the battlefield? Make your life count.
I'm going to take a nap. Now, go and find something to keep yourself busy.
Oh, please.
Take a look at that tree. I think it must feed on the escape plans of students like you; how else could it grow two inches taller every year?
I imagine it might even serve as something of a secret hideout for them.
But I wonder if anyone ever bothers to visit it again after they leave; likely not. A once beloved place all too quickly forgotten.
Do you know why?
Because they are too afraid to face the difficult truth.
That they wasted the most carefree days of their lives trying to escape from paradise into hell, and now there's no power in heaven or earth that can send them back.
You'll end up just as pathetic as them, unless you can go back there and prove your courage.
You won't have anything like the fanfare your French classmate received—she was proud as a peacock when she walked through that gate. But you'll not chicken out, will you?
What's beneath your hat?
My head.#My face.
Just a head, no creepy black bones sticking out from your temples?
Thank goodness. I'm not sure I could handle another conversation with those lunatics.
I do hope, if you ever find a bone stuck through your brain one day, that you won't hesitate to see a doctor.
But why bother covering such a pretty face? You're young and good-looking.
Don't be so shy to show it off. If that boneheaded lunatic doesn't bother to hide her face, you shouldn't either.
But seriously, if you do find a bone stuck through your brain one day, don't hesitate to see a doctor.
I don't call that woman a lunatic without good reason.
I doubt I would survive it.#It might hurt a bit.
So you say, but you know what happened to her: she died and came back.
That is a rare privilege. How many can say they had the same gift? Death tends to be terribly final for most.
She was the exception, and just look at what she's made of it.
Life is pain. Lately it seems like every bone in my body aches ... Worse, the pain seems to come no matter the weather.
But I wasn't rewarded with immortality for all my pains.
It seems unfair that a privilege like that should be given to such a troublemaker.
This whole damned world is coming to an end!
*sigh* I'm surprised, I must say.
Why would anyone else want to talk to you in riddles the same way I do?
It's kind of a chore being this vague, to be honest. He has to be getting paid for this.
Are you paid to talk to me?#Are you actually interested in talking to me?
If only.
All I've received in compensation for our little talks is a dry tongue. I've already poured three pots of tea today.
Do you think you're all that interesting a conversation partner?
I'm not some retiree who has nothing else to do.
The only reason I talk to you is because you won't leave my house.
What else should I do? I'm not strong enough to throw you out.
My only defense is a razor-sharp wit, though it seems to never cut you deep enough to matter. I swear at times I think you've been glued into that chair.
*sigh* Never mind. Sometimes we just have to accept the little disappointments in life.
That old dust whines about the plaster figures intruding in his room. But that's all he's done so far.
If he wants to take over for me, do let me know. If it means not having to come up with any more riddles, I'll even let him sit in my chair.
It seems that just about everyone has accepted that death must inevitably follow the rain.
But not you. How many loved ones have you lost? You keep count, don't you?
The same tragedy has played out over and over again ever since your "Acting Principal" first brought you into that stark gray building. Do you really think anything can be done for them?
This will be the last time.#They're still alive somewhere.
It won't—not yet; this isn't the last golden thread you'll follow. More will come. More upon more until you can't see anything else.
Then you'll wind up just as blind as she was ...
But I don't say that to scare you. You're lucky. Someone will always be there to show you the way.
I've said it before: anyone who has forgotten their own name is as good as dead.
But that might not always be the case, if that's any comfort.
It's far easier to help someone remember what they've once forgotten than it is to bring the dead back to life.
But that just means the burden on your shoulders is all the heavier.
You'll carry that weight until it breaks you. So, why not just save the world instead?
Dead or alive—drag them all into that magical Suitcase. It'll save you some trouble, and you'll get to be the savior you've always wanted to be.
But if you can't save them all, the least you can do is remember their names for them.
The rain has fallen on some more than others; each time it washes something away. In the end, who they are and who they become will be up to you.
Pre-Storm Field Observation Reports

According to field reports submitted by Marcus, Semmelweis, and other operatives across European branches, locations marked as "critical points of time" are now scattered across Europe in the current historical period. Both their number and distribution far exceed anything previously on record.
This is a turbulent era. The territorial and political disputes left by the war have Europe redrawing its map in blood and paperwork, while many nations are still rebuilding. Famine, unemployment, the lingering effects of influenza, and other post-war wounds pervade everyday life. Rebellious movements like Dadaism take root in the spiritual confusion of the age. The invention of wireless radio and small home appliances sparks the first stirrings of a technological revolution ...
Despite repeated reinforcements, new "critical points of time" continue to surface in cities and corners across multiple countries, and we are still unable to pinpoint where Manus Vindictae are most active. With a severe manpower shortage at the headquarters checkpoint, we can no longer spare operatives for continued observation.
In summary, based on reports from all teams, we are unable to confirm Manus Vindictae's operational direction, mount a targeted counteroffensive, or slow the deterioration and expansion of these "critical points of time." Headquarters has decided to execute the evacuation plan immediately in order to preserve as many of our forces as possible. All field team leaders are to order and urge their operatives to return to headquarters without delay or proceed to the nearest shelter to take refuge from the "Storm."

Legends of the School Watchtowers

[The last page torn from a book, treated with a visibility potion—the invisible ink now exposed.] This afternoon I overheard the instructor slip up—she said something like "back when the school didn't have the watchtowers ..." What does that tell us? Those five towers are no ordinary structures; they were built for a reason! Our earlier suspicions just might be right! Which one do you mean? The one about the towers being used to subdue ghosts? Or the one about locking up students who've gone mad? Both! Just think—why would the school suddenly put up towers that serve no purpose and ban every student from setting foot inside? Oh please. Maybe the name says it all—they're just there to watch us. The higher-ups have teachers on duty up there around the clock, holding a long-range stun gun, just waiting for the moment you try to slip out ... and bang, you're down. Even if there really are teachers on duty, I don't believe they can stay awake 24 hours a day. One of these nights we'll find our chance, sneak in, and figure out their secrets for ourselves! Have you lost your mind? What if there are machines inside that can spy on students? We'd get caught in no time. You're just a coward! We'll cover our faces. If something goes wrong, you run first, and I'll cover the rear. Just tell me—are you in or not? Fine ... for the sake of our friendship, I'll go. [A report lies beneath this "secret message," with a few sharp lines on the page.] After comparing handwriting, we have confirmed that the two students responsible are fifth-years Andrea and Oliver. I will personally reprimand them and impose a one-week detention as punishment. Given the recent rumors circulating among students regarding the watchtowers, I propose increasing patrol frequency around the watchtower perimeter and strengthening oversight of the weather-stabilizing doves housed within to avoid any lapses during inspections from the Pax House. Regarding my mistake, I can confirm that I did not mention the "Storm" or that reverse incident during the first "Storm." I will submit a three-thousand-word written apology and reflect seriously on my failures in student management.

Post-Incident Debriefing Record: Display Room Collection Losses

I. Incident Overview
This loss incident at the Headquarters Display Room was triggered by force majeure events, namely the recent Manus attack. The affected items include one Italian portable typewriter (c. 1969), one set of 1980s disco music cassette tapes, one sword hilt of unknown age recovered from the lake bed of Snowdonia, and 42 era relics in total (see appendix "Lost Era Relics Inventory").

II. Timeline
Occurrence: During the attack, the display room was temporarily used as part of the defensive structure, serving as an emergency shelter and wartime storage facility. In the process, multiple areas of the display room sustained severe damage, and a wall in the "1960s-1970s" exhibition area suffered complete collapse.
Discovery: Following the event, the Logistics Department carried out post-"Storm" cleanup operations in accordance with the "Storm" Clearing Protocol. During a subsequent review, the custodian cross-checked the era relics inventory and discovered that items were missing.
Response: On the same day, the custodian reviewed the arcane surveillance records and confirmed no entries related to lending, requisition, damage, or maintenance. The following day, investigators completed a preliminary value assessment and initiated internal debriefing process.

III. Cause Analysis
Logistics Department: Due to the lack of arcane value in the missing items, cleaning personnel exercised reduced vigilance during the post-"Storm" cleanup process.
Arcanum Containment Department: The "Storm" Clearing Protocol lacks clear criteria for distinguishing between "era relics" and "historic waste."
Security Department: Manus Vindictae may have seized the opportunity to steal items during the attack. Conclusion: Cause currently undetermined.

IV. Corrective Actions
Logistics Department: Establish a safeguard against accidental disposal—for example, by introducing a "72-hour holding period"—and incorporate this incident into the "Storm" Clearing Protocol.
Arcanum Containment Department: Refine the classification standards for the collection and consolidate the management of all non-arcane items in the display room.
Security Department: Upgrade the missing items tracking system and enhance overall security measures.

V. Recommendations
The tracking priority for this batch of historical relics is classified as "Low." Arcane items (including overdue loaned items) remain the primary priority.

Crossing most of that vast building—the long corridors, the broad staircases, the open ground beneath its fallen dome—left me exhausted. You can probably guess how I felt. I checked my notebook of hurried sketches one last time and told myself: "Just a little further—that drink the locals talked about is waiting for you."
Unsurprisingly, the "neighbors" were at the tavern too. The old woman behind the bar mixed me her specialty. Beside me sat a man in an old postal uniform, blank-faced, his shoulders worn pale. A ragged, half-transparent canvas mailbag rested on his lap. It seemed I had a "ghost" for company.
"You're welcome to move seats if he makes you feel uneasy. Old Michał never listens to anyone anyway," the old woman offered gently.
I thanked her but stayed put. It was, after all, a good chance to rest while observing a "ghost." The old postman's shade sat in silence, staring at the grain of the bar counter, as if an after-work vodka should have been waiting there. Not far off, an old woman wrapped in a heavy shawl stood by a table, taking out the same photo—a photo-shaped shade—again and again, turning it over in her hands. I guessed she must have lived alone in some apartment block, in a room that always smelled of coal stove and old cloth.
By the time I finished my drink and looked back, a man in work clothes was standing at the center of the empty tavern—I couldn't say when he'd arrived—as if he'd been waiting there for a hundred years, a thousand years. Half his face was burned, and I caught the faint scent of ash coming off him.
Something about his face must have drawn me in, because I found myself standing, trying to speak with him.
"Sir, if I may ask, what are you doing here?"
"Waiting." His answer came out hoarse.
"Waiting for whom?"
"A woman with eyes as blue as Lake Baikal."
"You're hurt, sir."
"No ... this isn't a wound."
"It's Her ... it's proof that God has forsaken us."
He raised a hand to the burn scarring his cheek.
"We were promised gold. That year, winter went on forever. I waved her goodbye and headed into the frozen wild.
The workers labored on, day and night.
Until the black oil erupted from the wells, flames rising and fading in the falling snow."
His pupils trembled faintly, a silent fire burning somewhere in him.
"Our sky broke open—but no dawn ever came."
I think I knew where he'd come from. Everyone in this country knew where he and his scars came from.

Saturday - Sunny
A rare good day today! The sky's still gray, but I actually saw the sun. I woke up early, since Róża and I had agreed to meet at the flowerbed. I'd packed sliced black bread and pickles into my bag the night before. I couldn't wait, and after breakfast I ran straight there. Róża was already waiting for me, but Emil and Andrzej were late. We waited ten minutes for them, and Róża talked the whole time.
We took the tram to see the new steel foundry. Emil and Andrzej wanted to see the chimney, and I wanted to sketch. It really was a huge chimney, like some beast breathing coal-fire smoke from its great mouth. Róża said that after all these years, Nowa Miedź finally having a factory this size is a good thing. I drew the chimney, the canal, and a few wildflowers. My river sketchbook keeps getting thicker. Andrzej said he thinks I'll become a river expert. But it's not the canal itself I want to draw, though it matters too, of course. Why do we build our houses by the river? Why do we build our factories by the river? Why does the canal bring more people here? Why does the river turn black? Could we live somewhere better? Róża's explained it all to me before, but I want to find the answers myself. Maybe once I've figured it all out, I can help Mom, Dad, and my friends live better lives.
The Story of a Brick

When I was still a student, I spent a year traveling, visiting all the great buildings of the world. I wandered the abandoned amphitheaters of Rome, its crumbling aqueducts and old, neglected churches and temples, sketching in the Mediterranean wind the way Brunelleschi and Donatello did in the 15th century. I was trying to find the essence, the true form of architecture, in those collapsed, unadorned ruins. Until at last I arrived in India. At their Institute of Management, I met an old man with scars on his face. He told me a story about a brick and an arch. The architect asks the brick, "Brick, what do you want to be?" The brick says, "I want to be an arch." The architect says, "I want you to be an arch too, but arches are too expensive. What if we use a concrete lintel instead?" Still, the brick tells you only this: "I want to be an arch." At the end of the story, the old man said, "It's important to respect the material you've chosen. If you're going to use this brick, the best way is to respect it, to let it become what it is, not just to make do with it."
A Hidden Letter

Dear Olga,
My warmest regards to you, old friend!
You might be surprised to get this letter. Marek and I wrote it together because we thought you'd want to know how we're doing. And we wanted to talk to you too—to our dear neighbor, someone who still remembers that we came from Nowa Miedź.
We're doing well in Gdańsk. The sky isn't so gray here. We've rented a house near the port and started a small business. Please, don't worry about us.
It's hard to put into words how we survived those first years. At least three times a week, I'd wake up crying because I'd dreamed of that day, the last time I saw Lucjan. Even now, I still feel sick when I see one of those cattle cars. Like the one that swallowed my little boy. They split families up between different groups, and by the time I finally got off that train alive, I'd lost my son forever.
Forgive me for writing about such painful things. But Lucjan loved you so much. I think about it often—if we could go back to Nowa Miedź, how he'd run straight into your arms, how he'd introduce you to his little sister. Though he never got to meet her. Maybe he's watching her from somewhere up above.
Which reminds me, I should introduce you to the newest member of our family—Maja. She was born two winters ago. I've included a photo of her with this letter. I wanted you to see her for yourself. She has my nose, Marek's eyes, and ears just like Lucjan's, the same shape that was passed down from my grandmother. I think Lucjan would be happy for us. He always wanted a little sister.
We asked around for a long time, and finally a fellow countryman told us your address hadn't changed—still the one I remembered. I can't really describe how that felt to hear. You're a brave woman, Olga, and that's such a rare thing these days. We've all weathered the storm. No one escapes its ravages. I wish you health and good fortune, and that you and your family are well. Marek and I think of you often, and we hope that someday we'll see each other again.
Always thinking of you,
Katarzyna
A Late Funeral

They left a small gap around the doors and windows. This building has plenty of windows. If it could hold voices in, then departing souls should be able to pass through those same gaps and reach heaven, or so the elders said. The young architect nodded and covered the mirror, as her hometown's traditions demanded—so the living wouldn't glimpse their reflection and trap the dead among them.
Someone should have done this for that boy years ago. He was left behind in a train car, among the other exiled, in the very building he'd once lived in. This was a funeral long overdue.
Jasio put on his best suit, the foreign wool one and the only decent clothes he owned. Everyone who'd known the boy dressed in their finest. There was no coffin, but people gathered at the little bar and kept a vigil for the boy all through the night. Candlelight rose soft and warm, lighting up the seat where he used to sit.
"You're singing," said the girl with the hand puppet. "What should I sing?"
They taught her how to sing a dirge. The wake needed no instruments, only song after song.
At dawn, the people set out from the bar with white candles in hand, heading for the dome. The boy had always wanted to see it finished.
"Say something, Stasia. He'd want to hear it from you," the old woman said softly.
The architect stepped forward and cleared her throat. The words caught there like fine sand—an itch she couldn't clear.
"I won't forget you, Lucjan." She began with those words, as sunlight spilled gently through the broken dome, and it made her think of the light that boy had become. "He ... he's with us."

"Living Electricity System"

"If blood turns to electric current, does the soul still stay in the body?"

The blood vessels change first. They stop their soft pulsing and begin to grow straight, silent, climbing upward along the wrists—red, yellow, blue, green, black, and white gelcoat sheathing thin threads of metal, pushing slowly through skin, through flesh.

The bakery clerk is the first to notice something wrong. She stops touching hot water. When the morning steam rises, her arms give off a faint glow, and in the places where blood should flow, something else now coils and branches quietly, like a tangle of wiring rewoven into place.

More and more people fill the hospitals. X-rays line the light boxes. Inside the pale bodies there are no organs, only crisscrossing wires, like the vast, silent power grid beneath a city. The doctors say the humming in the chest, the numbness in the neck, and the teeth that flicker with light now and then—all of it is nothing but insomnia.

Then even the chapel starts fizzing and crackling with prayer. The silver ornament on the host's chest is leaking current, throwing off tiny blue sparks. Someone weeps on their knees. Someone catches the smell of scorched metal in the air. An old woman looks up and quietly asks the question that has long lingered within her heart:

"If blood turns to electric current, does the soul still stay in the body?"

The host doesn't answer. A patch of bronze has surfaced on his palm too.

Excerpt from the Storm Act (Temporary) Before the term "Storm" was formally established, the Foundation used "Temporal Anomaly" as an umbrella term for this new class of phenomena. Anomalous incidents, including time reversal, the disappearance of buildings, the erasure of populations, and historical discontinuities, were filed separately for a long time. It was only after the Nowa Miedź Project that the Foundation confirmed these were manifestations of the same systemic disaster and began drafting the first edition of the "Storm" Regional Intervention Regulations. I. Confirmation of Terminology The "Storm" is provisionally confirmed as a highly dangerous disaster whose core manifestations are time reversal, historical erosion, and the reconstruction of reality. "Temporal Anomaly" is retained solely as a legacy term from earlier records. ... II. Duties of the Foundation The Supplementary Act on the Foundation's Duties specifies the following: The Foundation bears responsibility for the research and early warning of the "Storm," the takeover of endangered zones, personnel evacuation, the preservation of civilization, and the humanitarian restoration of survivors' identities. The primary bearer of responsibility and the details of implementation remain under dispute. The portions that have been finalized are recorded as follows: ... At this stage, "Storm" research prioritizes early-warning mechanisms, with continued work toward advancing and refining the "Storm" emergency response system, and ongoing exploration into the possibility of crossing or ending the "Storm" ... ... A system of disclosure rights concerning "Storm"-related information should be established, with strict controls against leaks of classified information, and close attention paid to staff panic, despair, and other emotional strain ... ...

Conference Room, Laplace
An unused conference room at Laplace serves as the venue for the interns' welcome party.
The setup is simple. Someone has put an automatic coffee machine in the corner, offering everyone as much free black coffee as they like.
The interns flock together, chattering about what lies ahead. Eagle, however, keeps to herself in the corner. She's no stranger to Laplace or its researchers.
Like the one standing at the podium right now.
"Welcome to the Laplace Scientific Computing Center."
"The Staff Committee has asked me to give a speech of at least 30 minutes to paint you all a beautiful vision of Laplace's future."
"But I think your handbooks cover that better than I can." He flips through the notice as he speaks.
"What's next ... Go over the latest [Security Guidelines]? I wasn't aware we even had those."
"Sheesh. We'll be here all week if I read all these out." He tosses the guide aside without a second glance.
"Let's cut straight to the point—introducing you to your future project teams!"
The interns straighten up without thinking, as if sitting a little taller might somehow bring them luck.
As names are called one by one, some interns light up at the mention of high-profile, well-funded projects, while others slink back to their seats with slumped shoulders.
"Next up ... from Washington, D.C., Eagle."
As Eagle gets to her feet, she catches X winking at her.
"You'll be stationed at the 'Storm' Observation Center as an assistant to Marguerite, one of our meteorological observers."
"G-Got it!"
"Unfortunately, she's busy with Foundation reports right now, so a tour might not be possible."
"Either way, your first assignment has already arrived. Once the party's over, start packing for fieldwork. No time to waste."
Eagle feels the other interns' eyes on her, colored with a mix of surprise and sympathy. She sighs, then tentatively attempts a wink back at X.
"Understood. Should I pack something warm?"
"Best cover all bases." He smiles.
Canteen, Laplace
As noon descends, the Laplace canteen is packed with interns gathered in clumps, sharing what little information they know.
Intern I
"Does anyone know anything about Doctor Olaf's project?"
Intern II
"Oh, me! A senior in my lab said that Doctor Olaf's portable rapid-casting research is one of Laplace's top-priority projects."
"It has its risks, though. Some people got turned into Carbuncles. But it's no big deal. Doctor Olaf's changed them all back within 24 hours."
Intern III
"What about Professor Nicholson? Anything from your senior about him? The look on his face when I checked in this morning was ... something."
"You got assigned to Nicholson? Well, let me put it this way." This intern, who seems to know everything about everyone at Laplace, gives his colleague a sympathetic pat on the shoulder.
"Enjoy your meal while you can. Pretty soon, all you'll be tasting is Critter saliva."

"That said, I did hear his Critter biochemical materials project is coming along well. Stressful, sure, but it's a project with real prospects, better than being buried in Foundation paperwork, anyway."
The interns all turn to Eagle, the newest member of the "Storm" Observation Center.
"If you just want to lay low and avoid the 'Storm,' it's a fine place for that. But I'd like to think we all came to Laplace with some scientific goals in mind."
"What's the 'Storm' Observation Center like?" She asks quietly.
"Your tutor's Marguerite, right? I've heard she's lovely. The type who sends New Year's cards to her colleagues. As for everything else, well ..." The intern falls silent.
"Apparently, the Foundation has majorly stuck their fingers in the ['Storm' Observation Center]'s pie. More of a documentation center than a lab these days."
"I heard she's buried in reports right now."

"Of course she is. Nowhere in Laplace has more Foundation bureaucracy than that place. For the checkered gray-and-white, you're only as valuable as your word count. And they love sending people out on pointless fieldwork. So, where are they shipping you off to?"
"Manchester. In England."
"Look, don't tell anyone, but there's a reason the 'Storm' Observation Center has been so on edge. Laplace just got another one of those letters."
"From who? Foundation higher-ups?"
"Bigger than that. My senior told me someone called 'Lorentz Butterfly' has been making trouble for Laplace. She's from that secret society—Institutum Lorentz!"
"I know that name! She wrote Samplings of Global and Regional Chaotic Energy Route Changes. Her ideas on the 'Storm' are entirely different from Laplace's mainstream thinking."
"More toward arcanum, if we're being honest. In fact, I bet the data in that paper came straight from Laplace's own sampling sites."
"Laplace's sampling sites? How would she manage that?"
"Who knows."
"Judging by the name alone, Ms. Lorentz Butterfly must be quite a mysterious, elegant person."
"Ha! Elegant? Every paper she sends is littered with cutting remarks."
"Apparently they're so beautifully brutal that more than one researcher has had to take a trip to the medical office for blood pressure meds after getting one."

"People have just assumed she's a woman—I guess because of the butterfly connection—but the truth is, no one really knows who or what 'Lorentz Butterfly' actually is. It could be an Awakened antenna for all we know."
"What I meant was ..."
As Eagle searches for the words, a figure slips into the crowd, doing their best to go unnoticed—a task made impossible by their brightly colored clothing.
"Hey, we badmouthing the Foundation? 'Cause count me in!"
"You're Ms. Regulus?"
"That's me! Oh wait, you're Eagle, right? I've been looking for you for ages! I'm an intern here too. We should look out for each other, don't you think?"
"I know you. You're that Regulus, the one who's never managed to pass the final assessment."
"Ahem. That's because I love being an intern!" She waves it off. "But never mind that. Eagle, you're heading to Manchester, right? Well, great news. I'm your partner!"
"Well, to be crystal clear, I'm here because Ms. Butte—uh, Ms. Marguerite—asked me to assist you. That's about as far as my plans go."
"It's good to be working with you, Ms. Regulus. But do you really need all those suitcases for such a short field assignment?" She glances at the four luggage bags behind Regulus.
"Hehe, Manchester is just crawling with legendary bands right now. So this Pirate's gonna be on the hunt for some serious plunder. I mean, picking up a bit of merchandise while we're there."

Bkornblume hangs her coat and bag on the hook behind the door, then takes out a newly bought packet of cornflower seeds and places it beside the flowerpot.
On a blank page of her diary, she pastes the note and a dried cornflower.
"And when I looked up, it was no longer there."

Abendmuse Radio

Abendmuse Radio's origins go back to 1964, legendary for supposedly broadcasting continuously for 99 hours. At different times it airs music from around the world, and it has also been home to several live performances.
It's been available in most regions since around the time I was born, and "Abendmuse" was a household name back in the 80s, though it was especially popular among younger crowds.
But most of the time, I listened by "borrowing" my targets' "ears."
One target wanted the radio station's "Music Connoisseur" title so badly that he went to bed at 8 PM every evening, just so he could wake up for the 4 AM "Morning Rock" program to write a review to send in. He helped me keep a healthy routine, that's for certain.
Another target would accept nothing but heavy metal, while his neighbor considered himself a staunch "defender" of electronic music. The two once came to blows over it, each mocking the other's "bizarre" taste.
Some targets were more open-minded, though, and gave everything a fair listen. One of them was a famous pianist, who took part in panels for programs such as "Weekly International Trends." Quite a few of my favorite bands can be traced back to her recommendations.
I think all of them influenced me at least a little. Back then, I sometimes wondered whether quitting my job to become a DJ or late-night radio host might let me experience a different kind of life. And to my surprise, that fantasy has become reality!

Today is the day X was taken in by the orphanage, which he thinks of as his birthday. When X was adopted, his eyes startled the director of the orphanage.|Few people could resist the pleas of the birthday boy—even if it meant becoming a guinea pig for a pull-over water paraglider.|X didn't seem to have any need for servers at his party. Whether it was cleaning, pouring wine, or cutting the cake, his incredible Goldberg machines could handle everything.|X loves opening gifts, but he values the information gleaned far more than the contents themselves. Through a single gift, he can learn his friends' understanding of him, how they've defined their friendship, the thought and care put into the selection ... Of course, opening something unknown is enjoyable, too.|While taking a stroll by the birthday billboard, X excitedly began studying all the bizarre structures and devices in the Wilderness. He finds these magnificent creations of unknown origin can at times spark inspiration.

Last year, the American Sweetheart agency released a special birthday movie at midnight, which fans celebrated worldwide for a whole week.|There was a saying that circulated in 1950s America, stating that once a boy reaches the age where he no longer celebrates the coming end of school, June 1st starts to take on a new meaning: the birthday of his dream Sweetheart.|Many politicians claimed to have received Sweetheart's birthday invitation and gladly went. Oddly enough, they all forgot the details of the night, leading the media to speculate it was some new kind of political publicity stunt.|For her birthday this year, Sweetheart's personal photographer published a book of her personal photos, which also includes anecdotes from her private and public life. According to the photographer, Sweetheart agreed to having the book published, wanting to give her fans a different type of surprise.|A certain department, suspicious of Sweetheart's true identity, sent an agent to infiltrate her birthday party. After the party ended, the agent submitted a report claiming her to be completely innocent and even became a loyal member of her fan club, leaving the investigation with no definitive conclusion.

It was the next day right after the Lord Protector's death, the day when the troupe performer named The Fool put on the funniest mask of the year.|The mysterious troupe wandering around the British Isles announced a show to be performed on that night. The Fool would fool the "king" in the performance by then.|The Fool loudly chanted a paean praising the day in a female voice. It was the day when the anticipated "entertainment" came back to life.|On this day, to play a baron who dresses as his deceased wife in memory of her, the Fool changes his voice, his posture, and even his subtlest mannerisms.|The Fool has found a tape of a Chinese opera piece in the Suitcase's warehouse. Even though he doesn't understand the language, he enjoys the tension presented by the performers.

On the night of August 15, the Rock 'n' Roll Pirate was suspected to be at a birthday party at some bar. Before the police could surround the bar, Regulus had ridden her motorcycle off with a whoop and cheer, leaving them in the dust.| London's pirate radio station "APPLe" announced today that those who celebrate the birthday of a great captain and "just happen to" present a rock record will be awarded a rare opportunity to cruise the high seas!| After blowing out the candles in the darkness, Regulus attempts to perform a prank using optical stealth, but it doesn't work - the LED birthday hat on her head betrays her.|At Regulus's birthday party, each of her friends gave her a record released on that day in history. "Rock music makes August 15 a great day," Regulus says.|Regulus submits an application to Ulrich for an unlimited supply of Dr. Papper because she heard that pirates in history would be given double portions of rum on their birthdays. Although the application is denied, Ulrich buys her a pack of Dr. Papper with his own money.

On this day, many years ago, Centurion was born in Las Vegas, with a Solidus symbolizing good luck in her clenched fist.|Centurion's birthday party will be livestreamed on the TV show Witch for a Day. Stay tuned for the mind-blowing reality show!|On this night, after Centurion won half of the entire casino's chips, the casino manager bribed her with a plate of tres leches cake stuffed with three bottles of hot sauce to temporarily throw away her Solidus, which might have saved the casino for the moment.|"What could be more exciting than getting rich overnight?" Says the laughing Centurion, "Spending that money in an even shorter time!" There is no better reason to waste money than a birthday celebration.|This year, Centurion joins Sotheby in her potion experiment to celebrate her birthday. She adds random ingredients to the cauldron and, unsurprisingly, cooks up a "surprise."

Leilani's classmates threw a birthday party for her, but she walked into the wrong classroom! Luckily, she made friends with everyone there in no time, and thus doubled the guests for the party.|It was Hawaii's off-season. When asked about the birthdays she had before those in Zeno, Leilani could only recall the empty beach and the boundless sea.|After Leilani warmly greeted everyone with "Aloha! Happy Birthday!", almost everyone in the academy knew it was her birthday.|Today happened to be the new Zeno cadets' first day of field training. With Leilani's enthusiastic guidance, the newcomers picked up basic survival skills in no time. However, nearly half the class missed their final assessment because they were too busy chasing wild rabbits with her.|There is never a shortage of friends at Leilani's birthday parties. Comrades who once trained alongside her—now fully-fledged Zeno soldiers—arrived to gift the birthday girl their theory notes and combat insights. Yet, their most important advice was to simply follow her heart and take her time.

Many years ago, the Tennants held a birthday banquet for their beloved daughter on this day. But now, almost no one remembers this déclassé family.|On this day, countless maidens in Paris went dizzy with love. They all just happened to encounter an elegant, charming gentleman who gave them a "unique" invitation to a birthday date.|On her birthday party, Tennant "accidentally" disclosed the source of her diamonds and received deposits from numerous rich Arabian merchants.|Tennant throws a diamond-themed party on her birthday. At the end of the party, she holds an auction to "make sure everyone has fun," which earns her a considerable profit.|"Honorable Officer," "Dear Ambassador" ... Tennant has received a pile of birthday cards, each addressing her with a different title. She throws most of them away and keeps only those that call her by her name.

It's Mesmer Jr.'s birthday, but she believes the celebration of a specific date is insignificant, given her belief in rationality and practicality.|Even though Mesmer Jr. stated that she needed no gifts on her birthday, she still said thanks to the gifters in a low voice, and she would even wait for them to leave before disinfecting the gifts.|Mesmer Jr. tried to hypnotize herself on this night, hoping to get rid of the stubborn, frantic illusions in her dream for a moment. Sadly, she failed again.|Unlike most, Mesmer Jr. holds no nostalgia for her childhood. Yet, she too once sat beside her parents, watching the flickering candlelight on a birthday cake. Now, when her friends approach with bright smiles and a cake in hand, the memory occasionally resurfaces.|On her desk, Mesmer Jr. discovered a gift from Ezra: a potted plant humming with gentle white noise. She briefly entertained the thought of disinfecting it, regifting it to a patient, or simply leaving it to its fate. Ultimately, she opened a search page for "houseplant care tips."

The mirror shattered on that day. Ever since, there has been Door and countless possible siblings.| Door hoped that there wouldn't be any balloons at his birthday party, otherwise he'd have to apologize profusely for the succession of explosions.| Today, you can see many similar and cozy scenes in the reflection of Door—a birthday party in a small living room.|Door reflects colorful ribbons and confetti almost every day in the Suitcase. On this day, however, these decorations seem a bit different from usual: they're prepared for him.|Rainbows, stars, flowers ... Door has captured many beautiful moments in his life. Today, he shares them with the friends who gather to celebrate his birthday.

Ezra is keen on inviting numerous arcanists, carefully noting each of their birthdays—a necessary part of the planning process, perhaps even more important than the birthday itself.|He always enjoyed the ritual: filling a glass bottle with colorful colonies, extracting spores with a water wand, and then tossing it into the air—resulting in a string of his numbers floating in the night sky.|Just for this night, he would whimsically plead with his mother after dinner to tell him about that place—a utopia free from strife and death yet cold as ice.|Within a relatively unknown room inside Laplace sits a collection of spore samples collected all over the world, with some even being taken from dangerous battlefields. This is Ezra's secret base, a place where he can enjoy a moment alone on special days.|At Regulus's "suggestion," Ezra held a birthday party in one of Laplace's guest rooms. The room ended up being so contaminated by a mixture of spores and Dr. Papper that Ezra had to initiate sterilization protocol before leaving.

For those who hang out in the streets, this day might not be worth commemorating. Pandora Wilson: Just as I mentioned, our readers want to know the real you. Feel free to say whatever's on your mind—I mean, relax.

Pandora Wilson: You seem excited at the opportunity for a conversation.

Pandora Wilson: You've listened and experienced so much. I'm sure our readers are curious.
Lady by the Lake: How kind of you to say so. Let me think ... Perhaps "witnessed" or "carried" would be more accurate than "experienced." I keep things hidden for people—things both precious and discarded; so many little unremarkable things. I always make note of their stories. Something to pass the time on those long and quiet days.
Pandora Wilson: And how about your story?
Lady by the Lake: It's hardly worth telling. But ...
Lady by the Lake: Every painting longs to be seen. To have someone to talk to. I've always wondered what different viewers find in me—the complete picture of "me" can only take shape inside the viewer's mind. And if a viewer were willing to share what they see ... that would be wonderful indeed!
Lady by the Lake: I even have a list of topics! We could talk about art, or the different ways profiles can be combined, or spring ...

"Left Arm"

A "left arm" that is extremely sensitive to arcane fluctuations. The strength hidden within almost caused a work-related injury to the interviewer.
After a long and unproductive conversation, the interviewer gave up on the idea of further investigation. The interviewee seems to believe that she was born with this arm, and when asked why no one else was born with an arm like this, she answered, "Everyone has something special about them, don't they?"
Nigh-Indestructible Blouse

This blouse is made of moleskin, a durable material that would not usually be chosen for such a delicate design. However, anyone who has learned the interviewee's ridiculous strength and careless movements would understand the purpose of this choice.
"Waltzing" Walkers

A pair of dance shoes, one tied and the other not, indicating the interviewee's unrestrained personality.
After breaking the ice, the interviewee showed us how to run without tripping over the shoelace: she followed a unique pace precisely, which reminded the interviewer of a waltz.
Understanding the World through Music

Pluck the string, then listen. Strike the anvil and record the relationships between tones.
"Vibration" is easy to produce and observe. Ever since the world first recognized the relationship between pitch and string length, theories of vibration have never stopped evolving.
In the era when these theories flourish, the rising and setting of stars mirror the rise and fall of pitch, and the planets themselves are seen as a kind of note. The ratios of beauty and harmony can be extended to all things.
Vibration is applied to the understanding of invisible things and used to bridge body, spirit, and mind. Perceiving every subtle vibration is the foundation of pure beauty—and of bringing all things into harmony.
Such perception demands purity, and purity brings absolute focus. It also demands rare talent—but talent must be rigorously refined.
A seed is selected and moved from a sealed blue container to a stage ringed by instruments. She is set to work among scores and notes—before she knows the meaning of "beauty," "proportion," or "the universe."
She can follow orders. That is enough.
I'M NOT THINKING

Fragment 1: "How would I know why she came here? I kept my word—I never told anyone where you were." Showing up exactly where she's needed, for reasons no one can explain—the Headless Press. Fragment 2: "I have no idea what made her defy orders. Instinct? She should instinctively follow orders. She always has." Another piece of evidence that instinct can overcome orders. The power of freedom! Something this pathetic crab-head could never understand. Fragment 3: "You actually care? Yes, she was kept under strict confinement and forbidden from speaking to anyone. She still stutters to this day." Sounds like there's a Frederick II in Manus Vindictae. Wait—isolated from the entire world? ... Conclusion: she governs herself—she has nearly broken free from the universe's grip. The ever-present shackles of reason compel me to write this down. But I'm learning to think like someone who has abandoned thinking. Learning from—Coppélia, is that her name? No matter—learning from her wisdom!
Trust for Magazine Editors

Pandora Wilson: Sorry if I startled you, but I think you're more curious than scared.
Pandora Wilson: Have you seen a similar arcane skill before?
Coppélia: You remind me of my friends ...
Pandora Wilson: How?
Coppélia: Your head is not with you. Where did you hide it?
Pandora Wilson: It's still with me. This mouth is just my arcane skill; it's how I do my interviews.
Coppélia: Oh. My friends have no heads at all. But they do have a magazine, just like you.
Pandora Wilson: I've never heard of anyone like them in the industry. Do they focus on niche markets? Or ...
Coppélia: I don't know. I haven't seen them in a long time.
Pandora Wilson: I'm sorry to hear that.  So many of us have lost track of old friends in recent years. Have you considered placing an advert in our magazine?
