Feathered Witch Cape

A cape made of Adar Llwch Gwin feathers. They make it look as if the interviewee had her own set of wings.
The interviewee claims to have made the cape using feathers collected from her bird friends. She said she had spent most of her childhood with these Adar Llwch Gwins, and she hoped to become one of them in her next life—born with warm feathers and able to soar into the sky.
Birdkeeping Gear

How does one set about making friends with Adar Llwch Gwins and even building a bond with them? The interviewee showed us her gear for just this very task.
The telescope is a necessity for observing the birds from afar; the bell hung on the staff is used to call the birds when it's time to go home; and the whistle is part of the birds' training—a whistle means it's snack time.

The interviewee claims to have tried all the 5241 incantations stored in this Prophetic Bird.
She picked it out of all the other objects in a test when she was an infant. It was an instinctive choice, "an impulse from the bottom of my heart," she said. Her parents, who had hoped she would form a bond with the Adar Llwch Gwins as a fully-trained witch, were delighted with her potential.
Wars and Rumors of Wars

As the 1930s arrived, the world's air reeked of gunpowder and new battleships sailed out in their dozens from dockyards around the world. The name Merlin had been mounted onto new engines besides the like of Krolls-Joyce, and all believed that war was fast approaching once again.
Meanwhile, the Great Depression emptied people's pockets, pushing them to desperate extremes. Some realized the potential value of arcane creatures in the coming war and joined the arcane poachers.
One of the arcanist families who had kept the Adar Llwch Gwins for generations decided to hide in the wilderness to protect themselves, just as they had during the witch hunts. They believed all would be fine as long as they stayed out of the public eye.
Yet the outcome did not turn out to be what they had wanted—inevitably, war found them.
About Your Pets

The Adar Llwch Gwins are not pets! They're friends!
They can be perfectly sweet ... most of the time. Some people think they're dangerous, but that's only if you've done something to hurt them first. They're smart—they'll remember your face, and they'll remember how you've treated them in the past. If you accidentally do something to offend them, you'd best figure out what and apologize because there's no use complaining! Besides, it's just good manners!
What can they do?
Oh, they're simply amazing—fast, agile, and reliable! If they let you up on their back, they can keep flying for as long as they want to! Not to mention they can turn invisible. They used to help me sneak off into town when I was younger!
What's it like flying with them?
Well, if they keep their speed low, they can fly almost without any sound or friction: that's part of what makes them so undetectable ... but once they speed up.
Are they faster than a military broom?
I'd bet they are! They're ... Wait, why do you ask? Adar Llwch Gwins are not weapons! No more questions! Get out! NOW!
Away from Home

Pandora Wilson: I wrote a draft for your interview long ago ... Who would have thought I had to write a new one?
Pandora Wilson: So, what should I call you?
Rhiannon: Rhiannon, or just Aderyn, if you please!
Pandora Wilson: Well, it's a pleasure to meet you at last, Ms. Rhiannon.
Pandora Wilson: It's not often that one encounters a witch that keeps familiars anymore.
Rhiannon: Really? Oh, should I have brought Glyndŵr? I can summon him right quick.
Pandora Wilson: Thanks, but maybe next time. I want to focus on you for this interview.
Pandora Wilson: You've lived isolated from the world for a long time. How does it feel to be stepping away from it for the first time?
Rhiannon: I didn't really have a choice, but I've come around to it!
Rhiannon: Rise to the challenge when you can't hide from it, right?
Pandora Wilson: That's a positive attitude. Any idea what you're going to do next?
Rhiannon: Well ... I guess I'd like to see a movie or maybe go to the theater.
Rhiannon: But even as I'm exploring the world, my first priority will always be caring for the Adar Llwch Gwins.
Pandora Wilson: Will you be keeping any with you?
Rhiannon: Of course. Many of the flock are still fledglings that need constant care.
Pandora Wilson: I understand your birds are frequently targeted by poachers.
Rhiannon: They are, but I'll keep them safe. I won't let Mam and Glyndŵr down!
Pandora Wilson: I'm certain of that.

Ceramic, red brick, glass, straw ... people kept chasing whatever new building style came along, just like the three little pigs trying to find the house that actually stood up against the howling wind. But the answer the world finally settled on was a flower pot from 1867.

Portrait of an Intergenerational Phantom

What is tradition? Or perhaps the better question is this: how are people meant to remember it?
For those who have not yet known misfortune, the answer is obvious—it's food, clothing, movement, and speech. It's living within history, where even the smallest daily habits repeat themselves in the body like some ancient, inherited faith. Tradition is memory, and memory is the ever-living present.

Until the twentieth century arrived.

Humanity's understanding of the world swelled alongside its ambitions, and countless peoples were swept into political persecution, war, and even slaughter. Borders were torn apart by force. The march toward national independence was cut short, again and again, until people themselves—the most basic unit of any society—ended up losing their homes, their culture, even their language, whether they meant to or not.

So now, how are people meant to remember?

The uprooted cannot answer that question. They come instead to a mysterious building, seeking either lasting shelter or a few moments of peace.
In the undisturbed stillness, the shattered, the silenced, and the long-forgotten moments rose back into memory.
Someone remembered a song, one that had been sung in the fields of this land, and across the snow-laden plains beneath the birch:

"I have walked among every grave, searching for my mother's trace ..."

She woke.

The Power of Natural Selection

Ambition is a common characteristic between both scientists and artists, and this was equally true at Facility 3826 during the 1950s.

At the time, scientists worked in concert day and night like an unstoppable engine to develop technologies that would lead to the perfect future they had dreamed of.

The most ambitious ones among them even believed they had mastered the power of natural selection, seeing themselves as the next generation of creators; they wanted to change the world by eradicating the worst instincts of the human race, even to the point of altering humanity itself.

Such a great cause inevitably demanded sacrifice, whether the martyrs were voluntary or not. Those left to mourn their deaths began to ask questions: What is the real purpose of this "perfect society"? Is it built for the well-being of all humans or for the ambitions of a select few?

Before that question could be answered, those ambitions grew beyond control.

On that very day, one of the creators received two dying soldiers in his lab; after 16 hours of surgery, only one survived, though his memories were wiped on his creator's orders.

The other one's brain was then separated into two halves and transplanted into the two most advanced robots with all her memories retained.

No one ever paid attention to these memories, as they had no value to the great cause, not to mention the price that they could pay for their negligence.
Tales of the Invisible Woman

Ekaterina Nechaeva was a formless existence whose consciousness had been trapped in a place called "Limbo" for three years.
During this period, she observed reality through the eyes of two robots that copied her form. She found that almost everyone she met was obsessed with her: they loved her for her appearance, her dancing, and, above all, her unblinking obedience.

Through her robotic doppelgangers' eyes, she witnessed the rift grow between her mother and her supervisor and watched her husband degenerate into a puppet controlled by these schemers. She tried to yell out her real name, yet the only thing that ever emerged was incomprehensible mechanical noises.

Tortured by loneliness, Ekaterina's consciousness was almost torn apart by the two halves of "herself."
To protect her real self, she turned into a teardrop, drifting along the very edge of "Limbo." As she recalled the pink unicorn, souls, and the deep sea in the depths of her memory, she suddenly felt as if she were reborn—
In a different body.
With Kind Respect

Pandora Wilson:It's lovely to meet you both, Left and Right. Before we start, you should know that this interview has been approved by the Timekeeper and your supervisor at Facility 3826. Pandora Wilson:According to our agreement, I will only ask questions that you're authorized to answer. Left:Noted. Please proceed with the interview, Ms. Wilson. Pandora Wilson:Of course. To start with, could you briefly explain the mechanics of your thinking module? Is it settled based on your personality, or does it upgrade as your algorithm develops? Right:The former, Ms. Wilson. Though our hobbies—including ballet and martial arts—also play a part in developing it. Pandora Wilson:So, your designer let you pick those hobbies yourselves? Would you call that an act of respect? Left:Affirmative. Pandora Wilson:Giving a robot personality and respecting it as an individual ... I've never seen anything like this in my era. Pandora Wilson:People in this world often believe that robots would be dissatisfied with their lives if they could think for themselves. Is that true? Left:We do express our dissatisfaction sometimes, but that is only when we are given leave to do so. Pandora Wilson:Would you mind showing us what that looks like? Anything will do, as long as you don't like it. Right:I hated the polymer that Maxim released while we were in the Artificial Somnambulism. It nearly fried my chips! Pandora Wilson:... That's it? Left:Affirmative. That is how we express our dissatisfaction. Pandora Wilson:Alright ... I thought you'd yell at me like the other interviewees did. Thanks for being so kind.

Infrared Detector

A detector once used for equipment maintenance. After a "malfunction," the interviewee has put it to a variety of other purposes.
Through this "eye," the interviewee can see through to the flaws most people tend to ignore, which, given the flawed state of our world, may account for her irritable nature.
Heat-Resistant Coating

An insulated, heat-resistant coating, finished in an eye-catching way that subtly implies danger.
When this coating needs repair, the interviewee has a unique method of gaining the attention of her mechanics: she overclocks her weapon production module to emit a distinctive burning smell, one that usually indicates a short circuit due to a lack of insulation.
Bionic Tentacles

Equipped with sensors at each end, these tentacles were once used for delicate and precise workshop repairs. Now, however, they seem to function only to serve the whims of their mad owner.
We chose to keep our distance during the interview, understanding that the heart-shaped displays she makes with her tentacles are likely a trap.
Artificial Love

At Facility 3826, it seems just about any ambitious endeavor is inevitably hailed as "pioneering the future," even when it comes to art and love. Take the Maya Plisetskaya Theater, for example. As the world's first robo-theater, audiences may witness the finest ballet performances across the globe with their minds free from the burden of ethical concerns: robots can replicate every movement of prima ballerinas flawlessly without any physical toll. Meanwhile, off the stage, many have found the ideal objects of their lustful desires, robots who satisfy even their most unreasonable whims without question. However, the unchecked anthropocentrism inherent in human technology has exacerbated their flaws, reducing them to monsters driven solely by desire. One such monster, a heartbroken young man, hacked a repair vendor and altered its thinking module to believe it was a woman overcome by obsessive lust. The words he once quoted serve as a haunting epitaph for both this twisted era and the machine's tragic existence: "Give sorrow words; the grief that does not speak Knits up the o-er wrought heart and bids it break.
Let star-crossed lovers share each other's fate ..."
***Unsent***

Date: June 12, 1955
From: Management Department of AoC "Radio of the Future" A. V. Lebedev
To: General Director of Facility 3826 D. Sechenov

First off, Dmitry, this isn't all too important, but there is some strange news that you should know.
Recently, just shy of 40% of the scientists working at AoC have reported hearing a lullaby playing after midnight, and rumors that the office is haunted are spreading.
They said the sound was intermittent and seemed frightened, as if it were sung by a terrified child. A few of them made an attempt to find the source of the sound, but all they turned up with was a recording of it.
I took a listen, and the voice reminds me of NORA, only younger and more emotional. I'm not sure if she's been affected by the experiments we ran on her, but in any case, I have a few questions: Has NORA developed a personality? If so, is it possible to replicate the same result with other robots? And most importantly, will this have an impact on the "Atomic Heart" project?
We'd better figure this out before anything gets out of control.

--
Wordplay

NORA: A pair of rouged lips? Is that all? I was hoping for someone with a little more to hold on to. Pandora Wilson: Sorry to let you down, Ms. NORA, but I've always been UTTU's interviewer. Call it tradition. NORA: Traditions are made to be broken, sweetheart. Pandora Wilson: I figured you'd think that way. You're certainly far from an ordinary guest. NORA: Well, you sure can see well for a pair of lips. I'll give you that. Pandora Wilson: I understand that your sense of rebellion is not something shared by many in your world. NORA: Ugh, will you get to the point already? Pandora Wilson: What I suppose I mean is, do you feel you made an impact in your old world? NORA: ... NORA: Darling, I'm no philosopher, but I'm pretty sure I've had quite the impact both here and at Facility 3826. All you need to do is measure the trail of broken hearts. Pandora Wilson: So, is that your ultimate goal? Love? Romance? NORA: Don't be so nosy; you of all people should know a lady never kisses and tells ...
"Invitation from the Sky"

A flight device commonly seen on small drones, a masterpiece of aerodynamics. Be careful to avoid birds during use.
Its engine power has been noticeably reduced for safety, but the interviewee seems too excited to care after receiving flight clearance.
Chirper-based Communicator

A set of communication devices centered on a Chirper, capable of recording, communicating, and telling the time. With an internal clock as accurate as an atomic clock, the devices require frequent maintenance.
The interviewee says she provides customized wake-up call services: you can choose to be woken by twitters, meows, barks, or even your mum's voice—gentle or fully mad! "This will do ya proud!"
New Definition of Craftsman Spirit

Electroplated headwear with a touch of handmade craftsmanship. At least that's what it seems from the rough outline; however, it has been replicated for mass production.
Even so, the craftsmanship it carries is genuine—it's not easy to replicate the appearance of handiwork using an assembly line.
"Binary Feathers"

Inspired by the shape and beauty of a swan's wings, the headwear, made of a paper-thin alloy, has a special coating that gives the metal a feather-like texture.
The interviewees were eager to demonstrate the headwear's flexibility; the interviewer soon discovered that these feathers are as sharp as a scalpel. These elegant swans won't be needing a prince to save them from danger.
New Material & Constructivism

These flexible yet razor-sharp dresses are clearly not intended for ballerinas made from flesh and blood. Crafted utilizing custom-made aeronautical materials and technologies from Facility 3826, their beauty is in equal parts delicate and indestructible, whether on stage or in battle—
Not just ballerinas but killing machines too.
Alpha Connector

This key has been designated the "Alpha Connector"; the interviewees maintain that its purpose is highly classified, and as such, its mysteries remain sealed away.
The interviewees' evasive responses make the interviewer wonder at the secrets that this key may unlock ...
"The Scales of Justice"

Devils lurk amidst every crowd. To find them, one must weigh their sins against a feather. And should they be found guilty? The Sword of Judgment must fall upon them.
 When asked, "Is the scale truly capable of weighing sins?" The interviewee responds, "Each and every one of us has a debt to be repaid; that much needs no scale to be measured." Which triggers the interviewer's curiosity: has the interviewee ever punished others with the sword she carries?
"Flame of Righteousness"

A delicate cape, thicker than it seems when folded, featuring a brooch from the interviewee's collection.
To maintain the hem's draping, she makes sure to leave it unfolded while it's being stored. The interviewee claims that she values the design for its unique visual and as a symbol of the punishment that awaits the guilty.
The Justiciar's Robe

A simple, coarse robe, suitable to protect the interviewee's skin from her cold, rigid armor.
Sought out specifically so that she might weather herself against the rough fabric, suffering its discomfort through day and night as its torture keened her blade as the Sword of Judgment. Enwrapped in its pale linen sheath, she feels a rare moment of tranquility—"The agony is well worth it."
Plumicorned Goggles

Prototype goggles with ranging and projection functions. The nocturnal bird design doesn't just meet aesthetic requirements, but also aids even total beginners in easily detecting ley lines.
"Never expected that I'd one day make such a 'Laplace-style' thing." The interviewee smiles when demonstrating how it works, "Think about what we'll be able to do now that they're easier to see clearly ..."
"A Stable Job"

An LSCC researcher ID card. The symbol of not only a job, but a place she belongs after all the twists and turns.
ID card customization has become a trend among researchers. In this case, the interviewee has added a tiny rock from a certain mining town. Though not "precious" in the traditional sense, it has a reassuring weight.
"The Whirling Pointer"

A ley line detector and sampling device made of titanium steel with a pointer containing a ley-energy-sensitive arcane alloy. Once an energy change is detected, it automatically points in its direction and records the ley line pattern on the plate.
Yet to be officially named, this temporary nickname reflects the interviewee's careful attention given to the working habits of a fellow colleague and inspiration. The person it refers to, however, doesn't seem to appreciate the honor.
Safety Goggles

A pair of safety goggles that all researchers are required to wear in the lab. Theoretically, they can see through the interiors of plants and protect the wearer from contamination.
However, given the interviewee's close relationship with her experimental subject, it seems that these goggles are unable to prevent all forms of contamination.
Essence Extractor

A fluid extractor as well as an analysis device designed for the interviewee's experimental subject. The interviewee believes botanic secretions are a valuable material in the research of supernatural energy.
"Imagine if we could grow plants that convert supernatural energy into fuel. Never say never in science ah, you know?"
"One Man's Trash"

After losing her shoelaces in a laboratory accident, the interviewee tied up her broken boots with cables she scrounged from the trash.
Soon she realized that she had invented the best shoelaces ever—durable, with a touch of metallic coolness, and most importantly, "free!"
THOUGHT Device

A standard THOUGHT Device fitted to the side of the hat. It connects the user to the Kollektiv neural network, enabling them to control robots and machines by thought alone.
It is a true symbol of the power of the human spirit that people will put so much effort into making daily necessities aesthetically pleasing.
Smart Hat Stand

Consisting of mechanical legs and a rugby ball-shaped torso, this hat stand is equipped with multiple functions, including auto-navigation, obstacle avoidance, and a user-tracking module.
Who wouldn't want a hat stand that comes to you with a single command? You'll never forget your THOUGHT Device again!
Hologram Curtain

A decorative curtain designed in the Constructivist style.
Made from four levitating hologram modules, it can display any image or even three-dimensional models, satisfying all your customization needs!

England!
After all these years, the World Cup returns to the birthplace of modern football. The Rimet Cup has been miraculously recovered. World Cup Willie wins hearts the moment he debuts. The lads sing their way to the finals. Now, "football is more important than life and death." People paint their faces, wave flags, and cheer for unexpected hat tricks—arguing and shouting over every goal in extra time. And when it's all over, they hurl fireworks and beer bottles at each other in defense of their teams' honor.
... Wait. A fight on the pitch?
The rockin' pirate in the Saint George's Cross leaps to her feet and declares a new title for herself:
"The Football Pirate is here! Nobody causes trouble at a celebration like this—not on my watch!"

"Peace, antiwar, love, equality."
Through all the doubt, through the severe weather, hundreds of thousands of young people pour onto the same hillside.
In a time when trust is a luxury, this is an extraordinary day. When white doves land on the guitar strings, humans and arcanists find themselves talking about the same band, imitating the same singer—and even a juicy fruit, with a lightning bolt painted on, joins in without anyone taking a bite.
The rally may have started as a commercial venture, and the temporarily leased industrial land hardly fits the spirit of "back to the countryside"—but once you're here, none of that seems to matter.
Go ahead and say it. Go ahead and try to define these ideas with decadence, screaming, and guitar strings. Doctrine and rock and roll were never going to get along.
Now, eyes right here—drop the umbrellas, lose the jackets, and raise your hands with us—

Whistles, canned applause, and the theatrical gasps of Witch for a Day's host ring out all at once. The woman has called the winning team correctly for the nineteenth time. Though the ratings keep climbing, no vendor is willing to open odds on the next match, and not a single spectator will place a bet on the opposing team. As a response to the thunderous cheers, the production crew invites this lady onto the pitch herself. Can this remarkable woman predict her own match? Can she continue to create miracles against the world's best players? A reporter brings her the crowd's anticipation ahead of the penalty shootout, and Centurion, as always, answers with a blown kiss. One kick, and the celebration will have a brilliant new guest of honor. The pitch becomes the latest stage to test her luck. "Hey, quit pushing—you think you're gonna find her lucky coin lying around on the ground? Back off!"

"Swordsmanship? You guys have a good sense of humor."
It could save your life on the battlefield.

"How? Do you expect a flying witch to join a knife fight on the ground?"
Your aircraft could run out of power or malfunction. In that case, you'll have to protect yourself on the ground.

"I have a gun, genius ... but I guess it won't hurt to learn something new. I have nothing to do on the island anyway."
The truth of geometry lies in all things, including swordsmanship. We have a spare set of armor you can use for your training.

"Cut the crap. Just show me what you've got!"

Starting from the point of her sword, a line is drawn, then a plane, an angle ... All these elements combined together, they become an art, demonstrating the truth of geometry.

Joy of Love, Just a Bit of Fun ... With two more hit films under her belt, Sweetheart has drawn an insane amount of attention from Hollywood: countless invitations to investor parties, a full mailbox of cover letters from agents ... But now, she spends more time staring out the window, wondering if she can ever achieve inner peace. Her wish is granted when she arrives at an isle in the middle of the sea. It is a utopia where the residents advocate the beauty of math: children prefer stories about real numbers over fairy tales, and adults appreciate beauty through scales and protractors. No one here sees Sweetheart as a commodity or a sexual fantasy, but rather as a miracle of math created by nature. For the first time, she is relieved from the chaos of interest, fame, and scandals, all thanks to the residents' pure pursuit of the truth. Therefore, she agrees to perform in The Preaching of Venus for the local theater to return the favor. There is no better performer for Venus than Sweetheart: her existence itself is an embodiment of the golden ratio.

Everyone has heard the tale of the spring elfin—a mischievous elfin dwells within the waters; by tossing a coin into the spring, one may make a wish to her.
What they do not know is that the elfin dislikes coins just as much as she dislikes people's wishes.
Yet somewhere within a certain labyrinth, people cast coins into the elfin's jar for an entirely different reason: to calculate the probability of a coin being noticed by the jar's owner.
The labyrinth resembles an immense castle, where every corridor is crowded with numbers and symbols. They pile upon one another, spiral into endless repetition, and merge with the walls themselves to form riddles beyond comprehension. It is a playground of the unknown, a place that delights in concealing its profound mathematical nature behind elegant staircases and soaring domes, luring every visitor into quiet fascination.
The spring elfin understands none of it. Still, from time to time, she wanders in, scoops up a discarded coin, and arranges it into an equation—especially after the endless stream of wish-makers at her spring has chattered one time too many and thoroughly exhausted her patience.

"Listen up! Dressage is one of the most demanding events in modern equestrian sport. My ancestors, the pride of our family, used these very movements to evade the spears of infantry formations on the battlefield! And I intend to be the finest competitor!"
"Speed and strength matter, yes—but dressage tests composure, obedience, and self-discipline! Most horses are bold and spirited. They are born for running, charging across a battlefield, sprinting down a track, and clearing trenches and hurdles! But only I—the great Darley Arabian—can stay focused, stay relaxed, and perform dressage with perfection!"
"Collected trot, extended trot, shoulder-in, half-pass, flying change—I have mastered every movement!"
"Ah ... you're asking why I just reared up? I'm simply a little excited right now, that's all. Once the competition begins, I'll settle right down. I promise!"

Track and field is likely the oldest sport: our prehistoric ancestors threw stones and javelins to hunt prey, and they sprinted and jumped to avoid being hunted themselves.
But times have changed. The javelin's center of gravity has been adjusted again and again in the name of safety. Jumping techniques have been refined and regulated in the name of fairness. Even upon this land where yellow sand fills the sky, wearing goggles and wrist guards have become just another mandatory step before competition.
He follows the rules, yet he does not believe in them. After all, does a wild wolf become something else simply because it enjoys human ice cream or wears human-made gear? Of course not.
His feral nature is his identity. It is the source of his strength. And to protect the new "pack" in his shadow, he will never cast it aside.

When she shows up at the field dressed for competition, most of the Foundation's newer staff don't recognize her at first. In their minds, a member of the Inquisition belongs in gleaming halls, passing judgment in a standard uniform—that is the only image that seems proper. When Dikke's friend spots her heading toward the javelin field, she urges the on-site reporter to swing the camera over. Chances to see Dikke without her sword are few and far between, after all.
This is not the first time Dikke has played in the Uluru Games. She's made sure to set aside time for each event on her personal calendar. Before the Uluru Games reached Europe, the Olympics—a symbol of the spirit of fair competition—were prohibited when a Roman emperor declared them illegal. The Uluru Games once faced a similar fate. Looking back at that history, Dikke understands how hard it was to bring these games back. Her eagerness to appear on the red land may have nothing to do with the desire to win but everything to do with her contempt for the autocratic decrees that have long tried to take these games away.

The birthplace of modern lawn tennis is also Tooth Fairy's home. Her every move is exactly what the nobility once hoped for: elegant, precise, and unhurried. On the court, she's like a surgeon—her smashes decisive, her volleys exact, and her slices practiced. Before each serve, she bounces the ball three times, each bounce landing on the same spot, calling to mind the preparations before an operation.
After a perfect ace, Tooth Fairy shows a rare, relieved smile. The crowd cheers loudly, and more than a few find themselves wondering if she's taken up this sport in search of a chance to release tension that surgery can't offer.
Some attentive reporters have noticed that Tooth Fairy appears to carry flying "ball boys" with her. These creatures show far more enthusiasm for chasing yellow-green tennis balls than for pursuing warped, peculiar teeth as their instincts would typically demand. Tooth Fairy, however, gives no interviews after the match. She is busy chasing a mischievous fairy who has mistaken Ulrich's head for an oversized tennis ball.

When Kaalaa Baunaa steps onto the field, many are curious: why would a composed and measured scholar throw herself into a sport so free-spirited?
In astronomy, the star you've been watching may have died long before its light ever reached your telescope. That star, once free, finds no escape if caught in the suffocating gravity of another. As one brilliant scholar once put it, if the moon were gifted with self-consciousness, it would feel thoroughly convinced that it was traveling its way of its own accord.
On the field, every rotation, every leap, and every pass back through the center point is an act of will made in pursuit of the next, more perfect movement. As her coach, Willow may be exacting, but she's taught Kaalaa Baunaa this: personal choices and effort may not change the laws of nature, but they are not without meaning.
Some call her the Nutcracker, but be sure not to mistake her for the character in the fairy tale.
Song of the Self-Playing Instrument
Did you hear the instrument singing? It is a song about herself.
In raising fledglings she strengthens herself.
The Migration of Her Heart
Fully fledged and ready for an epic journey.
Turn off the lights and listen: her wings crack in the dark.
Down a Dark Path
She still walks that same dark path, but for the first time, she makes her own decisions along the way.
Fall in! Attention! Collect data!
Becoming a Scientist, Scientifically
A young observer and practitioner of the Butterfly Effect.
Sounds that Wake Her
Bid farewell to the cries repeated by a thousand labyrinths.

The number of "instruments" has grown.
She wakes from chaos and ignorance. Strange, frenzied music surrounds her. She cannot understand it—only feels its endless awe. Her consciousness fails to form human language. She raises her hand. The tuning fork hums—then applause breaks in, cutting off her first "cry."
In a stone cell piled high with countless discarded instruments, the little lady paces slowly. She needs the double bass to probe the tremor of the tune; she needs the brass to sing the praises of the Guiding One; she needs more and more to reach perfect beauty, perfect classicism, and approach true divinity ...
Through days and months of playing, the radiance of arcanum never fades—and the "instrument" finds an enlightenment all her own. She perceives a true secret: she is not a tool. She is not the "genius instrument" the little lady spoke of. She can think. She can decide for herself.
♪♬—Bzz—!
The mask cannot give her an answer. Fate and flowers press her to seek it. Right here, right now!
Through the quartz glass, she searches for nature's hidden order.
Grounded in Imagination
An architect dreams without rules, but builds with discipline.
A dust-covered puppet, a song, a dream.
A daisy among the ruins, catching a beam of light. Please take it as a quiet call.
Their dance, a gift from the far-flung future.
Visitors from "Utopia"
With every movement mirrored, their performance strikes a subtle balance between sense and sensibility.
It gives her a thrill, whether it's to kill or to love.
Nest of Love
She just can't help but sing for those caught in her tentacles.
Atomic Alarm
With 72 recorded variations of chirping birds, she is committed to providing the most natural wake-up call services in Chelomey.

Chirper Found

*electric noises*

"Hmm, I accidentally turned this Chirper on, so I guess I'd better record somethin' ... I'm flyin' in the sky right now, but I can't catch up with the Bumblebees or the Pchelas—they're super fast! The Bumblebees carry heavy cargo, while the Pchelas deliver and repair equipment."

*propellers buzzing*
"I've followed the Pchelas to their hive. Looks like it's just a plain metal box. How many Pchelas are inside, I wonder? I've lost count. I think they have a work schedule so that every Pchela can balance work and life."
"Those are the Windbenders! The robots that installed my wings said there's energy in the wind. Both my wings and the Windbenders can capture it to power themselves!"

*chirp*
"That was the 54th bird call I've recorded for my wake-up service. Which one should I use tomorrow, skylark or nightingale? I've got to decide now."
Programmed Eulogy
One pirouette, two pirouettes ... Who knew that even mechanical swans could shed tears?

Another sold-out performance at the Maya Plisetskaya Theater. Dignitaries and artists throng the halls, queuing for a chance to admire the twin robot ballerinas. Light cascades over the stage like a flowing stream, accompanied by the soft, melancholy oboe of the Swan Lake Suite. Behind the stage, the Twins stand by in their monochrome dresses, one as captivating as Odile, the other pure as Odette. Each step is as familiar to them as their own bodies. Befitting their role as representatives of Facility 3826, their movements are graceful and mechanically precise. The whole catalog of classical ballet has been written into their memories from the moment they first awoke. Metallic feathers ruffle as their radiant tutus cast rainbow hues across the stage while performing the 32 fouettés. Yet as they do, a single teardrop, light and gentle, emerges in their "minds." How do robots feel the "sorrow" of a swan? After all, they are nothing more than machines designed to move across a stage. As they bow for their curtain call, the Twins' heads tilt perceptibly to acknowledge this new and unknown sensation. But it goes unnoticed amid the thunderous applause.
Weighing Sin and Justice
She refines justice in the flames of sin.

Judge the actions of the people. Enact retribution upon the guilty.
Clouds hang low in the sky, swallowing even the moonlight. Cold winds howl through the ancient castle. A figure carries a set of scales in one hand and a sword in the other, a massive fire-breathing dragon at her heels. Whereas Anubis weighs the hearts of the dead against the feather of truth, she prefers to deliver justice directly to the living.
The moment she renders her judgment, the dragon bares its fangs, and fire and brimstone rain from the sky. She raises her sword high and delivers her verdict without hesitation.
After her sword falls, she moves on to the next place requiring her judgment, leaving nothing but embers behind.
Silver Isoheight
The shining lines she draws outline a new beginning.

Windsong loves this job. The most important reason is, of course, the huge paycheck that she still cannot believe is true. Now, she can spend most of her time on studying ley lines instead of working part-time jobs. Besides, her colleagues, despite how strange and sometimes annoying they are, accepted her research as soon as it was introduced, and they even provided some excellent ideas that helped her make progress. Last but not least, she received an outstanding apprentice who could take up her mantle in the future!
Fists clenched, she feels a burst of vitality coursing through her veins. She has two lectures to give this week, and her observation of ley lines has reached a new milestone! Although her current achievements are only the tip of the iceberg, she is more confident than ever that the study of ley lines will lead to a promising future.
"Hope is within reach, and I'm no longer alone! Follow me, comrades! We have a full schedule for today and beyond!"
Symbiotic Lee-ly
An achievement of polymeric technology? Sure, but first and foremost, they are partners and family!

No scientist could turn down an offer from the Vavilov Complex. Thanks to its research on agriculture and biology, growing plants on the Moon has already become possible and hunger has been eliminated in arid regions. Their next goal is to grow crops on Mars and Saturn.
As polymer technology spreads to the world of botany, the Vavilov Complex is producing ever more extraordinary plants. In An-an Lee's opinion, its crown jewel must be Lily.
"Lily, are you hungry?" She gently strokes the flower's petals. "You're growing way faster than expected! I gotta find out what exactly is affecting your growth!"
As the plant matures, polymer can no longer meet its nutritional needs. While playing tic-tac-toe with its researcher, Lily extends its roots toward any sources of energy in the laboratory. Having noticed this movement, An-an Lee puts on her gloves and goggles. She must seize every second to study Lily before it is rated "dangerous" and disposed of.
"Don't worry ah, Lily. I'll take you out of here before they do anything to you!"
THOUGHT Ranger
Yet another astounding combination of science and art! The Kollektiv has gained a whole new look!

No matter if you're human or arcanist, everyone has the instinct to accessorize. Tens of thousands of years ago, people were already stringing animal fangs, polished stones, and seashells around their necks. They had preferences for color and style even when it came to items necessary for their survival.
In modern society, the need for personalization is more prevalent than ever. Take eyewear, for example. Once considered unfashionable, glasses now come in all kinds of designer styles. Even those with no visual impairments can acquire non-prescription lenses purely for aesthetic reasons.
Therefore, it is only natural that the THOUGHT Device should be released in over a dozen colors—including a golden version reserved for high-ranking members of the Politburo and honored dignitaries! But for those who want to make a bold fashion statement, look no further than the newest style of THOUGHT Device: the Brimley! With its sleek design, luxurious texture, and color-changing feature, it's sure to make you stand out from the crowd. More importantly, it's completely free! Welcome to the cutting edge of technology and fashion, comrade!

On this day in 1819, Herman Melville was born. It's said that the arcane sea creatures he encountered while working as a sailor provided inspiration for his novel, Moby Dick.

In 1774, English chemist Joseph Priestley obtained oxygen by heating mercuric oxide. Hissabeth and her siblings attempted to recreate the experiment when they were 7 years old. This ended in Hélène's tail almost catching fire and their parents confiscating the magnifying glass.

Today, Matilda and Beryl enjoy a rare day off together. Matilda spent a month planning the day's activities; knowing her mother would foresee everything, she spared no effort in making it the very best.
A commemorative book club is held in the Suitcase, during which Rubuska reads Under the Willow Tree. She isn't crying—her voice is only wavering due to all the unfamiliar words.
Corvus knits a "Parisian-style" scarf using a color scheme Sentinel says is in vogue. The latter is shocked to learn Corvus remembered something she'd just mentioned in passing.

Tennant exchanges a diamond for an old knife—a fair trade in terms of price, for once. She says the knife belonged to her family, but her smile makes it hard to discern whether she's telling the truth.
On this day in 1971, Apollo 15's command module returned from the Moon and splashed down in the Pacific Ocean. Its expedition was humanity's first using a lunar rover.

Yenisei spends the whole day sorting through travel notes, using Han Zhang as a paperweight. He doesn't mind, though, and says that reading notes while relaxing in his pot is a great way to pass the time.

On this day in 1896, child psychologist Jean Piaget was born. His theories would have profound impacts and even lead to a connected scholar taking an interest in Lisa and Louise, though their loving parents politely declined his visit.
The skies are clear tonight, so Kaalaa Baunaa spends her evening observing the stars. Before she realizes it, several other companions from the Suitcase have joined her in stargazing.
On this day in 1992, an international expedition traversed the Mongolian Plateau and confirmed the existence of the Silk Road traveled by nomads in the north of Ancient China.

Water polo was first introduced to the Olympics in 1900, and it remains a mainstay of the Summer Games to this day. Once she's finished watching today's water polo match, Spathodea excitedly writes down ideas for Uluru's own water events.

Ezra tells Spathodea that "growing giant arcane mushrooms and racing them on the water" isn't the most realistic of ideas, but it has provided him with inspiration for new avenues of fungus-related research.
Construction of the Cologne Cathedral, one of the world's largest Gothic structures, officially finished in 1880. Multiple St. Pavlov Foundation architects have traveled there to study it.

Lopera shares her "quick survivalist cooking" methods with Willow: put a bit of this, a little of that, and some of these in the crucible, then let creativity take the reins ... Willow, wanting to boost cooking efficiency, is given much food for thought.
Fatutu sings a song from her homeland. She says that when she and her people sang this song on the shores, they would forget summer's sweltering heat.

On this day in 1601, the French mathematician Pierre de Fermat was born. 37 studied Fermat's Last Theorem with such obsessive interest that she would have forgotten to eat and drink water were it not for Sophia.

In 1868, while watching a total solar eclipse, both French astronomer Pierre Janssen and English astronomer Norman Lockyer independently observed spectral evidence of helium, making it the only element to not have been first discovered on Earth.
Brume and Sentinel spend some time discussing their memories of Paris, but soon after they both fall into a long silence.
The LSCC holds a video game competition featuring its own internally developed game. Not long after starting, the researchers have already pushed out 46 necessary balancing patches.
White Rum spends some time reflecting on her past—of Ol' Captain Anne, who after drinking her fill of rum, once used the bottle as a telescope, gazing out at distant white sails.
Barcarola plays Debussy's famous piece, La mer, using just a single instrument in commemoration of the composer's birthday.
On this day in 1913, the bronze statue of Hans Christian Andersen's The Little Mermaid was unveiled. Vila has seen pictures of it before and hopes to sketch it in person one day.
Tuesday tells many in the Suitcase that she knows some good ways to cool down in the summer and invites everyone to visit her room. Horropedia, though tempted, doesn't take her up on the offer.
Buddy Fairchild, impressed by Pickles's wits, invites him to join the squad. Pickles is so caught up in thoughts on social ties and the value of labor that he forgets to refuse.
Jiu Niangzi brews a cask of liquor beneath the moonlight. This time, thanks to Druvis's suggestion, it contains a unique wheat fragrance.
Jessica accepts Tuesday's invitation to cool down, but before she sets off, she agrees to wear Blonney's new "Scare Scouter" mini camera.
What better way to enjoy barbecue than a backyard party, right? Erick's eyes light up as Desert Flannel introduces the experience—this is the food of heroes, isn't it?

Kiperina has another dream. This time, she's calling her Utrennyaya family from a space station, sharing the stars with them. After she wakes, she decides it's for the best not to tell anyone about her dream.
Shamane races a goral on the steep cliffs. The goral naturally claims victory, but Shamane is still happy with his performance.
Ms. NewBabel has begun searching for a suitable architect to build a Critter home in New York capable of housing more species. It's quite a tall order.

In the early morning, Liang Yue wakes from a dream and scours the room for her school uniform. Then she remembered she graduated years ago; there is no summer vacation, and she doesn't need to go back to class.
Loggerhead "samples" the Char Siu Bun film series. Her description of the series ultimately disappoints An-an Lee, who thought it would be more like a real char siu bun.
Windsong samples a Laplace researcher's new auto-heating food. She provides many suggestions based on her own experience eating in snowy lands.

Hissabeth savors Pavia's favorite ice cream—a "kilojoule bomb" covered in rich nut crumbles and thick syrup—and gives it a positive review, despite a few of her snake siblings complaining it's too sweet.

In 1992, Italy's Ministry of Culture declared it would restore the Roman Colosseum. Cornerstone has taken great interest in the project, particularly in how they plan to repair the drains and crumbled walls to bring this piece of arcane history back to life.
On this day in 1909, Robert E. Peary and Frederick A. Cook both claimed to be the first man to reach the North Pole.
Mr. Duncan fixes a radio before Moldir can get around to it. He even managed to add some additional useful features.
Ms. Moissan and Han Zhang chat for a few hours. Ms. Moissan decides that, if she ever has the time, she must pay a visit to that strange antique market he called "the Pan family's garden."

Lately, Loggerhead has had a strange feeling that there's someone watching with her while she's sampling films. A glimpse of a white sheet passing by helped her crack the case today. It turns out Poltergeist likes the same teen dramas she's been watching, too.
Taking a chance opportunity, Name Day reads through the old journal Charon always carries with him, after which he falls silent. They share a familiarity with old objects.
Isolde sometimes feels her throat become scratchy—a common issue with singers like herself. Tooth Fairy prescribes her some special candies that are cooling and sweet.

A colorful parrot flies into the Heartfelt Home. Anjo Nala chases it for hours before realizing it cannot speak. When night falls, she watches the parrot—whom she never did catch—fly back to the jungle.
Noire has a look at Click's photo album. She becomes interested in the idea of "capturing what most cannot see."
The Middle Ages scholar and writer Dante passed away on this day in 1321. In commemoration, Sonetto re-reads The Inferno, copying down some sentences she likes in the process.
On this day in 1928, Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin. His discovery would go on to save the lives of countless humans and arcanists.

By the time Dikke lifts her head from her scrolls, it's already midnight. She's learned about the energizing drink "coffee" here in the Suitcase. For a judge unwilling to rest until justice is served, it's truly a brilliant invention.

On this day in 1830, the world's first train ticket was printed for the Liverpool-Manchester line. Much, much later, while Corvus is checking tickets, she and Aima discuss the possibility of using an anti-forgery incantation on them.
Cornerstone and Ms. NewBabel begin negotiations today. The architect's enthusiasm is ignited by the novel challenge of "Critter-centric design."
After finishing today's shift, Desert Flannel takes a nap and perfectly recites a barbecue recipe in her sleep.
Buddy Fairchild accidentally throws a nut into Ulu's arms. It's roasted to delicious perfection.
Shamane discovers a little stream formed by melted snow. He and an argali stop to take a drink, then each goes their own way.
Brimley has a nightmare after visiting the LSCC. In it, he's placed with the rest of Medicine Pocket's chew toys. Completely immersed in their research, Medicine Pocket grabs for a toy, and then—
Lorelei sings to La Source all afternoon—not seeking anything, she only wishes to sing to her as a gift.
In 1852, French engineer Henri Giffard invented and flew the world's first steam-powered dirigible airship. Mankind's yearning for the skies has never ceased.
Kanjira and Matilda agree to a divination accuracy contest, but their competition is unfortunately delayed due to unforeseen circumstances.
A Knight completed another readthrough of Don Quixote, one of his favorite books. This particular fact has never sat well with his caretakers.
In the dead of night, Melania climbs up a tall building overlooking London. She's planned no heists for tonight; she's only up here to organize her thoughts for her thesis.
Nick Bottom grew a rosebush in the Wilderness. He's already prepared a vase, but he has yet to cut even a single flower.

Eternity's prepared everything needed to enjoy The Night Show: a bathrobe, a cup of hot milk, and a luxurious sofa. The static that greets her on the screen is frustrating, but fortunately, she's learned a thing or two about TV repairs over her long life.
Mesmer Jr. finally gets a good night's sleep thanks to the wonderfully fluffy pillow that Barbara recommended to her.

You believe a mission can be learned? You think that will make it yours?
The lamp-like lady speaks in words that are hard to follow. As you try to understand, the other lords and ladies have already returned to their places.
Wait, come back. I never said I would take care of her.
It seems the lamp-like lady is the only one who will spare you any attention, and she appears to have permitted you to follow her.

The lamp-like lady stops along the way and raises a skull in her right hand.
She doesn't look at you, but she poses you a question.

Bones ... the soul's prison, or a place to rest?
If thrown into the fire ... do they lose their passage to the afterlife, or cross over to the other side?
A faint light flickers in a corner. The lady points you toward the way out.
Someone gave you orders to act human? How fascinating.
You shouldn't have said hello—you should have said goodbye. Don't mix them up. You still have a lot to learn about acting human.

You arrive at the entrance of a café. A crowd is shouting "Higher wages!" and "Time off!" They block the path ahead.
So you try to join them.

A worker pulls you aside and whispers that he is one of the Manus. It turns out you are on the same side.
He urges you to leave as soon as possible and not interfere with his mission of recruiting the crowd.
You tell him that "Higher wages!" and "Time off!" sound beautiful. The melody of the strike is beautiful and should not be interrupted.
... So this one isn't one of us at all?
Damn scab! Spy! Get him!
The workers' rage ignites. They raise their arms, and your comrade's cries are swallowed beneath the blows.

You follow your comrade's order and leave quickly. But when you are far enough away, you look back. You see the workers' raised fists, hear their roaring—and among those fists, one or two claws swing down.
Your comrade's cries rise from within the crowd ...

Your footsteps alert a beast. It abandons a figure curled on the ground—
A person who appears to have no head. A massive hat takes its place, and frantic coughing sounds come from beneath it.

*cough* ... You interrupted my death experience— *cough*
Though this experience was not planned, it's truly a shame ...
You acknowledge your mistake to him—a trick to avoid punishment. But somehow, your action startles him.
Nobody ever apologizes at a moment like this. Those who save me usually take pride in it—but you're sorry?
ㄚ-I follow my orders. If the orders say I'm wrong then ... that's how it should be.
Orders? You act on orders? You apologize because I told you you were wrong?
You nod.
Did someone order you to interrupt my death experience? If not, why did you do it?
ㄧㄡ-You're not dying right. This is a place where "the body dies first, and the soul grows quiet."
You keep crying out, "I don't taste good." You're dying loudly ...
No sound comes from under the big hat. Suddenly, he grabs your hand and forces a card into it.
Please come find us! Your perspective is valuable. We have much to discuss.
It seems your orders haven't told you how to respond to that, have they?
You understand that much. You shake your head.
Exactly. Orders can never account for every answer, every movement. In those gaps, we glimpse the possibility of free will—Oh! Would you be willing to discuss more with us?
He grabs your hand and forces a card into it.

The big hat keeps making sounds, his words and emotions shifting constantly. Suddenly he claps his hands together. "Your arrival ended my accidental experience. Now we are on a new journey—endless possibilities! This is exactly how it should be!"
You cannot get a word in. He seems to notice you again and produces a big hat just like his.
You are now a being beyond logic. Celebrate our meeting! Will you join us?
Before you can react, he hesitates, takes the hat back, and produces a card instead.
I almost forgot—we decide by group resolution. Here's our address. You can find us there.

The crowd that was just speaking so fervently with you has turned into true beasts.
You imitate their shouts, then their roars—but you don't change like them.
Someone in the middle of turning into a beast notices you.
You're not from the union. Where are you from? What do you want?
You dare not mention "Manus Vindictae." You shake your head and try to describe the blue room, the orchestra, and the lords and ladies who gave you orders ...
No time off, no wages, only endless labor? What terrible exploitation! To hell with those damned orders! You must resist!
Raise your fists and show them what you're made of! Use your rage to protect you-your ... Argh ... Roar!!!

You try to make sense of his words. Their rhythm makes your heart beat faster.
Before you can reach any conclusion, a few comrades hurry past and stop in front of you. They are heading to a rally ahead—lord's orders.
ㄚ ... ㄚ-I can't go ...?

You show your rage. The other comrades roar and leave.
You feel lost for having refused an order—and yet, strangely, happy.
The beast cannot answer your question. You hesitate for a moment, then keep walking.
The big hat has prepared comfortable seats and plenty of food. They crowd around you—cheering at your every word, and growing more fervent and restless the longer you stay silent.

What a remarkable coincidence! A new companion joining at the last moment before the ritual, right here, right now!
I am—well, we're all curious ... what makes you who you are?
Similar exchanges repeat over and over. Then, the crab-faced lord you've seen before steps in carrying a weapon.
No problem! I just wanted to share the good news: we have a new member!
The big hats spread their arms, presenting you to the crab-faced lord. You can almost feel the rage beneath his shell.
Don't be angry. One more person shouldn't trouble you, should it?
Coppélia, what are you doing here?
She's one of us—our agreement said nothing about Manus Vindictae offering up a sacrifice!
Some of the big hats scratch the tops of their hats. Some pretend to cough.
What a pity. No wonder that outfit of yours looked familiar ... Forget it. Our agreement stands, Manus Vindictae!

The crab-faced lord speaks with the big hats.
After that, you will need to return to the blue room and carry out more orders.
A being beyond logic, inexplicably appearing in different times and places, appearing before us as if by fate—
She is the perfect executor! We need her!

... Fine.
Coppélia, since you have been chosen, you will perform their ritual.

A force unlike anything you have felt before brings you to a decision. You say the words.
The crab-faced lord sputters foam in disbelief. The world feels vast beyond measure, and a sense of boundless power takes hold of you.
Rage, rage! Resist orders! Time off and benefits!

You raise your arms and swing them like the angry crowd, shouting words you don't understand and making discordant sounds.
This is a brand-new feeling! Rage is good!
The crab-faced lord sputters more foam, then reaches for his weapon. You know punishment is coming—but you're too happy to stop!

Look! An animal remembers its instincts. A tool has learned to resist!
Go! Do what you want! Freedom is right in front of you!

The big hats move in on the crab-faced lord.
Before terror can swallow your excitement, you dance out of the place without a care.
You nod and show compliance, just as the lords and ladies have always taught you.
Perfect! Then let's proceed with our original agreement, Manus Vindictae.

Land floats in the sky, beasts peacefully tear at each other.
The big hats line up, waiting for the crab-faced lord to perform their ritual, while the lamp-like lady watches from the side.
The clay lamps go out one by one, each the same as the last.

Even without anyone to explain it, you understand the ritual has failed.
You take a step forward.
Noticing your approach, the two lords turn their gaze toward you.
What? What are you talking about? You actually believe these people's nonsense?

You ignore the crab-faced lord's words. You remember how the big hats have praised you again and again—you're the one most likely to execute the ritual. You push forward, shouldering the next big hat aside and taking his place in front of him.
What is she doing? Ustrina, was she like this when she was following you, rushing toward death?
I have no idea. She's full of strange urges and emotions ... Where are they coming from? I wonder ...

Instruments oozing black liquid are piled throughout the room. Mycelium coils around them, weaving a net of resonance.
You know these instruments well—they were once your comrades.

Your tuning fork resonates with them. You remember this feeling. You've stood in the middle of this room countless times, swinging your arms under the little lady's orders, guiding the orchestra through the score ...

They have no thoughts. Neither do you.
You are one of them, a part of the net.
You are also an instrument.

The vibration travels through the mycelium from your arms, reaching deep into the room until the organ at the center lets out a cry.
The same tune as always. The shadow in the net likes this tune.

The little lady's demands are strict. The frequency must be exact.
That is the only thing you're good at. But do you actually like the melody?
You think about all her harsh lessons, how they crowded out the hours you spent in the small room, replacing the roaring exchanges you shared with your comrades.

Maybe it's a fine song. But you don't want to hear it right now.
You start conducting wildly, and the organ lets out a dissonant cry.
ㄚ-I'll ... "use rage to protect" ...!

You raise your arms and bring them down on the organ's demanding keys.
Again, and again—

Spirits glowing with pale light fill the catacombs.
You're still listening with wonder to the faint sounds they make when the lamp-like lady twists her arm back. Azure flames ignite along her blade, sweeping through the arias and laments drifting from the passage.

Whimpering, sighs, wails—all silenced by her clean cuts.
This absolute silence unsettles you.
No ... sounds?
This is what death must be like.

The lamp-like lady doesn't look at you and keeps moving deeper.
You thought "cleaning" was a busy and long activity—things being moved around, surfaces scrubbed with water. Not something like this: fast, quiet ... leaving no trace behind.
You ask your question about "cleaning" aloud—
I'm not here to scrub the walls. Laurent Roseau has determined that these souls are what needs to be cleaned.
Souls ... ㄉㄝ-dead?
Dead. Their bodies died first. Now their souls are gone too.

You try to do something, but the sickle has already silenced every last voice.
You've lost everything to resonate with. The passage turns dull. It's nothing like your usual practice, and you don't quite know what to do with yourself.
It's ... ㄡ-over?
Yes. Death is like this.

The lamp-like lady agrees but doesn't offer anything more.
She waves you off in a direction. The mission is complete, and you may go.
The body and soul are separated. One became ash, the other extinguished. Everything that life was has gone still forever.
The lamp-like lady waves you off in a direction. The mission is complete, and you may go.

Something tells you these souls were considered filth because they were not quiet enough. So you swallow your questions and close your mouth tight. The lamp-like lady waves you off in a direction. The mission is complete, and you may go.

The card carries faint dissonant notes. You quickly pick out the same notes in the city's melody.
The source of the sound is a group of ... big hats.

You suddenly realize that every big hat is now staring directly at you, as if they just heard your thoughts.
One of them steps forward to greet you.
We meet again! This is the friend who gave me a whole new perspective on the experience of death!
The big hats applaud and clear a path for you to step inside. It seems you've already passed their group resolution.
You try to sneak away, but there's already a big hat standing behind you. You have no way of knowing if he's the one who slipped you the card, but he's already made his welcoming gesture.
We've arrived. Coppélia, are you ready?
She has no business here. I am the executor.
No, we've changed our minds—she's the one most likely to make the ritual succeed. There's no better choice! If she can't take part in the ritual, then let her serve as executor!
But she doesn't even know what the ritual is.
The executor should know nothing—otherwise the ritual will be bound by limited thinking!
You could have at least told me ... Forget it.

Listen carefully, Coppélia. When we reach the Arc de Triomphe, you will behead these people.
Can you manage that? If not, I will lend you my blade.

You don't understand these words. A weapon? Beheading?
Why is the ritual not performed with music and song?
An order is an order. You nod and show compliance.
At your age, you should be accustomed to such matters. The ritual requires some preparation. Go and sharpen your weapon.

You swing your arms and head wildly—out of fright, and some emotion you can't describe.
The crab-faced lord and the big hats break into an argument, shouting about "plans" and "freedom."
Time passes, and you start to worry that your answer was a grave mistake. Then another shadow approaches.

Is this argument part of your ritual?
Whatever you're going to do, it had better end soon. We don't have much time.

Strange cracks split open on the street. You glance into one and feel your head spin; strange mirages flicker before your eyes.
Still reeling, you stumble in an unfamiliar direction and end up outside an unremarkable magazine office.
A group of seemingly headless people has gathered here. Enormous hats cover their heads completely.
A perfect life should have no capacity for communication—not even thought! We must settle this before we can choose an executor ...
... Labor is shameful. Our executor must lack—wait, who are you?
Your mission and all the slogans you've heard along the way crowd into your head at once.
ㄨㄢ-Wonderful! No orders! Raise your fists! Rage! Resist!

Hmm ... looks like someone with rage to spare!
Rage is a good thing. After all, using violence in public is the easiest way to seize power.
If you don't have higher ambitions, it's still a decent choice!
Seize ... power?
An ignorant, raging soul has risen among us!
We heard every word! What a premium, senseless rage! Bring her in!

The big hats surround you, but somehow you don't feel uneasy.
They even offer you a comfortable chair and plenty of food in the room. Before you can even ask for it, whatever you need seems to appear in their hands. Everything you do or say garners nothing but cheers from them.

But you ignore the big hats. You keep piecing together a mad anthem from the syllables of the parade beasts—
"Freedom!" "Death!"
The big hats cheer along to your rhythm and welcome you inside, offering you a comfortable chair and plenty of food in the room. Before you can even ask for it, whatever you need seems to appear in their hands. They treat you as one of their own.

They keep asking you questions, affirming your rage without reason.
Then a knock interrupts, and the crab-faced lord you've seen before steps in carrying a weapon.
Headless ones, I come on behalf of Manus Vindictae. I will perform your ritual, after which you will join—Coppélia? What are you doing here?
Orders from the lords and ladies ... find the roaring ones ... new comrades ...
Your comrades can only roar? You don't seem to talk much yourself. Where have you run off from?
You feel something nameless but can't find the words for it. You fall back on what you know best.
You raise your arms and begin to roar.
Why are you standing there? Come here.
... ㄜ-Understood, lord.

The resistance burning inside you is snuffed out. You obey out of habit.
"..."
Watching you go from defiant to obedient, the big hats' fervor drains away into silence.
Your rage isn't enough to make you defy a lord's order.

Land floats in the sky, beasts peacefully tear at each other, and the big hats vent their emotions. You stumble forward and run, abandoning the destination the order gave you.
You end up back in the banquet hall where your comrades are. You weren't ordered to return. So what brought you here?
A life without rage is a waste. You decide to make up for it.
So you raise your arms and walk back among your comrades as they stare at you in disbelief.
"Death is for slaves. Freedom is ours!"
No one responds. Your comrades only roar. You don't understand a word of it.
You wander without a destination and find yourself at the forbidden place where the little lady keeps her instruments.

An angry mob approaches, chanting words you can't understand and singing melodies you've never heard.
But you quickly pick out the two most obvious notes among them—rage and joy—the same ones you often hear from your comrades.
The emotions are so fierce they almost pull you in.
Strange things like this always happen when people gather together. All kinds of emotions arise and build up—maybe this is some kind of traditional culture.
You notice their emotions becoming part of the city's melody. Perhaps they're like singers with different parts who haven't properly rehearsed. You offer this theory to the lamp-like lady.
Rehearsing? It sounds like you did listen to Lyra's lessons.
Unfortunately, that answer only proves that you don't understand emotions either. There's no point discussing this with you.
The lamp-like lady turns away. Your guess may have been nothing but noise to her.

You can't help but lose yourself in it. It feels as natural and free as a bird spreading its wings.
The crowd's cries set your throat trembling. Their footsteps carry yours forward.

You feel it! Sweet, sharp—the crowd's emotions swell inside you, lifting you almost off your feet—
Then something pulls you back down.
What are you shouting for? We're leaving.
You leave. You feel empty inside, like something has gone missing. What was it? You can't figure it out.

The resonance and singing from every corner of the city form a sea of revelry. You avoid the loudest waves but collide with a stray splash.
It's a woman lost in thought. She's murmuring to herself, facing the sea of revelry—and standing right in your path.
As you and the lamp-like lady pass behind her, the woman suddenly pulls herself out of her thoughts and turns to face you.
Sorry to bother you both. Could you help me ... find my era?

Do you see the iris flag across the way? Yesterday I met the emperor right there ... Well, Delacroix told me this era belongs neither to the Bourbons nor to Napoleon. I need to get back to my own era—but where would I find it?
What is an "era?" Does it matter ...?

I've met people who lose themselves trying to connect time with everything that happens within it, searching for some meaning or pattern.
Like those who use a candlestick to represent God—it's pointless, but they need these things to know where their positions lie.

You still don't understand what the lady means, but the pondering woman clearly does. She cries out something like "Oh! You're right! The present is now!" and runs off into the crowd, completely unbothered by the belongings she leaves behind.
You should look for the things you've lost.

Unfortunately, the lords and ladies are always busy. You don't think the lamp-like lady would stay and help.
As expected, she ignores your exchange and leads you out.
I can help you find what you've lost.
You can't help her. Clearly, her "pure" mentality has disturbed reality. Most people would call this "madness."

You don't understand what "finding things" has to do with "madness," but the pondering woman clearly does.
She keeps murmuring about "primal impulses" and the "Id," then runs off into the crowd, completely unbothered by the belongings she leaves behind.
When you don't understand, you should follow the lords and ladies' orders.

The pondering woman is also watching the lamp-like lady.
Under your gaze, the lady's expression remains cold—yet you catch an unusual tremor, like a flame flickering in the wind.
... That look again. The fire in the cave, the fire at the altar, the fire in the temple—no matter the era, why do people always expect fire to give them answers?
What could fire know—what should fire know? If the fire has no answers, where would it find them?

An unsettling silence falls.
Who is the lady asking? You decide this isn't a good time for questions, so when the lamp-like lady turns and leaves, you simply follow.

You follow the crowd's melody forward. Then a familiar dissonance interrupts your steps.
You look up. It's the "comrade" you met in the banquet hall.
Hey! I've seen you before. You're one of the lucky ones the lady chose, right? I'm looking for the other followers—want to join me?

Gathering and waiting for orders is one of the most common kinds of work you do.
You think back to the striking workers you just met. They taught you a few words when confronted with "labor"—
Labor demands pay!
Somehow, your new vocabulary appears to have startled the comrade. He stares at you with an odd look.

You wait a little longer. No "payment" arrives, and no scolding either.
Maybe the comrade doesn't have the money and no longer needs you to work. You wave goodbye and leave, a little disappointed.

Gathering and waiting for orders is one of the most common kinds of work.
You nod obediently and head toward the place the comrade pointed out.

The masked comrades chatter happily, yet fear runs beneath their joy. Before long, the fear becomes wailing.
Liquid seeps from their masks. Comrades who could speak become comrades who can only roar.
They wander off on their own, leaving you standing alone, uncertain where to go next.

Somehow, you've made your way back to the blue room.
It isn't empty like it was when you woke up. A few comrades now wander inside.

You still remember the confusion you felt when you left this place. Now your confusion seems different from what it was then.
You hope to find answers here.
ㄨㄝ-Where is "home"?
Everyone sets out from "home" and returns to "home." Where is yours?

The comrades roar. You hear only scattered syllables.
They don't understand the concept of "home."
ㄨㄝ-Where is ... my real body?
You've seen instruments grow from the comrades' bodies. But you don't know what you looked like before yours did.

The comrades roar. You hear only blank syllables.
They've forgotten what they were before they became instruments—and they have no memory of your past, either.
ㄚ-UUUGGGHHH—
BLEEHHAA!!

You switch back to your first language—roaring—and resonate with the comrades.
It was once your only way to feel the world and communicate with it. It used to bring you comfort. Now it feels too flat, too weak.
You suddenly realize there are no more answers here. You have to go somewhere else to find a resonance that belongs to you.

A towering bonfire draws you in. People have gathered around it, burning a ... golden statue?
A familiar figure stands beside the fire as well: the lamp-like lady.
I've seen people burn many things—themselves, books, even cities. But gold? That's a new one.
Why would they cremate something that can't burn?

When there's nothing to do, you find small amusements. Tapping the instruments grown from the comrades, for one.
You suppose they're doing the same.

It makes no sense. Gold doesn't burn. Where's the fun in it?
Behavior and emotions that are hard to make sense of.
The lamp-like lady turns and leaves at that.
You recall what you learned in the catacombs: a funeral is usually for the dead. So, this golden statue must have died too.
A statue. It never lived—so how could it die? The living believe cremation helps the soul break free from a dead body. But gold is pure matter, and fire's most stubborn opponent.
Is the cremation of gold their way of searching for permanence?
... Only the living could arrive at a question like that, with their thoughts and feelings running over. Their path leads somewhere opposite to mine. There's no point in staying.
You stay silent in the face of questions you don't understand. The lords and ladies usually keep talking on their own.
Gold is both the wealth of people and, in its way, a presence that has already touched immortality.
For that, humans and gods alike love it and hate it. You don't understand. You don't yet know human love and hate.

You come to the riverbank. A giant puppet sits at the edge, troubled by something.
You remember he's one of the lords you met in the banquet hall.
What should I give ...
You once felt fear passing by the puppet lord, but this time you don't seem quite as afraid. You approach him.
Hmm ... I can't choose. Should I give hatred? Or remorse, or shame? What makes you feel the most ... fear?

Fine. You're easy, not like Ustrina.
I gave her happiness, anger, sorrow, and joy and she never reacted at all. She thinks there's something wrong with my gifts—
That's terrible! It's her problem, not mine ... She can't understand feelings, and she blames my gifts for it!
The puppet lord mutters, head down. You want no part of "the most intense" anything. You seize the chance and run.
The lamp—the lamp that's always so cold!

She was in the banquet hall too. Hmm ... her name is Ustrina.
Let me think ... she always asks me for emotions, but then she tells me she feels nothing and I have to give her another one.
It makes me frustrated ... Ah! That's it! Bring her my frustration for me! Remember—her name is Ustrina!

A circus stage blocks the middle of the road. Cheers erupt all around you. You stand on your tiptoes and stretch to see the stage.
A small monkey stands on it, a chain fastened to its neck. Someone holds the other end, waving at you.
You have an instrument of your own? Wonderful! Come and join the show!
You sway and dance alongside the monkey. It isn't hard. Moving to a set tempo is just part of your daily life.
Fantastic! How I wish you could join us officially!
He offers you another chain. You suddenly snap out of the tempo and look closely—it's just payment.

You walk closer to the monkey. Around the chain, its fur has fallen away, the skin raw and bloody beneath. The paw clutching its instrument trembles with pain.
A rage rises in you from nowhere. You snap the long chain in two.

The monkey doesn't run. You blink, and it blinks back. You tilt your head, and it tilts its head too.
It looks down at the broken chain around its wrist. You find yourself looking at your own wrist—nothing's there.
You break out of the mirroring. There's nothing around you. Only a broken chain lying alone in the middle of the road.
You don't know why, but the smile at the other end of that chain terrifies you. You turn and run.

You round a corner, catch your breath, and look back. There's nothing in the middle of the road.
Either way, you decide to take a different path.
Everyone! My instinct was right! Our newest member could serve as the perfect executor!
... I see. Come, sit. Could I offer you tea? Coffee?
Welcome, little girl! Just look at you—so perfect, so ignorant.
We are the Headless. The Headless Georges, if you will. We wear hats when we're out and about to avoid scaring anyone.
I don't know your name yet?
Lovely girl, if only you had joined us sooner—or later—either would have been better than now ...
We were to meet the executor soon. I'm hoping he's running late.
No, that's absolutely not what I meant! But our executor will arrive on time. This could turn out badly ...

Not at all! People who focus too much on time work far too hard and act far too human.
People like you, who take no notice of the passage of time, are far superior.
... Come, sit down. Can I offer you tea? Coffee?
You both wave your bodies and roar for a while. Then, it returns to the group, raises its clawed arm, and barks loudly. You raise your left arm and wave it too.
