Lost Items
You see a lot of familiar equipment, as if someone guessed it might come in handy and deliberately left it here.
Abundant Brain Fluid Jar
God has bestowed lightning and abundance upon me.
Echoes of Desire
Reverence is a craving—a hunger that pounds out a pious echo through every heartbeat.
Suckling Tree Sap
Such incomparable sweetness! It enlightens me, consumes me—I shall tear flesh and blood for it!
Evacuation Signal
The thought of leaving swirls in your head. If you quit now, you might still get out in one piece.
There's dried blood on the item. You're wise enough not to ask the stall owner where it came from.
Strange Statue
It stands perfectly still, yet its gaze follows you everywhere. You get the feeling it wants something from you.
Temporary Camp
The order that still holds here puts you slightly at ease. At least tonight, you won't have to fall asleep to the sound of rushing wind.
Verdant Life
Lush grass and leaves block the path ahead. The life thriving here feels out of place—a glaring hint luring you forward.
Yet there's no gold for sale here.
Thorny Hidden Path
Thorns crowd both sides of the path. You might want to stop and think about how to get through them.
Mad Believer
Some poor soul lost in the legend of El Dorado—but then again, who's to say you're any different?
Eerie Mask
Put it on. Claim your promised reward.
Newborn Tree
A human-shaped tree holds up a sphere of water. Inside, a new growth lies like a sleeping child, in a stillness that verges on foreboding.
Withered Stone Tree
Even stone can flourish after death.
Abandoned Stone Sculpture
She gazes down at us, and thus we kneel at Her feet.
Dark Red Wooden Bowl
Fill it with water, and with an offering of flesh and blood you shall behold the God of Death.
Gold in the Corner of the Wall
This is what they all came for.
Teetering Attic
The wind blowing through the trees strikes it like a hammer.
Dust lies thick across the attic beams, but one corner has clearly been searched through more than once.
A weathered stone sculpture stands deep in the forest, its cracks lodged with fragments that don't belong to it.
The dilapidated temple sits half-swallowed by vines and shadows. Still, something at the top of the stone steps seems to be keeping watch over the offerings.
Everything inside has long since rotted away. A few corners are cleaner than they should be. Clearly, they've been left alone on purpose.
Damp clutter fills the corners of the house. Near the base of the wall, though, the mess looks as if someone has just sifted through it.
The stilt house stands raised off the ground. Its wooden planks creak softly in the wind, as if replaying the memories of footsteps past.
Swift Retreat
Everyone knows you shouldn't weigh yourself down when you're trying to make a run for it.
Grass Remains
A child of wood and water, and the secret to the rainforest's ability to heal itself.
Mutated Teakettler
The sound of a boiling kettle doesn't belong in the rainforest.
Poacher
One way or another, someone has noticed what you and your backpack are worth.
"Adventurer"
You're far from the only ones interested in the artefacts.
Zealous Scholar
Curiosity and the drive to explore have led him down a road of no return.
Blockade
An unnamed road should belong to whomever walks it. Though these people seem to disagree on that.
She should have died with the past.
Wet Moss-Covered Rock
Climbing is your only option.
Biting Flower
The species and habits of this creature have not yet been confirmed. Do not touch with bare hands!
Knotted Deadwood
The wind whistles through the gaps between the gnarled dead roots, carrying with it the faint sound of something on the verge of snapping.
Prison of Wood
It's hard to tell which came first—the tree or the house.
Broken Platform
A few vines hang down from the platform. This appears to be your only way through.
Slippery Stairs
An unknown slime and a few desperate claw marks on the stone surface are reason enough to watch your step.
Luminous Grass
What exactly are those faint glimmers hiding deep in the grass?
Tree Hollow Trade
Everyone here knows the rules of such a transaction.
Equivalent Exchange
It will only accept something of equal value.
Hungry Beasts Ahead
Provoking a pack of ravenous beasts is never a good idea.
Sleeping Pollen
Fine pollen drifts through the air, and with it comes a tide of drowsiness.
Greedy Critters
Before you realize it, you're already surrounded by these little gluttons.
Glimmer Through the Trees
A gentle light follows you through the gaps in the trees until you finally stop and turn to look at it.
Gift of Two Leaves
Two leaves hang before you, awaiting your choice.
Fallen Ruins
Beneath the rubble, things long-hidden see the light of day once more.
Someone Else's Camp
The camp is in disarray. You're clearly not the first to have passed through here.
Ongoing Fight
The cries of beasts echo through the woods. By the time you part the grass and see the two packs facing off, it's already too late.
Lingering Rage
A single defeat isn't enough to drive them off. The beasts are still prowling nearby.
Beasts' Lair
Animals always stash their spoils somewhere they think is safe.
Lurking Shadow
A light breeze passes through. Amid the damp scent of grass and leaves, you catch something dangerous.
Wet Drag Marks
Across the muddy ground, drag marks of varying depths overlap one another.
Wooden Guillotine
The sharp crack of branches snapping together in the distance makes you think of a guillotine.
Giant leaves open and close ahead, cutting down whatever comes without mercy.
Unclaimed Belt
A hunter's belt hangs from a tree. Why? The claw marks around it explain everything.
The Hunt
Before you even hear the subtle movement beside you, every hair on your body has already stood on end.
Extinguished Campfire
The scattered campfire on the ground is still warm. Whoever stamped it out can't have gone far.
A split rock lies across the path through the trees. From deep within the crack comes the faintest trace of breathing. Or is it just your imagination?
Road Blocker
A wall of thorns blocks the path ahead, the dark liquid on the spikes still catching the light.
Tripwire
The coiled roots are muddy and slick. Finding a solid footing is harder than it looks.
White Stone Circle
Several pale stones form a circle. The clearing at the center is suspiciously clean.
Hanging Vines
Vines hang down from unseen branches somewhere far above, their tips just grazing the top of your head.
Gravel Shallows
The shallows are strewn with gravel. A few pieces roll against the current.
Piercer
Several spikes jut from the shrubs like instruments of torture, glinting with a metallic sheen.
Hollow Fungi
Something underfoot makes a sound like thin bones cracking. You lift your shoe and make out the remains of some kind of fungus.
Lone Stone
A stone juts abruptly from the base of the slope, its flanks lined with vertical scratches, a few fresh leaf fragments crushed beneath it.
Humid Mist
A wet mist hugs the forest floor, yet from somewhere in the distance comes the crack and pop of dry wood.
Injured Companion
You study the figure for a moment before realizing that the person lying there, faint and bleeding, is one of your companions.
Gemstone in the Rock
Gems are wedged neatly into cracks in the stone. Which piece do you pry loose without bringing the whole thing down?
Inverted Mushrooms
Fungi are packed in on all sides, each of their inverted caps rimmed with clear droplets that never quite fall.
Fatigue and Torpor
The leaves and branches grow denser around you. You can't tell whether the dimness comes from light failing to reach the ground or from your own eyelids growing heavy.
Thick Fog
The shapes in the fog are like tree shadows cast on a white wall, shifting in ways that don't quite feel real.
Ancient Symbols
Several symbols mark the stone, a glance cast from somewhere deep in the past.
Geometric Obsidian
A triangular piece of obsidian sits wedged in the crack, its edges honed to a deliberate sharpness.
Flowing Obsidian
It rests in a hollow in the ground. Is it the light that's moving, or the obsidian itself?
Emerald Necklace
You notice what looks like unripe fruit on the vines. Stepping closer, you find it's actually an emerald necklace.
Ruby Heart
After studying it for a long while, you become certain that it's very slowly beating.
On the Verge of Death
The flame gives two exhausted flickers. You almost thought it was about to go out.
Gaze of the Crystal
Its facets couldn't possibly catch enough light to reflect anything into your eyes. So what exactly are those two points staring back at you?
Distant Notes
An unfamiliar melody drifts up from beneath the stone slab. The upper register of the ornamental flute is particularly striking.
Black Pearl Necklace
A pearl necklace hangs from a branch, its dark surface like a reflection of the deep sea.
Torch
A torch bound together with agave leaves. An unseen hand holds it, watching you.
A Key
The faint outline of a finely crafted key is barely visible in the muddy water.
Swaying in the Branches
A pendant sways from a branch. Something further away is moving in time with it.
Unyielding Will
The mechanism it once drove has long since crumbled to dust, but the clockwork still refuses to stop.
Trap
As your eyes fall on the box, its demand for supplies forces its way into your mind.
Lonely Golden Leaf
A golden leaf rests on the stone platform.
Bullet marks ring a slot in the surface. Something ought to be fitted in there.
Squirming vines cover the stele, a torn scrap of paper hidden beneath them.
Ancient Echo
You've taken what wasn't yours to take. Something is drawing closer from the dark.
The Weight of Offering
The statues between the trees have long since broken, but they're still watching you.
Within the Mirror, Without the Dream
What does the mirror show? Maybe you should step closer.
Sad Whisper
A slew of whispered messages and feedback reach your ears. It's hard to tell which voice to listen to.
Reply at the Door
The second reply arrives before the noise does.
In the Valley
A bright light sweeps past. You shut your eyes, but shapes still drift across the dark.
Rootless Person
A figure staggers ahead of you. Maybe you can get a little closer.
A Deal with a Demon
So you want to make that kind of bargain, do you?
Dark Stars
A lonely cabin, worn and cluttered. It looks like it's a safehouse left behind from a former expedition.
Newborn Egg
The pulse of something alive drifts up from the grass.
Merciful Nourishment
Sweet sap feeds everything around it. You included, apparently.
Eternal Embrace
The roots twist and tangle around you, as if drawing you into an embrace.
A Century's Invitation
That star is a radiant light falling from the sky.
Thorny Path
Sharp dark teeth cling to every thorned branch. Passing through unscathed may be too much to ask.
Silent Guard
A massive tree stands before you, every branch saying "no."
A man-made trap, waiting for a careless soul.
Water Spheres
Water spheres hang in the air. You reach out to touch one. It screams.
Wary Critter
Fur on end, it stares into the darkness nearby as if expecting a hand to reach out for it at any moment.
Prowling Fish
Somewhere in the dark, you think you see a fish circling you—shadowing your every move as if it were death itself.
Eyes Locked
That cold eye holds your gaze. You each have your own thoughts. Your own schemes.
Resonance Stone Pillar
A strange stone pillar stands by the road. Its carved grooves seem to be awaiting a familiar golden leaf.
Strange Noise from the Grass
Footsteps are closing in. Stay low. They could pounce at any moment.
Shrubs
The leaf edges are as sharp as blades. They'll cut through skin with ease.
The Wounded
You're not sure the person in front of you can be saved. But at least he's still breathing.
Empty Stomach
Hunger claws at your gut like a little devil, dragging your eyes to every spot that might hold something to eat.
Broken Case
It could be endless wealth. Or it could be knowledge or death. Whatever it is, the old case isn't telling.
Relapse
The infection takes hold again, the burning spreading through your body fast.
Old Campsite
Someone made camp here once and never came back.
Masked Sincerity
The hooded man reaches out a hand, waiting to strike a deal.
An Opening
Oh, someone's gotten carried away.
Tempting Treasure
Getting this may cost more than just an injury.
Hiring?
A stranger holds back a cough, trying to prove he can pay.
Survival Crisis
Hunger is tearing the group apart. Some food might fix that.

You read the ancient symbols on the rock, working through them one by one.
—Read, former, person ... this one, the explorer. You hear the rustle of reading on the wind.
The symbols glow faintly as your eyes pass over them, as if they're reading you back.
A faint candle flame flickers toward you in the still air.
It can no longer light anything around it.
A small amount of medicine could restore its strength.
The crystal skull is buried in the mud, faint light flickering in its hollow eyes.
Clear the dirt away and you'll see what it really looks like.
Until then, you'll have to endure its unblinking gaze.
The crystal hangs from a broken branch, each sway a summons.
Each summons draws a wave of restless noise.
If you want the crystal, you'd best be prepared to deal with those noises.
A stone spring turns on its own among the wreckage.
Click, clack—you hear the soft sounds of mechanisms knocking together.
Beneath that, a steady, low hum.
Old bullet marks ring the spot like a small altar waiting for its next sacrifice.
You study it for a moment. The edges of the grooves are smooth and clean, as if worn by countless insertions.
An offering ought to yield something in return. Time to prepare your "offering."
The reply comes back too fast for you to react.
As if someone were already waiting behind the door, listening for the knock.
As soon as you finish reading the words, the noise follows.
Eyes blink open in the darkness, blocking every way out.

Before you is a structure that could only belong here. Writhing vines cover the stele, their tiny suckers gnawing at the crumbling rock. There's a torn scrap of paper hidden beneath it. You ponder if you should pick it up. Do you stay in blissful ignorance, or gain a knowledge that scrambles the mind?
You pick it up and stare, the way an ancient priest might stare at a blood-soaked altar. Red liquid drips from somewhere above.
Flee like an arthropod predator under a giant wheel. The weight of fate is far beyond what you can bear.

Long ago, the reptiles that hungered for wisdom felt boundless joy when knowledge finally lit up their minds—a hunger which burned like a torch in the dark, bright and full of hope. Now, it makes you forget every pain, and the dangers that follow taste pure and sweet.

Your companion stares as you chew on the weathered scrap as if you were drinking golden honey, or tearing into a bloody rib. You claw and tear at your face, but there's no need to worry: your body is nothing more than metal now. All your companion hears is the shriek of something sharp dragging across a metal plate.

You taste the ancient wisdom. Your vision warps. The vines are even more threatening than before. You have taken something not meant for a creature like you, and now something is coming to collect it.

With each heartbeat-like tremor from deep underground, more eyes open in the darkness. 22 pairs of fleshy eyes, watching you in silence. The writhing ants close in without a sound, sealing off every exit.
This is what comes of knowledge. Run, while you still can!
A black statue stands among the deep green trees. Its gaze is fixed on the altar nearby, like a guard worshiping the sun. As you draw closer, you get the feeling that it is also watching you.

This is an altar to an unknown god. The god's image is carved into the stone platform—eight thousand eyes whose light brings life to the earth; eight thousand hands that shield the earth by blocking that same light.
Your steps feel heavy, and the air around you seems to thicken. Your companion sets down the portable equipment and begins to study the carvings on the statue.
The gaze grows sharper—and it's coming from more than one statue now. Before you realize it, you've been surrounded. You count: 16. It's not your imagination. They're closing in.

The thickness, the heaviness ... the statues drawing closer ... You understand now. The thickness is your brain starving for air. The heaviness is blood loss. You were never guests here. You are offerings.
You manage to bring down the statues, but there's no escape. Stay calm. This is a moment that calls for a clear head.
Would a god look down at those who bring offerings? Would you try to tell one ant from another? Perhaps you don't have to be the offering. Perhaps you could be the one giving the offering.

Broken stones litter the altar. You toss the bandages you just used onto it, and black smoke curls up around them. The god seems satisfied. You feel your whole body become attuned—and sense the darkness hungering for your power.
A broken mirror stands before you—a medium commonly used by arcanists to glimpse into other dimensions. But this mirror is far older than the invention of glass. Strange.
You wipe the surface clean, then try to peer inside.
The sea rises above the sky, then seeps down along your eyelids. Fire hides between words, melting into scalding lava that pours down your throat.
Clearly, you've seen something you weren't meant to see. But you're too curious to stop. You look again, enduring the pain.

You hear a sharp melody sung in a thousand languages. Everything you see gives off a piercing smell. The crack of breaking bones mingles with the low groan of tearing vocal cords—you have chosen to accept the gift of a higher dimension. You lose consciousness.
You wake up slowly. Your companions look wrong to you. They're adding moss and dirt to the pot, and the soup they pour out has bones in it. But you're so hungry.

Your drone presses gently against the food, as if you could devour it through the machine—a gift of surging life. The god of this place has blessed this land with abundance since ancient times. You feel moss creeping across your mechanical shell and vines pushing in through the seams. Everything feels newborn. You feel wonderful.

You refuse the strange gift. Your sanity tells you something is deeply wrong. You overturn everything—and your companions turn around, revealing vines pushing out through their eye sockets, working into the joints of their limbs. Their bodies no longer belong to their souls. You should set them free.

You fight with everything you have. Rest is the last dignity this land can offer them. But then you notice there are only broken trees on the ground, and your companions are watching you with concern. By their account, you were speaking nonsense, tears streaming down your face, and hacked wildly at the trees.
Perhaps you've actually lost your mind? Either way, you need to leave.
You stay quietly in camp—not slacking off, but working on something else. He needs the plan delivered today.

An hour passes and you're still revising. Your thoughts drift toward the ruins. You wonder what your companions are going through in there—strange vines, maybe, or gruesome flesh, or puzzles that can never be solved.

No. The unsolvable puzzle is right in front of you. Every plan you submit gets a vague reply, and you're forced to revise again based on a few hints—this is the kind of thing that normally happens inside ruins ... those creepy whispers. Like the following line:
"I feel like this could be bolder. Could you make the poster a bit more flamboyant? Not too flamboyant, mind you—there should still be some restraint. I'm sure you know what I mean."
There you have it. The whispers never leave your ears.

It's been hours since your last submission. Your sent message has gone the way of your companions—nowhere to be found. Maybe consumed by the chaos of fear? Or have you knocked on the wrong door again?
The communicator crackles. Your companions seem to have made it through and are heading back. Feedback comes in over the radio signal. Who's more frazzled—them or you?

The answer is that whispers are always whispers. You hear your companions murmuring through the communicator, as if their minds have just been torn apart by fear. You read the pointed words on the feedback screen. Now it's your turn—like those unblinking gazes. No one gets out.

The radio crackles again, and this time there's an argument on the other end. The whispers haven't reached a consensus on the plan you submitted. Maybe you should pick one voice to listen to, but you can't tell who outranks whom.

Your companions are listening to the echoes of ancient terror. You're waiting to find out whether you'll have to put in overtime suffering inside the ruins. Which is the real horror? "Go with the first version. Merge the first and third and give me a new draft."
Light blazes across the sky. You shut your eyes tight and see its true form through your eyelids.
All souls find peace, returning to the earth. A lingering horn sounds from the mountains.
She moves nimbly through the trees, fangs buried in fruit, drinking down the red juice. The hissing is everywhere. You feel a rush of excitement.
You look at the figure before you. His body is covered in branches and white flowers. Vines grow beneath his skin. Flowers bloom between his eyes.
He whimpers, searching for soil to take root in. Isn't there mud everywhere here?
Or is the soil he's looking for actually another body?
A stone demon sculpture blocks your path, its great mouth looking ready to consume you entirely.
How do you bribe a greedy demon?
You offer gold, dropping it into the demon's mouth. The coin seems to hit something scorching and melts instantly into liquid. It seeps out from the corner of the sculpture's mouth.
You may pass. But next time, bring different people.
You offer the fat rat from your bag. You watch it writhe until it doesn't. Red liquid seeps out from the corner of the sculpture's mouth.
The house is empty. No surprise there. But there are human-shaped black marks on the floor. Something happened here.
You search the cabin carefully. Faint, broken signals reach you from somewhere ahead. *bzzzzz—*
You point your equipment at the black marks on the floor, and in an instant, every sound vanishes. You see a line of words as if it were carved directly into your eyes.
You don't recognize the language, yet you understand what it means. It's an ancient melody carrying the gaze of the starry sky.
You find the artefacts—buried deep in the soil, hidden under grass and brush, visible only when you push the branches aside.
The moment you touch the artefacts, a rumbling rain begins to close in. The ground trembles. A sound loud enough to drive through your skull crashes down on you.
You collapse under the weight. You curl around the artefacts, pulling them close.
They cry out beside your ear, trembling without end. They hatch from their shells—newborns crushed under the fear of being alive.
Maybe children born too soon are meant to suffer.
Gnarled roots push up out of the soil. You slice open the bark and draw out some sap—colorless, flavorless, just enough to get you through.
You press on. The ground beneath you grows softer. It trembles underfoot, rising and falling as if breathing. It's the roots.
Where the roots converge, you sense something breathing in a slow, steady rhythm. An eye opens, unhurried. Definitely not a plant's organ.
It extends its "roots" toward you.
On second thought, the root reaching toward you doesn't feel threatening at all. Maybe it just thinks you need feeding.
This is the third time you've seen this tree. It looks like a slightly folded human figure—the trunk is their legs and torso, the branches their arms and hair.
You know it by its strange shape. Its silhouette makes you think of someone, and a trembling overtakes you. An answer is within reach—the first echo in this noisy world.
You find a curved, raised scar on its belly.
You fold yourself into her arms, finding a moment of stillness in your mother's embrace, and listen to the soft murmur of her delirious words.
You arrive at a perfectly still lake where light and color have stopped. You part the light like a curtain and step carefully onto the mirrored surface.
Moving toward the center, the flowing colors of the stars and moon pour down from between the clouds, painting the frozen fish and waterweeds below—as well as the hem of your clothes.
You meant to cross quickly. But condensed color is spilling from your eyes.
The stars and moon reflect on the lake's surface, their light and color flowing out of you like water. You must refuse their invitation before you merge completely with the lake.
The lake is as still as when you arrived.
You reach your hand toward the crack in the rock and feel air moving across your fingertips.
A cold, damp wind, coming from somewhere unexplored.
As if sensing your approach, the great rock hums along with the current.
You recognize the thorns' scheme.
It's waiting for a stray insect to wander in. Each snap means another meal.
The roots run deep here, tangled and tough.
What lies beneath slippery mud isn't always a swamp.
The center of the stone circle is spotless. You find no sign that anyone has cleaned it.
Something used to sit here—keeping dust out, holding back the moss.
A light breeze sways the vines.
A breeze? You look more closely.
Deep in the vines, something stirs. Whatever it is, it isn't the wind.
In the shallows, a few stones roll against the current, leaving behind trails of bubbles.
You trace where they're coming from and find a crack between the rock strata.
The thorns' spikes tremble when touched. Maybe fear. Maybe the best they can do to hurt you.
Only a hollow shell makes a sound that brittle.
Your footsteps play a melody for the mushrooms.
The lone stone sits at the base of the slope. The scratches spread all the way around to its back.
You notice a few blades of grass between the rock and the soil. That didn't happen naturally.
Not with mud this wet and grass this fresh.
The damp mist of the forest fills your nose and mouth as you step onto a soft, muddy path. Dead leaves cling to the soles of your shoes.
From somewhere deep in the mist comes the sharp crack of breaking branches.

The statue reaches out to a future without darkness.
It's you, Vertin the Small Hat!
Good morning! Good afternoon! Good evening! I've learned so many ways to say hello.
Energy? You mean sound louder and brighter?
Yeah, my hands and my stomach are feeling pretty energetic right now!
Yes! A few girls, an apple, and some friends with wings—they all played with me. Everyone makes such wonderful music.
I've learned so many new songs. Want to hear them? I'll play one for you!
Hmm ... Hmm ... It's a little hard to perform an ensemble all by yourself ...
Mr. Knight gave me a bottle of oil and told me to rub it on my arm regularly.
But I can never get it right ... It always drips onto my clothes.
That's right! He said the metal won't rust if I use this.
If I'd had this sooner, many of my instrument friends wouldn't have had to be replaced.
Mr. Knight said that even if my arm breaks down, someone in the Suitcase can fix it for me. I like it here.
Is that okay? I don't want to keep you from your grown-up things.
Mr. Knight gave me a soft cloth, but I can't get it into the gaps between my joints.
If you can help me, that'd be wonderful!
Wow, Vertin, the Suitcase is incredible! I've only ever read about expanded space this complex in The Ninety-Nine Lost Arcane Skills!
Everyone's room is completely different and suits them perfectly. It's like ... like the Suitcase grew them itself!
By the way, what's your room like? Can I stop by sometime?
Oh, okay, fair enough. I wouldn't want Mam going through the box under my bed either.
But if you ever feel like coming to my room to play with the fledglings, you're always welcome!
Really? That's amazing!
I've never been to a temple before. There's a ruined castle in the forest near my home, but all that's left are a few broken walls.
What's it like, living in a temple? Please, just let me have a look around. I promise I won't touch anything!
There you are! Ever since the little ones figured out they might run into you here, they haven't stopped chirping about coming out.
If they don't see you, they'll sulk the whole way home ... Hey! Leave her hat alone!
One of these days, they're going to peck a hole in it.
That's just how they are. When they want something, there's no stopping them.
I'll do my best to teach them not to dive at people's heads—or at least get you a new hat ...
It's not really about the hat, though. What they're drawn to is someone's specific scent and warmth.
Just like puppies—to them, a brand new sock is just a sock.
It only becomes the best toy once it carries someone's scent.
Ah, Timekeeper. What a pleasant surprise, running into you on a day like this. It seems we've both found a little time for ourselves.
It feels ... novel.
Wonderful. It turns out that without any preset preferences, the world has far more left to try than I ever expected.
For now, I find myself equally drawn to everything new. Eventually, I'll find what truly appeals to me.
I've adapted surprisingly well. Having the Suitcase's residents to observe has made my new life more interesting and fulfilling.
Everyone has different habits and interests. Even I have encountered new and fascinating things.
From the delicate art of corpse suturing to how to brew a specimen preservation potion ... I've picked up quite a lot.
Lately, I've been asking everyone in the Suitcase how they spend their holidays. I've received all kinds of answers.
Playing music, knitting, writing, watching and even shooting films, tending to animals ... All sorts of things.
Many invited me to join them—but I'd also like to hear your answer. What do you usually do with your free time?
They say workaholics find they have no energy left for anything complicated once they finally rest.
Maybe I should clear my mind as opposed to keeping busy ...
Thank you. Your answer has given me much to think about.
Oh, sleep. With quality sleep, I'd say you're halfway to leading a good life.
Once, everything I had went into fighting through mental torment. Now, I can finally address the most basic of needs.
Perhaps finding a comfortable pillow is where a good holiday begins.
Hello, Ms. Vertin! You don't mind if I run a detection inside the Suitcase, do you?
Ms. Marguerite didn't assign me any tasks, but whenever I learn something new, I can't help but put it into practice.
I really thought I wouldn't be able to keep up with everyone at Laplace, but once I got into it, it wasn't as frightening as I thought it'd be.
It's just like what you do as a Scout—focus, think, act. Stick with it and you'll break through eventually.
Or maybe interest really is the best teacher?
Yes! My arcane skills are more practiced now, and with the All-in-One Particle Detector, I have more ways to analyze things.
For example, many of the landscapes inside the Suitcase look completely different from one another—but they're essentially made up of the same type of energy particle, just in different arrangements.
Analyzing those particles would require more complex equipment. It's a shame I haven't gotten that far in my studies yet.
Oh! Ms. Vertin.
Sorry, I was just remembering how I used to love practicing tent setup right here in the Suitcase.
These days I'm so busy with studying and research that I haven't had any time for that. I might've gotten rusty.
Haha, thanks! I'm afraid my camping gear's at home. All I've got is this heavy detector.
But sitting here and talking with you feels just like it used to. That's enough for me.
Tents and campfires are nice, but when it comes to camping, the most precious memories are the ones made with friends.
To be honest, I am a little tired—but more than anything, I feel fulfilled.
Ms. Marguerite says we should never waste our talents. It's just like how you and I have both found our places.
Even if we're busy, we've managed to do more and help more people. That's what matters.
The owl ... the baker's daughter ...
Oh, it's you, Vertin.
Ms. Charlie invited us to join the troupe's performance. She says puppet shows are pretty fun. I'm trying to make sense of ... all these long lines.
I learned this part fast! I can sing it for you.
White his shroud as the mountain snow, larded with sweet flowers; Which bewept to the grave did go, with true-love showers.
What a sorrowful song.
To hell with you, you darkest of demons! Down into the bottomless pit!
Honza drops a few lines here and there, but Ms. Charlie says his performance is wonderful.
That's called—brilliant improvisation!
This toffee looks just like an eraser ...
But they taste nothing alike.
Do you have any more of that toffee, Vertin?
I like sunny days ... the light feels so warm.
Come sit in the sun with me, Vertin.
Yes, nice and soft ...
If you're worried about getting your clothes dirty, we can sit on my veil together.
You always seem so busy. You should slow down and catch some sun for a while.
That's right, this is the best spot for sunbathing ...
(a gentle hum)
This is a lullaby Ms. Lorelei taught me.
Are you falling asleep, Vertin?
Vertin, you seem interested in these blocks.
Want to give it a try?
Ah, the dome of the building in Nowa Miedź ...
I don't think I'll ever forget that golden light, cascading like a waterfall.
The riverbank whispered to me ...
I learned this song too.
Precise, orderly—and I'd guess you worked out the load-bearing capacity of every block, or this part would've collapsed easily.
No wonder this place looks so eclectic.
If you ever need a house designed, I'll sketch something up for you, no cost.
As you can see, Vertin, I'm sketching out some designs.
I've taken on quite a few commissions.
What do you think an architect loves most while they work?
Of course. Wild ideas almost always seem to need cash to back them up.
Other than that, a hot cup of coffee helps too.
There's no sweeter phrase than "no revisions needed."
But it rarely works out that way—I'm trying to combine Plan A and Plan B into a Plan D. Plan C? Rejected completely.
(take a big sip of coffee)
Let's just say it's a necessity.
Want a cup? Like, right now.
There's an admiral around here who brews a really good cup of coffee. I love that rich, smooth bitterness.
Our analysis suggests heightened security protocols may not be necessary here. Our current precautions may come across as unfriendly to the other residents.
Would you like us to switch to another mode, Comrade Timekeeper?
Understood. We will switch to our exploration and learning protocol from now on.
We estimate that this will reduce negative impressions significantly within the next two weeks.
Understood. Observation priority adjusted.
Should there be any aggressive behavior, we will request authorization before interfering.
We will adopt low-intensity measures to protect your safety while avoiding unnecessary damage. Please rest assured, Comrade Timekeeper.
There are many scientists and soldiers living here as well, but I have to say they are startlingly different from those at Facility 3826.
So much more energetic and passionate! I positively adore them!
I was worried that I might get bored after moving here, but I've actually been overwhelmed with requests!
Well ... we've played some games together, and we've tried out a lot of toys ... the Electro, the Snowball, the Dominator, the Fat Boy ... Oh! And they've all tried the SHOK module.
Would you like to try, darling?
Heh heh, what am I saying? You're too young for those kinds of things.
Heh heh heh ... You still have a lot to learn.
Sleep isn't the most important thing to maintain your beauty. A lady must stay active!
The Wilderness has a diversity of weather systems, hydrological characteristics, terrain, plants, animals, and even cultures, all of them co-existing in harmony.
It all seems worth analyzing, Comrade Timekeeper. Would it be alright if we collected some data here?
That is precisely the reason for our interest. We would like to investigate the technological and cultural differences between our worlds.
The science behind this could be used for the Venus terraforming experiment in the Vavilov Complex.
Even though we are unable to assess the data's suitability for now, we will continue with our analysis. Thank you for sharing, Comrade Timekeeper.
Affirmative. We have tagged ourselves as a known "variable" in the database.
In addition, we must appreciate the speed at which we have been integrated as residents here.

The credit goes to Madam Lucy. She gave us some suggestions on how to acclimatize ourselves with the other residents. We have even submitted a request for similar facial masks to further integrate ourselves with the other residents.
You know, darling, I was concerned about you when we first met. You seemed almost emotionless—dull even.
But now, I've developed a different opinion.
My dear, I've realized that you are like Polymer ...
You attract people to you, across so very many identities and backgrounds, because you make their lives better.
Including me, of course!
See, this is what made me change my mind.
Since I moved in, I've wanted for nothing. You and your friends have kept me well fed and happy.
I feel as though I should give you something in return for being such a peach.
Good to see you with so much energy.
Learned anything new lately?
Maintenance oil?
Let me help you apply it.
Everyone needs their privacy.
My room is a grand temple.
That's fine. As long as they enjoy it.
I should give them a few hats just like this one to nest in.
How's everything going?
How are you finding it, living with so many people?
Sleep in.
It looks like you've settled in well at Laplace.
Anything new you've noticed compared to when you were in the Suitcase before?
Let me help you put up the tent, for old time's sake.
Do you find it tiring?
Why don't you start with the parts you can already sing?
How's Honza coming along with his lines?
Take a break and enjoy a toffee.
This grass looks nice and soft.
You seem to have been here a while.
(try building a dome)
(try building a house)

The Soft Rain of Yesterday

Fainter than a whispered tale,
quieter than a dying cry, It reshapes the world in silence. Swifter than fleeing footsteps,
keener than a tempered blade, It sunders every bond without a trace. Scatter your memories
into the valley's mist— On the morrow,
a clear chirp shall tap on your pane.
Until I Am Me

Weave a cocoon from drifting aliases and bleeding memories. Forsake the flesh, shed the burden, Erase the path you used to walk, Let the passing stares of others
shroud your face, layer upon layer. Whatever is destined to claim the sky,
must first tear free From the scarred rupture of a broken husk.
The Silent Anthem

How can an infant prattle amidst the choir? A delirious anthem has no room
for such whimpers. Her throat sits hollow, an echo chamber For a thousand darkened horns,
shrieking strings, and pounding drums. Swallow the soul! Bite back the tears!
From the stifled sobs, she realizes— She can sing only when her neck is unchained.

What day was it that she outgrew her old uniform?
"Live by the Oath," the little girl told herself. "March onward, stand tall."
Eyes front, her heavy rucksack left behind, she looks back but just once.
A Dream Beyond Light

Softly, I drift to sleep ...
A gentle, dim light warms my face.
It spills down into my dream, bringing sweet old memories.
My dearest friends, the daisies are awake in the fields.
The yesterdays are gone, but I will hold their echoes close ...
And I will walk with you into unknown tomorrows.
Where Light and Shadows Rest

Sketch it, measure it, erase it all and start again.
My past for the rubble, our future for the frame.
Light and shadow. Hard and soft. Fleeting and enduring.
Separating them all, stroke by stroke—to find that shelter not yet found.
For the life here is heavy, yes ... but beautifully real.
And when the last brick finally settles, I will be standing right there beside you.
Farewell to the Old Night

Over the course of this year we stayed quiet,
None save for the cornflower chose to speak:
Do not avert your eyes, and do not fear the world fading away;
What winter has taken, spring shall return.

Heat is emitted from her metal body. Keep burning, keep burning. No one would have thought The world is made of countless
insignificant atoms. Look where the dancer's finger points— That is the true North of our civilization.

The future courses through her wires.
Keep running, keep running.
No one would have thought
Wisdom could be built on countless grains of insignificant sand.
Look where the dancer's toe points—
That is the foundation of our knowledge.

Even now, there's still Żubrówka.
People who lost their homes drift from one place to the next. They carry little in the way of belongings, but the taste of home? That taste's always with them. You can lose a country, but you cannot lose that. And as long as tomorrow keeps coming, someone will be cooking old-fashioned stew and pierogi, served piping hot on a checkered tablecloth. Someone will raise a glass of Żubrówka, and the warmth of it will soften a strange new age into something familiar.
I stopped at a small place called The Old Oak while gathering material for this piece. The bartender, a lovely old woman, mixed me her house cocktail. It smelled good. It smelled like days gone. You won't find the place in any guidebook, but if you come to Nowa Miedź, give it half a day. Sit under the dim neon sign. It isn't home, but somebody there is trying to make it into one, and that counts for something.
Made of Concrete

If you've read this column before, you'll remember the concrete giants. Their faces are cold, hard geometry. Their skeletons hang out in the open, and they don't care who sees. They declare their harsh, unadorned presence to any and all who look upon them. An era's ideals, aesthetics, and memories are branded into them. They call these giants Brutalist, yet "brutal" as they are, they were built for people.
From the forties on, more and more architects became enamored by a single ideal: show the material as it truly is, build cheap, and build modern. They found beauty in reinforced concrete, in its weight and roughness. Their apartment blocks went up fast and put roofs over many heads. Their public facilities, plain-faced yet built in strange shapes, spoke the language of the avant-garde. And just like that, a generation of Brutalist giants rose from the earth.
A building embodies the lives of the people—at least, that's what one architect stepping onto the gray, dusty streets of Nowa Miedź believes.
Story from the Communal Block

"When I was a kid, that gray apartment block was practically the center of the world. Everything seemed to grow out of it and spread from there. Beneath its low ceilings, we woke up, read the newspaper, ate bread, and went to school. Outside the window stood more buildings just like ours.

"That year, we realized the world was changing before our very eyes. There was a state-run shop on the first floor of our building. Some evenings, Mamuska would send me down to buy bread. She'd hand me a few banknotes, but the numbers printed on them changed every week—always getting larger. Then one day, several new stalls appeared beside the shop. Someone was selling secondhand clothes from the West."After school, my friends and I played in the apartment block's shadow. Sometimes we went to watch the trains or visited the arcade, but mostly we played hopscotch and pushed each other on the swings. Whenever the swing carried me into the air, I could see the sunlight more clearly than I ever could through our little window. I'd think, maybe when I'm older, we'll live in a home that gets more sunlight."

"What else can we do?" they say.
Said "neighbors" pass through the dim, winding corridors, stand atop the lengthy staircases, and occupy seats in the pub. In this dark, quiet building that's almost become one with the early spring fog, the "Shades" are like concrete—part of the building itself. The lively residents and the gloomy shades each occupy their own end of the building, and though they don't always get along, life continues nonetheless.
"Or rather, they can't get rid of us, and we can't get rid of them ... It is what it is," laments a resident.

Without sufficient intelligence, the visitors decide to avoid direct contact with the robot.

They flee at full speed, yet the robot keeps coming nearer as it runs on four limbs like an animal.

Join the Kollektiv!

A THOUGHT Device salesman accosts the visitors near the Chelomey Square.

Salesman: Hey, comrades! You're not equipped with the THOUGHT Device yet, are you? Get one now! You'll be able to memorize an entire encyclopedia in no time! Here's a sample! It's completely free!

An-an Lee takes the sample and puts it against her temple, murmuring "Please get me more clients ah, good device."

Salesman: Hmm ... I can't access your biological data. Something must have gone wrong with the sample. Sorry.

Seems like some extra protection has been applied to the visitors this time, in case any of them implant unidentified objects in their brains like X did.
Facility Pioneers Press

The visitors notice a newsstand. It looks rather antiquated compared to the futuristic technology around it. Tereshkova: Would you like a copy of the Facility Pioneers, comrades? It reports on the most advanced achievements in every field! Biology, engineering, weaponry ... The visitors buy a copy for research purposes.

The engineering column introduces a series of robots that are in service in the Kollektiv network.

It emphasizes the MUC-1 Drofa, a drone widely used for transportation and agricultural production. It can fly at 30 mph while carrying cargo.

The column also mentions that old robots will be updated with multi-layered artificial skin for their expression modules. Perhaps, in the near future, robots will look almost the same as humans.

The weaponry column introduces a variety of weapons.

Besides conventional ones, it highlights the latest high-tech inventions, such as the Electro.

And it introduces a man named Kalashnikov, who is trying to increase the power of electromagnetic weapons by 3-5 times based on Gauss's research.

Some starlight projections catch Flutterpage's interest. Following the lights, she leads the visitors to a planetarium.

A worker at the entrance is talking loudly about the universe and mankind—an inevitable topic for every developed civilization.

Lucy is very interested in the topic and joins him in the conversation.

An intriguing question. The worker hesitates for a moment.

Identity & Access Management

All employees are required to wear their identification badges at all times while within the building's work areas.
Staff are advised to display their badges prominently, whether around the neck, on branches, above display screens, or on any other visible part of the body or attire.
Do NOT use the identification badges of current or former employees for any of the following reasons: divination, chewing, writing, unauthorized applications for funding or experimental equipment without the owner's knowledge and consent, malicious occupation of laboratory space, or any similar activities.
Information Privacy & Cultural Values

Confidential archives, employee privacy data, and any other sensitive information encountered in the course of work must not be used for purposes unrelated to official duties.
Employees are expected to respect the cultures and behavioral customs of individuals of different races, genders, and regions. The harassment or intimidation of colleagues through means including, but not limited to, inquiring into internal structures, imitating special vibration frequencies, excessively organizing social gatherings, unauthorized adjustment of charging-station voltage, or viewing certain content in animal documentaries is strictly prohibited.
Laboratory Safety

When experimental procedures involve flammable or explosive materials, specialized equipment, or other high-risk operations, at least two full-time employees must be present at all times. As a general rule, employees without independent mobility are not permitted to participate.
In the event of an accident, personnel must, while ensuring their own safety, immediately contact the laboratory supervisor, the security department, and the rehabilitation center.
Resignation & Dismissal

Employees may submit a resignation to the LSCC for legitimate reasons, provided that a written notice is given at least 30 working days in advance.
Departing employees are required to sign a confidentiality agreement and organize and archive all materials under their responsibility prior to departure. Any personally developed shorthand notation systems must be accompanied by a reference key. Recording critical information in a manner comprehensible only to oneself is strictly prohibited.
Arcane Creature Housing & Training

To satisfy the needs of the biotechnology division and facilitate related experimental work, the headquarters maintains an arcane creature housing and training chamber.
Within this facility, any actions performed by living organisms—including fellow employees—should be regarded as part of normal experimental procedure by default. Personnel who are not directly responsible for the facility should not report unusual organisms, behaviors, or phenomena observed within the chamber.
Use of Equipment

Before operating any instrument or equipment, employees must read the operating instructions and ensure that they fully understand the device's functions and procedures. Unauthorized use of unfamiliar equipment under excuses such as "I thought it was a coffee machine" or "The structure looked simple enough" is strictly prohibited.
If an instrument displays error messages, emits unusual odors, undergoes violent vibrations, or claims to be an Awakened during operation, its use must be stopped immediately and the issue must be reported. Unauthorized repair or disassembly is strictly forbidden.
Overtime & Duty Shifts

The LSCC operates under a flexible working system and does not enforce uniform attendance hours.
Employees are required to maintain an average daily workload of no less than eight hours, while continuous working periods must not exceed ten hours. Personnel who work continuously for more than ten hours will be required to take mandatory rest periods.
Employees are expected to comply with scheduling arrangements and may be assigned to either daytime or nighttime duty shifts according to operational needs. Applications to volunteer for duty shifts more than three consecutive times will not be approved, as such behavior is deemed inconsistent with Laplace's standards for humanitarian management.
Work Ethic

Employees are expected to conscientiously comply with the Center's rules and regulations and maintain a professional attitude toward their work. Employees should show respect towards superiors and colleagues, and composure towards their duties.
Any concerns or objections regarding institutional policies, work-related matters, or other employees should be submitted through official feedback channels, namely the anonymous suggestion boxes installed on each floor or the Employee Management Committee.

The relationship between the materials and their space in the design is essential.
Pay attention to the faint differences in texture on these Echo Stones. Remember, they'll only lock into place in the right slot.
Oh ... so we just need to put them in place?
Yes, but we have to be careful. It's not as simple as dropping them in at random. We need to understand the nature of each stone's structure.
Hmm, a harmonious melody. Looks like you're picking this up fast.
Strange ... I put it in place, but nothing's happening.
Maybe that's just how they work—they remain silent and conceal their true form until they've been settled into the right slot.
Huh? ... I can't get it back out.
That's beyond anything I anticipated. Maybe it's developed some feelings about its new home or maybe it's something else we don't understand yet ... Don't worry, let's keep trying.
Finding order is a delicate process. Every Echo Stone seems to have a "longing" of its own—a yearning to discover its place within the greater structure.
So, we need to listen close for every little sound these stones make when they touch—maybe a faint scrape, or some tiny vibration between them.
Only after we've picked up on those sounds and fully understand their needs can we find their inner rhythm.
I see—it's like the interplay between musical notes. What we need to do is sense their "melody."
Exactly. The relationship between each pair of stones is like notes arranged within a piece of music. Only when the rhythm and pitch meet in perfect harmony does the correct melody rise.
We'll have to keep testing, keep adjusting, until we hear their true voices.
Oh, it worked!
A perfect symphony ... When every Echo Stone has found its place, the structure naturally harmonizes their sound.
Every part must serve the whole, and the whole is only complete because of every part within it. I think that's the charm of architecture—it's all about details and precision.

Destiny may take much from us, but in doing so leaves us its gifts.

Death draws near.
A gift of myrrh—that red-brown incense, so fragrant, yet bitter and sharp, like a layered aria.
A gift of fragrant boughs, to build the precious nest of death.
A gift of dawn's light, so that the song of rebirth may be sung.
In the bronze censer, the flames burn hotter. It blazes, radiant as a heart being reforged. Nothing in the world could shine brighter. The poets, gods, and sages gathered around it cry out. Even they cannot bear a flame of life so pure.
At last, the fire dies. No one dares draw near. She spreads her snow-white wings from the half-spent ashes and flies toward the city where the sun was born.
That is the source of all fire, the first light in every eye, and hope rekindled in the long darkness. Even if this rebirth is priceless, even if the light destroys what draws too near, the goal is there. The future is there. She decides to press on once more, flying into the unknown without hesitation.
The shattered pieces will eventually return homeward.

Dusk and nightfall devour each other. The returning tide rises over my ankles again.
My new shoes cannot bear the salt, so I've set them aside, or exiled them to the edge of the beach. My bare feet feel out their memory of the sea.
Shattered shells grind sharp against my soles. Are they gifts from the tide? Then why does the tide crush them so wantonly?
Those roaring dreams quietly lose their warmth, their color, and the shapes I once traced with my fingers ...
If tears could breach the wall of memory like a capsizing wave—if those collapsed dwellings have already scattered across islands and the ocean floor like shells in the evening tide ...
If I am the one who witnesses, the one who remembers, the one who barely escaped—
How fortunate that I can still light a "Sea Mother's Eye," to watch and wait in this storm that swallows everything, and go on once more.
The differential equations describing the flow of milk over complex curved surfaces will be the topic of her next research project.

Sweet and sour, soft and cool—she leaps out of a dream, escaping the little jar that held her, and drifts through this frozen, sweet sea.
"Cream makes it smooth. Sugar controls the freezing point. The right ratio stabilizes the structure of the fluid."
"Thorough mixing lets sweetness be reborn in a lighter form. That allows us to shape the perfect structure within the frozen ice cream."
"With cream, nuts, cones, and a hand-cranked ice cream maker, we've completed a brilliant proof—this is the perfect fluid!"
Today is a remarkable day. It is the only international holiday in the world named after a food. On this blessed day, even the ice cream proof runs smoothly—and from the heart, a sincere wish that every child may have a glass of milk.
The north wind sweeps across a desolate land; on it flies a grim angel with scythe in hand.

In the vision, divine radiance envelops the angel-like figure.
No one knows what he is or what to call him, for few who pass through the valley of death ever return. We know him only from the dying's last murmurs—the highest image, a saint of downcast gaze, a presence no mortal may give form. Throughout his passage, his merciful grace brings eternal rest to the dead.
Wherever he walks, all who linger at the veil of death are overcome by transcendent rapture. Wherever his gaze falls, blood-red lilies take root among shrouds and poke above pierced ribs. Wherever his voice reaches, sleep-luring song drifts down from the sky.
Every soul of goodness, at his revelation, glimpses a corner of paradise before death claims them—bearing witness to the land flowing with milk and honey. And so, in trance-like ecstasy, they step into sweet death with the grace of dancers and embrace its eternal silence.
Fire Lotus
Her robe shakes, sparks scatter and lotus blooms erupt from the embers.

In the marketplace, a foreign girl arrives with a merchant caravan. Brown-haired, green-eyed, and nimble, she is a performer of the hundred arts with a special talent for illusion. Wherever she performs, crowds gather and cheers roll through.
One day, lanterns and drums fill the stage—then the girl appears, smiling. She spreads open a blank scroll roughly ten feet long. She stacks stools one atop another and climbs to the top, then dashes ink freely across the scroll, painting lotuses. Before the ink can dry, she flicks her hand, opens her mouth, and breathes flowers of flame onto the canvas. Within moments, vivid petals curl out from the fire, some hanging heavy as lotus pods. The crowd takes it for a trick. One spectator, bold enough to reach out, has his hand burned by the lotus and can only cut away the scorched sleeve.
Then the flames surge, and the girl steps calmly into the fire. Cries ring out from the crowd, only to watch her step out of the ashes, untouched. She's met with thunderous applause, and not one voice doubts her any longer.
The Deathless Quiet
In the deathless quiet, a man is blessed with the power to know and love his people.

Long, long ago, before the oak leaves had fallen, people had already learned to use language to explain all things: the snake had already become a symbol of both chaos and rebirth; the morning star, the bond of fate; the swallow, herald of spring and of God, carrying sacred words into your soul.
"That is why we are given the right to carry these words—to recognize our companions among the happiness of this world."
A group of children listens. One of them understands more than the rest. He stares uneasily at the branch changing in his hands and understands that names are definitions. To name is to commit violence against the shapeless.
As he leaves his hometown, he turns to the endless snow in search of an answer. Why did everything happen this way, and not some other? So sudden, and so impossible to resist—is this what they call "life"?
Leonid Anatolyevich Belyakov. The birch tree bends toward him. A swallow flies past. The answer to his question is another question. What kind of story is this to you? What words will you choose to name it? Will you declare its ending, or its beginning?
The snow falls without a sound.
