On the eve of the "Storm," Ms. Stranger informs her that Team Timekeeper is not permitted to leave headquarters. She calms the team members and waits for the Timekeeper's return.

After receiving intelligence from Ms. Stranger about Manus Vindictae's raid, Ms. Druvis begins planting seeds throughout the Foundation's facilities to block and counter any enemies that arrive. The other survivors also take matters into their own hands.

From the Committee Building: Team Timekeeper's druid is using her arcane skills to control branches and thorns, halting the enemy's advance. She's also cleared passages between floors to cover the movement of personnel and supplies.
All members of Team Timekeeper survive the Manus Vindictae attack. Afterward, Ms. Druvis replants saplings and flowers in the Foundation's garden to replace those damaged or lost in the battle.

Team Timekeeper is currently housed in the Foundation's guest rooms. Upon learning of the unrest outside, Regulus sends Mr. APPLe to look into the Timekeeper's whereabouts. She also gets an overview of the situation from Ms. Stranger.
Team Timekeeper now serves as a reserve unit of the Pre-Storm QRF to help secure headquarters—though not every member fully understands what that actually means.
From the Committee Building: Team Timekeeper's captain and chief mate are supporting Foundation soldiers with optical arcane skills and working alongside other arcanists to counter the enemy forces.
As the fighting rages on, Regulus and Mr. APPLe break off on their own to track down the enemy commander hiding in the rear.

All members of Team Timekeeper survive the Manus Vindictae attack. Afterward, Regulus gleefully accepts several cases of Dr. Papper from the Foundation's logistics department as a token of their gratitude.

She tries to pass a few bottles along to Lilya to "pay her back," but is turned down.

The Foundation president operates from the shadows and remains a mystery. Even within the Foundation, only a select few employees, including Vice President Constantine, have direct access to him. He appears to have deep ties to the Pax House.

On the day of Manus Vindictae's raid, the president orders a full-force defense. Though he does not know Arcana's purpose, he understands that the Foundation cannot handle this crisis alone. He seems to be buying time—but for what, none can say.

The president willingly answers Arcana's questions, stalling long enough for a mysterious force known as the Core Guard to arrive and "drive out" Arcana. Between the counteroffensive against Manus Vindictae's forces, Arcana's power, and the intelligence behind the scenes, it seems everything unfolded just as the president had anticipated ...

Ms. Stranger is a Foundation spy who once went undercover inside Manus Vindictae. During the Antarctic incident, she helped the Timekeeper stop a Manus ritual, after which she fell into a coma and was sent to the rehab center for treatment. Now recovered, Ms. Stranger is temporarily stationed at Foundation headquarters, serving in the Pre-Storm Dispatch Center to coordinate between departments before the "Storm."

She also filed a report on Manus Vindictae's leadership. Through her efforts, we've learned that Manus leaders are numerous, scattered across regions, and active in every post-Storm era, but the intel she gathered still isn't enough to see the full picture of their inner workings.

During the raid, Ms. Stranger encounters Arcana and loses consciousness. When she wakes up, Mr. "Razor" and the others suspect her of betrayal due to the Manus mask in her hand. Once the misunderstanding is cleared up, she returns to the Arcanum Containment Department with Eagle and rejoins the group.

After sharing her intelligence on Manus Vindictae's leadership with the others, Ms. Stranger ventures into the Manus-occupied zone alone, trying to find their entrance into the Foundation. Before leaving, she takes the mask she knows all too well from Ms. Marguerite.

Unable to use her arcane skills due to Arcana's influence, Ms. Stranger puts on the mask once more. She directs the Foundation toward Manus Vindictae's point of entry and seizes control over the enemy's ritualist.

Ms. Stranger fights the mask's whispers to recite a Manus incantation and block the enemy's entry into the Foundation. The punishment that follows nearly turns her into a monster, but in the end, Ms. Stranger tears off the mask and takes back her mind.

After everything she's been through, Ms. Stranger considers giving herself a new name, but she ultimately decides against it. She no longer wants to live as a Foundation spy—she's found a better place to be, one where she can live as an ordinary arcanist.

Since the tenth "Storm," Vice President Constantine has kept a close eye on the conflict between the Doves and the Hawks, working to mediate so the Foundation's internal power balance doesn't tip too far in either direction. She believes that maintaining stability within the Foundation is essential to withstand the threat posed by Manus Vindictae.

During the Manus raid, the vice president quickly coordinates reinforcements, directs operations at the front, and begins weighing additional strategies for what's to come.

Acting on the president's orders, Vice President Constantine is reaching out to surviving members of the Committee and the House of Integratus, preparing to escort them to the top floor of the Spire for shelter. She appears to trust the president's judgment completely.

The chaos from the Manus Vindictae raid has settled. Filling the Foundation's personnel gaps, rebuilding the SPDM's facilities and education system, handling and reassigning the work of those lost in the attack, and building a consensus and policy on how to handle future "Storms" are all crucial decisions that the vice president must address.

During the Manus raid, Madam Z remains at her post, maintaining communication between Committee members and House of Integratus representatives and helping Vice President Constantine organize the evacuation.
Acting on the president's orders, Madam Z is directing the surviving members of the Committee and the House of Integratus to take shelter in the president's office on the top floor of the Spire.

In the wake of the raid, Madam Z takes on the role of acting principal of the SPDM, while her duties within the Foundation continue as usual. She approves the Timekeeper's field mission request and welcomes Ms. Stranger as an official member of Team Timekeeper.

Mr. Creius has been called before the Committee to answer for a range of alleged violations stretching from the Western Front campaign to the present. While he doesn't deny the allegations, he doesn't appear to consider himself to be "in the wrong," either.
He once disclosed intelligence on Urd to the Timekeeper, which led us to the Eastern Front. Should the Committee learn of this, it could change how the Foundation regards the Timekeeper and Team Timekeeper as a whole.
An unexpected emergency broadcast cuts the Committee's trial short. Those present face two options: trust the Foundation's standard evacuation protocol to hold, or take more drastic measures.

Mr. Creius has been moving through the Committee Building, organizing the Foundation's security forces and staff to hold the line. When faced with Arcana, whom bullets cannot kill, he orders the soldiers to stop engaging her and focus on fighting the Manus rank-and-file instead.
Mr. Creius survives the raid, and the inquiry against him is put on hold. He'll be searching for his missing teammates, though he appears to have other plans as well.

With the Eastern Front campaign now ended, Merel has been brought back to the Foundation and assigned to Team Timekeeper as a temporary member.
After visiting Ms. Marsha, Merel heads to the SPDM to assist the school ahead of the "Storm" as a Foundation staff member.
As Matilda's assistant, Merel is responsible for checking on the Shelter Doves' operations and "catching" certain "troublemakers."
At the SPDM watchtower, Merel spots the Manus Vindictae invaders and reports the situation to the Foundation while Matilda holds them off.

After learning the Timekeeper has decided to use the "boon," Merel resolves to act on her own. She heads to the central watchtower to retrieve the still-functional Shelter Doves and bring them to the library as a backup plan against the "Storm."

At the central watchtower, Merel receives help from two students who had been held in the guardhouse and manages to find operational Shelter Doves—but the three are attacked by Manus followers. To protect the students and everyone still sheltering in the library, Merel chooses to face the enemy and the coming "Storm" alone.
With the Timekeeper's immunity zone just a step away, the "Storm" comes down, and Merel disappears into the downpour.

In the Tylwyth Teg Berry Garden in the United Kingdom, we meet a girl called "Rhiannon" for the first time. Though she's a new friend, it's as if someone we'd lost in the rain is standing before us again.
This is what the Timekeeper spoke of: an opportunity from the new era.

Matilda is an outstanding graduate who previously served as a monitor assistant in the SPDM. After passing a series of evaluations, she is now an official special investigator of the Foundation.

In the lead-up to the "Storm," Matilda is dispatched to the SPDM to maintain order as leader of the Security Assistance Team and ensure the Shelter Doves are functioning properly.
Matilda discovers the enemy is targeting the Shelter Doves in the watchtower. She tries to stop them but is struck down by Manus Vindictae's incantations.

After the "Storm" passes, Matilda wakes up in a ward at the rehab center. We plan to wait for a better moment to tell her about the school ... and about Merel.
For now, she seems to be focusing on "repaying everyone's kindness."

Lavender is the current monitor assistant in the SPDM and Matilda's successor. According to Matilda, she's a conscientious and serious student.

Before the "Storm," she notices that some students are absent from the opening ceremony and reports it to Matilda.

Lavender spots intruders in the school during her patrol and reports them to Matilda. School rules don't allow her to make contact with outsiders, so she leaves it to Matilda and Merel when they arrive.
After the Manus raid, Lavender leads the students from the opening ceremony to the library for shelter as per her emergency training, which is where we encounter her.

Given her status as an upperclassman who witnessed the raid, Lavender is asked to submit a damage report covering personnel and facilities at the SPDM. Madam Z, serving as acting principal, notes that the report will be an important reference for the school's reconstruction.

In the Antarctic incident, the once-eliminated Arcana returned through a Manus Vindictae ritual, triggering a "Flood" even more devastating than the "Storm." Time was reversed once more, and she vanished into the waters.

Now, Arcana and her Manus forces have launched a raid on Foundation headquarters. Is it revenge for past interference that drives her, or an attempt to destroy the heart of her enemies' authority? Even now, nobody knows.

Nautika and the rest of Team Timekeeper arrive as reinforcements, and together, the Foundation barely manages to hold against the Manus assault. Then Arcana turns the tide, robbing our arcanists of their ability to wield arcanum and hurling Team Timekeeper out of the building.
Arcana pays no mind to anything in her path, instead ascending to the top floor of the Spire.

After the Core Guard intervenes, Arcana departs, though not without leaving one of her creations as a "gift." She seemed to have gotten the answer she came for from her conversation with the president.

On the Eastern Front, the defeated Krutov escaped with the help of a Manus ritualist and vanished. Now he has followed Arcana's lead, bringing the Manus forces to assault Foundation headquarters.
Could the arcane skill they used to infiltrate the Foundation be the same one he used to flee the battlefield?

Despite being impeded by Foundation security forces, Krutov presses his advantage with the surprise attack and drives the Manus soldiers through our defenses. His abilities as a field commander pose a formidable threat.
Ms. Stranger sealing Manus Vindictae's entry into the Foundation cuts off enemy reinforcements and slows the troops' advance.
With Arcana having left the battlefield, Krutov chooses not to linger and orders his troops to withdraw rather than face the Core Guard. The battle ends with the Foundation holding its ground.

Like Krutov, the ritualist follows Arcana to join the raid. To carry out her task, she splits off from the main force and acts alone—and in doing so, crosses paths with Ms. Stranger, who is also operating solo.
Her faith in Arcana appears to run deeper than that of the other Manus believers.
To contend with Arcana silencing our arcane skills, Ms. Stranger chooses to put on the Manus mask. The ritualist falls under Ms. Stranger's control once she's reclaimed her arcane power.
Thanks to Ms. Stranger, we captured the ritualist. She will be a valuable lead for the Foundation in understanding Manus Vindictae's "Windweave" and other arcane skills.

Eagle is a member of the Institutum Lorentz. Too old to enroll in the SPDM, she completed her studies by moving between schools across different eras with Mr. X's help. She went on to become an official Laplace intern studying under Ms. Marguerite. In the lead-up to the "Storm," Eagle accompanies her to Foundation headquarters to assist with research on the "boon."
In the chaos of the raid, Eagle gets separated from Ms. Marguerite. She finds Ms. Stranger unconscious in a hallway and brings her to safety.
Eagle rendezvous with Ms. Druvis and the rest of Team Timekeeper and follows them to the front to help the Foundation forces fend off Manus Vindictae.

Arcana's attack sends everyone crashing onto the plaza of the Committee Building. While waiting for their arcane power to recover, Eagle and Mr. "Razor," along with everyone else still capable of fighting, stand to protect Nautika, who is now an easy target due to her size and inability to move her lower body.
After the dust settles, Eagle follows Ms. Marguerite back to Laplace to help repair damaged instruments. She'll also be helping to analyze data on Manus Vindictae retrieved during the raid.

January 30, 1921. People have extended a war that should have long ended, resulting in the fires of conflict sweeping across the world and deepening the era's chaos. According to the Foundation's observations, the next "Storm" is approaching.
January 31, 1921. Foundation headquarters. The Committee has summoned the captain of the "XII" Squad to answer for a series of alleged violations during and after the Western Front campaign.
January 31, 1921. The SPDM is holding an opening ceremony for the new school year.
January 31, 1921. Several SPDM students have planned an escape, but the Security Assistance Team stops them just in time.
January 31, 1921. Laplace sends a research team to the Foundation to investigate the "boon" the Timekeeper acquired on the Eastern Front.
January 31, 1921. The Foundation receives word of Manus Vindictae's raid on the SPDM.
January 31, 1921. To support the SPDM in fending off the attackers, the Foundation assembles and dispatches the First Squad of the Pre-Storm Quick Reaction Force.
January 31, 1921. Guided by senior students, those who gathered for the opening ceremony take shelter in the school library.
January 31, 1921. The First Squad is ambushed on its way to assist the SPDM and suffers casualties.
January 31, 1921. Foundation headquarters sounds a stage one alert—the Foundation is under attack.
January 31, 1921. With the alert sounded, the Foundation scrambles to coordinate a response and assess the situation.
January 31, 1921. Unexpected reinforcements arrive and turn the tide for the First Squad.
January 31, 1921. To find a way to turn the tide before the "Storm" arrives, the Timekeeper, still trapped inside the SPDM, decides to activate the "boon" and seek its protection.
January 31, 1921. The Foundation's remaining forces rally and launch an effective counterattack against Manus Vindictae.
January 31, 1921. Arcana's silencing incantation renders every Foundation arcanist unable to use arcanum, granting Manus Vindictae the upper hand.
January 31, 1921. In the SPDM, the survivors move to prevent a mass "Storm" reversal—the worst-case scenario.
January 31, 1921. The Timekeeper finds guidance amid the chaos and follows where it leads.
January 31, 1921. Without their arcane skills and overwhelmed by Manus Vindictae, Foundation personnel struggle to hold out.
January 31, 1921. The portal Manus Vindictae had used to infiltrate the Foundation is sealed, cutting off their reinforcements.
January 31, 1921. Within the discord, the Timekeeper attempts to wield a power that she cannot yet understand.
January 31, 1921. In the SPDM, the survivors' efforts to save themselves pay off—but the "Storm" is nearly here.
January 31, 1921. The leaders of the Foundation and Manus Vindictae meet at the top floor of the Spire. The discussion quickly becomes a desperate battle against the clock.
January 31, 1921. The "Storm" arrives as expected. The Timekeeper uses the "boon" to create an immunity zone, allowing everyone in the SPDM library to weather the "Storm."
April 1, 1935. With the conflict over, personnel begin discussions on rebuilding the Foundation and the SPDM.
April 2, 1935. Having uncovered a new lead during the "Storm," the Timekeeper sets out into the new era.
April 6, 1935. The Timekeeper meets a new companion—albeit one with a familiar face. Together, they set off to face the unknown.

From: Osborn

When the Storm Reaction Protocols are active, the primary duty of the First Squad is to provide armed support—whether inside headquarters or outside. I need you to head to the storage depot and ensure that the wearable Equilibrium Umbrellas there are functional for emergency use.

To: Yermolai

"I didn't expect the Foundation to have this many Equilibrium Umbrellas, and they're in good shape, too. Looks like those warehouse clerks aren't just sitting around after all. With a stock like this, there's nothing to worry about—though ideally, we won't need them. Time to get back to the gate."

From: Druvis III

I heard from Ms. Stranger that there's an emergency at the SPDM. Vertin has already left to deal with it. The "Storm" is imminent, so we need to prepare extra potions in advance.

To: Sotheby

"I see, I see! In that case, I'll brew some other kinds of potions on top of the Pain-Relieving Dew and Misty Mist Spray! Like the Bouncing Energy Potion for physical fatigue, and the Spotless Detergent for stains ...Oh! And with the 'Storm' almost here, anyone who doesn't make it into the Foundation in time might come down with Storm Syndrome. Maybe I can brew up something for them, too!"

From: Todd

Wh-Why'd the emergency alert go off? Something big must be happening. I need to get to the gate and help evacuate people ... Right, go check the Arcanum Containment Department first. You might find something useful there.

To: J

"Man, I've never seen Todd so freaked out. The alert must be serious. I should do what he said and hurry back to help."

"Let's see what we've got here ... Huh? A Chattercap? The Foundation's growing mushrooms now? Whatever ... Oh, a howling box. That might come in handy—I'll take it."

From: Pre-Storm Dispatch Center

Manus Vindictae is attacking the Foundation headquarters. Civilian evacuation has been handed off to other staff. Please guide the arcanists inside the facility to safety. For now, the Arcanum Containment Department should serve as a suitable shelter.

To: "Razor"
"The Manus? Here?! The nerve ...! No, calm down. This isn't the time for that. I need to find Team Timekeeper, check for separated arcanists, and get everyone to shelter. That's the plan."

From: Rehab Center Staff

Manus Vindictae is attacking Foundation headquarters. They've even started targeting us here at Laplace. The guards have limited experience dealing with arcanists. If you're able, please help them hold off Manus Vindictae.

To: Marsha

"Manus Vindictae ...! I saw what they did to Charon and the others back on the Don. I won't let that happen in front of me again. I've only just recovered, but I should still be able to fight with Laplace's equipment. Nautika is still here, too. If I can find her, we can take on Manus Vindictae together—maybe even make it to headquarters to help."

From: Moldir

Manus Vindictae isn't letting up. Can you cook up some heavy fog to cover our counterattack? We can talk about everything else once we've made it through this.

To: Lopera

"... Understood. That's nothing for me. I'm not like you all, standing by while your companions are in danger. What happens with the First Squad isn't my call, but once this is over, you owe me an explanation."

From: Ms. Stranger

The verification data on the Timekeeper's "boon" is still in the southern garden office. This is critical research material. Please back it up as soon as possible, before Manus Vindictae can destroy it.

To: Lorentz Butterfly

"I wouldn't forget something this important even without the reminder. The backup is already in the data storage device I have with me. I'll bring it back to Laplace."

"Interestingly enough, on my way out of the garden, I found this strange black mask. I think you'll find this little 'souvenir' quite interesting."

From: "Razor"

The arcanists in the building have gathered. Please have them work together to defend the facilities that haven't fallen yet. Places like the Arcanum Containment Department hold many critical items. We can't let Manus Vindictae get their hands on them.

To: Loggerhead

"Right you are, sir! I spend so much time keeping these collections in order. There's no way I'm letting Manus Vindictae ransack them—not even if it means using up all my film!"
"There are other places like the Arcanum Containment Department in the Foundation, too. We have to defend them!"

From: Pointer

Hissabeth's methods were extreme, but they've bought us time against Manus Vindictae's advance. The situation is coming under control, and we can spare some hands to support the Foundation. We'll still need a backup plan to minimize Laplace's losses.

To: John Titor

"4e6f2070726f626c656d2e2047697665206d6520736f6d652074696d652e" John Titor suggested loading Laplace's Anti-Strike Paint I into automated robots, then using the IDM5100 to map out the optimal route and have them move through the facility, continuously coating the equipment. That should keep most of it intact.

From: Pre-Storm Dispatch Center

Arcana's arrival has made the situation inside the Committee Building dire. Personnel still capable of fighting, please proceed to the facility, protect the survivors, and minimize our casualties.

To: Lilya

"What happened?! My arcane skills and Red 38 are down! What kind of Flying Witch fights on the ground?! ... At least I didn't fall out of the sky, and I'm still in one piece ... Tsk! Forget it, I'm moving!"

From: Enigma

John Titor had a backup plan ready in 10 minutes. We need to implement it now, while the situation is still under control.

To: Ulrich

"According to the plan, we need to get people in position and prepare the containers for Anti-Strike Paint I, functional automated robots, and computers to connect and input the route data ... Manus Vindictae is still attacking, but things are coming under control. We just need a little more time!"

From: Creius

Arcana is gone. The silence effect should start to lift. Wake the sleeping trees now and help us push back against Manus Vindictae's forces.

To: Druvis III

"... My control over the trees is returning. It seems Arcana's departure will give us a chance to win. I have no intention of taking orders from the Foundation, but I won't stand by while Manus Vindictae harms innocent people. I'll wake the thorns and branches to drive them out."

From: Ptolemy

The battle is over, and we don't have much time before the "Storm" hits. Count your casualties as quickly as you can, then bring both teams together. It's time to decide whether we stay or go.

To: Paravyan

"Yermolai doesn't seem opposed to the rebels. Sure, they saved our lives, but that doesn't mean we forgive them for what they've done. And being branded as rebels along with them ... But if we stay here, there's no question we'll all vanish in the rain. Even at full speed, we'd never make it to the SPDM in time ... But under these circumstances, maybe we really have no other choice ..."

From: Mesmer Jr.

Given your size and physical structure, you were likely the most affected when Arcana cast the silence incantation. Could you describe what it felt like? It would help us research countermeasures.

To: Nautika

"What it felt like ... When Arcana cast that incantation, my body gave out completely. My talons and wings stopped responding, and I couldn't move at all ... I came down hard on the plaza. My body wasn't injured, but I had no strength left, like I'd suddenly lost all feeling in my lower half ...
"Come to think of it, only my lower half was affected. My original body felt fine. How strange ..."

As one of the witnesses—though I'd rather not talk about it—maybe what happened did leave a bad influence on the students who came after.
Every year there are escape attempts, and they always use George the Oak's tree hole as their base. Lavender told me the students even call Vertin and Sonetto ... ahem, and Special Investigator Matilda here "campus legends"! I mean, they're not wrong, but ... No, it's too much! Running away is wrong, and they need to be disciplined accordingly!

SPDM Emergency Response Manual Contents Campus Fire Evacuation Procedures Uncontrolled Arcane Power Suppression Protocol Countermeasures Against Wild Flying Critters Student Escape Incidents (Revised Edition) ... The emergency manual is thorough, but it still doesn't cover the current situation.

This was my first real battle since joining the Gryphon Legion. When Lieutenant Moldir gathered everyone to head to the Foundation's aid, I thought I might get to see some friends from Zeno, or maybe Merel, so I joined without a second thought. Manus Vindictae's interference messed up the admiral's teleportation, and we were sent somewhere strange. Still, we got lucky and managed to save some Foundation members.
There's a girl about my age in the Foundation's forces who seems to be a soldier, too. She actually dared to shout at Admiral Igor and Lieutenant Moldir. I wonder if they know each other ...

Manus Vindictae is far more frightening than I'd imagined.
Not long ago, when Ms. Semmelweis came back to report to the Foundation with Ms. Marcus, I heard her talking about Manus Vindictae. I thought they were just thugs in strange masks, muttering mumbo-jumbo and worshiping this "Guiding One." Just a bunch of lunatics, and the Foundation was overreacting.
I never thought they'd turn out to be monsters ...

Most of the students who left the opening ceremony have taken shelter in the library. But Manus Vindictae's monsters are closing in on the school's crucial zones.
According to Special Investigator Matilda, their goal is to destroy the Shelter Doves inside the school, which would leave the entire SPDM exposed to the "Storm." No one would be spared.
We couldn't stop the monsters, let alone eliminate them. For the students' safety, all we could do was protect the Shelter Doves in the central watchtower. That should at least keep the library covered when the "Storm" arrives.

Avian Critter Behaviors and Feeding Methods This guide covers the ecology and habits of Adar Llwch Gwins in detail. They live in berry orchards, and they have strong bodies and powerful wings. Riding one through the sky must feel incredible! Unfortunately, there are very few of them left. Griffins are also large, bird-like Critters. Could they be related to Adar Llwch Gwins? Five Easy Recipes to Brew an Invisibility Potion Shapeshifting is great, but invisibility is even better. Rather than letting others see you in a different form, why not make sure they can't see you at all ... The brewing method for invisibility potions is fascinating, but the ingredients aren't easy to come by. Fiddler Crab Shapeshifting for Dummies Shapeshifting is important no matter what! It lets me slip away without anyone noticing. When things get dangerous, it's my way out! Notes found among Merel's personal belongings. They seem to have been written during her school days.

It seems you've found a place for the "loyal" advocate I mentioned before. Joining Team Timekeeper doesn't mean leaving the Foundation, but I believe she'll have more freedom than she used to.
That said, there are indeed certain individuals within the Foundation who have the privilege of temporarily separating from it due to their special circumstances. That vampire investigator, for instance. The Foundation always maintains contact with such individuals, of course, and occasionally sends them urgent commissions. During their time away, however, they have the right to decline.
It's Manus Vindictae's Olitiaus! Watch out!
The numbers are insane ... Just how many flying Critters have they bred?
Less talking, more fighting. One's flying your way—shoot it down.
That was close! It nearly got away ... Wait, where's the captain?
She broke through the encirclement while we were fighting the Olitiaus. She's heading straight for Foundation headquarters.
That's our captain!
We need to finish off these monsters and get back to help.
Soldiers in the rear are reporting that one of the "Windweave" entrances has been closed!
Who did it? Don't tell me ... there's someone in the Foundation who knows our arcane skills?
I don't know the details, but that was our reinforcements' entry point. Which means ...
Don't panic. Report to Krutov—he'll tell us what to do.
Tsk, what timing ... If they close the other entrances too, we'll be cut off.
We're not going anywhere until the Guiding One leaves. Report in and get back to your post, soldier.
Hey, you alright?
No, I ... Captain Osborn was shot dead right in front of me and ... and there was nothing I could do.
Bad luck happens to everyone. Worry about what comes next instead.
So what are the commanders from the "XII" Squad planning to do? Are we pulling back with the rebels, or staying on the mission?
I don't know, but the "Storm" is near. If the choice were yours, what would you do?
I don't want to be labeled a rebel, but ... I choose to live.
While at Foundation headquarters, the Timekeeper, Sonetto, and Merel visit Marsha, who was injured at the Don. Afterward, the Timekeeper handles various administrative tasks.
After news comes in that the SPDM has been attacked, the Timekeeper and Sonetto use a teleport disk from Ms. Marguerite and arrive at the school first to provide support.
After meeting with the survivors at the school, the Timekeeper leads everyone to the school library, where they will hold out for Foundation reinforcements.
With reinforcements blocked and the "Storm" near, the Timekeeper decides to activate the "boon" and search for a refuge.

Inside the chaotic world the "boon" unveils to her, the Timekeeper, trying to understand the world's rules, accidentally unlocks the doors in the central watchtower for Merel, who is still in the real world.
The Timekeeper continues helping Merel through the realm of the "boon." At one point, she even senses Arcana's presence.
The Timekeeper finds a way out—a way back to the real world and a way to lead everyone through the "Storm."
Back in the library, the Timekeeper uses the "boon" to create an immunity zone, shielding everyone in the Library from the "Storm."

Back at the Foundation, the Timekeeper and Sonetto set out for Laplace. After visiting Matilda, who was knocked unconscious and injured, they work with Laplace researchers to verify the lead uncovered within the "boon."

The Timekeeper and Sonetto set out to find Merel, who vanished during the "Storm." Following the lead, they find a "new friend" who looks just like her—but it's clear this isn't the Merel they knew.
They will set off from the Tylwyth Teg Berry Garden in the United Kingdom and head north with their new companion.

"Long time no see, Timekeeper, Sonetto." Now recovered, Ms. Stranger has been assigned to work at Foundation headquarters, assisting with research on the "boon." She brings the Timekeeper to meet with the researchers from Laplace.

"Meanwhile, I will mobilize the reserves and take over security here." After receiving news that the SPDM has been attacked, Ms. Stranger relays orders to the First Squad and takes over work at Foundation headquarters.
"Apparently ... neither you nor I like the characters we're playing on this stage." During the raid, Ms. Stranger visits Team Timekeeper's temporary room to brief everyone on the situation.

"Arcana? No, this can't be happening ..." Ms. Stranger crosses paths with Arcana, who has come to attack the Foundation's headquarters. She is rendered unconscious by the interference of Arcana's arcane skill.

"I hate what they made me do—stealing people's names and lives. The guilt of it sits in my chest. But today, my choice is my own." Ms. Stranger sets off to investigate how Manus Vindictae had infiltrated the Foundation.
"Stay calm. This will only take a moment." Ms. Stranger seizes the opportunity to attack the lone ritualist.

"But whatever lies they tell, it makes no difference to me. I am loyal only to my own cause now." To break free of Arcana's silencing incantation and overpower the ritualist, Ms. Stranger puts on the Manus mask once more.

"To leave here ... To never ... never come back ..." Though the mask nearly turns Ms. Stranger into a monster, she breaks free of it and succeeds in sealing Manus Vindictae's portal into the Foundation.
"I just want to live my own life, as an arcanist under the Timekeeper." After everything she's been through, Ms. Stranger finally joins Team Timekeeper as an ordinary arcanist.
"So, it's just a routine check, then?" Merel is sent to the SPDM to help Matilda maintain order.

"War ... There's a war raging out there. Honestly, I wish I could stay here at the school where it's safe. And that's not even the worst part ..." Merel and Matilda catch two students trying to escape. They hand them over to the teachers and get to work checking the Shelter Doves.
"I'll be back as soon as I can! Stay safe, Matilda!" When Manus Vindictae attacks, Matilda covers Merel's retreat so she can report the situation to the Foundation.

"And this time ... I've got one!" After learning the Timekeeper is planning to seek refuge using the "boon," Merel decides to check the central watchtower for functional Shelter Doves, hoping to improve everyone's chances of survival.

"I'll get you to the library. But first, there's something important I need to get from upstairs." Merel is surrounded by Manus believers after arriving at the central watchtower, but she makes it out of harm's way thanks to the two students who tried to escape earlier.
"Now, come on. After everything I've been through ... I can survive this!" Merel retrieves the working Shelter Doves from beneath the body of a dead teacher, but the "Storm" is already starting.
"I ... don't want to go ..." So close, yet Merel cannot make it to the Timekeeper's newly created immunity zone in time. She is reversed by the "Storm."

"At last, some peace and quiet." Arcana arrives at the front line and casts a silencing incantation, stripping the Foundation's arcanists of their powers. Then, she sweeps her enemies from the building along with everything else nearby using an unknown arcane skill.
"Ah, guns. How quaint." Arcana ignores every hostile and continues her ascent of the Spire.

"Thy Foundation's hospitality hath grown cold, Mr. President." Arcana meets with the president at the top of the Spire, but the Core Guard cuts their conversation short. After leaving behind an arcane creation, she makes her departure.

"It's not your fault, Ms. Stranger. I made that decision myself." In the chaos of the Manus Vindictae raid, Eagle stumbles upon the unconscious Ms. Stranger, and together, they make their way to safety.

"Did she ...?!" While the team swept out of the building are recovering, Eagle receives contact from Ms. Stranger through her arcane skill. She realizes that Ms. Stranger has put on the Manus mask again.
"Just think about how many they've already driven to our side." Creius has been summoned before the Committee at Foundation headquarters to answer for allegations dating back to the tenth "Storm."

"We have to mobilize everyone—anyone who can stand needs to be a part of this fight." As the Committee members hesitate in the face of the crisis, Creius urges them to put aside their differences, ready everyone for battle, and buy time to get people to safety.
"If you encounter Arcana, do not engage—I repeat, no hostile action!" Foundation personnel are pushed to the brink, but Creius refuses to give up, continuing to organize their retreat to the Spire.

"If the Timekeeper won't work with us, then we proceed in our own way." After learning what had happened to the First Squad, Creius resolves to track down his team members. He also braces himself mentally for the struggle against Manus Vindictae in the new era.

Observations indicate the next "Storm" will arrive within the next 24 hours. In the meantime, the Timekeeper will remain at Foundation headquarters to handle various administrative tasks. Team Timekeeper will also stay until the "Storm" passes.
After the Foundation comes under attack, Team Timekeeper takes shelter in the Arcanum Containment Department. Ms. Stranger arrives later and shares intelligence on Manus Vindictae's leadership.
Reaching the front line amid the fierce fighting, Team Timekeeper begins lending their support with arcane skills.

With the battle ended, most of Team Timekeeper joins the reconstruction efforts at the Foundation and Laplace, while the injured receive treatment at the rehab center. The rest are waiting for the Suitcase inspection to conclude before heading back inside.
Now under attack, Foundation leaders begin considering how to counter Manus Vindictae's next moves; buying enough time for reinforcements to arrive is paramount.
Following orders from above, the Committee members leave the hearing room and head for the top of the Spire.
The front-line soldiers' relentless resistance gives the Committee members the chance to take shelter in the president's office on the top floor.

The SPDM suffered heavy personnel losses due to Manus Vindictae's raid. As a result, the Foundation will appoint Madam Z as acting principal, with the rest of the reconstruction proceeding in order.
The Foundation will also continue investigating the Timekeeper's "boon" and the truth behind Manus Vindictae's "Windweave."
Following the Foundation's orders, Marguerite and Eagle leave Laplace for the Foundation's headquarters to verify the latest progress on "boon" research.
Like the Foundation, Laplace has also come under Manus Vindictae attack. The researchers there are doing their best to fight back.

In the wake of the raid, Laplace researchers are busy organizing the previously backed-up data and repairing equipment. Eagle, now back from the Foundation, brings a report on the encounter with Manus Vindictae, which will serve as an important reference for future research.

Drawing on Eagle's report alongside intelligence from the Foundation, Laplace has gained a general understanding of Arcana's silencing incantation. Laplace may need some assistance from Nautika for the research ahead.
As the Guiding One makes her move, Manus Vindictae's forces follow through the "Windweave," preparing to launch an assault on the Foundation.
Led by their commanders, Manus Vindictae soldiers clash with Foundation forces across multiple locations.
With their Guiding One gone and the "Windweave" sealed, Manus Vindictae's forces are cut off from any support, leaving them no choice but to retreat.
The success of the Foundation raid has confirmed the "Windweave's" value in combat. Manus Vindictae will likely make further use of it for operations around the world going forward.

People have extended a war that should have long ended, resulting in the fires of conflict sweeping across the world and deepening the era's chaos. According to the Foundation's observations, the next "Storm" is approaching.
Foundation headquarters. The Committee has summoned the captain of the "XII" Squad to answer for a series of alleged violations during and after the Western Front campaign.
The SPDM is holding an opening ceremony for the new school year.
Several SPDM students have planned an escape, but the Security Assistance Team stops them just in time.
Laplace sends a research team to the Foundation to investigate the "boon" the Timekeeper acquired on the Eastern Front.
The Foundation receives word of Manus Vindictae's raid on the SPDM.
To support the SPDM in fending off the attackers, the Foundation assembles and dispatches the First Squad of the Pre-Storm Quick Reaction Force.
Guided by senior students, those who gathered for the opening ceremony take shelter in the school library.
The First Squad is ambushed on its way to assist the SPDM and suffers casualties.
Foundation headquarters sounds a stage one alert—the Foundation is under attack.
With the alert sounded, the Foundation scrambles to coordinate a response and assess the situation.
Unexpected reinforcements arrive and turn the tide for the First Squad.
To find a way to turn the tide before the "Storm" arrives, the Timekeeper, still trapped inside the SPDM, decides to activate the "boon" and seek its protection.
The Foundation's remaining forces rally and launch an effective counterattack against Manus Vindictae.
Arcana's silencing incantation renders every Foundation arcanist unable to use arcanum, granting Manus Vindictae the upper hand.
In the SPDM, the survivors move to prevent a mass "Storm" reversal—the worst-case scenario.
The Timekeeper finds guidance amid the chaos and follows where it leads.
Without their arcane skills and overwhelmed by Manus Vindictae, Foundation personnel struggle to hold out.
The portal Manus Vindictae had used to infiltrate the Foundation is sealed, cutting off their reinforcements.
Within the discord, the Timekeeper attempts to wield a power that she cannot yet understand.
In the SPDM, the survivors' efforts to save themselves pay off—but the "Storm" is nearly here.
The leaders of the Foundation and Manus Vindictae meet at the top floor of the Spire. The discussion quickly becomes a desperate battle against the clock.
The "Storm" arrives as expected. The Timekeeper uses the "boon" to create an immunity zone, allowing everyone in the SPDM library to weather the "Storm."
With the conflict over, personnel begin discussions on rebuilding the Foundation and the SPDM.
Having uncovered a new lead during the "Storm," the Timekeeper sets out into the new era.
The Timekeeper meets a new companion—albeit one with a familiar face. Together, they set off to face the unknown.

The attack damaged several Foundation facilities, and though it seriously affected our operations, even worse was the loss of life. I saw so many of our colleagues get ...
Since Arcana was targeting the president, the Committee Building suffered the most damage. But thanks to the help of Ms. Cornerstone and Team Timekeeper's arcanists, I'm sure the building will be back in use soon.
Then there's the matter of the traitors. Madam Z mentioned that Manus Vindictae coerced some staff members into opening the way. It seems the higher-ups plan to give them a chance to redeem themselves by assisting with investigations on Manus Vindictae ...
Those people ... They're the ones responsible for this tragedy! How can they be forgiven so easily?! Even if they provide intel, they should be locked up afterward ... Yes, they must be. That's the only way to do right by our fallen companions ...

Laplace has to knock it off with the explosions—or at least not blow things up on a daily basis. Just imagine how much we could accomplish if we spent our time on research rather than clean-up ...
Still, thanks to Researcher Hissabeth's plan, we survived this attack. Combined with the backup plan from Researcher John Titor, Laplace's losses were kept to a minimum.
The Foundation also reported something interesting. Arcana seems capable of sealing an arcanist's ability to cast incantations, and this seal even works on arcane items.
Knowing this, we're going to have a lot of work on our plates ...

On the eve of the "Storm," Manus Vindictae's attack put us in a very dangerous situation. Many people survived thanks to the Timekeeper, but others have been reversed.
This could have been avoided.
For administrative reasons, the Timekeeper is required to regularly submit the Suitcase for inspection and maintenance. This time, the check coincided with the eve of the "Storm."
Normally, maintenance should have been postponed during such critical times. Furthermore, considering the Timekeeper's abilities and track record, the Suitcase should be kept and maintained by the Timekeeper personally—after all, no one else can actually use it.
I will submit a formal request to reduce how often the Suitcase is checked and propose that future maintenance should only happen with the Timekeeper's approval.
That way, no one else will be forced to vanish before our eyes.

The attack on the SPDM was a diversion by Manus Vindictae to weaken the Foundation's headquarters. The school suffered heavy losses, with most of its faculty and staff dying in the assault.
Fortunately, thanks to the Timekeeper and her companions, most of the students survived. The monitor assistant, Lavender, acted quickly and decisively during the attack. I am confident she will be a valuable asset to the Foundation going forward.
Another issue was the "Storm." We used to keep it a secret from the students, but it was Lavender's partial knowledge of it, granted due to her status as monitor assistant, that enabled her to act accordingly. Given that our conflict with Manus Vindictae will only continue to escalate, we must re-evaluate the school's policy on the dissemination of "Storm"-related information and even consider reforming our entire educational system.

Reports from both the Eastern and Western Fronts show that Manus Vindictae has been using the "Windweave" for a long time. If their previous attempts were just tests, then this attack was a planned operation, prepared since the last "Storm" ... the "Flood."
The entrance to the "Windweave" has been closed and reduced to ruins, but we should be able to restore it in time. Doing so will help us understand how Manus Vindictae carried out their attack.
We also need to consider the makeup of Manus Vindictae. High-ranking members followed Arcana, but not all share the same goals. Prima is loyal to Arcana, but Krutov seems to have other motives. Their leadership may be more complicated than we realize.
With the preliminary information on the "Windweave" and the capture of Prima, we may be able to reverse-engineer it and plan our counterattack.

On the eve of the "Storm," the Gryphon Legion used Admiral Igor's arcane skill to support the First Squad on a battlefield where Manus Vindictae had set an ambush. The enemy was stronger than expected, and with the "Storm" approaching, the First Squad faced a difficult choice after the battle.
In the end, the First Squad did not return to the Foundation, but they are safe. We have no intention of detaining any Foundation personnel. Whether they stay or leave will be decided once the situation stabilizes.
Please forward this message to the relevant Foundation officials and let them know that the Gryphon Legion does not intend to make an enemy of you.

Thank you so much for sheltering us, Vertin! I didn't expect that the Suitcase had enough space to house Glyndŵr and all the fledglings! But are you sure about this? The little ones can be very noisy sometimes ... Maybe I should build a birdhouse in the Wilderness for them.

After I moved in, I finally had the time to think about my life. So far, I've confirmed only one thing about myself: it calms me to watch the snow fall from the sky. I think I'll go to Iceland one day to see the snow there. Will you join me?

The world is changing too fast. I keep seeing, hearing, and feeling new things ... The instructors encourage me to ask questions when I don't understand something. Since your Suitcase has so much space, could you move the entire SPDM in here? That way, they can answer my questions at any time.

Vertin, I've gotten much better at controlling my body compared to when I first transformed: I only damaged five trees last month! You and all our other friends will be much safer next time we go on an adventure together. You can even fly on my back.
Hey, Vertin! How do you like my new record? I've saved it for a special day like this! What? I can play it all day today?! Blimey, now that's a celebration!

Hmph hmph! On this special day, you are given the privilege to ask the Great Matilda anything you want to know! I will divine for you ... How to write an operation report? That is not what divination is for!
Timekeeper, from the campus to the battlefield, I'm glad that we've stood together, side by side. Whatever lies in our way ... I will be there to assist you, as always.
